removed: (601) 866-9100 bennie_thompson@bellsouth.net Donate Home Meet Bennie Accomplishments Media Events Gallery News and Video Endorsements Get Involved Contact Home Meet Bennie Accomplishments Media Events Gallery News and Video Endorsements Get Involved Contact Top Homeland Security Democrat backs impeachment of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem Home Uncategorized / Top Homeland Security Democrat backs impeachment of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem Top Homeland Security Democrat backs impeachment of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem January 27, 2026 jones Uncategorized 0 0 Rep.
Bennie G.
Thompson, the senior Democrat on the House Homeland Security Committee, announced his support Friday for an effort to impeach Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.
The Mississippi lawmaker said Ms.
Noem has “enriched herself” on taxpayers’ dime, ignored Congress’s laws, defied court orders and hindered congressional oversight.
He said that amounted to abuse of power and a violation of her oath of office.
“Therefore, we must build a record and begin the process of impeachment.
It is not a remedy we pursue lightly, but it is also a duty we cannot ignore.
Be assured that accountability is coming,” Mr.
Thompson said.
He backed the impeachment resolution introduced this week by Rep.
Robin Kelly, Illinois Democrat.
She cited three articles, namely obstruction of Congress, violation of public trust and self-dealing.
Impeachment is unlikely to go anywhere with the GOP in control of the House, but Mr.
Thompson’s support for the idea made clear that Ms.
Noem will be a target if Democrats gain control of the chamber in November’s elections.
The same situation faced then-Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas, President Biden’s DHS chief.
When Republicans won control of the House in the 2022 election, he became a target.
He would go on to be impeached, becoming the first-ever sitting Cabinet official to suffer that ignominy.
Ironically, the charges against him were similar to those Ms.
Kelly has aimed at Ms.
Noem.
He was accused of breach of public trust and refusal to comply with the law.
The Senate, then under the control of Democrats, dismissed the impeachment case against Mr.
Mayorkas without holding a trial.
Ms.
Noem has brushed aside impeachment talk, saying she is focused on her job.
Anger at Homeland Security has boiled over this month with the slaying of Renee Good, a U.S. citizen who died in a confrontation with a U.S.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Minneapolis.

Video of that confrontation has deeply divided the country, with President Trump’s supporters saying it showed Good ignore orders to get out of her SUV and lurch the vehicle at the officer, who was justified in firing.
Mr.
Trump’s opponents say the officer was too quick on the trigger and could have gotten out of the way.

Bennie Thompson Endorses John Horhn for Mayor of Jackson January 27, 2026 jones Uncategorized 0 0 Mississippi Sen.
John Horhn should be the next mayor of Jackson, Mississippi, U.S.
House Rep.
Bennie Thompson said in an official statement endorsing the state senator for the position on April 16, days before Horhn faces incumbent Mayor Chokwe A.
Lumumba in the April 22 runoff.
“I have represented parts of Jackson both as Congressman and county supervisor and I’ve worked with mayors, from Dale Danks to Chokwe Lumumba, Sr. and Chokwe Antar Lumumba, the current mayor.
Given the many challenges facing Jackson, I am convinced that John Horhn is better suited to handle these challenges.

During lengthy talks with John, he shared his vision for the City of Jackson about crime, public safety, urban blight, housing, economic development and transportation,” Thompson said in an announcement on Wednesday.
The congressman represents Mississippi’s 2nd Congressional District, which includes Jackson and most of the Delta.
He is the latest official to throw their support behind Horhn.
Mississippi House Rep.
Zakiya Summers, a Jackson Democrat, and Mississippi House Rep.
Earle Banks, another Jackson Democrat, have also endorsed the longtime senator and both attended Horhn’s Oct.
3, 2024, campaign launch at the Jackson medical mall.

The City of Jackson holds “tremendous potential” and needs “a leader who sees not only the problems but the possibilities, and John Horhn is that leader,” Summers said. ‘I Have Concerns’ Horhn garnered over 48% of the vote during the Democratic municipal primary election on April 1, while the incumbent, Chokwe A.
Lumumba, received 17% of the vote, securing a runoff election to stay in the race.
“This campaign is about making sure that our city remains our city,” Lumumba said in a speech to his supporters the night of the primary election.
The mayor—who will face trial next year for federal charges related to a bribery investigation—vowed to change what he called a “false narrative” around his administration.

Some voters have voiced concerns over whether city-controlled assets will be threatened under Horhn’s leadership; the senator has a relatively friendlier relationship with Republican state leaders than the incumbent.
Still, Lumumba and Horhn have both stood in opposition to state-sponsored attempts to wrest away control of Jackson’s assets.

Thompson addressed that concern directly on Wednesday, saying that Horhn is “100% opposed to the State’s hostile takeover actions of the Jackson Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport.” “I know that federal, state and local resources, along with private investments, are required to address Jackson’s many current problems and are essential for future long-term City of Jackson’s progress,” Thompson’s April 16 endorsement states.

“After listening to and discussing with John his vision and plan, I encourage the voters of Jackson, MS to support John Horhn on April 22nd in the Democratic Primary Run-off Election.” Earlier this month, the congressman avoided directly endorsing a mayoral candidate while talking with constituents during a town hall meeting.
Instead, he told voters to look at the track records of the candidates before casting their ballots for mayor and city council representatives.
“If people have a record, they need to run on that record.
If it’s a bad record, you’re in trouble,” he said.
“But you’ve got to defend it.
I have concerns—I talk about it every day—but ultimately, the voters are the ones who are going to decide who will be the mayor and who will be the councilmen.
The potholes, the crime, all of that is a concern.” General Election Is June 3 The last day to vote in-person absentee is April 19.
Municipal Clerk’s Offices around the state will be open from 8:00 a.m. until noon.
After that, the only option for in-person voters will be on the day of the primary runoff: Tuesday, April 22.

All mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked by April 22 and received by the Jackson Municipal Clerk’s Offices by 5:00 p.m. on April 30 in order to be counted, the Secretary of State’s office says.
Whoever wins the Democratic primary runoff election will face off against the winner of the Republican primary runoff and the Independent candidates for mayor during the general election on June 3.
You must be registered # days before an election to cast a ballot in Mississippi and must bring an accepted form of voter ID.
More information on voter ID, including how to obtain a free voter ID, is available here .
For questions, contact the Elections Division at 1-800-829-6786, email ElectionsAnswers@sos.ms.gov, or visit YallVote.ms or contact your municipal clerk’s office directly.

Bennie Thompson visits Bean Path to support tech growth in Jackson January 27, 2026 jones Uncategorized 0 0 JACKSON, Miss. — U.S.
Rep.
Bennie Thompson visited the Bean Path in Jackson on Friday to support the nonprofit’s efforts in advancing technology and workforce training in Mississippi.
The Bean Path, founded by Dr.
Nashlie Sephus, is located in the Jackson Tech District and provides technical advice and guidance through workshops, robotics, and coding to people of all ages.
“The city will grow, and we want to make sure the community isn’t left out of that growth,” Sephus said.
“And also that we aren’t left behind when it comes to technology.” After more than six years of bringing tech to the capital city, Thompson paid a special visit for the first time.
“I’m very impressed,” Thompson said.
“I know a lot about this area.

I’ve represented it for quite a while and I’ve seen the highs and the lows, and so now we are back moving toward the top.” “We love it when our leaders and elected officials come to see the great work that we are doing right here at the Bean Path in downtown Jackson,” Sephus said.

“Our need and passion for wanting to share workforce training, especially AI and tech all across Mississippi — the more people involved the better.” Sephus said the Bean Path has helped many people get their certifications to help them in the job market.
They have also helped young people and small businesses.

“The fact that they are now working with school districts and other nonprofits in the state means that other folks are paying attention too, so we just want to be a part of it and be as helpful as we can,” Thompson said.
Sephus said in the near future she would like to have the Bean Path in multiple locations across the state.

Bennie Thompson’s Questions ‘Where Does Antifa Exist?’ Top FBI Official Struggles to Answer Rep.

Bennie Thompson’s Questions January 27, 2026 jones Uncategorized 0 0 A top FBI official struggled on Thursday to answer basic questions about Antifa after a Mississippi congressman pushed him to explain why he described the left-wing political movement as the nation’s top domestic terrorism threat.

“The first one—President Trump has just announced an executive order, the domestic organization Antifa—that’s our primary concern right now,” FBI National Security Branch Operations Director Michael Glasheen said during a U.S.
Homeland Security Committee meeting in Washington, D.C.
“OK, that’s what President Trump did.
What does the FBI say?” Rep.
Bennie Thompson, a Mississippi Democrat who serves as the ranking member of the committee, replied.
“We share the same view,” the FBI official replied.

“When you look at the data right now, you look at the domestic terrorist threat we’re facing, right now, what I see from my position is that’s the most immediate violent threat that we are facing on the domestic side.” In September, Trump signed an executive order labeling Antifa as a domestic terrorist organization.
Antifa is an anti-white supremacist, anti-fascist ideology, but has no organizational structure or leadership.

A Congressional Research Service report in 2020 said that Antifa adherents “view themselves as part of a protest tradition that arcs back to opposition groups in Nazi Germany and fascist Italy prior to World War II.” But it noted that U.S.

Antifa groups trace back to antiracist groups that “mobilized in the 1980s while opposing the activities of racist skinheads, members of the Ku Klux Klan (KKK), and neo-Nazis.” “So where is ANTIFA headquartered?” Thompson asked Glasheen during Thursday’s committee hearing.
“What we’re doing right now with the organization—,” the FBI official began.
The Mississippi congressman cut him off.
“Where in the United States does ANTIFA exist if it’s a terrorist organization and you’ve identified it as number one?” Thompson reiterated.
“We’re building out the infrastructure right now,” Glasheen said.
“So what does that mean?” Thompson pressed.
“I’m just, we’re trying to get the information.
You said ANTIFA is a terrorist organization.
Tell us, as a committee, how did you come to that?
Where do they exist?
How many members do they have in the United States as of right now?” “Well, it’s very fluid,” Glasheen said.
“It’s ongoing for us to understand that.

It’s no different than Al Qaeda and ISIS.” In October, the FBI brought what FBI Director Kash Patel called the first-ever Antifa-related terrorism charges against two suspects accused of setting off fireworks at an ICE facility in Texas before entering and firing upon officers using semiautomatic rifles.
The attack, which a federal indictment says “Antifa cell members” carried out, left one officer injured.

But while the Trump administration has focused on the threat of terrorism from individuals associated with Antifa beliefs, U.S. government assessments have repeatedly found in recent years that white supremacist and other racially motivated groups pose the highest threat.
During the committee hearing on Thursday, Rep.
Thompson appeared increasingly frustrated as Glasheen avoided directly answering his questions about Antifa.
“I asked you one question, sir.
I just want you to tell us: You said ANTIFA is the number one terrorist organization operating inside the United States,” the Mississippi Democrat said.
“I just need to know where they are, how many people.
I don’t want a name.
I don’t want anything like that.
How many people have you identified with the FBI that ANTIFA is made out of?” “Well, the investigations are active,” Glasheen said, repeatedly raising his hands and dropping them down.
“Sir, you wouldn’t come to this committee and say something you can’t prove, I know.
I knew you wouldn’t do that,” Thompson said.
Glasheen smiled.
“But you did.” Prev Next Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published.

added: Karaoke A Night of Fall Fun Sat, 10/24/2026 - 16:30 Join us at our Fall Fun Fest!
This is a free, family-friendly event for the community with music, free food, pumpkin carving and more!
We highly encourage you to RSVP so we can ensure we have enough food and pumpkins for all of our neighbors.

Schedule of Events: - 4:30pm: arrival - 5:00pm: Traditional dance by dancers from the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians and our Hispanic neighbors with Grupo Folklorico Xochiquetzal - 6:15pm: Taco bar (free dinner provided for all guests) - 6:45pm-9:00pm: Pumpkin carving, dancing and karaoke Our goal is to build community by spreading joy and meeting our neighbors.
We hope you can join us! *The karaoke will be an homage to Dolly Parton, so guests are encouraged to sing their favorite Dolly song.
Singing Dolly Parton is not required to participate, and all family-friendly songs are allowed. **Please note this is an indoor/outdoor event, so dress accordingly.
removed: Karaoke A Night of Fall Fun Sat, 10/24/2026 - 16:30 Join us for our Fall Fun Fest!
This is a free event for the community with music, dancing, pumpkin carving, karaoke and performances from Grupo Folklorica Xochiquetzal and the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians!
Snacks, dinner, non-alcoholic beverages, and one pumpkin per family will be provided.
The Fall Fun Fest is open to community members of all ages!
Please spread the word and invite your friends, family, and neighbors to join!

Schedule of Events: - 4:30pm: arrival - 5:00pm: Dances performed by Grupo Folklorico Xochiquetzal and powwow dancing from members of the Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians - 6:15pm: Taco bar (free dinner provided for all guests) - 6:45pm-9:00pm: Pumpkin carving, dancing and karaoke Our goal is to spread some joy and feed our neighbors.
We hope you can join us!

added: Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Donate → Home Meet Andy Meet Sine Endorsements News Action Center Issues Media Kit Donate Online Donate By Mail Store Donate Donate By Mail Store Katie Hobbs’s Campaign Caught Misleading Arizonans October 13, 2026 Press Release Hobbs’s latest smear against Andy Biggs “omits key facts” GILBERT, AZ— Katie Hobbs’s campaign was caught misleading Arizonans in their latest smear against Andy Biggs as voters begin casting their ballots with three weeks until Election Day.
Chief Correspondent Howie Fischer of Capitol Media Services writes that the latest attack from Hobbs’s campaign “omits key facts” around a 2012 bill opposed by then State Senator Andy Biggs.

According to Fischer : “ But what neither the media outlet nor Beyer mentions is that Biggs voted against the 2012 bill after citing a last-minute amendment that actually weakened the measure. ” The bill to crack down on sex offenders receiving some types of occupational licenses was weakened by a last-second amendment that created a loophole for offenders who hadn’t registered in the past 10 years.

Biggs noted at the time in a floor speech that the amendment would weaken the bill and voted no, but that context was maliciously left out of the Hobbs campaign’s attack as it was filtered through a website connected to a pro-Democrat Party organization.
Fischer wrote: “ The neutrality of American Journal News can be called into question.
A prime investor is the American Bridge 21st Century Foundation.

And that is the nonprofit sister of American Bridge 21st Century, which lists itself as “the largest research, tracking, and rapid response operation in the Democratic Party. ” Andy Biggs has a long track record of protecting women and children in his time as a prosecutor and through his decades of service in elected office.

Biggs worked directly with Senator John McCain to pass the Ashlynne Mike Amber Alert in Indian Country Act into law and most recently passed his CSAFE Act through the House of Representatives to crack down on predators.

removed: Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Donate → Home Meet Andy Meet Sine Endorsements News Action Center Issues Media Kit Donate Online Donate By Mail Store Donate Donate By Mail Store Katie Hobbs’s Culture of Corruption Continues to Haunt Campaign August 31, 2026 Press Release Just when Hobbs thought the Democrat AG had bailed her out, new reporting brings to light additional corruption accusations GILBERT, AZ—New reporting from multiple Arizona media outlets has revealed additional corruption and ethics accusations against Katie Hobbs as her Culture of Corruption continues to bring negative scrutiny and headlines to her campaign.

The Arizona Republic reported that Hobbs’s favorite political donor Simon Kottoor, the CEO of Sunshine Residential Homes, had told then-Department of Child Safety Director Mike Faust that Kottoor could help him keep his job if he approved a massive taxpayer-funded rate hike for Sunshine.

Faust declined to do so and was later fired by Hobbs, whose administration ultimately approved a rate hike only for Sunshine Residential after their executives made additional political contributions to support Hobbs and her endeavors.

Arizona Capitol Media reported this morning that Katie Hobbs is still refusing to disclose who has made donations to her dark-money “Legal Defense Fund”, despite donations from Sunshine Residential to that fund being made public through the course of the criminal investigation for corruption.

In response to the additional reporting, the Biggs for Arizona campaign released a new ad, “ Katie Hobbs’s Culture of Corruption ”, which includes details on: -The ongoing criminal investigation for an alleged pay-to-play scheme where Katie Hobbs’s administration approved a massive $# million rate hike for a six-figure political donor; -Hobbs’s administration awarding a $700,000 contract for a new state logo , which included funds sent to a crony of the Arizona Office of Tourism Director’s former consulting firm; -Hobbs’s Department of Housing wiring $2 million in taxpayer funds to a scammer.

added: Meet Bobby NEWS Issues ACtion center Get Involved Events STORE X DONATE BOBBY CHARLES DECLARES VICTORY AFTER TONIGHT’S CBS13/FOX23 DEBATE — EXPOSES PINGREE’S INSIDER DEALING AND THE MILLS-PINGREE RECORD OF FAILURE October 13, 2026 Pingree Disqualifies Herself as a Serious Candidate by Showing She Doesn't Know Size of State Budget ‍ PORTLAND, Maine — Republican nominee Bobby Charles dominated tonight’s televised gubernatorial debate on WGME CBS 13 and FOX 23, putting Democrat Hannah Pingree on the defensive over basic math errors, misstatements about public charter schools, serious questions of self-dealing, and the documented failures of the Mills-Pingree administration. ‍ Pingree claimed that Bobby’s plan to cut $4 billion from the budget amounted to “more than half” of the state budget.
The current state biennial budget is approximately $30 billion.
Four billion dollars is not half of $30 billion — it is roughly 13 percent.

The exaggeration was clear to viewers and underscored a pattern of loose numbers when defending the status quo. ‍ Pingree also attacked Charles for supporting charter schools, describing them as private schools that divert money from public schools.
Under Maine law (Title 20-A, Chapter 112), public charter schools are public schools.
They are tuition-free, open to all students through lottery when oversubscribed, and part of the public education system.

The funding follows the student within the public system. ‍ “Hannah Pingree spent the night misstating the size of the budget and mislabeling public charter schools as private,” said Dale Crafts, Jr. , campaign manager for Bobby Charles for Governor.
“Mainers watching at home know $4 billion is not half of a $30 billion budget, and they know charter schools in this state are public schools by law.

When the math and the basic facts don’t add up, it tells you everything about the record she’s defending.” ‍ On housing — one of the night’s central issues — Bobby Charles delivered a direct contrast in the debate: ‍ “Mills/Pingree have killed the American Dream.
Most Mainers cannot afford a median house.
It’s a $30 billion problem, we’re 80,000 units down, Hannah has suggested 250 houses being built solves the problem with $100 million, I don’t agree.
What I’m going to do is roll back the burdensome regulations on builders, number one.
Number two, use the tax code to accelerate manufacturing.
Number three, use the governorship to speed up permitting.
Number four, promote tax exemptions for first-time homebuyers, particularly those that are young and they’re out there trying to pay rent right now.
Next, reduce and eventually eliminate the noncitizens in our public housing.
Mainers do not need gimmicks, like a 250 house answer to a $30 billion problem.

What they want is real housing, they want their housing to be available to them and as governor, that’ll be a priority to me.” ‍ While Pingree tried to change the subject and defend the status quo, Charles repeatedly returned to the core choice facing Maine voters: continue the insider deals and declining results of the last eight years, or elect a former federal prosecutor and naval intelligence officer who will cut taxes, cut crime, lower costs, and demand real accountability. ‍ “Tonight made the choice crystal clear,” Charles said after the debate.

“Hannah Pingree and Janet Mills doubled housing costs, drove up electricity bills, left Maine last in the nation on children’s well-being, and oversaw a system where tens of millions in Medicaid dollars for autism services were improperly paid while vulnerable kids went without.
You don’t invite the people who created the fire to put it out.

Mainers saw that tonight.” ‍ Corruption and transparency questions that will not go away ‍ Charles again pressed Pingree on the $37,458 Community Resilience Partnership grant her office (the Governor’s Office of Policy Innovation and the Future) awarded to the Island Institute in 2022 while she served as director.

At the same time, the Institute was a client of her husband Jason Mann’s Beechwood Film company, which produced the climate film “Climate of Change – Clean Energy Solutions for the Working Waterfront.” ‍ Public records do not yet prove the grant dollars went directly to Mann or Beechwood Film — which is precisely why Charles has demanded the contracts, invoices, payment records, conflict disclosures, and communications.
Pingree has called the questions “completely made up,” and the Island Institute has said no state or federal dollars funded the film series.

Charles has responded that if nothing improper occurred, the full records should be released immediately so Mainers can judge for themselves. ‍ Additional questions surround an $840,000 forgivable housing loan connected to North Haven Sustainable Housing (where Mann has served in a leadership role and Pingree previously had involvement) and the evaluation process for the Island Institute grant, including the role of a former Island Institute Fellow who participated in scoring and certified no conflict. ‍ “These are not abstract ethics questions,” Charles said.
“They are about whether taxpayer money under Hannah’s watch ended up benefiting her family or connected organizations, and whether proper recusals and transparency occurred.

The only way to restore it is full disclosure — not denials and stonewalling.” ‍ The broader record of failure ‍ Charles tied the ethics questions to concrete results under the Mills administration, in which Pingree served as a senior policy official from 2019 to 2025: ‍ Housing costs that have roughly doubled for the median home, pricing young Mainers out of ownership.
A projected budget shortfall exceeding $1.3 billion.
Child welfare crises, including multiple child deaths in short order in 2021, a rising foster-care population, and a 2024 U.S.
Department of Justice lawsuit over failures to serve children with disabilities in the community.
Declining education outcomes, with Maine ranking near the bottom nationally in fourth-grade reading proficiency.
At least $45.6 million in improper Medicaid payments for autism and related rehabilitative services identified in a federal audit.
High electricity and property tax burdens that continue to squeeze working families. ‍ “Hannah wants credit for her years next to Janet Mills, but she refuses to own the results,” Charles said.
Tens of millions went out the door improperly.

That is the record she is asking Maine to extend for four more years.” ‍ Independent Rick Bennett offered process critiques and bipartisanship rhetoric but did not present a clear break from the status quo on taxes, spending, or accountability. ‍ The choice for Maine ‍ Charles closed by outlining his priorities: a major homestead exemption increase fully reimbursed by the state, zero property taxes for 100% disabled veterans, regulatory relief to speed housing production, a hiring freeze and restructuring of key agencies, an end to insider contracting, and immediate steps to lower energy costs.

He reiterated that he will confront Washington — including the Trump administration — when Maine’s interests are at stake, particularly on tariffs affecting Canadian trade. ‍ Early voting is underway.

Election Day is November 3, 2026. ‍ To watch clips from tonight’s debate and learn more about Bobby Charles’s plans, visit BobbyForMaine.com or follow @Bobby4Maine on X and the campaign’s Facebook page. ‍ ABOUT BOBBY CHARLES Bobby Charles is the Republican nominee for Governor of Maine and a native of Wayne.

A former federal prosecutor and naval intelligence officer, he is running to cut taxes, cut crime, bring down electricity and fuel costs, and end the insider dealing that has defined eight years of the Mills administration.
He faces Democrat Hannah Pingree and independent Rick Bennett on November 3.

removed: Meet Bobby NEWS Issues ACtion center Get Involved Events STORE X DONATE Bobby Charles for Governor Campaign Launches New Digital Ad “Ruth & Gerry” Highlighting Impact of Soaring Property Taxes on Seniors Maine Couple: “Everybody is Struggling.
My Kids are struggling.

My Grandkids are Struggling” August 17, 2026 AUGUSTA, ME — Today, the Bobby Charles for Governor campaign announced the launch of a new digital ad highlighting the severe financial strain that skyrocketing property taxes and the rising cost of living are placing on elderly residents and working families across the state.
The ad, titled "Ruth & Gerry," features a senior resident detailing the devastating reality of trying to survive on a fixed income under the current political establishment.
“Ruth and I worked very hard all our lives,” the narrator explains, noting that their local taxes have nearly doubled.

This hike has stretched their budget “to the max,” forcing the couple to take more money out of their Social Security just to cover the tax bills. ‍ The deeply personal message underscores a broader economic crisis.
As the speaker notes, “Everybody is struggling.
My kids are struggling.

My grandkids are struggling”. ‍ The ad also draws a sharp contrast between hardworking taxpayers and out-of-touch political insiders, specifically calling out Governor Janet Mills and gubernatorial nominee Hannah Pingree.

The narrator points out that these politicians “have no idea what it's like to struggle,” while “taxpayer dollars keep them happy, keep us broke”. ‍ “We cannot continue to price our seniors out of the homes they have spent their entire lives working to keep,” said Bobby Charles.
“This ad is a direct reflection of what I hear from voters every single day.
They are being crushed by out-of-control taxes and a political establishment that simply doesn't understand their struggles.

AsGovernor, I will reduce taxes and ensure that our elderly residents can afford to stay in the communities they helped build.” ‍ The ad concludes with a strong endorsement of Charles's proposed solutions: “I believe in Bobby Charles, reduce taxes and help elderly people that can't afford where they're living.
They're afraid they're going to lose their home.” The digital ad will run across multiple online platforms as part of a targeted statewide buy.
To watch the full ad, click here. ‍ To learn more about Bobby Charles’s plan to lower property taxes and protect seniors, please visit BobbyForMaine.com.

added: Skip to content HOME Front Page – ES ABOUT BOB About Bob – ES WHY WHY VOTE FOR BOB WHY VOTE INDEPENDENT WHY THE FORWARD PARTY MAKE THE SENATE WORK AGAIN ISSUES EVENTS NEWS VOLUNTEER HOME Front Page – ES ABOUT BOB About Bob – ES WHY WHY VOTE FOR BOB WHY VOTE INDEPENDENT WHY THE FORWARD PARTY MAKE THE SENATE WORK AGAIN ISSUES EVENTS NEWS VOLUNTEER PAID FOR BY BOB CHEW FOR SENATE DONATE LATEST NEWS on October 13, 2026 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE DENVER, CO – October 13, 2026 – The Center Party is proud to announce its official endorsement of Bob Chew for the United States Senate representing the state of Colorado.

At a time when partisan gridlock and political extremes are increasingly dividing the nation, Bob Chew emerges as a pragmatic, solutions-oriented leader dedicated to serving the majority in the middle.
Bob Chew, US Senate Candidate for Colorado The Center Party’s endorsement is rooted in Bob Chew’s unwavering commitment to the core principles of balance, compromise, and common sense.

After a thorough review of his platform and vision for Colorado, the Center Party recognizes that Chew perfectly embodies our Eight Pillars of reform: • Fiscal Responsibility: Chew understands that out-of-control spending threatens our nation’s future.

He is committed to reigning in the national debt and implementing sensible budgeting that protects taxpayer dollars without compromising essential services. • Government Efficiency: A firm believer in cutting red tape, Chew is dedicated to streamlining federal agencies, eliminating waste, and ensuring that government programs work for the people, not the bureaucracy. • Balanced Policy: Rejecting the extreme agendas of the far-left and far-right, Chew advocates for evidence-based legislation that finds common ground and delivers real results for everyday Americans.

Global Strength: Chew supports a strong, smart foreign policy that protects American interests abroad, strengthens alliances, and ensures our military remains the most capable in the world. • Fair Representation in Government: Recognizing the dysfunction of the current two-party system, Chew is an advocate for structural reforms that empower independent-minded voters and guarantee all citizens have a meaningful voice in Washington. • Equal Opportunity for All: True to his own life story of hard work and resilience, Chew is passionate about restoring the American Dream and ensuring that every Coloradan has the tools to succeed, regardless of their background. • Ensure American Jobs and Prosperity: Chew’s pro-growth agenda focuses on supporting small businesses, investing in future-focused industries, and keeping high paying jobs within our borders to secure long-term economic stability. • Protect Our Environment: Acknowledging the natural beauty and resources of Colorado, Chew champions practical, market-driven environmental protections that preserve our land and water while maintaining energy independence and economic growth.
“Americans are exhausted by the toxic division in Washington,” said CEO, Scott Brennan of the Center Party.
“Bob Chew represents the common-sense leadership that our country desperately needs.
He isn’t beholden to radical ideologies; he is committed to the people of Colorado.
We are thrilled to stand behind his campaign for the U.S.
Senate.” “The enthusiasm for my candidacy has been overwhelming.
Everywhere I go, people are so glad to know there is a viable candidate willing to break through the political dysfunction and offer real courage for real solutions,” said Bob Chew.
“I want to thank the Center Party for its vote of confidence and support.

Together, we can fix our political system and deliver real results for the American People!” The Center Party invites all moderate Republicans, moderate Democrats and Independents who feel unrepresented by the current system to join the movement for a better tomorrow.
For more information about the Center Party please visit our official website at w ww.centerparty.com .

removed: top of page HOME ABOUT BOB BLOG EVENTS ON THE TRAIL WITH BOB FIORETTI VOLUNTEER Fioretti Direct Mail Campaign PODCASTS/MEDIA CONTACT US DONATE Search All Posts safe t act Search Bio Series Part 6: Bob Fioretti's Independent Record of Reform Oct 6 2 min read Bio Series • Part 6 Leadership • Integrity • Public Trust Independent Reform & Accountable Leadership Bob Fioretti’s tenure on the Chicago City Council established a benchmark for principled, independent governance.
Throughout his service, Bob consistently put taxpayers and neighborhood integrity ahead of backroom politics, standing up for genuine transparency and structural reform.
A Proven Record on the Chicago City Council For the past seven weeks, we have shared the experiences that have prepared Bob Fioretti to serve as Illinois Attorney General.
Bob has built his career around independent leadership, professional integrity, and accountability to the public.
The Illinois Committee for Honest Government presented Bob with a Distinguished Service Award for his commitment to his ward and the people of Chicago.
Independent organizations also recognized Bob’s record of reform-minded public service.
He received the Leon Despres Award for independent reform and public-interest leadership.
Highly respected University of Illinois Chicago professor Dick Simpson also highlighted Bob’s consistent independence as a Chicago alderman, noting that in one year he voted “no” 38% of the time.
Bob has also served on the Illinois Supreme Court’s Character and Fitness Committee and contributed to the Chicago Bar Association’s Judicial Evaluation Committee.
These responsibilities require careful judgment, professional integrity, and a commitment to maintaining public confidence in the legal system.
“Public service is a sacred trust.

When government operates behind closed doors, taxpayers pay the price.” The leadership Bob Fioretti will bring to the Attorney General’s Office Bob will expose corruption, protect consumers, defend victims, uphold civil rights, and make government answer to the citizens.
He will not allow political insiders to determine which cases receive attention and which problems are ignored.
Bob is traveling across Illinois, meeting voters and building a campaign powered by people rather than the political establishment.
Every community visited, and every conversation held, moves this campaign forward, but we cannot finish the job without you.
Bob Fioretti will be the People's Attorney Please support Bob by volunteering, attending an event, sharing our message, or contributing whatever you are able.
No contribution is too small.
Every bit counts as we approach Election Day.

title.before: House GOP sets up panel to probe government ‘weaponization’ – Boyle for Idaho

removed: Skip to content Home News & Media Issues Volunteer Menu Home News & Media Issues Volunteer Donate Here House GOP sets up panel to probe government ‘weaponization’ hiraafzal615 August 17, 2024 No Comments By Michael Macagnone (originally posted on rollcall.com ) Posted January 10, 2023 at 4:54pm House Republicans on Tuesday established a select subcommittee to investigate the “weaponization” of the federal government.
It will have the power to investigate executive branch agencies and their ties to private sector entities and have oversight of ongoing criminal probes.

The House voted 221-211, along party lines, to approve the resolution to create the subcommittee, one of the first actions of an aggressive Republican approach to oversight since they took control of the chamber.
Republicans likened the panel, which falls under the Judiciary Committee, to prior committees that investigated oversteps by the FBI and intelligence agencies.
Democrats called it dangerous and a way for Republicans to interfere with ongoing investigations into former President Donald Trump.

During floor debate, Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan of Ohio pointed to a litany of alleged oversteps by the Justice Department in recent years, including investigations of parents who spoke at local school boards and communications with companies like Twitter about taking down posts during the 2020 election.
“We don’t want to go after anyone, we want it to stop, and we want to respect the First Amendment to the Constitution that the greatest country in the world has,” Jordan said.
Jordan likely will helm the subcommittee, which will have access to information available to the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence as well as subpoena power.
The panel will include 15 members — nine Republicans and six Democrats approved by House Speaker Kevin McCarthy , R-Calif.

The resolution directs the panel to issue a final report on its findings before the end of the current Congress on a wide range of topics, including government information collection and potential civil liberties violations of American citizens.
House Judiciary Committee ranking member Jerrold Nadler , D-N.Y., called the panel a “dangerous and unprecedented attack” on law enforcement agencies.

“Make no mistake, the Destroy Democracy Subcommittee will enable the House Republicans to interfere with the free operation of businesses they do not like, to inhibit the fight against domestic terrorism, and to settle political scores on behalf of Donald Trump,” Nadler said in a floor speech.
Rep.
Jim McGovern , D-Mass., called the panel “deranged” and compared it to the House Un-American Activities Committee at the height of the Red Scare.
McGovern and other Democrats said they viewed the select subcommittee as a partisan exercise following last week’s fight over the speaker gavel.
In a floor speech, McGovern alleged that the panel was created at the behest of those who did not back McCarthy in the rounds of speaker votes, because they were looking to protect Trump.
“There is a reason why after 13 times they added another line giving this committee the authority to look at ongoing criminal investigations,” McGovern said.
Republicans countered by alleging that Democrats have ignored ongoing civil liberties violations by the federal government.
Rep.
Dan Bishop of North Carolina, one of the Republicans who objected to McCarthy’s election on several speaker ballots last week, touted the subcommittee’s creation as a victory.
“Today we are putting the deep state on notice.
We are coming for you on behalf of everyday Americans,” Bishop said.

11/8/2025 • IN THE NEWS Read More Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Brad Chambers Announces Campaign for Pennsylvania’s 41st State House District with High-Profile Endorsements FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE August 20, 2025 LANCASTER COUNTY, PA (August 20, 2025) - Brad Chambers has announced his campaign for PA HD-41 in 2026.
HD-41—comprising Columbia Borough, East and West Hempfield Townships, Mountville Borough, and part of Manor Township— is recognized as Lancaster County’s most competitive State House District.
Chambers previously ran in 2024 in a campaign that knocked more than 26,000 doors.

Chambers, a labor administrator and community advocate, intends to run on a campaign that fights for housing that is affordable for all, the funding our schools and children deserve, and lifesaving universal healthcare coverage.
Chambers has also obtained a number of significant endorsements from across the 41st District and Lancaster County.
Brad Chamber’s endorsements include: State Representative Ismail Smith-Wade-El (HD-49) - “Brad is my first endorsement of the 2026 cycle, and that’s no accident.
People in Lancaster are tired of politicians who have a lot of bark, but are leashed to their corporate donors.

Hempfield, Mountville, Columbia - they ought to have a State Representative who works for them, and no one works harder than Brad Chambers.” State Representative Nikki Rivera (HD-96) - “It is with great respect and admiration that I endorse Brad Chambers for PA State Representative in House District 41 in 2026.

Brad’s unwavering loyalty to his community, his outstanding work ethic, and his commitment to serving absolutely all of his neighbors earn him a spot on the ballot and the opportunity to serve in the PA General Assembly.” County Commissioner Alice Yoder - “It is my pleasure to endorse Brad Chambers for PA House in District 41.
Brad is hardworking and committed to serving his community and I know he will be an excellent representative for his district— which includes me!

I have been a witness to the way Brad has thrown himself into serving his community outside of politics and his dedication, integrity, work ethic, and genuine commitment to helping people make him an outstanding representative for all of us in the 41st.” Hempfield School Board Member Judy Brady - “Brad’s energy and devotion to building trusting, personal relationships with the Hempfield, Manor Township, and Columbia communities is truly remarkable.

I have full confidence that when elected, as he is ALREADY doing, Brad will tirelessly fight to bring equitable education funding, health care reform, and affordable housing to benefit his district constituents and all Pennsylvanians.

Brad Chambers is the exact person the HD-41 has been waiting for to represent the interests of all residents in this western region of Lancaster County.” Hempfield School Board Member Megan Eshleman - “As a local school board director, I am excited about having a representative like Brad who doesn't just talk about the importance of public education, but will back it up with actions in Harrisburg.” East Hempfield Supervisor Bob Johnson - “I endorse Brad Chambers for the position of PA State Representative for the 41st district in the 2026 election.
Brad is extremely hard-working, dependable, and energetic.

His positions on issues are well thought-out and consistent with what I believe are most beneficial to the residents of our district and the state.” Columbia Borough School Board President Charles Leader - “I give my support to Brad Chambers.
Brad is willing to serve the public.
Brad understands people and realizes their everyday concerns, challenges and issues.
He has the energy and commitment to be a positive force in Harrisburg.
I am convinced Brad will help initiate and bring about the needed changes in both his district and the state.

Giving Brad a chance to prove his ability will show he will work for the people and that is what is needed.” State Senator James Malone (SD-36) - “I'm honored to endorse Brad Chambers for PA's 41st statehouse District.
I've seen Brad's dedication to progress and working people first hand.

I can think of no one better to join me in representing Columbia and Hempfield in the state legislature.” “These past few months have demonstrated to me that the same issues that first called me to run for State Representative last year are more urgent than ever.
Donald Trump and Pennsylvania Republicans continue to gut our health care.
Rent and mortgage costs continue to soar.
Our teachers and students go without the resources they need.
Only when we realize that no one is coming to save us can we truly meet this political moment.

We must step up in any way we can, which is why I've decided I will be running for the 41st PA State House District in 2026.” - Brad Chambers, Candidate for HD-41 The Pennsylvania House Democratic Campaign Committee (PA HDCC) has previously identified Chambers' race in HD-41 as " one of the most competitive races in the state. " James Malone’s win in SD-36 with nearly all precincts in the 41st, as well as the promising primary vote totals in Hempfield and Columbia suggest the same.

Little joins third lawsuit challenging Biden vaccine mandates Dec 10, 2021 Boise, Idaho – Governor Brad Little announced today Idaho joined another lawsuit challenging President Joe Biden’s unprecedented government overreach and vaccine mandates.
Idaho and 11 other states are part of a Louisiana lawsuit seeking to stop Biden’s vaccine mandate on healthcare workers.
The lawsuit follows a similar but separate 10-state challenge filed in Missouri.
The Biden Administration proposed using the Medicare and Medicaid system to impose a vaccine on 17 million healthcare workers.
“President Biden has no legal authority to force hospitals and other healthcare facilities to require their employees to get vaccinated.
His illegal attempt would intensify a problem confronting our country – we already have a short supply of healthcare workers available to handle the pandemic.
As I’ve stated before, Biden’s coercive, threatening attempts to increase vaccination rates damage a country already divided.
He is breeding a level of resentment and distrust of government that will take generations to heal.
His actions simply are not good for our country, now or in the long term,” Governor Little said.

At Governor Little’s direction, Idaho is party to two other lawsuits challenging Biden’s mandates –one involving federal contractors and another involving private employers with 100 or more employees.
Idaho’s involvement in each was facilitated by Attorney General Lawrence Wasden and his office.

Little slams Biden, proposes more tax cuts in State of the State address Jan 31, 2022 Idaho Gov.

Brad Little scorned the Democratic President Joe Biden and the federal government and touted Idaho’s frugality, as he proposed investing billions in tax cuts, public safety and education, during the final State of the State address in his first term as governor.
Little, who is expected to join an already crowded gubernatorial campaign in the coming months, spoke to a joint assembly of the House and Senate at the Idaho Capitol on Monday.
Little spoke shortly after the two bodies kicked off the second regular session of the 66th Idaho Legislature.
The Republican governor framed his speech around Idaho’s economic success during the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.
He also notched a number of GOP talking points, including election integrity and border security.
He took aim at the federal government and Biden, repeatedly using the term “Bidenflation,” to signify that the Democratic president is responsible for recent inflation increases.
“While other states liquidated their rainy day funds and begged politicians in Washington, D.C., for a bailout, together we rolled up our sleeves, made tough decisions, and led Idaho,” Little said.
Little went on to criticize Biden’s COVID-19 vaccination mandates — one of the few times Little mentioned the pandemic Monday.
Little signed onto a lawsuit with other governors that challenged the vaccine mandates.
Little also ctiticized Biden’s policy on the U.S.-Mexico border.
Last year, the Idaho governor sent Idaho State Police troopers to Arizona to assist law enforcement officers there.
Little announced a new program, “Operation Esto Perpetua,” which “will bring together law enforcement and communities in new ways.” Little said more details on the program will be released later.
“Biden’s inaction has spawned a growing drug threat in our state,” Little said.
“The vast majority of illicit drugs in Idaho are now sourced in Mexico.” Little on Monday released his budget proposals for the current and upcoming fiscal year.
He announced a new plan, called “Leading Idaho,” which includes more than $1 billion in tax cuts and more than $1.1 billion in education funding.

title.after: How we won

added: How we won First: Thank you to all the volunteers, donors, and campaign team.

1 Brad: 36.8% Thompson (R): 32.7% Levine: 15.2% Others: 15.3% Levine's campaign and Super PAC spent heavily and effectively on a professional digital and mail campaign, albeit false, to convince voters that President Barack Obama had endorsed him.
Polls showed that many voters believed him, but they voted for Sherman anyway.

Levine had over $3.5 million in resources: Raised by Levine Campaign: $2,739,028.302 Raised by New ERA Leadership PAC (exclusively dedicated to helping Levine): $779,577.503 Spending for Levine by the Progress Action Fund: $100,0004 Total: $3,618,605.80 Levine's fundraising included $750,000 of his own funds contributed to his campaign and $550,000 from his parents to New Era Leadership PAC.
Levine was a full-time candidate; he did not earn a paycheck for 16 months.
He had all of the classic credentials for a serious candidate.
Served on White House National Security Council and served as Chief Climate Officer of the DFC, the U.S. government agency that invests tens of billions in lower-income countries.

1 California Secretary of State, Statement of Vote — June 2, 2026 Statewide Direct Primary Election, United States Representative, at 76–89, accessed July 17, 2026, https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/sov/2026-primary/sov/76-us-rep.pdf.
2 Federal Election Commission, Candidate Summary, Jake Levine (H6CA32207), accessed July 17, 2026, https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H6CA32207/.

3 Federal Election Commission, Committee Summary, New Era Leadership (C00945824), Independent Expenditure-Only Committee, 2026 Cycle, coverage 04/01/2026–05/31/2026, accessed July 17, 2026, https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00945824/.
The 2026 primary cycle was a unique once-in-a-decade anti-incumbent cycle due in part to the Biden implosion; Democratic voters demanded Youth and Change.
Levine and his IE’s spent millions behind that message.

Levine had a host of endorsements, including the League of Conservation Voters, California Environmental Voters, luminaries from the Obama and Biden White House, three former local congressmembers, and many Democratic Clubs.
The hosts of Pod Save America and David Letterman both did fundraising for him.
He had the support of John Favreau, Tommy Vietor, Ben Rhodes, Samantha Power, and Jake Sullivan.
So why did Sherman beat Levine nearly 2.5 to 1?
Seniority and skill that brought home funds for nearly 200 community projects.

A record of championing progressive causes that earned him endorsements (every labor endorsement, the Sierra Club, the Planned Parenthood Action Fund, and every local elected official who endorsed in the race).
A large war chest (despite no self-funding).
In every other seriously contested race Sherman has had, he has put his own money into the campaign, often over half his net worth.
This time, Sherman put in none of his personal money.
Sherman for Congress ended the campaign with nearly $3 million cash on hand.
Allies who contributed but were also prepared to do far more if necessary — but it did not prove necessary for Sherman’s allies to go all-in.
Sherman had scores of volunteers from every neighborhood and ethnic community in his district.
And Sherman has even more room for improvement.
Sherman had never represented the Ventura County portion (Simi Valley) of the post-Prop 50 32nd Congressional District - and this showed in the results.
Sherman received only 25.9% of the Ventura County vote.

However, soon Simi Valley will see Sherman’s legendary community involvement, frequent presence at community functions, outstanding constituent services, and record of using his seniority and legislative prowess to bring back federal dollars for community projects.
In 1996, Thousand Oaks was the most Republican city in Ventura County and was included in Sherman’s first district.
It voted against Sherman by 20+% in his first contested general election (1996).
Four years later, Sherman carried Thousand Oaks, a 20-point improvement.

KEEPING OUR DISTRICT FIRST Who is Brian Lanoue?
Brian is a life-long resident of Eastern Connecticut.
He graduated from the Norwich Free Academy, earned his bachelor’s degree from Eastern Connecticut State University, and a Master’s degree from Southern Connecticut State University.
Brian is also a former champion powerlifter- one of the youngest athletes ever having won the Men’s Open World title for the deadlift, substance-free, at just 21 years of age.
Tired of what the State legislature was doing to Connecticut, Brian took these life experiences and put them to work for the people of Eastern Connecticut.
In 2018, Brian was elected to the Connecticut House of Representatives where he has been a constant champion for children, workers, small businesses, and farmers in his district.
Keeping Our District First 100% Score from the Connecticut Business and Industry Association (CBIA) and endorsed by the NFIB.
Brian introduced legislation to cut regulations and taxes to support workers, business owners, and farmers.
Strong advocate to protect children from sexual predators and violent felons.
Brian's legislation requiring background checks on all prospective children’s camp employees got passed into law with Public Act 21-82.
This successful program combats the opioid and mental health crises by bringing together our police and mental health professionals.
A staunch supporter of the right to bear arms.
Endorsed by both the CCDL & NRA.
Introduced H.B.5227, to prevent towns and cities from imposing firearm restrictions on law-abiding citizens.
Also fought and defeated the 35% ammo tax on gun owners.
6525, to examine breaking up the Eversource monopoly and creating competition in the energy market to protect Connecticut ratepayers.
Fought to upgrade Voluntown into the top tier for the new PILOT funding formula.
Supported our local volunteer first responders by introducing H.B.
5722, which tax exempts their stipend payment.
Called an amendment to protect private property owners from eminent domain abuse.
Helped our veterans and volunteer fire departments.
Advocated for small businesses and working-class families.

added: Skip to content 45th Assembly District – Griswold, Ledyard, Lisbon, Preston, Voluntown Menu Home Privacy Policy Privacy Policy Who we are Our website address is: https://brianforthe45.com.
Comments When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.
An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it.
The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/.
After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.
Media If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included.
Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.
Cookies If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies.
These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment.
These cookies will last for one year.
If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies.
This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.
When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices.
Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year.
If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks.
If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.
If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser.
This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited.
Embedded content from other websites Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.).
Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.
Who we share your data with If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.
How long we retain your data If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely.
This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.
For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile.
All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username).
Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us.
You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you.
This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service. © # Brian Lanoue State Representative 45th District Paid for by Brian 45, Jennifer McDowell, Treasurer, Approved by Brian Lanoue privacy policy Close Skip to content Open toolbar Accessibility Tools Increase Text Decrease Text Grayscale High Contrast Negative Contrast Light Background Links Underline Readable Font Reset
Double funding for California’s critical Homeless Housing Assistance and Prevention program (HAAP) to prevent struggling renters’ slide into homelessness.
Expand the effective moderate and low-income Housing Voucher program at the state level to compensate for Federal cutbacks.
Scale up non-profits' acquisition and management of existing affordable housing properties.
(The program is called “NOAH” to describe Naturally Occurring Affordable Housing.

Under NOAH, nonprofits raise a mix of local public/private funds to purchase such housing to then preserve its affordability long term, provide supportive services, and perform needed repairs.) Extend the Tenant Protection Act past 2030 to cap rent increases, require “just cause” to evict long term tenants, and provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
Support and defend the rent control currently in place.

added: Coalitions A statewide coalition of pastors, sheriffs, state lawmakers, business owners, educators and civic leaders supporting Byron Donalds for governor and Bryan Ávila for lieutenant governor.

Join the Coalition 25 Leaders Statewide Earn, Learn, Own The Plan Tallahassee To Miami THE COALITION Earn, Learn, Own: from Tallahassee to Miami Twenty-five Black leaders from across Florida launched the Florida Coalition of Black Leaders for Donalds, a statewide coalition supporting Republican nominee Byron Donalds for governor and his running mate, Bryan Ávila, for lieutenant governor.
The coalition includes pastors, sheriffs, state lawmakers, business owners, educators and civic leaders from Tallahassee to Miami.

Donalds and Ávila have spent time in Black communities across the state, in churches, barbershops, small businesses and on HBCU campuses, hearing from families about the cost of living, public safety, education and economic opportunity.
Donalds began his college education at Florida A&M University and finished at Florida State University.
If elected, he would be Florida’s first Black governor.
Coalition members will carry Earn, Learn, Own, the campaign’s plan for jobs, education and ownership, into churches, barbershops, campuses and small businesses across the state.

Voter Guide Contact Us Solutions Events Volunteer Donate Voter Guide Contact Us Solutions Events Volunteer Donate Policy Platform Solutions for Georgia's 9th District Clear priorities for working families across North Georgia.
Support Our Campaign Volunteer Voter Guide Caitlyn's Policy Priorities People-First Solutions Caitlyn Gegen will take an inclusive approach to all policies.
Select a priority below to read her full position.
01 Affordability I am committed to fighting for a livable minimum wage, expanding the stock of affordable housing, and advocating for universal healthcare.

I will fight for a future where every hardworking person in Georgia’s 9th Congressional District can live a life of dignity, where they have extra savings at the end of the month and are confident they will be able to buy their home.
02 Universal Healthcare Nobody should be dying, in the wealthiest country in the world, because they are unable to access the medical care they need.
I will fight for Medicare for All, because it will save about $1 trillion in healthcare costs per year, and it will save more than 100,000 lives every year.
03 The Epstein Class Pays Their Fair Share The Epstein Class needs to pay their fair share in taxes, which they are not currently doing .
If the government properly taxed the Epstein Class, we could use the extra funds to pay for social programs that would benefit everyone.
04 Hold the President Accountable Congress needs to take its power back and reinstitute the system of checks and balances it was meant to contribute to.
I will fight to help Congress to take back its war and taxation powers.
05 Stand Up to Flock, AI, and Data Centers Private companies with ALPRs are infringing on our rights, and tech companies are not acting responsibly.

We need representatives who understand the developing threats and are prepared to take action, such as creating a federal AI regulatory commission, working with other international actors, and fighting against the data centers that are taking our community resources.
06 Improve US World Standing The United States used to be a champion for human rights and a leader in global politics.
One way to regain it is by having a Congress that reins in the president’s power, so that the international community is not left to the whims of a new administration every 4-8 years.
07 Support Small Businesses Right now, big corporations are being prioritized, at the expense of smaller, locally-owned businesses.
That’s why I am committed to breaking up consolidation and monopolization in the marketplace, fully funding the small business administration, and lowering interest rates on small business loans.
08 Support Our Workers As someone who has helped unionize my workplace, I am familiar with the fear and hesitation workers feel when they try to demand better conditions.
That’s why I’m committed to fighting for the PRO Act and a livable minimum wage.

09 Abolish ICE ICE does not serve a unique purpose in the federal government, and its two main duties (enforcing immigration laws and investigating international crimes) could easily be absorbed by other federal agencies that do not routinely violate human rights.
This is not a call for open borders, but an acknowledgement that our current immigration enforcement system is threatening the safety of our communities, and we need to change.
10 Protect Human Rights I am committed to taking a proactive approach to protecting women’s rights, LGBTQIA+ rights, and the right to due process.
I will fight against discrimination in all forms, including in healthcare, in the workplace, in the military, and in the making of a family.
11 Protect Voting Rights The right to vote is fundamental to our democracy, but the Supreme Court has gutted the Voting Rights Act, removing the protections that guaranteed our right.
I am going to support legislation like the John R.
Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, and fight to make Election Day a federal holiday.
12 Protect North Georgia’s Forests The current administration is not protecting our beautiful forests.

I am committed to fighting to make sure the US National Forest Service is fully funded and staffed, and to protecting the Roadless Rule, so that our forests are protected from intensive logging and road building.
13 Invest in North Georgia’s Rural Water Infrastructure North Georgia’s rural water infrastructure is outdated and in need of investment.
The degradation of the current system has made people go many days without water .
As your representative, I will fight for the funding we need to remove lead water pipes and ensure access to clean drinking water.
14 Improve Rail Safety Conditions I will fight to improve federal rail safety standards, to protect communities near rail lines.
This is especially important with the inland port coming to Gainesville.
15 Invest in Clean Energy in Georgia We are seeing the increasing impact of climate change, but it is not too late.
There is so much potential for clean energy investment in Georgia.
We are 5th in the country for solar energy, and investments in this sector will lead to decreased energy prices and increased energy independence .
16 Protect Women’s Rights Every woman should have the right to her own body, and should not have to travel out of state to get the care that she needs.
I will support legislation like the Women’s Health Protection Act, so that every woman can get the care she needs when she needs it.
I will also support legislation like the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act, because maternal mortality rates are 2-3 times higher for Black women, and we need systemic change to address the issue.
17 Get Money Out of Politics The amount of money in politics right now is causing politicians to prioritize corporations over communities.
That’s why I will advocate for campaign spending caps and legislation that overturns the Citizens United decision.
18 Support Our Rural Hospitals Our rural hospitals need increased investment so that they can keep serving our communities.
I will fight for universal healthcare because it will disproportionately benefit our rural hospitals, and I will fight to fully fund the federal programs that already benefit rural hospitals.
Support Our Campaign Comparison Caitlyn Vs.
Clyde Comparison Compare Caitlyn Gegen and Andrew Clyde on the issues that matter most to Georgia’s 9th District.
Healthcare Andrew Clyde voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act, and opposes Medicaid expansion.
Caitlyn Gegen is committed to providing universal healthcare for every person in Georgia’s 9th District.
Human rights Andrew Clyde does not respect women’s rights or the rights of immigrant communities.
Caitlyn Gegen will defend and advance the rights of every person living in Georgia.
Cost of Living Andrew Clyde voted against the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, and does not support increasing our wages.
Caitlyn Gegen will fight to increase the national minimum wage to $20/hour, break up monopolies, and redistribute wealth in our country the right way.
Small Businesses Andrew Clyde supports President Trump’s tariffs and does not support investing in clean energy.
These policies will cost small businesses, both today and in the future.
Caitlyn Gegen will repeal Trump’s illegal tariffs and invest in clean energy, to bring down energy costs in the future.
Support Caitlyn Gegen Support Our Campaign Today!

This 10DLC & Toll-Free Privacy Policy is in addition to and supplements all other privacy and data security obligations of "Caleb Price for OH 30", including our operations, employment and website privacy policies (collectively, our “Privacy Policy”).
It describes our obligations and practices of how we collect and use customer consent and opt-ins for our texting and/or email services and programs.
This 10DLC & Toll-Free Privacy Policy applies to SMS and MMS texts from Scale to Win.
CATEGORIES OF INFORMATION COLLECTED: We will collect your name, phone number and indication of consent to receive text (SMS and MMS).
HOW WE USE THE INFORMATION COLLECTED: In addition to providing the services and complying with our Privacy Policy, we use the information to confirm consent to receive text (SMS and MMS).

TO WHOM DO WE SHARE THE INFORMATION COLLECTED: Text messaging originator opt-in data and consent will not be shared with any third parties, provided that the foregoing does not apply to sharing (1) with vendors, consultants and other service providers who need access to such information to carry out work on our behalf (and who will not use such information for their own purposes); (2) if we believe disclosure is required by any applicable law, rule, or regulation or to comply with law enforcement or legal process.
Mobile information will not be shared with third parties/affiliates for marketing/promotional purposes.
This Privacy Policy may be updated periodically and without prior notice to you to reflect changes in our information practices and applicable law.
We suggest that you periodically review the Privacy Policy for amendments.

added: Tax Code Compensation is income and it should be taxed.
For the vast majority of Americans, their entire compensation is taxed at the same rate with few ways to lower their taxable income.
For a much, much smaller minority, their income is taxed at higher rate, but there are multiple avenues to avoid taxes on their intentionally unrealized wealth.
One of the most intriguing options to avoid taxable income is through borrowing against assets such as stocks with interest rates much lower than the tax rate on capital gains.

And then on the same assets, when they pass away, the heirs receive a step up in basis which resets the value of the assets negating any capital gains that have been realized and would have been taxed.
It is time to close these avenues and redefine what is constituted as income.
If it is considered compensation, then it is income.
No more compensation packages that have less than 20% of total compensation as ordinary income with the remainder in unrealized wealth options.
I don't know of an American that would find this burdensome.
Employers offering compensation packages with less than 67% ordinary income and more than 33% other income will have an additional tax burden on their earnings.

Publicly traded companies, not for profits and private government contractors that overly bias their compensation to reward executives at the expense of their lowest earners will also realize an additional burden in their taxes.
This is about getting compensation taxed equitably and eliminating billions of dollars in earnings that is never recognized as income.
