description.after: Steven St John's proposed federal protections to prevent eligible Medicaid patients from losing coverage because of hospitalization, serious illness, incapacity, homelessness, failed notices, or administrative errors.

title.after: Proposed Medicaid Patient Protections | Steven St John for Congress

added: Steven St John for Congress Home Solutions Healthcare Contact Proposed Medicaid Patient Protections A practical federal framework to prevent eligible patients from losing healthcare because a medical or personal crisis made it impossible to meet an administrative deadline.

Proposed legislative framework The problem A person can remain legally eligible for Medicaid yet lose coverage because a notice went to an outdated address, paperwork was misunderstood, work hours were not documented, or a patient was hospitalized, intubated, incapacitated, homeless or too seriously ill to respond.
When coverage is interrupted for an administrative reason, the consequences may include delayed treatment, denied prescriptions, medical debt and uncompensated hospital care.
Patients and families should not face those consequences solely because a crisis prevented them from completing paperwork on time.
An eligible person should not lose healthcare solely because hospitalization, serious illness, incapacity, homelessness, a failed notice or an administrative error made timely compliance impossible.

Protections I intend to propose Automatic protection during hospitalization or incapacity Pause termination and reporting deadlines when reliable health-system or government information shows that a person is hospitalized, seriously ill or incapacitated.
A meaningful grace and correction period Provide additional time to submit missing information and correct an error before coverage is terminated.
Coverage while eligibility is being resolved Continue coverage during a timely review or appeal when available records indicate that the person may remain eligible.
Rapid and retroactive reinstatement Restore coverage promptly—and without a harmful gap—when a person proves continued eligibility or shows good cause for missing a requirement.
Reliable notice before termination Require more than one reasonable contact attempt, using available mail, telephone, text or electronic channels, before ending coverage for failure to respond.
Protection for homelessness and unstable housing Do not terminate an otherwise eligible person merely because that person lacks a permanent mailing address or never received a notice.
Help for families and authorized representatives Give legally authorized family members, caregivers and representatives a workable way to protect coverage when a patient cannot act personally.

Use existing information before demanding more paperwork Require agencies to check reliable government and healthcare data already available to them before asking a patient to prove the same facts again.
Clear explanations and accessible assistance Notices must explain, in plain language, what is required, the deadline, the consequences, available exemptions and how to obtain immediate help.

Accountability and public reporting Require reporting on administrative terminations, reversals, processing delays and coverage restored after appeal so Congress and the public can see where eligible people are falling through the cracks.
Why I am proposing these protections For nearly ten years as a Las Vegas hospital chaplain, I have stood with seriously ill patients and overwhelmed families at the bedside.
I have seen how difficult it can be for a family to understand insurance, locate documents and make urgent decisions while someone they love is intubated, incapacitated or near the end of life.
Public policy must account for what actually happens inside a hospital room.
They are protections against eligible people losing healthcare at the moment they are least able to defend themselves.
Status: This page describes a proposed legislative framework and is not the text of an introduced bill.

Specific statutory language would be developed through consultation with patients, families, healthcare professionals, disability and homelessness advocates, state Medicaid agencies and legislative counsel.
Steven St John Independent candidate for Congress, Nevada's First District 702-913-5264 chaplainforcongress@gmail.com Steven St John for Congress · Nevada's First Congressional District

added: Blog Posts AFFORDABILITY: Making Life More Affordable Charles Booker on gas, groceries and tariffs, and his plan to end the trade wars raising costs for Kentucky families.
SMALL BUSINESSES: Growing Kentucky Small Businesses How Charles Booker will fight tariffs, expand lending and stand up to big corporations for Kentucky small businesses.
GAS PRICES: Lowering the Price at the Pump Charles Booker on ending the war in Iran, suspending the federal gas tax and refilling the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
ENERGY: Lowering Energy Costs & Standing with Energy Workers Charles Booker on lowering Kentucky utility bills, making data centers pay their share and protecting coal miners.
INFRASTRUCTURE: Building Kentucky’s Infrastructure Charles Booker on roads, bridges, rural broadband and clean water, built by Kentucky workers at union wages.
DATA CENTERS: Stopping Data Centers in Kentucky Why Charles Booker supports a national moratorium on new AI data centers until we know the cost to Kentucky.
CORRUPTION & DEMOCRACY: Fighting Corruption & Draining the Swamp Charles Booker on term limits, a congressional stock trading ban and closing the lobbying revolving door.
HEALTHCARE: Making Healthcare Affordable for All Kentuckians Charles Booker on restoring ACA subsidies, building on Medicaid expansion and lowering prescription drug costs.
RURAL HOSPITALS: Supporting Kentucky’s Rural Hospitals Charles Booker on reversing Medicaid cuts and keeping at least 35 at-risk Kentucky rural hospitals open.
THE DISABLE: Supporting Vulnerable Kentuckians Charles Booker on expanding Medicaid services and opposing cuts that threaten care for disabled Kentuckians.
FARMERS & TARIFFS: Supporting Kentucky’s Farmers Charles Booker on tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs, the Farm Bill and a $12 billion farm aid package.
EDUCATION & TEACHERS: Supporting Public Education & Teachers Charles Booker on protecting special education, keeping public money in public schools and supporting rural teachers.
ELDER SUPPORT: Supporting Older Kentuckians & Retirees Charles Booker on protecting Social Security and his Medicare for the Future plan for dental, vision and hearing.
YOUTH SUPPORT: Supporting Young Kentuckians Charles Booker on Pell Grants, apprenticeships with organized labor and reducing student loan debt.

DONATE Greene Launches First TV and Radio Ads of Re-Election Campaign October 13, 2026 Categories: Campaign Update The spots highlight Greene’s Senate work to help everyday Michiganders save money, and his leadership as a Marine and Fire Captain SAGINAW, MI : Today, State Senate candidate Chedrick Greene launched the first television and radio ads of his re-election campaign for Michigan’s 35th Senate District.
The 30-second TV spot, titled “ Neighbors ,” gives a nod to Greene’s working-class experiences and efforts to improve the bottom lines of everyday Michiganders.
The ad will run on mid-Michigan broadcast stations in advance of the November 3rd rematch against the Republican opponent he resoundingly defeated in the MI-SD-35 special election earlier this year.

The radio spot, also 30 seconds, is on the air in the Saginaw media market, and features veteran Shane Peltier attesting to Greene’s decades of leadership while serving his country and community as a U.S.
Watch “Neighbors” “Neighbors” full transcript, tv ad: I’m Chedrick Greene, and the best part about Mid-Michigan is the people… [car drives by as passenger says] Hey, Chedrick! … like my neighbors.

As Mid-Michigan’s newest state Senator, I work for them —making insurance companies cover the cost of inhalers and insulin, securing funding for the Lafayette Bridge, … Heads up, Chedrick! [Chedrick throws football back to neighbor] Thank you, sir! … still pushing to lower taxes for working families. [neighbors walk by] Thanks Chedrick.
We’re working hard to create a better Mid-Michigan.
Full transcript, radio ad: [Peltier] I served with Sergeant Major Chedrick Greene in the Marine Corps.
He immediately took me under his wing, and I’ve seen it time and time again.
In Iraq, he led from the front. [Voiceover] Senator Chedrick Greene. [Peltier] One of his best traits in my eyes is the fact that he cares, he’s got compassion.
It’s shown just by his commitment to serving our country in the Marine Corps, his time serving as a firefighter.
Serving is the greatest honor of all. [Greene] I’m Chedrick Greene, and I’m asking for your vote for State Senate.
Greene launches both ads on the heels of consolidating highly sought-after support from Michigan’s business, farming, and labor communities.
The Small Business Association of Michigan and Detroit Regional Chamber PAC s endorsed the Marine veteran and retired fire captain as the first absentee votes were being cast.
Michigan Farm Bureau AgriPac endorsed Sen.
Greene this summer, the first time that organization has endorsed a Democrat for MI-SD-35.
And when the Michigan Fraternal Order of Police named him as their favored candidate last month, it marked Greene’s 25th labor organization endorsement .
Sworn in as Senator for Michigan’s 35th district on May 21, 2026, Greene is completing the final months of the term vacated by Kristen McDonald Rivet after she was elected to Congress.
MI-SD-35 has been trending red at the presidential level for over a decade.
After McDonald Rivet won the district by nearly seven points in 2022, Donald Trump only lost to Kamala Harris here by less than one percentage point in 2024.
Absentee voting in Michigan for the November 3, 2026 general election began September 24, 2026.
Michiganders also have nine days of early, in-person voting: Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1, 2026.

added: Donate to Chris Pappas for U.S.

Senate, former Senator John Sununu, claimed, “ It’s not privatization […] it wasn’t anything even remotely close to that. ” However, as was reported , detailed , catalogued , and panned at the time, Sununu led efforts to privatize Social Security , which would enrich Wall Street while jeopardizing the guaranteed retirement benefits for tens of thousands of New Hampshire workers.
Chris Pappas offers New Hampshire voters a stark contrast to Sununu’s dangerous and costly record.
He’s committed to shoring up and improving Social Security to ensure that current retirees and future generations can trust that their benefits will be there.
Get the facts below: FACT: John Sununu led efforts to privatize Social Security.
When he was last in the U.S.

Senate, Chris Pappas’s Trump-endorsed opponent John Sununu repeatedly introduced legislation to privatize Social Security that would have exposed Granite Staters’ retirement savings to stock market crashes and increased profits for Wall Street firms.
As a “ leading figure in the effort ” to privatize Social Security, Sununu co-sponsored legislation that had been projected to accelerate the timeline of Social Security’s insolvency.
Sununu supports Donald Trump’s Big Ugly Bill that has sped up Social Security’s insolvency timeline, threatening the benefits that hundreds of thousands of Granite Staters rely on.

Trump’s own Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, characterized a provision in the bill as a “ backdoor for privatizing Social Security .” Just this month, John Sununu touted his plan to privatize Social Security on a local TV station while refusing to answer whether he still supports privatizing Social Security.

WATCH: Sununu refuses to oppose privatizing Social Security on WMUR’s Closeup , 8.30.26 FACT: Sununu called for increasing the retirement age — a cut to guaranteed benefits — and his plan would have put guaranteed benefits at risk.
Sununu told the Concord Monitor, “ the retirement age must be gradually increased over time ,” a de facto cut to guaranteed benefits after a lifetime of hard work.
Analysts from the Economic Policy Institute , the Century Foundation , and the Center for American Progress (CAP) warned Sununu’s proposals would inevitably reduce benefits.

The Economic Policy Institute described required “clawbacks” in the Sununu-backed Bush privatization plan as “ substantial benefit cuts ,” and AARP, APWU, and other advocates noted that workers could lose up to 15 cents of every dollar to fees charged by private money managers.
CAP found that a retiree with a private account under Sununu’s plan who left the workforce during the 2008 financial crash “would have lost approximately $26,000” after 35 years of contributions .
FACT: Chris Pappas will never vote to cut benefits or move the goalposts for our seniors.
Pappas led House and Senate Democrats in a letter demanding the Republican majority in Washington commit to protecting social security.
Pappas cosponsored the bipartisan Social Security Fairness Act , which restored full retirement benefits for teachers, firefighters, police officers, and other public servants.
Pappas fought against the Trump Administration’s efforts to gut the Social Security Administration, fire staff, and close field offices, including an office in Littleton, New Hampshire.
Pappas opposed Trump’s Big Ugly Bill, which included a provision Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent praised as being a “ backdoor for privatizing Social Security .” Pappas’s campaign for U.S.
Senate has been endorsed by the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare PAC, a leading national organization dedicated to protecting Social Security and Medicare.

Chris Pappas’s record stands in stark contrast to Trump-endorsed John Sununu, who led efforts to privatize Social Security and supports President Trump’s Big Ugly Bill that has sped up Social Security’s insolvency timeline, threatening the benefits that hundreds of thousands of Granite Staters rely on.
In fact, just a few weeks ago, John Sununu touted his plan to privatize Social Security, and just yesterday he refused to say what he would do to protect the program.
Chris Pappas on Protecting Social Security: “We have to figure out how we prevent drastic cuts from going into effect that would devastate our population in New Hampshire.
This not only is a lifeline for seniors, for disabled individuals, but it also is good for New Hampshire’s economy.
Cuts to Social Security are unacceptable to me.
I will oppose any cuts in benefits because people have paid into this system.

They’ve paid in throughout their working years and it’s a benefit that needs to be there for them when they retire . ” Chris Pappas on the Choice in This Race: “Now this is an important choice in the race.
Yesterday I had a debate with John Sununu, and he said he was unwilling to talk about his ideas for Social Security because he didn’t want to be attacked in the campaign.
He didn’t want to put something on the table that people might oppose.
Well, I think we’ve got to be transparent about what we support and what we don’t support.

I’m the only candidate who’s clearly saying I don’t support cutting Social Security benefits, that it’s not a solution to shore up the program.” Chris Pappas on Why He’s Running for Senate: “I’m running for the United States Senate because this is a gut check moment for American democracy, and we need leadership that is going to stand up for what’s right against this broken presidency and focus on how we can lower costs and get this economy working for everyone . ” ### Join Team Pappas Sign up here to learn more about Chris, our campaign, and how you can get involved.

Rush a donation to keep NH blue and help Democrats win back the Senate. $# $# $# $# $# Other amount Close Facebook X Bsky Instagram TikTok Threads Substack YouTube Chris Pappas for Senate Menu Home Meet Chris Priorities Anti-Corruption Agenda Tax Cuts and Lower Costs Blueprint Endorsements News Take Action Store Donate Press Release At Salem Debate, Chris Pappas Shows He’s the Only Candidate Who Will Stand Up to Donald Trump October 14, 2026 MANCHESTER, N.H. — At this afternoon’s Southern New Hampshire Chamber of Commerce’s Candidate Night Debate, Chris Pappas again highlighted for Granite Staters that he is the only candidate in the race who will stand up to Donald Trump and lower costs.

Pappas showcased his vision for a freer, fairer New Hampshire, while John Sununu not only refused to say he would vote to end the Iran War, but he took his rubber stamping of Trump to a new level by defending Pete Hegseth against pushes for accountability.

Sununu’s move was of little surprise to those who know his record: John Sununu has already said that he’s running for Senate because this race is “ important to President Trump’s agenda ” and that he supports and has downplayed the worst parts of that agenda — including Trump’s war with Iran , Trump’s tariff taxes , and Trump’s cuts to health care.

“Chris Pappas is running to lower costs and stand up to Donald Trump, and as he again made clear on the stage today, John Sununu can’t run from his own words calling this race ‘important to President Trump’s agenda,’” said Jen Hughes, Spokesperson for Chris Pappas for Senate .

“Granite Staters have rejected John Sununu before and they will again, because as today’s debate made clear, Chris Pappas will fight corporate special interests while John Sununu will fight for them.” Key highlights from this afternoon’s debate are below: Chris Pappas Made a Powerful Case to Voters on Why He’s Running: PAPPAS : “This is a critical midterm election where we have to reestablish checks and balances in Washington D.C. and fight every day to make progress for people all across the state of New Hampshire that are counting on us… I fought to bring solutions to New Hampshire, to invest in our infrastructure, in our water and wastewater, in our broadband and our roads and bridges.

I’ve pushed for legislation to make things better for New Hampshire veterans, to expand access to care and benefits for New Hampshire’s veteran community, and to rebuild a new facility at the Manchester VA.
I fought for funding for addiction and mental health.

I’ve stood up for big fights, including defending a woman’s right to choose, fighting to keep our air and our water clean, and making sure that we’re getting big money out of politics and confronting the culture of corruption that exists in Washington.” Chris Pappas Will Lower Housing Costs PAPPAS : “Let’s take on these predatory practices.
Let’s take on private equity and big companies that are gobbling up single-family homes and mobile home parks, and pricing people out of their own communities.
Second, let’s make it easier to build.
Let’s make it easier to get a project from the planning stage to the construction phase, and then to allow people to occupy it.
Let’s make sure we’re incentivizing young people to be able to put a down payment on their first home.
I support legislation that would give a tax credit to first-time homebuyers to be able to achieve the dream of home ownership, which for young people now, on average, is in their 40s.
So we got to be doing a lot better with respect to housing.” Chris Pappas Showed Voters He’s the Only Independent Voice For New Hampshire PAPPAS : “Senator Sununu went to Washington #ago.
I was still in high school at the time, bussing tables at my family restaurant.
He served in Congress, a term in the Senate, and he might still be our U.S. senator today if he actually showed the independence he was just talking about.
He was down the line for George W.
He supported the invasion of Iraq.
He supported the privatization of Social Security, he put anti-choice judges on the bench that overturned Roe v.
He voted for a massive $700 billion bailout of Wall Street, while Main Street got screwed during the housing crisis.
The fact is, for the last 18 years, he’s been on corporate boards.
He’s worked for one of the biggest lobbying firms in Washington D.C. that has clients like Big Pharma and the insurance industry, earning up to and having a net worth of up to $35 million.
The fact is, we need someone who isn’t just seeking to ride the revolving door.
We need someone who’s going to put the people of New Hampshire first, and to stand up to the recklessness of Donald Trump’s presidency.

This is about who will be independent for New Hampshire.” Chris Pappas Will Never Cut Social Security Benefits, Sununu Too Scared of Past Record PAPPAS : “Senator Sununu talked about the need for transparency, but the fact is he hasn’t been transparent.
Just yesterday in a forum, he said he was unwilling to discuss the details of reforms to Social Security because he was afraid of being attacked in a political campaign.
This is a moment to put ideas on the table.

And one thing that I will not support is a cut to benefits for New Hampshire seniors and for workers that are looking forward to retirement.” Even When Pushed Directly, Sununu Refuses to Take Iran War Powers Resolution Position PAPPAS : “Senator Sununu has not been willing to join the effort [to end the war].

He’s been critical of late, now that we’re within weeks of the election, of the war, but he hasn’t been willing to say that he would support a war powers resolution to stop Donald Trump’s war effort and to bring our troops home.” Sununu, who has previously called the war “ important and critical ,” rambled in response but at no point said that he would support a War Powers Resolution to end this war.

John Sununu Defends Pete Hegseth SUNUNU : “I’ve certainly had disagreements with Secretary Hegseth, but at the same time, the question’s about impeachment, and that’s something that’s extremely serious.
You shouldn’t be impeached for a bad decision.” ### Join Team Pappas Sign up here to learn more about Chris, our campaign, and how you can get involved.

description.after: PRINCIPLES before COLORS (Official political campaign T-shirt of Philippe Cicchini for Michigan State Senate District 9) Because values matter more than labels. This shirt is a clear statement about how decisions should be made — guided by principles, not party colors. The design underscores a commitment to fairness, integrity, and judgment that isn’t dictated by red or blue, but by what’s right and what works. With restrained typography and a subtle use of color for emphasis, the message is direct without being divisive. Printed on a soft, lightweight unisex tee made from Airlume combed and ring-spun cotton, it’s built for long campaign days and everyday wear alike. Reinforced seams, a retail crew fit, and a durable, high-clarity print ensure the message remains sharp and readable over time. Wear it as a reminder that leadership starts with values — and that principles should always come before politics. Attorney General Eric Holder Endorses Cinde Warmington for Governor PRESS RELEASE With Cloud of Corruption over Court, Warmington Demands Justices Step Aside Pending Investigation PRESS RELEASE ICYMI: Cinde Warmington Visits Exeter on Cut the Costs Tour PRESS RELEASE WATCH: Warmington Launches New Ad Addressing Ayotte’s Misleading Attacks and Failed Record PRESS RELEASE ICYMI: Cinde Warmington Visits Berlin on Cut the Costs Tour PRESS RELEASE Ayotte Lies Fill New Ad, Warmington Campaign Calls On Media Outlets To Stop Ad, Files Complaint Oct 14 2026 PRESS RELEASE Ayotte Lies Fill New Ad, Warmington Campaign Calls On Media Outlets To Stop Ad, Files Complaint MANCHESTER, NH — Today, the Warmington campaign is calling on media outlets to pull off their channels an Ayotte campaign ad blatantly lying about Cinde Warmington’s position on a sales or income tax and energy.
The campaign also has filed a complaint with the New Hampshire Attorney General’s office.
The facts and a long public record, ignored by Kelly Ayotte, show Warmington is a steadfast opponent to a sales or income tax, and has never called for any ban on natural gas or heating oil.
In addition, the ad fails to comply with state disclaimer requirements.

“Now Kelly Ayotte is resorting to lies in a last-ditch ad because she knows she’s in trouble, running on a failed record of skyrocketing costs, corruption, and chaos,” said Andrea Cervone, Campaign Manager.
“Despite the Ayotte campaign pouring millions of dollars into stale, cringeworthy ads, Cinde continues to close the gap in this race.

If Costly Kelly wants to talk about energy, she should start by explaining to Granite Staters why her Public Utilities Commission just rubber-stamped rate hikes and why she rolled out the red carpet for data centers that threaten to send electric rates even higher.” FACT: Cinde Warmington Will Veto an Income or Sales Tax Warmington has repeatedly pledged to veto an income and sales tax.

The citation wrongly referenced in this ad says that Warmington “insists she does not support an income tax. ‘I do not believe a broad-based sales or income tax is the right way to go in our state.’ " FACT: Cinde Warmington Has Never Supported a Ban on Natural Gas and Heating Oil Warmington is fighting to lower utility costs for Granite Staters, who are now paying 17% more for electricity as a result of Kelly Ayotte’s failed energy policies.
While Ayotte signed a law that rolled out the red carpet for data centers that threaten to send electric rates even higher, Warmington is calling for an immediate data center moratorium.
Warmington supports a temporary suspension of the state gas tax to put money back in the pockets of Granite Staters who can’t afford to fill up their tanks.
Ayotte opposes suspending the state gas tax and has been silent on Donald Trump’s reckless war of choice.
The full complaint, a copy of which was sent to WMUR, can be found here.

added: Skip to main content About Issues Supporters News Store Get Involved Donate Donate Press Release 100 Kansas Republicans Are Now Backing Cindy Holscher for Governor For Immediate Release · October 14, 2026 TOPEKA, KS – Today, the Cindy Holscher for Governor campaign announced that 80 additional current and former Republicans from across Kansas have endorsed Senator Cindy Holscher and joined “Republicans for Cindy,” bringing the coalition to 100 members.
They joined the 20 current and former Republican elected officials who launched the coalition, many of whom served alongside both Holscher and Masterson in the legislature.
Throughout her time in Topeka, Holscher has brought Republicans and Democrats together around practical and pragmatic solutions.
That record began in her first term in the Kansas House, when she co-founded a bipartisan coalition that ended the Brownback tax experiment and restored stability to the state.
“I served in the Legislature alongside both Ty Masterson and Cindy Holscher, so I know their records better than most,” said former Republican State Representative Linda Gallagher.
“Cindy is a pragmatic leader who has always been willing to work with anyone, Republican or Democrat, to get things done for Kansas families.

That’s exactly the kind of governor our state needs right now, and as a lifelong Republican, I’m proud to support Cindy Holscher for governor.” “I’m proud to have the support of so many Republicans who know that what matters to Kansans isn’t party labels but whether their governor will work for them.
They know both my record and Ty Masterson’s, and they chose me.
This campaign is for everybody, and as governor I’ll work for every Kansan,” said Senator Cindy Holscher.

added: Skip to main content About Issues Supporters News Store Get Involved Donate Donate Press Release Cindy Holscher Launches New Television Ad Vowing to Clean Up Ty Masterson’s Messes For Immediate Release · October 14, 2026 TOPEKA, KS — Democratic nominee for governor Cindy Holscher launched a new ad today, “Muck,” highlighting the toughness she learned cleaning up after farm animals and her readiness to clean up the even messier, costlier plans from Ty Masterson.
The ad airs statewide on broadcast, streaming, and digital platforms starting today.
WATCH “Muck” contrasts Holscher’s record with Ty Masterson, one of the chief architects and authors of the Brownback tax experiment.
Holscher helped build the bipartisan coalition that cleaned up the Brownback and Masterson mess and restored stability to Kansas.
Now, Masterson wants to drag the state back into that pile of manure.

Since the end of the Brownback era, Masterson’s wealthy backers have benefitted from enormous tax breaks while working families face rising property taxes, higher utility bills and the costs of unchecked data center development.

“Cindy Holscher is well-versed in cleaning up messes from her time on the farm, and Ty Masterson’s may be nastier than those, but Cindy’s ready to keep shoveling and clean up after him too,” said campaign spokesperson Hans Torgerson .
“Masterson is sinking because Kansans can smell the shams and scams from a mile away.
Families remember his contributions to the disastrous Brownback plan that gave every break possible to the highest bidder while ordinary Kansans paid the price.
Cindy grew up on a farm, and she’s cleaned up messes like this before.

She beat the Brownback agenda before, and in three weeks she’s going to beat it again.” As governor, Holscher will stay focused on lowering costs, delivering meaningful property-tax relief, stopping giveaways to greedy corporations, and pausing data centers.
Transcript of “Muck”: [CINDY HOLSCHER]: I’m Cindy Holscher, and I grew up on a farm cleaning up messes from these guys.
Then I ran for office to clean up the mess from these guys.
Now, I’m running for governor to clean up the corruption driving up your costs.
From the Brownback plan, to property taxes, to data centers, Ty Masterson’s rich backers get huge tax cuts.
Ty gets a million-dollar no-show job, and we pay the price.
# # # State Senator Cindy Holscher understands the struggles everyday Kansans face.
Holscher was raised on a farm by parents who worked hard for a living in construction and public schools.
She worked her way through college and is one of the first in her family with a college degree.
She is a mom who sent her three kids to public schools.
Holscher will make sure government serves everyday Kansans, not the wealthy and powerful.
She will fight to fully fund our public schools, lower property taxes, and make things more affordable in Kansas.
To learn more about the campaign, visit cindyforkansas.com .

title.before: New Report: Ty Masterson Ran His Business Into Bankruptcy and Left Kansans Unpaid | Cindy Holscher for Governor

removed: Skip to main content About Issues Supporters News Store Get Involved Donate Donate Press Release New Report: Ty Masterson Ran His Business Into Bankruptcy and Left Kansans Unpaid For Immediate Release · September 10, 2026 TOPEKA, KS – Ty Masterson wants Kansans to trust him with the state’s finances, but new reporting out today from American Journal News shows how the last operation under his leadership turned out.
MasterBuilt Homes, the Andover homebuilder Masterson co-founded and led as CEO, collapsed into Chapter 7 bankruptcy carrying $1.13 million in debts it could not pay.

Masterson’s response was to blame an employee instead of taking accountability, yet Statehouse Republicans responded by handing him the keys to the state budget as chair of the Senate Ways and Means Committee, where he helped ram through the Brownback tax experiment that gutted Kansas schools and drove the state’s finances into the ditch – similarly to his failed business.
Ty Masterson bankrupted his business, then bankrupted the state, and everyday Kansans were left holding the bag both times.
More from the report: Masterson was the CEO of MasterBuilt Homes, a residential construction company based in Andover, KS.
The company went under in 2006 and officially filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy at the end of 2010.
Chapter 7… MasterBuilt reported owning roughly $300,000 in assets while owing $1.13 million in debt.
Some of the outstanding debts included $209,000 to Corner Bank, $53,890 to Emprise Bank, and $85,000 to Fisher Lumber of Garden Plain.
The company also reported more than $160,000 in credit card debt Masterson was elected to the Kansas Senate in 2009.
Despite his business record, Republicans in the legislature chose Masterson to lead the Senate Ways and Means Committee in 2012.
The committee is responsible for reviewing state agency budgets and proposed expenditures.

Masterson blamed the bankruptcy on an employee and claimed he had little oversight of the company in this period because he was “getting engaged and excited about politics.” # # # Cindy Holscher grew up on a farm with common sense, Midwest values, and a love of her country.
Cindy and her husband Greg have lived in Kansas for over 25 years, and their three kids graduated from public schools.
She first ran for office to end the disastrous Brownback experiment and restore school funding.
As a legislator, Cindy co-founded the Women’s Bipartisan Caucus, and she focused on lowering costs for working-class and middle-class Kansans.
Now, she’s running for governor because Kansas deserves a leader who has a proven track record of fighting for all Kansans.
To learn more about the campaign, visit cindyforkansas.com .

removed: Skip to main content About Issues Supporters News Store Get Involved Donate Donate Press Release United Food and Commercial Workers District Union Local Two Endorses Cindy Holscher for Governor For Immediate Release · September 10, 2026 TOPEKA, KS — Democratic nominee for Governor Cindy Holscher today announced the endorsement of United Food and Commercial Workers District Union Local 2 (UFCW Local 2), adding the support of thousands of Kansas workers to her growing coalition.
UFCW Local 2 represents over 15,000 workers across Kansas, Oklahoma and Missouri.
Its members include the workers who keep Kansas' meatpacking and food-processing plants running, as well as retail and food-safety sanitation workers.
The endorsement recognizes Holscher's record in the Kansas Legislature standing with organized labor and fighting for working families — including her 100% score on the AFL-CIO Legislative Scorecard.

Throughout her time in public office, Holscher has stood against efforts that undermine workers and has fought for policies that put the needs of Kansas families ahead of wealthy corporations and powerful special interests.
“UFCW Local 2 is proud to stand with Cindy Holscher in this race because she has always had our backs,” said UFCW Local 2 President Martin Rosas .

“Our members work some of the toughest and most essential jobs in our state, and they deserve a governor who respects their work and will stand up for their right to good wages, safe workplaces and a dignified retirement.
We are confident that Cindy will be that governor.” Holscher has made supporting Kansas workers a cornerstone of her public service.
Her father was a union member, and she has frequently credited the stability his union job provided with helping her family get by and for helping put her through college.

“This endorsement is important to me because UFCW Local 2 members represent the very best of Kansas — people who work hard, take care of their families and keep our communities and our economy moving,” said Senator Cindy Holscher.
“I grew up in a union household, so I know firsthand what a good union job can mean for a family.

As governor, I will keep fighting for better wages, safer workplaces and an economy where the people who do the work actually have a chance to get ahead.” Holscher is committed to lowering costs and making Kansas a more affordable place to raise a family.

She has pledged to fight back against corporate giveaways, lower property taxes for everyday Kansans, protect public education, and ensure state government works for working people rather than the wealthy and well-connected.
Holscher has also been endorsed by AFGE, AFT-Kansas, and the Kansas AFL-CIO.
State leaders have also lined up in support of Holscher, including Governor Laura Kelly and former Governor John Carlin.
### Cindy Holscher grew up on a farm with common sense, Midwest values, and a love of her country.
Cindy and her husband Greg have lived in Kansas for over 25 years, and their three kids graduated from public schools.
She first ran for office to end the disastrous Brownback experiment and restore school funding.
As a legislator, Cindy co-founded the Women’s Bipartisan Caucus, and she focused on lowering costs for working-class and middle-class Kansans.
Now, she’s running for governor because Kansas deserves a leader who has a proven track record of fighting for all Kansans.
To learn more about the campaign, visit cindyforkansas.com .

added: The problem 7 of 8 Springs Coast springs exceed safe nitrate levels — SWFWMD.
Septic and fertilizer runoff contributes an estimated 5 million pounds of nitrogen to springs annually — DEP.
Weeki Wachee is struggling with algae, water withdrawals, and nutrient runoff, threatening the $800M+ Nature Coast economy — Visit Florida.
The Water Management District board overseeing our springs isn't elected by the people who depend on this water.
All nine members are appointed by the Governor, rather than elected by Nature Coast residents — SWFWMD / Florida Statute 373.
Development continues to put pressure on springs and waterways.

Questions remain about whether post-permit monitoring and enforcement adequately protect water quality, particularly as septic systems are added near Weeki Wachee and Homosassa — Tampa Bay Times, October 2025.
Hyperscale data centers are expanding into Florida, potentially placing additional pressure on water resources, electricity supplies, and infrastructure.
Florida Statute 145.031 ties county commissioner compensation partly to county population.
As population increases, the statutory salary formula can increase commissioner pay.

Although commissioners are not paid for approving individual developments, this creates the appearance of a financial incentive for population growth, even when residents are concerned about overdevelopment and environmental damage.
Tony's solution Provide incentives for native ground covers and Florida-friendly landscaping to reduce water consumption and nitrogen runoff.
Establish a moratorium on new development that threatens our springs and waterways, using legally enforceable environmental criteria.
Require full transparency and accountability for environmental spending — no backroom deals, no polluter carve-outs.
Make Water Management District board members elected, not appointed , giving residents a direct voice in who oversees their water resources.
Oppose further hyperscale data center development in Florida.
Reform Florida Statute 145.031 to eliminate population growth as a factor in determining county commissioner salaries.
Establish a fair and transparent compensation structure that is not tied to county population increases.
Require greater transparency in development approvals, including public disclosure of projected impacts on water resources, infrastructure, and the environment.
Amy Grant Big Yellow Taxi Donate Sound like your priorities too?

title.before: Education | Clint Collamore

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE Education is Key Education is a complex issue, but vitally important to all of us, even those who no longer have children or grandchildren who are school-age.
Young people are our future.
They are our future doctors, nurses, caretakers, fisherman, farmers, scientists, caretakers, and stewards of this land. ​ I would like to see a renewed belief in the importance of education.
No matter what career path one chooses, fundamental skills in math, science, and language arts are critical.

To run your own business, as many fisherman do, those core skills are essential to success and to the creative thinking that is needed to address the many challenges all of us face in work and our daily lives.
Schools should integrate more in the community.
While Lincoln Academy has a public service requirement for students, Medomak Valley High School does not.
Many of our local groups need volunteers to meet needs, and younger generations need to see the value of this work first hand.

Older students should go to a couple of town Select Board meetings in their community and see how local government works. ​ Perhaps this could be a state-wide initiative to support greater youth involvement as stewards of our beautiful state and how each and every one of us can make differences big and small.
We each play a role in the future success of this state.
For example, people need to understand the impacts of small actions on an our environment.

Citizens need to be reminded that voting is something everyone should do as being part of a community, a state, and a nation. ​ I went to the small elementary school in Bremen, followed by Medomak Valley High School and Region 8 Technical School.
After high school graduation, I followed up with an Associates in business and Bachelor of Science in Public Administration from the University of Maine.
I credit my education not with teaching me everything I need to know in life, but rather laying the foundation for lifelong learning.
I know how to get information, gathering from all sides, and I enjoy continuing to learn and grow as a person.
Education is another space where Federal and State regulations often challenge small local schools and school districts.
This is not to say that all of these laws are bad, but they are often unfunded mandates that can be very demanding on a local school district.

Every single child deserves a free and appropriate education, but some children have enhanced needs and the State and Federal governments should share the burden more fully so that meeting these mandates as the local level doesn't mean losing teachers or educational opportunities for all students. ​ How a Maine State Legislator Can Support Schools ​ A Maine legislator can strengthen public schools by improving funding, supporting student mental health, reducing administrative burdens, investing in workforce development, and ensuring schools have the resources to provide a safe, high‑quality education.
Maine’s education system faces challenges ranging from staffing shortages to rising special‑education costs, and legislators play a central role in addressing them.
Ways Legislators Can Support Maine Schools ​ 1.
Strengthen School Funding & Reduce Local Burdens ​ Maine’s schools rely heavily on local property taxes.
Legislators can help by: Ensuring the state meets or exceeds its 55% school funding obligation.
Increasing support for special education, which is one of the fastest‑growing costs for districts.
Expanding funding for school facilities, including HVAC upgrades, safety improvements, and energy efficiency.
Supporting predictable, stable funding so districts can plan long‑term.
Support Student Mental Health & Well‑Being ​ Maine schools are seeing increased student mental health needs.

A recent legislative proposal ( LD 1123 ) highlighted how many districts struggle to access federal Medicaid funds for school‑based services, with only 45% of districts participating in eligible reimbursements. ​ A legislator can: ​ Fund school‑based mental health professionals, including counselors and social workers.
Improve MaineCare reimbursement support, helping districts access federal funds for services students already receive.
Support partnerships with community mental health providers.
Reduce Administrative Burdens on Schools ​ Schools often struggle with complex state and federal requirements. ​ A legislator can: ​ Streamline reporting requirements.
Fund positions (like the proposed MaineCare coordinators) that help districts navigate complex systems.
Ensure new mandates come with funding (“no unfunded mandates”).

Support Safe, Healthy Learning Environments ​ Legislators can help schools create environments where students can focus and thrive. ​ Examples include: ​ Funding school safety upgrades and emergency preparedness.
Supporting nutrition programs and access to healthy meals.
Supporting programs such as Farm and Sea to School , which benefits students, fisherman, and farmers.
Invest in Teachers & School Staff Maine faces teacher shortages, especially in rural areas. ​ A legislator can: ​ Support competitive salaries and benefits.
Fund professional development and mentorship programs.
Support pathways for ed techs and paraprofessionals to become certified teachers.

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE Frequent Asked Questions This is to address the public's concerns about Clean Elections donations in the past.
General What happened with Clean Elections in 2022/23?
I made a mistake where I accepted $# cash donations from people I know while I was at events such as the Friendship Lobster Boat Races, a yard sale, and didn’t have the forms with me.
The people asked me to just fill it out for them.
I did, with no attempt to disguise my handwriting.
Why were there so many charges?
There were two charges per person who made a $5 donation as there is a list of donations they are supposed to put their name on, as well as an individual slip of paper saying they made the donation.
They dropped the charges on the forged people,because they all did.
Therefore,as a result, it was considered by all as no ill-intent on my part.
What charges did you plead guilty to?
I pled guilty to 12 misdemeanors for filling out the donation slips for real people, who made real donations.
Why did you choose to plead guilty if there was no ill intent?
The court process takes a long time, and is very costly both financially and emotionally.
I wanted it done.
I actually saw a therapist.
I was very embarrassed, and it was hard on my family.
What was your punishment?
From the court, I was given 100 hours of community service.
That was no problem for me as I do that anyway.
I did that at Medomak Exchange and I cleaned veteran’s headstones at Wavus Camps in Jefferson for a weekend.
I also voluntarily paid back all the clean elections money I received, as well as voluntarily paying back money I received for the brief time I was in the legislature.
Why did you resign?
It would take too long to clear my name and I didn’t want it to negatively impact my constituents.
The party made it clear I would have no committees and they didn’t want to work with me.
The Speaker of the House requested that I do.
Why do you think people should trust you now?
It was a mistake and I have learned from it.
The donations were all legitimate and from real people, the mistake was that I filled out the paperwork for the people.
When the State investigated, the 12 people who were contacted all said they had given me the $5, but not filled out the forms.
I also did what I could to make things right.
Many people voted for me knowing the state was investigating because they knew the donations were genuine.
Why are you running again?
Many in the community have asked me to run.
I had no intent to, but as time has gone on, I figured it is now or never.
I want to do it right this time.
People are having issues with rent/housing, heat, food, bills, taxes, just getting by, and the list goes on.
We need people working together to resolve the issues that impact all of us.
There is way too much fighting in Washington, DC, and in Augusta.
This is Maine.
Mainers work together and get things done.
What were the charges against you?
The investigators thought I made up names of individuals who contributed to my campaign.
It was just the opposite.
The contributors all donated and that’s what they found out.
Then I was charged with forging some names even though those contributors requested that I do so.

title.before: Farms | Clint Collamore

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE Family Farms Food is essential to human life, and we all need access to safe, healthy farm products.
Keeping it close to home ensures we retain access.

How a Maine Legislator Can Support Family Farms ​ A legislator has several powerful levers—policy, funding, and regulation—to strengthen family farms, especially around PFAS contamination, drought resiliency, and food sovereignty. ​ 1.
Addressing PFAS Contamination PFAS (“forever chemicals”) have become one of the most significant threats to Maine agriculture.
Contamination has occurred through sludge spreading, groundwater, and other environmental pathways.
Maine has taken national leadership in responding, but the work is ongoing.
Maine’s response includes banning land application of sludge, creating a PFAS Fund , and conducting statewide testing of farms, soils, and water.
Farmers have been directly affected, with some losing herds, crops, or land use due to contamination.
Maine’s agricultural agencies continue to test and support impacted farms.
What a legislator can do: Expand and sustain the PFAS Relief Fund to compensate affected farmers, support income replacement, and fund long‑term monitoring.
Increase funding for soil and water testing, remediation research, and safe disposal of contaminated materials.
Support mental health and financial counseling for affected farm families.
Ensure transparent communication between state agencies and farmers as testing continues.
Strengthening Drought Resiliency ​ Maine has experienced more frequent and severe droughts in recent years, affecting hay yields, livestock feed, irrigation needs, and crop reliability.
Legislative actions that help: Invest in water infrastructure, including grants or low‑interest loans for on‑farm irrigation, ponds, and water‑capture systems.
Support soil‑health initiatives (cover crops, composting, rotational grazing) that improve water retention.
Fund climate‑resilient agriculture programs, including technical assistance through UMaine Extension .
Expand crop insurance access and emergency relief programs for small farms.
Advancing Food Sovereignty Maine is a national leader in food sovereignty , with many towns passing ordinances that give communities more control over local food systems.
Food sovereignty supports family farms by: Strengthening local markets.
Reducing regulatory burdens for small‑scale producers.
Encouraging direct sales and community‑based food systems.
What a legislator can do: Protect and expand Maine’s food sovereignty laws, ensuring small producers can sell directly to consumers without unnecessary barriers.
Support local food infrastructure, such as community kitchens, farmers markets, and small‑scale processing facilities.
Increase institutional purchasing of Maine‑grown food for schools, hospitals, and state facilities.
Promote land access programs for new and beginning farmers.

title.before: Business | Clint Collamore

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE Supporting Local Business Small Businesses are the backbone of the Maine economy.
They make up over 99% of Maine businesses and employ over half of the state’s workforce.
Legislators play a crucial role in strengthening this sector by improving access to capital, reducing regulatory burdens, and supporting workforce and infrastructure development.
While prices are climbing, our small businesses are struggling to make ends meet.
Small businesses are owned by our neighbors and we keep working to help our own economy to grow and be resilient.
Doing this will help younger folks living here and raising their families to be able to find some comfort in living.
Why Small Business is Essential in Maine They make up 99.2% of all Maine businesses.
They employ 290,518 people, representing 54.5% of all Maine employees.
They drive job creation: small businesses contributed 98.5% of net new jobs between 2023–2024.
They support rural communities, local supply chains, and Maine’s identity — especially in tourism, fishing, agriculture, trades, and professional services.
They help stabilize the economy by circulating money locally and fostering entrepreneurship.
Source: U.S.
Small Business Administration Office of Advocacy Why Small Business Matters Even More in Maine Maine’s economy is heavily rural and community-based.
Small businesses keep towns vibrant, provide essential services, and create opportunities where large employers may be scarce.
They also help buffer the state against economic shocks by diversifying local industries.

Regulations come from the federal government and by the state.
Every time you turn around they are trying to reduce or close another fishery.
Sometimes these regulations are put forward with no consideration for how they impact heritage industries here in Maine such as lobstering and clamming.

They need to be included in all decision-making processes that effect their industry.
We need to stop and reevaluate what is working and what isn't. ​ Until the people that are involved in the industry are at the table, no doubt it will be a failure waiting to happen.

As a State Representative, I would be both a legislator and a fisherman fighting for these iconic industries. ​ I was involved in efforts to clean up the Medomak River.

This is has not been just a recovery effort, now it is about sustainability. ​ Why Maine's Fisheries Matter Maine’s commercial fisheries—lobster, scallops, groundfish, elvers, aquaculture, and more—are essential because they: Support coastal economies from Kittery to Eastport.
Provide thousands of jobs in harvesting, processing, boat-building, gear supply, and marine trades.
Sustain working waterfronts, which are increasingly threatened by development and climate impacts.
Anchor Maine’s identity, tourism, and food culture.
Contribute significantly to Maine’s export economy, especially lobster.

Protect Working Waterfronts ​ Working waterfront access is one of the biggest long‑term threats to Maine’s fisheries. ​ A legislator can: ​ Expand the Working Waterfront Access Protection Program to help fishing families and co‑ops secure permanent access.
Support tax incentives or zoning protections for commercial fishing infrastructure.
Fund climate‑resilient upgrades to piers, wharves, and harbors.
Ensure Maine has strong representation in regional fisheries management councils.
Reduce Regulatory Burdens & Improve Communication ​ Fishermen often face complex, rapidly changing regulations.

Support programs that help small fishing operations navigate licensing, reporting, and compliance.
Ensure that new regulations consider the realities of small‑boat, owner‑operator fleets ​ 3.

Invest in Workforce & Maritime Trades ​ The fishing industry depends on skilled workers—boat-builders, welders, marine engineers, and deckhands. ​ A legislator can: ​ Expand vocational training in marine trades.
Support apprenticeship programs for young fishermen.
Fund safety training, including cold‑water survival and navigation.

title.before: Clint Collamore: Bridging Political Gaps in Maine

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE All Posts Clint Collamore: Bridging Political Gaps in Maine Clinton Collamore Mar 31 4 min read Updated: Apr 2 In a time when political divisions seem to widen daily, Clint Collamore stands out as a beacon of hope in Maine.
His commitment to bridging political gaps and fostering dialogue among diverse groups has made a significant impact on the community.
This blog post explores Collamore's journey, his strategies for uniting people, and the lessons we can learn from his approach.

Understanding the Political Landscape in Maine Maine's political landscape is unique, characterized by a mix of rural and urban populations, progressive and conservative ideologies, and a strong sense of community.
This diversity can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts, but it also presents an opportunity for collaboration and growth.
The Challenge of Division Political polarization is not just a national issue; it affects local communities as well.
In Maine, residents often find themselves at odds over key issues such as healthcare, education, and environmental policies.
This division can create an atmosphere of distrust and animosity, making it difficult for individuals to engage in constructive dialogue.
The Role of Community Leaders Community leaders like Clint Collamore play a crucial role in addressing these challenges.
By fostering open communication and encouraging collaboration, they can help bridge the gaps that divide us.
Collamore's approach emphasizes the importance of listening to different perspectives and finding common ground.
Clint Collamore's Journey Clint Collamore's journey into politics began with a strong work ethic and desire to be an active leader within his community.
He grew up in the town of Bremen, and he still fishes out of there on his lobster boat.

As someone who lobsters and digs clams, he is acutely aware of the balance needed to protect the environment for these heritage industries to thrive, while balancing some of the burdensome regulations that are sometimes brought forward without proper research.
It's a difficult balance, and decisions need to be made with consideration for the fisherman and for long-term sustainability.
Collamore has been active in the successful effort to clean up the Medomak River, which impacts all of the communities in House District 45.
Community Involvement Collamore went to Medomak Valley High School and settled in Waldoboro to raise his children.
In addition to his shellfish conservation activities, he was on the Waldoboro Select Board for 18 years and has served on several other town committees.
Collamore is still a member of the Waldoboro Day Committee where he is in charge of the parade.
He is an avid volunteer who has helped with the Waldoboro Free Clothing Closet and Good Things Thrift & Crafts.
These days people can see him loading cars at the food pantry, and Collamore also helps in less organized ways such as answering the call to help someone finish off a chicken coop.
This past winter he enlisted the help of some friends to put a big lobster trap tree in front of The Waldo Theatre.
It was the first time in over a decade that there was a big tree in the village.
Clint Collamore with Sierra and Buddy Murphy after they constructed a trap tree.
Building Bridges As Collamore's influence grew, he focused on building bridges between different political factions.
He recognized that many residents felt disillusioned with traditional political processes and sought to create an inclusive environment where everyone felt heard.
By inviting individuals from various backgrounds to participate in discussions, he was able to foster a culture of collaboration.
Strategies for Bridging Political Gaps Collamore's success in bridging political gaps can be attributed to several key strategies: 1.
Encouraging Open Dialogue One of the cornerstones of Collamore's approach is encouraging open dialogue.
He believes that honest conversations can lead to understanding and empathy.
By creating safe spaces for discussions, he allows individuals to express their views without fear of judgment.
Fostering Inclusivity Inclusivity is essential in bridging political gaps.
Collamore actively seeks to involve individuals from diverse backgrounds in his initiatives.
This not only enriches the conversation but also ensures that all voices are represented.
We learn a lot from our differences, but only if we listen to each other.
Focusing on Common Goals Collamore emphasizes the importance of identifying common goals.
By shifting the focus from political differences to shared objectives, he helps unite individuals around a common purpose.
This approach fosters collaboration and encourages participants to work together toward solutions.
Most Mainers agree that citizens should all have access to healthcare.
Our environment is important not just for the natural beauty of Maine, but for healthy farms and fisheries that make sure our population is fed.
People want to be able to afford their taxes, to heat their homes, fuel their cars, and make sure their family is safe.
There is so much to build upon.
Utilizing Technology In today's digital age, technology plays a significant role in facilitating communication.
Collamore leverages social media and online platforms to reach a broader audience and engage individuals who may not be able to attend in-person meetings.
This strategy allows for greater participation and inclusivity.
Leading by Example Collamore understands the importance of leading by example.
He consistently demonstrates respect and empathy in his interactions with others, regardless of their political beliefs.
This sets a tone for discussions and encourages others to follow suit.
He admits his mistakes and vows to move forward with new knowledge and continued commitment to his community and to the State of Maine.

title.before: Collamore Statement

removed: top of page Home Blog Events Frequently Asked Questions DONATE All Posts Collamore Statement Clinton Collamore Mar 31 2 min read “I intend to run for Maine House District 45 because many constituents asked me to represent them,” Clinton Collamore of Waldoboro said in a statement.
Collamore was elected to the seat in 2022 but resigned after making a mistake with Clean Elections paperwork.
He said he collected some $5 donations from community members and later filled out the paperwork himself not realizing that wasn’t allowed.
“It was an honest mistake for which I have paid dearly.” All the campaign money was paid back, and Collamore says he felt a great deal of embarrassment.

“The hardest part was having my constituents go unrepresented while the issue was sorted out, but they still believe in me and know I care about our communities and our state.” This time, Collamore is running unenrolled.
“Mainers are independent, so it feels like a good fit.” He is also running a traditional campaign this time and has a team on board to help.

“I plan to be present for all votes,” Collamore said, “just as I always try to be present in my community through volunteering and as a former select board member.” Collamore is both a lobsterman and a clam digger, so he is acutely aware of the environmental concerns around Maine’s traditional fisheries.
He also understands the concern for inland waterways and farmlands.
There is a lot of pollution in our waters from old, leaking leach fields and animal waste.
“I will work with the EPA to end the pollution that closes our clam flats and affects the other water critters as well.

“The Maine Emergency Management Agency (MEMA), is surveying drying wells that are causing Mainers to conserve water, have to purchase bottled water, and even drill new or deeper wells,” Collamore said.
“This is a huge and sometimes unmanageable cost for homeowners.” Besides environmental concerns, Collamore said, “I have a few issues that are very important to me.
I want all Mainers to have access to the healthcare they need.
“We also need to make some changes in property taxes so that elderly and fixed income adults are not forced out of their homes because they cannot pay their taxes,” Collamore said.
“It is a tricky issue where there must be income guidelines, and it has to be done in a way that doesn’t shift the burden to younger taxpayers.
This needs to be a state program in order to accomplish that.” “As a father and a grandfather, good education and affordable housing are important to me as well,” Collamore said.
“We need our young people to be able to afford to stay in the communities they grew up in.
Right now, that is hard in each of the towns I would be representing.
“I want to work together with others to find common sense solutions that respect our state’s heritage and keep us moving forward in a positive direction.” Recent Posts See All How to help!

removed.text: [image: #Ready to knock some doors and help elect Democrats across Spokane County? Join Carmela Conroy, Callie Gee, Julia Payne, Elliot Robison, and volunteers from across the area for a Spokane Coalition Canvass in Medical Lake this Sunday! Whether you’re an experienced canvasser or have never knocked a door before, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started. Bring a friend, meet fellow volunteers, and help us reach voters where it matters most—right at their doors. 📅 Sunday, September 20 ⏰ 11:00 a.m.–1:30 p.m. 📍 Medical Lake We need you. Sign up today using the QR code or here: https://www.mobilize.us/conroyforcongress/event/1035813/ and join us Sunday! #Volunteer #Canvass #SpokaneCounty #EasternWashington #wa05 #conroy4congress]

[image: A few weekends ago, Team Eastern Washington joined Walla Walla Frontier Days Parade, and what a welcome! Neighbors on both sides of the street, kids waving, people stopping us to say what they need from their representative in DC. This is how you earn a district – one conversation at a time. Thank you, Walla Walla!]

[image: A full hall in Usk for the Pend Oreille County Democrats fundraiser – good food, good company, and a couple of dogs who came along for the conversation. Pend Oreille County is big, rural, and easy for Washington, D.C. to overlook. The people here are organized, generous, and paying close attention to this race. Thank you for having me, and for all the work you are doing to turn out every vote up north.]

[image: Are you ready to knock on some doors and help elect great progressive candidates across Spokane County? Join Carmela Conroy, Callie Gee, Rob Tupper, Michaela Kelso, Julia Payne, Elliot Robison, Danny Tarkenton and volunteers from across the area for our Spokane Coalition Canvasses! Whether you’re an experienced canvasser or have never knocked a door before, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started. Bring a friend, meet fellow volunteers, and help us reach voters where it matters most—right at their doors. We need you. Sign up today at www.conroy4congress.com/volunteer/ #Volunteer #Canvass #SpokaneCounty #EasternWashington #wa05 #conroy4congress]
[image: Canvassing and tabling opportunities are available. If you're in Pend Orielle county, I'll be at the next Pend Orielle county Democrats fundraiser! See you out there! #conroy4congress #wa05]

[image: Days at the Spokane County Interstate Fair, one folding table, an issues spinner wheel, and hundreds of conversations. We talked with lifelong Democrats, lifelong Republicans, and a lot of people who told us they had stopped paying attention. That last group is toughest to reach, but all of our voices matter. Thank you to the Spokane County Democrats and every volunteer who took a shift in that hall. Showing up where people already are beats any ad we could buy.]

[image: Delighted to speak with the Retired Public Employees Council of Washington at their chapter lunch, and to do it at the Longhorn Barbecue. My parents used to take me there before I flew off to overseas assignments, so walking back in felt deeply nostalgic. RPEC members spent their careers serving Washington – in our schools, our hospitals, our cities and our state agencies. They earned their pensions and their health care, and I will defend both in Congress. Retirement security is not a line item. It is a promise. Thank you to RPEC for the invitation, and for the questions – this group does its homework.]

[image: Do you want a Conroy for Congress Yard Sign? Signs can be picked up, during office hours, at our Spokane Campaign HQ, 1106 N. Washington St., Suite B, or the Walla Walla County Democrats office, location and hours at https://www.wallawallademocrats.com Outside of these areas or would like a sign delivered? Contact: volcoord@conroy4congress.com]

[image: Dog day at HQ, and he should have been here. Our volunteers brought their best coworkers, the phones still got dialed, and nobody left without a treat. Come by, bring your (well-socialized) dog, take a clipboard: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Donald Trump just posted a video attacking me by name as a "dumb-o-crat" and giving Michael Baumgartner his "Complete and Total Endorsement." Trump does not get involved in a race until his party is in trouble. Eastern Washington has his attention because we put this seat in play, and people here are done being taken for granted. But when Trump weighs in, the money follows. This endorsement always brings a surge of cash. I don't have an army of billionaires with an endless supply of dark money. I have you. I spent my career as a prosecutor and a diplomat. I am not intimidated by a man who thinks a social media post decides an election. Help me make sure voters here get the facts instead of Trump's version of them – and we'll win this: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Eastern Washington, we’ve got a busy week ahead! 🎉 From Newport to Airway Heights, Lewiston, and Liberty Lake, Carmela will be out meeting voters, canvassing with local candidates, and connecting with supporters across the region. Check out the upcoming events below, grab a friend, and come join us! 💙 We’d love to see you there! Volunteer and donate at www.conroy4congress.com]

[image: Front page of the Seattle Times: "Democrats say U.S. House race is in play." National Democrats consider us a District in Play. Incumbent Michael Baumgartner was the only Republican on the primary ballot, and most voters here voted for change. Nobody handed us this. Volunteers, house party hosts, and neighbors chipping in $26 at a time put this seat on the map. Now let's finish the job. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Grateful to the Walla Walla County Democrats for having us at their County Fair booth!. Local volunteers do the unglamorous work – tabling in the heat, signing up volunteers, talking with neighbors nobody has asked for their vote in years. If you are in Walla Walla and want in, we have a place for you: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Hillyard Pride, and our table was one of the busiest in the park – thanks largely to the volunteers who staffed it and the campaign dog who held down the chair. Eastern Washington is a place where people look after each other. Pride here is neighbors, kids, dogs on leashes, and a community where everyone belongs. I am proud to stand with it, in Hillyard and in Congress.]

[image: Honored to earn the endorsement of the @allianceforgunresponsibility Victory Fund. Every family deserves to feel safe at school, at work, in their place of worship, and in their neighborhood. In Congress, I’ll fight for common-sense gun safety to protect our communities.]

[image: If you haven't voted yet, today is the day! Return your completed ballot to an official drop box by 8pm. Need a replacement ballot in Ferry, Spokane, or Stevens County? Contact your County Elections or Auditor’s Office right away. Stay safe, and let's get out there and vote.‌‌💙]

[image: It's going to be a busy weekend in WA05! Carmela will be at the EWU Neighborfest in Cheney on Friday and there will be canvassing Friday, Saturday and Sunday, in Cheney, Deer Park and Spokane Valley. We need volunteers to staff the Conroy 4 Congress Table at Valley Fest on Saturday and Sunday. To sign up for a shift for two visit www.conroy4congress.com/volunteer/]

[image: James joined his brother Murphy at the campaign office – it's safe to say both are keenly interested in the yard sign situation. Our office runs on volunteers, coffee, and lately a fair amount of dog hair. Come by and say hello. The welcoming committee is ready.]

[image: Join our Election Night Gathering with Team Conroy for Congress! Come gather with our team, connect with fellow supporters, and watch the election results roll in with us at BrickWest Brewing (1318 W. 1st Ave.) from 6:00–9:00 PM.]

[image: Lanterns over the water, neighbors on the lawn, and not one dollar from a corporate PAC. Tonight at midnight the fundraising quarter closes. This is the last report before ballots go in the mail, and it is the number every political reporter and every DC group will use to decide whether Eastern Washington is worth taking seriously. They already decided Trump's endorsement was worth spending on. Let's show them what neighbors chipping in looks like instead: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Michael Perry & Eric Horsted opened their beautiful home to us on the Autumn Equinox. String lights, a yard full of neighbors, and – we did not see this coming – aerialists! One of the most memorable nights of the campaign. Everyone who came out that night helped put this race in play. We are so grateful!]

[image: Nearly 300 people participated in person at the #WA05 forum at Whitman College in Walla Walla, and they came with real questions about affordability, health care, and datacenters. Thanks to AAUW Walla Walla and Northwest Public Broadcasting for hosting the forum, and Rasa Vineyards and the Network of Exceptional Women for the after party. We'll be back!]

[image: Now that is craftsmanship. Volunteers across Eastern Washington are building and planting signs on their own land, on their own time, because they want a representative who actually shows up here. Thank you for this one – it is a beauty. Want a sign of your own? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: One of our canvassers knocked on a door in Spokane and left with a loaf of banana bread. This is the part of campaigning that never makes the news. Someone gives up a Saturday, walks a neighborhood, and gets a real conversation and a sweet treat out of it. That is how you win a district Washington, D.C. wrote off. Thank you for the bread, and for the welcome. Want to come with us? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Porchfest is Spokane at its best – neighbors on lawns, music on porches, strangers turning into friends by the third song. Thank you to everyone who stopped to talk with us between sets. Being out in community is the best part of being a candidate.]

[image: Rain, shine, and new and returning Eagles. We participated in EWU Neighborfest, walked Cheney in a coalition canvass with Karina Wallace (@karina_justfiguringitout), who is running for State Rep in the 9th LD. Go Team! Students, make your vote count HERE. Register online at VoteWA.gov through October 26, or in person through Election Day.]
