removed.text: [image: #Ready to knock some doors and help elect Democrats across Spokane County? Join Carmela Conroy, Callie Gee, Julia Payne, Elliot Robison, and volunteers from across the area for a Spokane Coalition Canvass in Medical Lake this Sunday! Whether you’re an experienced canvasser or have never knocked a door before, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started. Bring a friend, meet fellow volunteers, and help us reach voters where it matters most—right at their doors. 📅 Sunday, September 20 ⏰ 11:00 a.m.–1:30 p.m. 📍 Medical Lake We need you. Sign up today using the QR code or here: https://www.mobilize.us/conroyforcongress/event/1035813/ and join us Sunday! #Volunteer #Canvass #SpokaneCounty #EasternWashington #wa05 #conroy4congress]

[image: A few weekends ago, Team Eastern Washington joined Walla Walla Frontier Days Parade, and what a welcome! Neighbors on both sides of the street, kids waving, people stopping us to say what they need from their representative in DC. This is how you earn a district – one conversation at a time. Thank you, Walla Walla!]

[image: A full hall in Usk for the Pend Oreille County Democrats fundraiser – good food, good company, and a couple of dogs who came along for the conversation. Pend Oreille County is big, rural, and easy for Washington, D.C. to overlook. The people here are organized, generous, and paying close attention to this race. Thank you for having me, and for all the work you are doing to turn out every vote up north.]

[image: Are you ready to knock on some doors and help elect great progressive candidates across Spokane County? Join Carmela Conroy, Callie Gee, Rob Tupper, Michaela Kelso, Julia Payne, Elliot Robison, Danny Tarkenton and volunteers from across the area for our Spokane Coalition Canvasses! Whether you’re an experienced canvasser or have never knocked a door before, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started. Bring a friend, meet fellow volunteers, and help us reach voters where it matters most—right at their doors. We need you. Sign up today at www.conroy4congress.com/volunteer/ #Volunteer #Canvass #SpokaneCounty #EasternWashington #wa05 #conroy4congress]
[image: Canvassing and tabling opportunities are available. If you're in Pend Orielle county, I'll be at the next Pend Orielle county Democrats fundraiser! See you out there! #conroy4congress #wa05]

[image: Days at the Spokane County Interstate Fair, one folding table, an issues spinner wheel, and hundreds of conversations. We talked with lifelong Democrats, lifelong Republicans, and a lot of people who told us they had stopped paying attention. That last group is toughest to reach, but all of our voices matter. Thank you to the Spokane County Democrats and every volunteer who took a shift in that hall. Showing up where people already are beats any ad we could buy.]

[image: Delighted to speak with the Retired Public Employees Council of Washington at their chapter lunch, and to do it at the Longhorn Barbecue. My parents used to take me there before I flew off to overseas assignments, so walking back in felt deeply nostalgic. RPEC members spent their careers serving Washington – in our schools, our hospitals, our cities and our state agencies. They earned their pensions and their health care, and I will defend both in Congress. Retirement security is not a line item. It is a promise. Thank you to RPEC for the invitation, and for the questions – this group does its homework.]

[image: Do you want a Conroy for Congress Yard Sign? Signs can be picked up, during office hours, at our Spokane Campaign HQ, 1106 N. Washington St., Suite B, or the Walla Walla County Democrats office, location and hours at https://www.wallawallademocrats.com Outside of these areas or would like a sign delivered? Contact: volcoord@conroy4congress.com]

[image: Dog day at HQ, and he should have been here. Our volunteers brought their best coworkers, the phones still got dialed, and nobody left without a treat. Come by, bring your (well-socialized) dog, take a clipboard: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Donald Trump just posted a video attacking me by name as a "dumb-o-crat" and giving Michael Baumgartner his "Complete and Total Endorsement." Trump does not get involved in a race until his party is in trouble. Eastern Washington has his attention because we put this seat in play, and people here are done being taken for granted. But when Trump weighs in, the money follows. This endorsement always brings a surge of cash. I don't have an army of billionaires with an endless supply of dark money. I have you. I spent my career as a prosecutor and a diplomat. I am not intimidated by a man who thinks a social media post decides an election. Help me make sure voters here get the facts instead of Trump's version of them – and we'll win this: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Eastern Washington, we’ve got a busy week ahead! 🎉 From Newport to Airway Heights, Lewiston, and Liberty Lake, Carmela will be out meeting voters, canvassing with local candidates, and connecting with supporters across the region. Check out the upcoming events below, grab a friend, and come join us! 💙 We’d love to see you there! Volunteer and donate at www.conroy4congress.com]

[image: Front page of the Seattle Times: "Democrats say U.S. House race is in play." National Democrats consider us a District in Play. Incumbent Michael Baumgartner was the only Republican on the primary ballot, and most voters here voted for change. Nobody handed us this. Volunteers, house party hosts, and neighbors chipping in $26 at a time put this seat on the map. Now let's finish the job. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Grateful to the Walla Walla County Democrats for having us at their County Fair booth!. Local volunteers do the unglamorous work – tabling in the heat, signing up volunteers, talking with neighbors nobody has asked for their vote in years. If you are in Walla Walla and want in, we have a place for you: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Hillyard Pride, and our table was one of the busiest in the park – thanks largely to the volunteers who staffed it and the campaign dog who held down the chair. Eastern Washington is a place where people look after each other. Pride here is neighbors, kids, dogs on leashes, and a community where everyone belongs. I am proud to stand with it, in Hillyard and in Congress.]

[image: Honored to earn the endorsement of the @allianceforgunresponsibility Victory Fund. Every family deserves to feel safe at school, at work, in their place of worship, and in their neighborhood. In Congress, I’ll fight for common-sense gun safety to protect our communities.]

[image: If you haven't voted yet, today is the day! Return your completed ballot to an official drop box by 8pm. Need a replacement ballot in Ferry, Spokane, or Stevens County? Contact your County Elections or Auditor’s Office right away. Stay safe, and let's get out there and vote.‌‌💙]

[image: It's going to be a busy weekend in WA05! Carmela will be at the EWU Neighborfest in Cheney on Friday and there will be canvassing Friday, Saturday and Sunday, in Cheney, Deer Park and Spokane Valley. We need volunteers to staff the Conroy 4 Congress Table at Valley Fest on Saturday and Sunday. To sign up for a shift for two visit www.conroy4congress.com/volunteer/]

[image: James joined his brother Murphy at the campaign office – it's safe to say both are keenly interested in the yard sign situation. Our office runs on volunteers, coffee, and lately a fair amount of dog hair. Come by and say hello. The welcoming committee is ready.]

[image: Join our Election Night Gathering with Team Conroy for Congress! Come gather with our team, connect with fellow supporters, and watch the election results roll in with us at BrickWest Brewing (1318 W. 1st Ave.) from 6:00–9:00 PM.]

[image: Lanterns over the water, neighbors on the lawn, and not one dollar from a corporate PAC. Tonight at midnight the fundraising quarter closes. This is the last report before ballots go in the mail, and it is the number every political reporter and every DC group will use to decide whether Eastern Washington is worth taking seriously. They already decided Trump's endorsement was worth spending on. Let's show them what neighbors chipping in looks like instead: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609]

[image: Michael Perry & Eric Horsted opened their beautiful home to us on the Autumn Equinox. String lights, a yard full of neighbors, and – we did not see this coming – aerialists! One of the most memorable nights of the campaign. Everyone who came out that night helped put this race in play. We are so grateful!]

[image: Nearly 300 people participated in person at the #WA05 forum at Whitman College in Walla Walla, and they came with real questions about affordability, health care, and datacenters. Thanks to AAUW Walla Walla and Northwest Public Broadcasting for hosting the forum, and Rasa Vineyards and the Network of Exceptional Women for the after party. We'll be back!]

[image: Now that is craftsmanship. Volunteers across Eastern Washington are building and planting signs on their own land, on their own time, because they want a representative who actually shows up here. Thank you for this one – it is a beauty. Want a sign of your own? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: One of our canvassers knocked on a door in Spokane and left with a loaf of banana bread. This is the part of campaigning that never makes the news. Someone gives up a Saturday, walks a neighborhood, and gets a real conversation and a sweet treat out of it. That is how you win a district Washington, D.C. wrote off. Thank you for the bread, and for the welcome. Want to come with us? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Porchfest is Spokane at its best – neighbors on lawns, music on porches, strangers turning into friends by the third song. Thank you to everyone who stopped to talk with us between sets. Being out in community is the best part of being a candidate.]

[image: Rain, shine, and new and returning Eagles. We participated in EWU Neighborfest, walked Cheney in a coalition canvass with Karina Wallace (@karina_justfiguringitout), who is running for State Rep in the 9th LD. Go Team! Students, make your vote count HERE. Register online at VoteWA.gov through October 26, or in person through Election Day.]

[image: Rush hour at Five Mile Plaza, and this is what our campaign looks like: neighbors on a corner, signs in hand, waving at people they have known for thirty years. Nobody paid them. Nobody bused them in. They decided this seat is worth standing on a sidewalk for. If you have ever wanted to help but did not know where to start, this is where to start: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Spotted downtown: a Silverado with an Air Force plate, a lumber rack, and a Carmela Conroy sign strapped across the back. This campaign does not run on billionaires. It runs on veterans, tradespeople, and neighbors who put our name on their own truck and their own front lawn. Every one of these is somebody publicly announcing their decision. Want one? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Strong leadership starts with listening. That's why Carmela is committed to showing up in every corner of our district and having conversations with every community. Thank you to the Ferry County Republican Party for hosting a #WA05 candidate forum in #Republic!]

[image: Thank you to everyone who joined Carmela and Team Conroy at BrickWest Brewing on Election Night! With votes still being counted, we're encouraged by the results and energized for the work ahead - join the movement today at conroy4congress.com 💪]

[image: Thank you to our hosts, the Chases and Kuhlings, for inviting your friends to join us! A beautiful old living room, every chair filled, and neighbors who came ready with good questions and stayed long after the last one. Ballots arrive soon! If you would like to host a gathering like this before then, we would love to come: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Thank you to the Skeims for opening their home to us. A living room full of neighbors, real questions about health care and the cost of living, and no talking points. I would take one of these over a rally any day – you cannot dodge a question in someone's kitchen. If you want to host one before ballots go out, we will bring the buttons: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Thank you to the Stevens County Democrats for the warm welcome in Chewelah, and to everyone who came out to talk and then headed out to knock doors with us. Rural Eastern Washington is not a flyover on my map – it is the job. Want to canvass with us? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: The Garfield County Democrats set up at the fair with a flip chart and one question: what matters to you this election? Look at what people wrote in. Social Security. Health care. Gas and diesel prices. Food prices. Farming costs. Education. Misinformation. No forever wars. Data centers, and guardrails on AI. Not one person walked up and said culture war. People in Garfield County are worried about the cost of running a household and a farm, and about being told a story instead of the truth. That list is my agenda. Thank you to the Garfield County Democrats for asking the question.]
[image: The writing is on the wall. Literally. #FlipWA05 Let's do this, Eastern Washington.]

[image: There’s a lot happening across Eastern Washington! Carmela is heading to Walla Walla, Spokane, and Spokane Valley, with two upcoming candidate forums and plenty of opportunities to get involved. Check out this week’s events flyer and find a way to join Team Eastern Washington — whether you’re ready to canvass, phone bank, table, or wave signs! Election Day is getting closer. Let’s finish strong!]

[image: VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES!!! If you’ve been thinking about volunteering with Conroy for Congress, now is the time! With Election Day getting closer, there are more ways than ever to help Carmela & local candidates across our community. 🏠 Knock doors with a canvassing team — training is provided, so no experience is necessary. ☎️ Make phone calls from campaign headquarters or from the comfort of home. 👋 Looking for something a little smaller? Wave signs, staff the campaign office, or help at Carmela’s information table at a local event. Whether you have a few hours or want to get involved regularly, there’s a place for you on this campaign. Pick what works for you and sign up today: www.conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

[image: Valleyfest weekend, sharing a booth with "Rational Rob" Tupper, candidate for the 4th LD. We enjoyed lots of good conversations about what people in Spokane Valley need from their representatives. Thanks to everyone who showed up!]

[image: Walla Walla — we need you! Help Carmela Conroy and Derek Sarley and the Vote NO on 645! campaign for two combined canvasses this weekend as we talk with voters and build support across the community. Friday, October 9 | 4–6 PM Sunday, October 11 | 11 AM–1 PM Every door knocked and every conversation matters. Grab a friend, sign up, and come help us finish strong! Sign Up Here! https://www.mobilize.us/conroyforcongress/event/1054338/]

[image: We stopped by Masters Brewhouse in Deer Park on the way home from canvassing in Chewelah, and folks who had seen me at the WA-05 candidate forum waved us over. We talked rising costs, high school sports, and what Eastern Washington needs from its representative in DC.]

[image: Yard signs are flying out the door and new canvassers signing up! Two months from Election Day, this is what it looks like when a district decides it is not sitting this one out. Want a sign, or a door-knocking or phone-banking shift? Sign up at https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer]

Thank you for this one – it is a beauty. Want a sign of your own? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/816953237_17971377708150272_208569718414384202_n.jpg|Dog day at HQ, and he should have been here. Our volunteers brought their best coworkers, the phones still got dialed, and nobody left without a treat. Come by, bring your (well-socialized) dog, take a clipboard: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/817296989_17971559949150272_2102014395182255478_n.jpg|Thank you to the Stevens County Democrats for the warm welcome in Chewelah, and to everyone who came out to talk and then headed out to knock doors with us. Rural Eastern Washington is not a flyover on my map – it is the job. Want to canvass with us? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

We talked rising costs, high school sports, and what Eastern Washington needs from its representative in DC.

Sign up at https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/819336003_17971855800150272_8540365009655150371_n.jpg|Donald Trump just posted a video attacking me by name as a "dumb-o-crat" and giving Michael Baumgartner his "Complete and Total Endorsement." Trump does not get involved in a race until his party is in trouble. Eastern Washington has his attention because we put this seat in play, and people here are done being taken for granted. But when Trump weighs in, the money follows. This endorsement always brings a surge of cash. I don't have an army of billionaires with an endless supply of dark money. I have you. I spent my career as a prosecutor and a diplomat. I am not intimidated by a man who thinks a social media post decides an election. Help me make sure voters here get the facts instead of Trump's version of them – and we'll win this: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/819741544_17972132217150272_7882768188036716837_n.jpg|Rush hour at Five Mile Plaza, and this is what our campaign looks like: neighbors on a corner, signs in hand, waving at people they have known for thirty years. Nobody paid them. Nobody bused them in. They decided this seat is worth standing on a sidewalk for. If you have ever wanted to help but did not know where to start, this is where to start: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/825277380_17972898033150272_4501363739985233281_n.jpg|Spotted downtown: a Silverado with an Air Force plate, a lumber rack, and a Carmela Conroy sign strapped across the back. This campaign does not run on billionaires. It runs on veterans, tradespeople, and neighbors who put our name on their own truck and their own front lawn. Every one of these is somebody publicly announcing their decision. Want one? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/825322442_17972386047150272_2825254085217457944_n.jpg|Days at the Spokane County Interstate Fair, one folding table, an issues spinner wheel, and hundreds of conversations. We talked with lifelong Democrats, lifelong Republicans, and a lot of people who told us they had stopped paying attention. That last group is toughest to reach, but all of our voices matter. Thank you to the Spokane County Democrats and every volunteer who took a shift in that hall. Showing up where people already are beats any ad we could buy.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/825996804_17972538837150272_2983924273974436782_n.jpg|Thank you to the Skeims for opening their home to us. A living room full of neighbors, real questions about health care and the cost of living, and no talking points. I would take one of these over a rally any day – you cannot dodge a question in someone's kitchen. If you want to host one before ballots go out, we will bring the buttons: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/826110940_17972713473150272_3423129184639354632_n.jpg|Hillyard Pride, and our table was one of the busiest in the park – thanks largely to the volunteers who staffed it and the campaign dog who held down the chair. Eastern Washington is a place where people look after each other. Pride here is neighbors, kids, dogs on leashes, and a community where everyone belongs. I am proud to stand with it, in Hillyard and in Congress.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/830632499_17973207984150272_7214689790643353596_n.jpg|Lanterns over the water, neighbors on the lawn, and not one dollar from a corporate PAC. Tonight at midnight the fundraising quarter closes. This is the last report before ballots go in the mail, and it is the number every political reporter and every DC group will use to decide whether Eastern Washington is worth taking seriously. They already decided Trump's endorsement was worth spending on. Let's show them what neighbors chipping in looks like instead: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/839559388_17974238577150272_5666357825033501132_n.jpg|Nearly 300 people participated in person at the #WA05 forum at Whitman College in Walla Walla, and they came with real questions about affordability, health care, and datacenters. Thanks to AAUW Walla Walla and Northwest Public Broadcasting for hosting the forum, and Rasa Vineyards and the Network of Exceptional Women for the after party. We'll be back!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/840264308_17974101222150272_2697571734605207110_n.jpg|Valleyfest weekend, sharing a booth with "Rational Rob" Tupper, candidate for the 4th LD. We enjoyed lots of good conversations about what people in Spokane Valley need from their representatives. Thanks to everyone who showed up!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/840589609_17974398468150272_6279657702099450158_n.jpg|Michael Perry & Eric Horsted opened their beautiful home to us on the Autumn Equinox. String lights, a yard full of neighbors, and – we did not see this coming – aerialists! One of the most memorable nights of the campaign. Everyone who came out that night helped put this race in play. We are so grateful!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/841012494_17974711122150272_5119648225189960708_n.jpg|James joined his brother Murphy at the campaign office – it's safe to say both are keenly interested in the yard sign situation. Our office runs on volunteers, coffee, and lately a fair amount of dog hair. Come by and say hello. The welcoming committee is ready.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/841120902_17974435464150272_1153027006282809405_n.jpg|A full hall in Usk for the Pend Oreille County Democrats fundraiser – good food, good company, and a couple of dogs who came along for the conversation. Pend Oreille County is big, rural, and easy for Washington, D.C. to overlook. The people here are organized, generous, and paying close attention to this race. Thank you for having me, and for all the work you are doing to turn out every vote up north.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/842821366_17974749465150272_5403233037197265969_n.jpg|Thank you to our hosts, the Chases and Kuhlings, for inviting your friends to join us! A beautiful old living room, every chair filled, and neighbors who came ready with good questions and stayed long after the last one. Ballots arrive soon! If you would like to host a gathering like this before then, we would love to come: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/844544792_17974725390150272_2695542744322842977_n.jpg|Front page of the Seattle Times: "Democrats say U.S. House race is in play." National Democrats consider us a District in Play. Incumbent Michael Baumgartner was the only Republican on the primary ballot, and most voters here voted for change. Nobody handed us this. Volunteers, house party hosts, and neighbors chipping in $26 at a time put this seat on the map. Now let's finish the job. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609

added: top of page ​ About Priorities Press Neighbors for Susan All Posts Search In support of Culp #ago 1 min read Peggy Hewes Newbury, VT Well, I am breaking my own rule here.
As an employee of the Town of Newbury, albeit in a very minor capacity, I’ve avoided making public my political positions.
But I feel impelled to do so now in support of Susan Culp’s candidacy for VT State Representative.
I’ve seen how Susan’s leadership on the Newbury Selectboard and her work on the Planning Commission and other volunteer boards have benefitted our town.
She is unfailingly respectful of everyone and brings such a valuable background of experience to the table.
Even better, she looks at every issue without partisan bias.
Susan follows in the footsteps of many other Newbury leaders (Signa Carbee, Al Stevens, and Alma Roystan come to mind), with vision, diplomacy, and integrity.
I will vote to have Susan represent us in Montpelier.

Home About News Volunteer Donate Contact News October 15, 2021 by webmaster 1 Comment LANSING, Mich., Oct.
Gretchen Whitmer and the Michigan Economic Development Corp. announced the $23 million expansion of two businesses in Genesee County.
NorthGate has been a fixture of the Flint business community for decades since it was founded by Jack Goggins in 1984, while DAG Technology conducts work across the globe.
Together, NorthGate and DAG Technology will bring more than 400 jobs to Genesee County.
The Genesee County House Democratic Delegation applauded the announcement.
“Genesee County is open for business,” said state Rep.
“For too long, our cities and towns have been overlooked and underutilized.

I know the incredible work that our community members can do and am proud to see that investments are catching up with what we have always known to be true: Genesee County gets things done.” “Now more than ever, we need to create good, decent-paying jobs,” said state Rep.
“Initiatives like this will not only create jobs today but help to rebuild our economy tomorrow.
When we foster collaboration between business and government, everyone benefits.” “I am always happy to hear about investment in our community.
New jobs bring new life and opportunity to our economy,” said State Rep.

“Genesee County is home to many hardworking folks, making it the perfect place for businesses to thrive.” Tags: articles Opinions Share: twitter facebook youtube Post navigation Previous post Celebrating our Men & Women frontline and remembering 9/11 Next post “Genesee County is open for business!” You May Also Like Family News March 1, 2021 Flint mayor, state rep promote free community college program for Michigan residents News January 26, 2022 Cynthia Neeley on Gov.

removed: Dale Hawkins for Idaho Home About Issues Governance Get Involved Donate About Dale Hawkins A common man standing up for Idaho's freedom and traditional values The journey to Idaho In 1998, my family made a life-changing decision.
We moved to Idaho seeking something that was becoming increasingly rare in America: the freedom to raise our children according to our values and beliefs.

We wanted the liberty to homeschool our six children, to live out our Christian faith without government interference, and to be part of a community that still believed in limited government and individual responsibility.
Idaho welcomed us with open arms.
Here, we found a state that understood what it meant to respect parental rights, to honor constitutional principles, and to let families make their own decisions.
That freedom is what drew us here, and it's what I'm fighting to protect for every Idaho family.
I'm not a career politician.
I'm not a lawyer looking to climb the political ladder.
I'm a husband, a father, and an everyday citizen who believes that government works best when it stays within its constitutional boundaries and lets people live their lives in freedom.
Faith, family, and freedom My Christian faith is the foundation of everything I do.
It shapes how I view government, how I approach policy, and how I interact with my fellow Idahoans.
I believe that our rights come from God, not from government, and that those rights must be protected at all costs.
As a father of six, I understand what's at stake when we talk about education policy, parental rights, and the future of our state.
Every decision I make in the legislature is guided by one simple question: Is this good for Idaho families?
Will this protect their freedom or diminish it?
I'm pro-life without apology.
I believe in the sanctity of human life from conception to natural death.
I believe in the Second Amendment.
I believe in property rights, self defense, and limited government.
And I believe that Idaho should remain a beacon of freedom in an increasingly regulated world.
Fighting for your freedom Since entering public service, I've worked tirelessly to defend the principles that make Idaho special.

I've fought for homeschooling rights, pushed back against federal overreach, defended the Second Amendment, pushed hard for stronger immigration enforcement, and stood firm on pro-life values even when it wasn't politically convenient.
I believe in accountability and transparency.
Elected officials should answer to the people, not to special interests or political insiders.
That's why I make myself available to constituents and explain my votes, and why I'm willing to stand alone when principle demands it.
Idaho is worth fighting for.
Our way of life, our values, and our freedoms are under constant attack from those who think government knows better than families.
I'm committed to standing in the gap, to being a voice for common-sense conservatism, and to ensuring that Idaho remains a place where freedom thrives.
From Fernwood, Idaho Proud to call Fernwood home and honored to serve the people of Idaho.
Together, we can preserve the freedom and values that make our state exceptional.

title.before: Governance & Leadership - Dale Hawkins for Idaho

removed: Dale Hawkins for Idaho Home About Issues Governance Get Involved Donate Proper Governance Limited Government · Individual Liberty · Free Enterprise · Traditional Values The foundation of freedom I am a Republican dedicated to the preservation of our Constitutional Republic.
Governmental power must be limited, defined, and constrained by the state and federal Constitution while being kept in check by an informed electorate.
Our founders were wise to set up checks and balances to limit government, but it is up to every generation to preserve them.
The Constitution isn't a suggestion.
It's not a living document that changes with the political winds.
It's the supreme law of the land, and every elected official takes an oath to uphold it.
That oath means something to me.
It means that when I vote on legislation, I ask first whether it's constitutional, not whether it's popular or politically expedient.
Too often, politicians treat the Constitution as an obstacle to be worked around rather than a framework to be honored.
They expand government power, create new regulations, and pass laws invoking powers not granted to them, all in the name of solving problems government often created in the first place.
Constitutional Limits Government authority must remain strictly within the boundaries established by the Constitution.
When government exceeds these limits, individual liberty suffers.
Protection of Rights Our rights come from God, not from government.
The primary role of government is to protect these God-given rights, not to grant or restrict them based on political whims.
Rule of Law Laws must be applied equally to all citizens.
No one is above the law, and no one should be subject to arbitrary government action.
Due process and equal protection are non-negotiable.
Accountability to the People Elected officials serve at the pleasure of the people, not the other way around.
Government must be transparent, accountable, and responsive to those it serves.
Defending Idaho's sovereignty Idaho is not a subdivision of the federal government.
The 10th Amendment makes this clear: powers not delegated to the federal government are reserved to the states and the people.
Yet time and again, we see federal overreach that treats states as mere administrative units of a centralized government.
Idaho has the right and the duty to push back against unconstitutional federal mandates.
Whether it's land management, healthcare, education, or gun rights, Idaho should be free to chart its own course based on the values and priorities of its citizens.
I've worked to strengthen Idaho's sovereignty by opposing federal mandates, defending our natural resources, and ensuring that Idaho law reflects Idaho values.
I'll continue to stand firm against any attempt to turn Idaho into a puppet of Washington, D.C.
Accountability matters I believe elected officials should be transparent about their positions and accountable for their votes.
If you have questions about what I stand for or want to know how I voted on a particular issue, I want to hear from you.
Reach out: P.O.
Box 245 Fernwood, ID 83830 Dale Hawkins for Idaho Fighting for limited government, individual liberty, and traditional values in Idaho.

added: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/848935933_1609125274565813_3574131812245543781_n.jpg|THIS JUST IN! 📣 My campaign has received the endorsement of @jonossoff 📣 I am enormously proud of our Senator and proud to have cast my vote for him in his bid for reelection. He is a calm, steady, truthful presence in a landscape that deserparetly needs effective leadership. The differences between him and his opponent have been on stark display in their recent debates. See the Atlanta Press Club debate from last night and judge for yourself. GPB.org/events/news/2026/10/13/us-senate-i-atlanta-press-club-debate Thank you, Senator Ossoff, for trusting me with your endorsement, and I very much look forward to working with you to serve the people of Georgia! #PublicServant #GeorgiaDemocrats #GeorgiaSenateDems #2026Midterms #ElectWomen #UseYourVoice #LeadershipThatPutsPeopleFirst
removed: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/843494837_1604081428403531_6967070358599171801_n.jpg|Thank you to @brookslawpartners, @tanyaforgeorgia, @gawinlist and @emilys_list for hosting an insightful discussion on Reproductive Freedom & Maternal Mortality in Georgia. It was an honor to be counted amoung leaders working hard for women's healthcare, economic opportunities, and ability to have a child without fear of being denied lifesaving care in the event of miscarriage. Those creating the laws tend not to be the ones that suffer from them. The incumbent who I am running to unseat is the primary author of the bill that puts the government between a woman and her doctor, stripped us of our bodily autonomy and has resulted in the death of women in our state. HB 481 is quite possibily unconstitutional, and while the courts (deliberately slowly) try to figure that out, I am confident that electing my fellow WIN List candidate Tanya Miller as Georgia's next Attorney General will change the course of maternal mortality and women's healthcare in our state. There is no justice for women if we don't have agency over our own bodies. We must be at the center of the work for reproductive freedom. However you stand on women's reproductive rights, we must address the unacceptably high ranking of Georgia's maternal mortality. Let's get back to common sense lawmaking that stands up for the women of Georgia. #UseYourVoice #PublicServant #LeadershipThatPutsPeopleFirst #WomensRightsMatter #2026Midterms #GeorgiaDemocrats #ElectWomen

Darcy Castro Candidate for Georgia Senate District 37

title.after: News from Darcy Castro

added: NEWS from the Campaign Trail Hello #TeamCastro!
We are officially in our Early Voting Era...
AND have received the endorsement of Senator Jon Ossoff!
I am grateful for this wonderful vote of confidence and look forward to collaborating with the Senator to serve the people of Georgia.
If not, have you made a plan?
The blue wave doesn't happen if we don't mobilize absolutely everyone.
Help us make this crucial impact volunteering with us in the Get Out the Vote (GOTV) push.
We need you to stay strong with us to the finish line!
Reminder: Make your plan to vote today!
You can check your registration, view your ballot and find your polling location here !
Darcy Castro Candidate for Georgia Senate District 37 HOW TO HELP Where You Can Join Us Volunteers Needed!
Want to make sure that every eligible voter is energized to get to the polls?
Join us in daily activities to reach voters!
I challenge you to sign up for at least 3 ways to help.
Democracy doesn't happen in a vacuum.
We need to vote, but we also need to serve.
Join me on this journey of civic engagement!
We are entering the home stretch of this campaign.
In order to make the most of our content and outreach efforts, we need Ambassadors to coordinate with us to amplify content and get our materials out to those who need to see it.
Email me at Info@DarcyCastro.com to join the team!
October Donation Drive Join us in supporting the residents of The Extension.
They have two campuses and need community support to meet their cruicial mission goals.
I have personally toured their facility and met with staff, and know the importance of their work in our community.
Drop off at our Wednesday night gatherings at Kirkwood or at the Campaign Pantry located at 3439 Elm Creek Drive.
Join our weekly in-person volunteer group starting Wednesday, October 7th, at Kirkwood Presbyterian from 6 - 8 pm for an evening of phone banking with #TeamCastro.
Park in the lower parking lot and meet us in the lower fellowship hall, near the playground.
We will provide training and lots of encouragement.
It's an easy, free way to reach voters.
Please bring your charged phone and compatible headphones , if you have them.

Virtual Phonebanking Join us this week for our virtual phonebanking sessions: Thursday, 10/15 Friday, 10/16 Monday, 10/19 Tuesday, 10/20 Saturday Canvassing Join Senate Minority Leader Harold Jones and Darcy Castro this Saturday at 10 am as we connect with voters to build a stronger future for our public schools and our communities.
We will meet at 3655 Cherokee St NW.

Additional Canvassing Join us for our other important canvassing launches: Thursday, 10/15 Friday, 10/16 Sunday, 10/18 Monday, 10/19 Tuesday, 10/20 Night on the Farm Join us Sunday, October 18th from 6 - 8 pm for our Night on the Farm fundraiser!
I hope you can join us for an evening of BBQ, animals and good company!
Join us November 3rd for a #TeamCastro election night watch party from 7-10 pm at unWine'd & Tap Marietta.
Let's wrap up this tremendous experience together - celebrating community, friendship and (hopefully!) new beginnings.
#TeamCastro volunteers will gather on Wednesday, November 4th from 6-8 pm to assemble 250 early childhood education book kits in partnership with Cobb Collaborative.
Enjoy some time together while serving our community!
(And let's blow off some steam together after this hectic election season, lol!) What I've Been Up To Phonebankin' Nothing beats direct voter contact.
Thank you to the volunteers who came out to phonebank with us at our weekly Wednesday meet up.
And thank you Matt for the fun phone receivers to plug in!
Round two of our volunteer-supported postcards hit the post office and are on their way to our swing voters!
Senate Dems Canvass Thank you to the staff of the Senate Democratic Caucus for coming out to SD 37 to canvass with me on opening day of early voting!

Sign Waiving Thank you to Indivisible Cobb for coordinating sign waving at key locations around our District... and thank you to the volunteers who are joining me to smile, wave and encourage our fellow neighbors to get out and vote!
Ladies Meet & Greet Thank you to my new friends for taking the time to learn more about me and this important campaign.
I think having open conversations about real issues affecting our communities is crucial to learning how to best serve the people and families of SD 37.

Reproductive Freedom Forum Thank you to Brooks Law Partners, LLC , Tanya for Georgia , Georgia WIN List and EMILY's List for hosting an insightful discussion on Reproductive Freedom & Maternal Mortality in Georgia.

It was an honor to be counted among leaders working hard for women's healthcare, economic opportunities, and the ability to have a child without fear of being denied lifesaving care in the event of miscarriage.
After the brunt of it passed, Representative Lisa Campbell and I headed out with Beth (one of our #TeamCastro Super Volunteers!) to knock doors in Kennesaw.
Candidate Meet & Greet Thank you to the West Cobb Islamic Center and the Georgia Muslim Voter Project for inviting me to particpate in a fun and informative candidate meet and greet.
It was wonderful to spend the afternoon with my fellow Cobb candidates, including Congressional candidate Shawn Harris and former Secretary of State candidate Adrian Consonery!
Voting together is a Castro family tradition.
Unfortunately, my oldest son is away at college and can't join us... but he will be voting via absentee ballot!
We had a new batch of large signs go out this week, with a few more still available.
We're looking for property owners and business owners within the district that can host our sign.
Get Your Campaign Swag Signs, Signs, Signs!
Thanks to our wonderful supporters in the community, our large campaign signs are beginning to pop up around District 37!
If you have property that has good visibility and would like to host one of our 4'x4' signs, please reach out to me at 203-297-4994 or Info@DarcyCastro.com.
We also have a fresh batch of yard signs, including VETERANS for Darcy Castro!
Bumper Stickers We have bumper stickers available for you to get on to LOTS of cars ASAP!
These will be like traveling yard signs!
They are available in the Campaign Pantry at 3439 Elm Creek Drive.
Donations for swag are always appreciated, but not necessary.
Reach out to info@darcycastro.com with your request!
Community Resource Highlight LEARN MORE The Zone The Zone is a safe haven of acceptance for anyone in any stage of recovery.
It is a Recovery Community Organization to support long-term recovery and re-entry.
Check out their fantastic thrift store and gift boutique, which is a fun way to support their mission!

Civic Engagement Opportunity Watching the Funds-Cobb Watching the Funds-Cobb is a powerful grassroots organization that demands transparency, accountability, oversight and fiscal responsibility from Cobb County Schools Board Members and Superintendent.

All Articles Search Republican State Representative Mark DeCaprio Announces Re-Election Bid in 48th District Gena Hamilton Feb 1 2 min read LEBANON – Republican State Representative Mark DeCaprio (48 th ) has announced he is running for re‑election in the 48th General Assembly District, which includes all of Bozrah, Colchester, Franklin, and part of Lebanon.
“We are in an affordability crisis in Connecticut,” DeCaprio said.
“Families, seniors, and small businesses are being squeezed by high taxes, high utility rates, and rising costs.
I’m running for re‑election to keep fighting for relief and to make our state more affordable for the people who live and work here.
I have worked very hard on behalf of all of our residents - it would be my honor to have that opportunity once again.” A U.S.
Navy veteran and 40‑year Lebanon resident, Mark has devoted much of his life to public service.
He and his wife, Cathy, raised their family in Lebanon, where he previously served on the Lebanon Board of Selectmen, the Zoning Board of Appeals, and the Lebanon Board of Education.
He also served as Lebanon’s Emergency Management Director, helping communities prepare for and respond to natural disasters and other crises.
At the state level, he spent many years working in emergency management and environmental protection.
In the General Assembly, DeCaprio currently serves on the Appropriations where he believes in responsible budgeting, Judiciary, Public Safety & Security and Veteran Affairs Committees.
“In Hartford, I’ve worked hard to stand up for our veterans, strengthen public safety, and push back against policies that drive up costs and utility bills,” DeCaprio said.

“If I’m honored to be re-elected, I’ll continue fighting every day for lower costs, safer communities, and a stronger future for Bozrah, Colchester, Franklin, and Lebanon.” DeCaprio is seeking re‑election to continue bringing experienced, local leadership to Hartford and to keep fighting for lower costs, safer communities, and a stronger future for the 48th District.

added: Skip to content Get Sandy's Diary in your Email Δ Legislative Session Summary Header Link Voting Rights Act | My Legislative Diary My Key Issues: Sandy's Answers to candidate questionnaires Primary Menu Why I Run About Sandy Bills I’ve Introduced 2020 Session Summary Endorsements Contact Sandy Tag: Supreme Court Waiting for the Court February 26, 2024 | by delsandy | Uncategorized | No Comments When the Supreme Court issues an opinion that requires a change in Maryland law, I often introduce a bill.
I did so this session after the court’s decision modified the standard for when a verbal threat is a criminal offense, no longer protected by the First Amendment.

Today, the nine justices heard a challenge to a Florida statute that prevents websites from permanently barring candidates for political office in the state and a Texas law that prohibits removing any content based on a user’s viewpoint.
Until the court issues its opinion, most likely in June, the state of the law is in flux.
A provision in my House Bill 333 would regulate the posting of incorrect or misleading information about election procedures, election results, or voting rights in Maryland on major web platforms.
That portion of the bill needs to be set aside until next session, when we will know the legal standard resulting from today’s case.
However, HB 333 also provides for a portal maintained by the State Board of Elections where voters can submit examples of misinformation about the above topics.
This evidence will help us build the case that we need to regulate misinformation, consistent with the state’s ability to do so.

Tags: First Amendment , Supreme Court , web platforms Gun Safety – No Longer Settled Law June 3, 2022 | by delsandy | Uncategorized | No Comments We used to have a Handgun Permit Review Board in Maryland.
Starting in 1972, if you wanted to carry, wear, or transport a handgun outside of your home, you sought a permit from the State Police.
You could appeal that decision to the Handgun Board.
In most instances, the State Police allowed individuals to carry a gun only when on the job.
Over the years, there were few reversals of those holdings, until Governor Hogan’s appointees rejected 83% of those decisions in 2018 for being too restrictive.
The next year, Delegate Atterbeary and I introduced legislation eliminating the Handgun Board.
In its place, administrative law judges now hear appeals from the decisions of the State Police.
The full-time job of these judges is to hear appeals from actions taken by state agencies.
However, this structure is in the cross hairs of the Supreme Court.
By the end of June, the court is widely expected to rule that a similar New York law violates the Second Amendment.
What should we do if that happens?
We should seek legal advice from Attorney General Brian Frosh.
What action, if any, regulating handguns can the Governor take by executive order?
When the General Assembly returns in January, what action can the new legislature and the new Governor take?
During his term in office, Governor Hogan has stated that both gun regulation and abortion are matters of settled law.
That is no longer the case. — A Celebration of Life for my Mother, Babette Hecht Rosenberg, will be held on Sunday, June 12 at 2:30 at the Har Sinai – Oheb Shalom, 7310 Park Heights Av.
You are welcome to join us.
Tags: Attorney General Brian Frosh , Gov.
Hogan , gun safety , handguns , Supreme Court January 11 – Acting Before the Supreme Court Does January 11, 2022 | by delsandy | Uncategorized | No Comments Del.

Rosenberg (D-Baltimore City), the longest-serving current member of the General Assembly, said the level of activity in any legislative session — including in election years — is often dictated by outside forces.

He observed that even though the legislature is expected to take action on abortion rights and gun control legislation this session, pending Supreme Court rulings on abortion and guns, depending on when they’re delivered, could galvanize lawmakers into more aggressive action.
“I think the circumstances are such that a lot of issues will get an airing this year and we may be addressing more than we would normally do in an election year,” Rosenberg said.
(Above is from article in MarylandMatters.org) It’s not until June that the Supreme Court usually issues its opinions in the most important and controversial cases.
Our 90-day legislative session in Annapolis ends on April 11.
Consequently, our bill drafting on abortion and guns has to anticipate what action we should require after we adjourn.
This year, those decisions will also have an effect on the state-wide elections.

Maryland General Assembly Set to Convene in Another Session Shaped by COVID Tags: abortion , guns , Supreme Court A First Time on a First Amendment Case January 28, 2021 | by delsandy | Uncategorized | No Comments I was prepared for today’s hearing, or so I thought.
The Consent of the Governed Act would severely limit the Governor’s power to act in an emergency.
I prepared a question for the bill’s sponsor, Delegate Cox, that compared his legislation to a recent Supreme Court case.
The court held that a New York regulation limiting the number of people who could attend a religious service violated the 1st Amendment protection of the free exercise of religion.
There are “less restrictive rules that could be adopted to minimize the risk to those attending religious services,” the court held.
“As I read your bill,” I asked Delegate Cox, “it would not allow for the limitations on attendance at services that the court would permit.” The delegate said I was misreading his bill.
That was mild, compared to what happened next.
Delegate Saab requested that someone’s written testimony be removed from the official record because it did not speak to the issues raised by the bill.
In my 30+ years as a legislator, I don’t recall anyone else making such a request.
As fate, and my chairman’s discretion, would have it, I was chairing today’s hearing.
I had to respond to this unique request.

“This testimony is exercising an individual’s First Amendment right to petition the government,” I replied “I suggest that you ask the Attorney General’s Office if your request is permissible.” Tags: First Amendment , Supreme Court Same thing for Supreme Court decisions May 21, 2013 | by delsandy | featured , Sandy's 2013 Legislative Diary | No Comments Society wins not only when the guilty are convicted, but when criminal trials are fair; our system of the administration of justice suffers when any accused is treated unfairly.
Douglas wrote that in the majority opinion in Brady v.

Maryland , where the Supreme Court held that the government cannot withhold evidence favorable to an accused, upon request, where the evidence is material to either guilt or punishment, regardless of the good faith or bad faith of the prosecution.
As a legislator, I know that enacting a bill isn’t the end of the process.
You have to make sure it’s correctly implemented.

Same thing for Supreme Court decisions, according to an editorial in Sunday’s New York Times. http://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/19/opinion/sunday/beyond-the-brady-rule.html Prosecutors don’t always inform a defendant’s lawyer of evidence that could be favorable to the accused.
The Brady rule has been limited by subsequent rulings of the court, and there is virtually no punishment for prosecutors who flout the rule.

A North Carolina statute requires prosecutors in felony cases, before trial, to make available to the defense “the complete files of all law enforcement agencies, investigatory agencies and prosecutors’ offices involved in the investigation of the crimes committed or the prosecution of the defendant.” Yesterday, I asked the lobbyist for the Office of the Public Defender if he was interested in pursuing a similar law in Marylam was interested in pursuing a similar law Maryland.
“We would be very interested in discussing this,” he responded.
Other lawyers will be joining us.
One of them is Clint Bamberger, my lead paint and legal adviser and mentor.
He represented John Brady before the Supreme Court fifty years ago this month.

Maryland , Supreme Court Counting, on the bench and in the House March 28, 2012 | by delsandy | Sandy's 2012 Legislative Diary , Uncategorized | No Comments At the Supreme Court today, much of the discussion dealt with what I do for a living.
The legal question was this: If the Court finds that the individual mandate is unconstitutional, what is the effect on the other provisions of the health care law?
Are all of the other parts of the law nullified?
Phrased another way, should the judiciary revise the legislation or should the Congress, which wrote it in the first place?
None of the justices has ever run for office or had to count to a number higher than five to reach a majority.
The late Justice William Brennan reportedly said that counting to five is the most important principle of constitutional law because five votes constitute a majority on the Supreme Court.
Several of the Justices spoke today of their need for a test, an objective standard that would apply to similar cases in the future.

(They also made clear their less than favorable view of the legislative process, as today’s transcript demonstrates.) In Annapolis, our guiding principles are our assessment of sound public policy and how to address the ideological and political needs of 71 members, a majority of the House of Delegates.

September 20, 2025 – Exemplary Support Score from The School District Governance Association of New Hampshire.

This score is awarded to those whose voting record exemplifies the institutions core values of: responsible governance, fiscal prudence, and academic excellence in our New Hampshire public education system.
I will always fight to ensure NH students continue to have access to some of the best educational resources in the country!
September 16, 2026 – Legislator of the Year by the New England Water Works Association (NEWWA).
This is an award for championing public policy that ensures safe drinking water for communities across the state.

May 23, 2026 – The Center for Effective Lawmaking, which is a research, education and outreach initiative between Vanderbilt University and the Frank Batten School of Leadership and Public Policy at the University of Virginia ranked NH Senator Denise Ricciardi as one of the most effective Republican representatives during the last legislative session of 2023-2024.
Ricciardi was invited to participate in a national policy roundtable hosted by the U.S.
Administration for Children and Families (ACF) in Washington, D.C.
October 16, 2024 – Legislator of the Year Award from the NH Retail Association.
September 22, 2024 – Granite State Rural Water Association Advocate Annual Award.
April 19, 2024 – Disability Justice Champion Award from ABLE NH.
March 11, 2024 – The NH Water Pollution Control Association “Water Policy Champion” of 2024.
November 4, 2023 – Commended by the BIA as one of 9 Policy Leaders in recognition of her commitment to pro-economic growth policies and solutions during the 2023 session.
October 18, 2023 – New Futures Legislator of the Year Award for support of children and families across the Grante State.
July 12, 2023 – The Council of State Governments has announced that New Hampshire State Senator Denise Ricciardi has been selected to participate in the 2023 CSG Henry Toll Fellowship.

Bringing together 47 individuals representing 29 of the states and U.S. territories and from all branches of state government, the Henry Toll Fellowship is the nation’s premier leadership development program for state government officials.

February 18, 2023 – Legislative Champion Award from the New Hampshire Food Access Coalition on February 10, 2023 December 15, 2021 – Americans for Prosperity New Hampshire’s “Ebenezer Mudgett Champion of Freedom Award” winner for 2021.

All Posts Latest Political News Culture and Opinions Events Your Community Vaccines & Health Search DiPietro: ‘No-Vote’ on Majority’s Omnibus Corrections Bill David Dipietro Jun 12, 2025 2 min read Omnibus bill A.8871 fails to address main causes of strikes In response to the Majority’s passage of a sweeping omnibus bill on correction reform, Assemblyman David DiPietro (R,C-East Aurora) issued his criticism, calling the legislation “a blatant failure to address the very issues that forced thousands of correctional officers to risk their livelihoods and walk off the job.” The bill comes in the wake of the largest correctional officer strike New York State has seen in decades.

But according to DiPietro, the legislation does nothing to correct the underlying problems that drove the strike to begin with: the dangerous consequences of the HALT Act and the inhumane practice of mandatory overtime that has left correction officers overworked, underappreciated and unheard.
“This bill is window dressing, plain and simple.
The governor and the Majority are pretending to solve a problem they still don’t understand because they never listened in the first place.

The officers walked out in desperation, begging the state to address mandatory triple shifts, being denied sick and vacation time and the devastating impact this job is having on their families and mental health.
Instead of compassion or reform, they got punishment." “The governor’s executive order blacklisting officers from state employment was vindictive, authoritarian and disgraceful.
Terminating 2,000 officers didn’t solve the crisis, it escalated it.
And now, this so-called reform package completely ignores their pleas for help.
There are no OT protections, no staffing mandates and no HALT Act reforms." “If you want safe prisons, you need to start by treating our officers like human beings.
The Majority failed these men and women.

I stand with the officers, those who are still serving and those this state cast aside.” DiPietro vowed to continue fighting for correctional officers and pushing for real reform that includes a repeal of the HALT Act, mandatory overtime protections, mental health support and restoration of employment opportunities for wrongfully terminated officers.
Assemblyman David DiPietro represents the 147th Assembly District, which includes parts of Erie and Wyoming counties.

David Dipietro Dec 12, 2025 1 min read This Isn’t Enough — And New Yorkers Deserve the Truth As the Ranking Minority Member on the Assembly Corrections Committee, I’ve reviewed the prison package now sitting on the Governor’s desk.
After reading the coverage here , I need to set the record straight — because what’s being presented to the public is simply not enough, and in some cases, flat-out misleading.

This bill does nothing to address the real crisis inside our prisons: • chronic understaffing • Zero recruitment efforts • forced overtime • escalating assaults • unsafe conditions for officers and incarcerated individuals • and the complete lack of meaningful reforms recommended by the state’s own corrections experts Albany can pat itself on the back for passing another “transparency” bill, and parts of the bill are good, but transparency without action is just political theater.
New Yorkers deserve genuine reform — not a headline.
I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: if we don’t fix staffing, safety, and the day-to-day realities inside our facilities, we are not solving anything.
This package ignores the root problems, and pretending otherwise does a disservice to the men and women who keep our prisons operating.
Bottom line: This isn’t reform.
It’s a distraction.

And I’ll keep fighting for real solutions that protect our officers, improve safety, and bring honesty back to our corrections system. — Assemblyman David DiPietro Ranking Minority Member, NYS Assembly Corrections Committee Tags: New York Assembly Albany Hochul corrections DiPietro prison officers Culture and Opinions Latest Political News Recent Posts See All DiPietro Blasts Hochul for Shielding Criminals and Ignoring Victims DiPietro: ‘No-Vote’ on Majority’s Omnibus Corrections Bill Hochul’s Budget Betrays Western New York’s Correctional Officers Donations by mail can be sent to: DiPietro For You PO Box 700, E.
