title.after: On to the General!

added: Double check your “load all images” fIlter above) On to the General!
As summer winds down, we’re ramping up for the general election.
While I am eager to begin drafting policy and building relationships with fellow legislators, I still have another election to win.
We are going to do that the same way we have built this campaign from the beginning: by talking directly with people.
We are hosting town halls, knocking doors, and expandinf our peer-to-peer outreach across the district.
Most importantly, we will stay focused on what I hear again and again from the people I meet: we want Montana to be a place where our families can thrive.

That means making it easier to afford a home, supporting strong public schools, protecting access to healthcare and clean water, defending our freedoms, and building an economy that works for people who live and work here.
I’m grateful to have the support of my primary opponent, Dana Toole.
Dana has spent decades serving Montana and knows as well as anyone that if we want to make progress, we have to work together.
I’m proud that after a competitive primary, we are coming together around the work ahead.
Support MaryAnn Dunwell for Senate District 42!
In addition to keeping SD 41 blue, there are three very important races to support this cycle so that we can keep and possibly grow our voting block in the Montana Senate.
Remember, it was 18 Democrats in the Montana Senate that renewed Medicaid, protected our impartial courts, and more.
MaryAnn Dunwell cast a critical vote on all of our accomplishments.
We need her to return and she needs our help!
As a result of redistricting, SD 42 has a very close margin.
We need MaryAnn and she needs our support.
I hope you will donate , volunteer, and reach out to her campaign to offer your support in whatever way that you can.
Rob and I are personally pitching in monthly so MaryAnn can count on our support as she makes critical campaign decisions.
Two other close races to track are Scott Rosenzweig , (SD 29- Park & Gallatin Counties) and Margaret Mitchell (SD 10- Great Falls).
We have the chance to turn 18 votes into 20 and keep bringing balance and compromise to the Montana State Senate.
What We're Doing… Defining the Campaign Platform This June the Montana Democratic Party met to discuss their platform priorities for 2026.
You can find the updated platform HERE .

Building on the work of the Montana Democratic Party, this campaign is putting forward the first draft of the THRIVE Platform, which is a focused list of priorities shaped by what I am hearing from constituents, the issues I anticipate will come before the 2027 Legislature, and initiatves that I can confidently champion as a Senator for SD 41.
This is a starting point and I look forward to hearing your feedback and continuing to refine a vision for a Montana where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

Save the Date for Let’s Talk About It Town Hall Series Thursday, October 15th, East Helena Firehall, 6:00p Sunday, October 18th Lewis & Clark Library, 3:00p Wednesday, October 28th, Plymouth Congregational Church, 6:00p What We’re Cooking… Rhubarb Shrub Despite the smoke and the heat, the garden rhubarb is still thriving!
After tarts, squares, pies, and of course, tucking some into the freezer for February, I’m still finding delicious ways to use it.
This rhubarb shrub is lovely mixed with club soda, sparkling wine, or your favorite cocktail.
It pairs perfectly with the joys of summer’s dog days, especially when they’re accompanied by the crisp, clean air the rain brought us this week.
The primary is behind us, but the work ahead is just as important.
We need to purchase more yard signs, pay for digital ads that share our values and priorities in our own words, and support the local organizations that are hosting our town hall conversations.
If you're able to chip in $10, $25, or whatever feels right, it goes straight into reaching voters across SD41 this Fall.
Have other ideas on how to help?
Reach out anytime or simply respond to this email.
Erin Donate Checks can also be made out directly to: Erin 4 Montana, P.O.

added.text: Thank you @Meriwest for answering my dream!! 🏡Cong [image: Thank you @Meriwest for answering my dream!! 🏡Congrats to Meriwest Credit Union on launching its new HomeFast ADU Loan, an innovative financing solution designed to help homeowners build Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs)! ADUs are an important part of addressing California’s housing shortage. They create more affordable housing opportunities, provide space for aging parents or adult children, generate potential rental income, and help families build generational wealth. I applaud Meriwest Credit Union for supporting creative financing solutions that can help more Californians turn their backyards into opportunities! Meriwest’s program, introduced in 2025, offers loans starting at $25,000, with a 25-year fixed term and interest-only payments during the first 12 months, subject to approval. Learn more: https://www.meriwest.com/loans/homefast-adu-loan #MeriwestCreditUnion #HomeFast #ADU #AffordableHousing #HousingSolutions #CaliforniaDream #Homeownership #MultigenerationalLiving #CaliforniaHousing]

“She’s a hard worker and she does it for the right [image: “She’s a hard worker and she does it for the right reason.” Thank you so much, State Senator Laura Richardson of the 35th District, for your incredible endorsement and trust! Having leaders who understand government inside and out and who truly care about the people, is what this campaign is all about. Let’s keep working for California! #FionaMa #vote #California #TeamWork]

🎨 Thank you Carlos Benitez, Founder and Creative D [image: 🎨 Thank you Carlos Benitez, Founder and Creative Director of ACCA (Artists Corner Contemporary Art) in Beverly Hills for your endorsement. 🙏 An art dealer, collector, inventor, and entrepreneur, Carlos founded ACCA in 2012 and has helped showcase extraordinary contemporary art and emerging talent through exhibitions in California and beyond. Through ACCA Gallery and ACCA Journal, he is bringing together art, fashion, culture, and media while creating opportunities for artists to share their creativity with the world. 🌎 California’s creative economy is powered by visionaries like Carlos who remind us that art isn’t just beautiful…it inspires, connects, and creates opportunity! 🎨 accaart.com #CarlosBenitez #ACCABeverlyHills #ACCAJournal #SupportTheArts #CreativeEconomy #BeverlyHills #CaliforniaArtists #ArtAndInnovation #ContemporaryArt]

🏭 Made in California! Built for the Future! 🇺🇸 Yes [image: 🏭 Made in California! Built for the Future! 🇺🇸 Yesterday, my California State Treasurer’s Office hosted our 2nd Annual California Creates: Golden State Manufacturing Forum at Aggie Square in Sacramento! California is home to more than 45,000 manufacturing businesses, supporting 1.24 million jobs and generating $382 BILLION in annual economic output! We brought together manufacturers, innovators, policymakers, and financial experts to discuss access to capital, cutting red tape, workforce development, AI, biotechnology, and growing California’s creative economy. I especially enjoyed our fireside chat highlighting women shaping the future of manufacturing! Our goal: Help businesses start, grow, innovate, and create more good-paying jobs right here in California! Let’s keep making things in California! 💪 #MadeInCalifornia #CaliforniaCreates #Manufacturing #Innovation #SmallBusiness #EconomicDevelopment #GoodJobs #WomenInManufacturing #California @caltreasurer @camanufacturers @khaimmorton @rachell_reinwald @sarecycling @sacstate]

removed.text: A one-of-a-kind California collaboration! Gary Bal [image: A one-of-a-kind California collaboration! Gary Ballen and Helane Freeman bring music and visual art together as Rhythm & Hues. Gary sings and plays guitar while Helane sings, plays percussion and paints with her hands—creating a live performance you have to see to believe. Their story is a reminder that creativity can take shape in unexpected ways. Catch Rhythm & Hues bringing art and music to life across Ventura County! https://wearerhythmandhues.com #RhythmAndHues #GaryBallen #HelaneFreeman #CaliforniaArtists #LiveMusic #ArtAndMusic #VenturaCounty #CreativeCalifornia]

Celebrating National Savings Day with my new inter [image: Celebrating National Savings Day with my new interns! #piggybanksarefull #fionama #calkids #nevertoolatetosave #scholarshare529 @calkidsprogram @scholarshare529 @caltreasurer]

Happy National Farmers Day! 🌾 Today, we celebrate [image: Happy National Farmers Day! 🌾 Today, we celebrate the farmers and ranchers whose hard work produces the food that sustains and nourishes us. There is no culture without agriculture! #NationalFarmersDay #ThankAFarmer #ThankARancher #CaliforniaAgriculture #NoCultureWithoutAgriculture @cafarmbureau @sanfranciscofarmbureau]

Thank you to Saratoga City Councilmember Yan Zhao [image: Thank you to Saratoga City Councilmember Yan Zhao for bringing together members of local clubs to support me for Lt Governor this Nov 3rd. I enjoyed our fireside chat with Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen who asked very thoughtful questions. Just 23 more days until Election Day! Please remember to sign and date the back of your ballot envelope and return it to an official ballot drop box—not the U.S. Mail. Thank you! #ElectionDay #vote @sccpubliceddems @yanzhao.ca @jdcbayarea @gilbertswong @gkremen @gary_kremen_4_u]

Call 651-266-2171 Ramsey County Elections Find My Polling Place Early Voting Locations & Hours Check My Registration What I Stand For Fighting for the East Side ★ Community Leadership Nearly a decade on the District 2 Community Council and years of volunteer service before ever running for office.
Foung listens first, then brings Eastsiders’ voices to the Capitol.
Economic Opportunity Chief author of the Getting to Work program, which offers job training and reliable transportation to work.
Foung also champions The Heights, a project that will bring new jobs and housing to the East Side.
Livable Neighborhoods Safe, healthy, green neighborhoods: renovated libraries and parks, a new community health center, gun violence prevention, and clean air and water for our kids.
A Message from Foung Dear Eastsiders, I arrived at the Capitol this year under extraordinary circumstances.
Federal enforcement was targeting immigrants and communities of color, and three Minnesotans were killed.
Gun violence had taken the lives of children and elected officials.
Rising costs were pushing families to the edge.
I led the charge to help Minnesotans through these challenges.
We passed $40 million in rental assistance , I advocated for gun violence prevention, and my office connected neighbors with housing support and other resources.
Our district, and your voices, guide my work every day.
It is a privilege to work alongside you and uplift your stories at the Capitol.

He went on to earn degrees from the University of Kansas and the Rochester Institute of Technology.
After that he worked as a computer programmer, a series producer at Twin Cities Public Television, and IT manager for the Minnesota Council of Nonprofits.

He also served on a watershed advisory board.
He speaks 5 languages, including Hmong, Lao, Thai, and Chinese.
Hobby includes fishing, canoeing and gardening.

Paul, MN 55106 info@founghawj.com (651) 592-3129 Prepared and paid for by Foung for Senate 67 Committee Minnesota state senator of district 67 Foung Hawj Home Background Donation Supporters Contact Us When I left my home country of Laos over four decades ago for a new life in America, I could never have imagined I could one day be elected to public office.
I have worked hard all my life, achieved bachelors and masters degrees, started my professional career as a computer programmer and later was able to start my own multimedia production company.
I became interested in public service through my years of volunteering, working with many different groups to improve my community.
As I told my senate colleagues on that first day in 2013, I was new to politics, though I was not new to helping people.
Moving from a war-torn Laos to urban America, I have experienced much adversity and overcame many obstacles.
This has given me a great appreciation for the struggles people go through and also a boundless optimism about what is possible when we work together.
This is why I look forward to the challenges in this chapter of my life.
I will serve the office of Minnesota State Senator to the best of my ability.
As an American of Hmong descent and as your State Senator, I could not be more appreciative and thankful for your support and trust.
We are neighbors, one community, and what we do together improves the lives of everyone.

Paul’s District 2 Council 2004-2010 • Vice-president, Lake Phalen Townhome Association - served 2 terms • Helped refugees in Thailand through UNHCR 1996 RECOGNITIONS • State Legislative Leaders Foundation: Emerging Leaders Program 2015 • BILLD Fellowship 2014 • Snow and Ice Control Best Practices Certificate from MPCA 2012 • Department of Agriculture's Merit for Engaging Urban America 2011 • Confined Space Training 2009 • Bush Leadership Fellows 1998 LANGUAGES: English, Hmong, Lao, Thai, some Chinese and basic ASL HOBBIES: Gardening, Fishing, Camping, Canoeing and more outdoor activities.

added: Skip to content ★ Re-Elect Foung Hawj · Early voting open now · Vote early → Campaign: (651) 592-3129 · info@founghawj.com FOUNG HAWJ MN State Senate ☰ Home About Results Vote Photo Gallery Endorsements Get Involved Contact Donate ★ 2026 Legislative Session ★ Results for District 67 What Senator Hawj delivered for the East Side and for all Minnesotans.
A Message from Foung Dear Eastsiders, I arrived at the Capitol this year under extraordinary circumstances.
Federal enforcement was targeting immigrants and communities of color, and three Minnesotans were killed.
Gun violence had taken the lives of children and elected officials.
Rising costs were pushing families to the edge.
I led the charge to help Minnesotans through these challenges.
We passed $40 million in rental assistance , I advocated for gun violence prevention, and my office connected neighbors with housing support and other resources.
Our district, and your voices, guide my work every day.
It is a privilege to work alongside you and uplift your stories at the Capitol.

Foung Hawj $ #M in rental assistance for families destabilized this winter $ #M for 50 habitat, wetland, forest & prairie projects $ #M for #+ outdoor recreation, education & conservation projects $ #M in community grants for smaller local organizations Delivering for You 2026 Highlights ★ District Successes PROCEED Community Health Center Groundbreaking, May 2026 Sunisa Lee Mural, $500,000 Coming soon The Heights Development 20 acres of housing, light-industrial jobs & green space Wakan Tipi Center Grand opening, June 2026 Hayden Heights Library renovation DNR St.
Paul Fish Hatchery renovation Jobs, Workers & Families Getting to Work program Chief author.

Crossbows now allowed in archery season for all ages Infectious waste study $125,000 to keep unsafe waste out of local facilities DNR electronic licensing Buy and carry hunting and fishing licenses on your phone Minnesota Regional Parks & Trails Environment & Natural Resources Protecting Minnesota's outdoors $102 million for 100+ outdoor recreation, education, and conservation projects via the Environment & Natural Resources Trust Fund. $30 million for ENRTF Community Grants, plus guidance to help smaller organizations spend state funds. $190 million for 50 Outdoor Heritage Fund projects that protect, enhance and restore habitats, wetlands, forests and prairies. $3.5 million for metro-area and larger-city projects, and $3 million for first-time applicants, through Conservation Partners Legacy Grants.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE About Teresa Fox Not a Career Politician.
A Proven Leader.
A Hands-On Public Servant Teresa Fox is not a career politician.

She is a hands-on safety professional, emergency manager, and public servant who has spent her life protecting workers, strengthening institutions, and standing shoulder to shoulder with the people who build and power Washington.
From shipyards and naval bases to fish processing vessels in the Bering Sea, Teresa Fox has led in high risk, high accountability environments where results matter and excuses do not.

Two Decades of Leadership Naval Safety Operations Seven years overseeing safety operations for the Naval Inactive Ships Maintenance Office in Bremerton Maritime Leadership Environmental, Health, Safety and Emergency Manager aboard a 380-foot fish processing vessel with a 232-member crew in Alaska waters Industrial Safety Leadership roles at Olympic College and Washington State Department of Labor and Industries, supervising teams and reducing accident rates Support the Campaign Help Teresa Fox bring practical leadership and real-world experience to Washington's 6th District.
DONATE NOW Stay Informed Get updates on the campaign and learn how you can help bring real leadership to Congress.

SUBSCRIBE Experience That Matters At Puget Sound Naval Shipyard Building on a proud tradition of service Leading in High-Risk Environments Where results matter and excuses do not Credentials Earned Through Experience Secret Security Clearance and numerous federal safety and emergency management certifications Former Kitsap County Fire Marshal's Office inspector conducting fire inspections and enforcing safety codes Supervised teams of welders, mechanics, riggers, inspectors, and public employees Completed college degree while continuing professional advancement, demonstrating commitment to lifelong learning What Teresa Fox Stands For Working Families Understands working families because she has lived that life Public Safety Respects and supports our first responders and safety professionals Industry & Jobs Supports timber, maritime jobs, and industrial workers Military Communities Protects and advocates for our military families and installations Practical Solutions Focuses on results instead of ideological agendas Community Service Running to work for hardworking people, not to build a political brand A Legacy of Service The Fox name has been around cars and racing in the PNW and Kitsap County for decades.
Teresa Fox's grandfather started Fox Auto Electric in downtown Bremerton, and her uncles Jim and Leon owned Fox Motors.
Her dad ran Tom Fox Automotive, and Uncle Bobby operated his own repair business as well.
The Fox brothers were later inducted into the Kitsap Sports Hall of Fame as the first family of racing in Kitsap County.
"But more important than trophies or race wins was how they treated people." When military families downtown could not afford repairs, they fixed cars anyway.
When customers struggled with payments, they worked with them.
When the community needed sponsorship dollars, they stepped up.
That spirit of work hard, give back, and take care of your neighbors is the legacy Teresa Fox carries forward.
Ready to Go to Work for the 6th District Teresa Fox isn't running to build a national political brand.
She's running to work for the hardworking people of the 6th Congressional District.

October 11, 2026 Campaign Staff Communism, Socialism & the Consequences for America Sunday, October 11, 2026 | 2:00–5:00 PM Gig Harbor Vintage Aero Museum | Gig Harbor, Washington Teresa Fox for U.S.
Congress, WA-06, invites you to join us for a special afternoon gathering focused on Communism, Socialism & the Consequences for America.
This event will bring together powerful voices, firsthand experiences, and important perspectives for a meaningful discussion about freedom, government, history, and the choices facing our country.

Featured Speakers Agnes Gibboney , Angel Mom Founder, Angel Families of America Cezar-Victor Nastase Alliance for the Union of Romanians Jim Walsh Chairman, Washington State Republican Party Presenting a special “State of the States” address Teresa Fox Candidate for U.S.
Congress, WA-06 Teresa will share her personal connection to communism and why the lessons of history remain relevant to the choices Americans face today.
Master of Ceremonies David McMullan will serve as Master of Ceremonies for the afternoon.
Guests are invited to attend, listen, engage, and be part of this important conversation in one of Gig Harbor’s most distinctive settings.
Event Details Date: Sunday, October 11, 2026 Time: 2:00–5:00 PM Location: Gig Harbor Vintage Aero Museum Hosted by: Teresa Fox for U.S.
Congress, WA-06 Donation is not required to attend.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Campaign Update Teresa Fox at the Puget Sound Patriots Picnic: We Have Not Yet Begun to Fight At the Puget Sound Patriots Picnic, Teresa Fox delivered a powerful message on patriotism, sacrifice, liberty, and the responsibility every generation bears to preserve the Republic.

August 15, 2026 Campaign Staff Teresa Fox was honored to speak this afternoon at the Puget Sound Patriots Picnic , joining community members, constitutional conservatives, and longtime supporters connected through the Bremerton Kitsap Rifle and Revolver Club.
In her remarks, Teresa spoke about the ordinary Americans who built this country, defended it, and handed its freedoms forward through courage and sacrifice.

She described herself as a strict constitutionalist, a strong Second Amendment supporter, a lifelong supporter of veterans, and a candidate focused on public safety, lowering government waste, and providing adequate representation across all six counties of Washington’s 6th Congressional District.
Teresa also made clear that she sees a stark choice before voters this November.
“I am the contrast.” For Teresa, that contrast begins with public safety and constitutional rights.
“Public safety, both foreign and domestic, is the number one priority of government under the U.S.
Constitution, period.

Protection of individual rights is number one in the Washington Constitution.” She pledged to listen to the people she seeks to represent and told the crowd: “I will listen to you and will do everything I can to restore our right to keep and bear arms.” But Teresa’s message reached beyond any single issue.
She spoke about the generations of Americans who came before us, ordinary people who answered extraordinary calls, sacrificed for liberty, and left future generations a Republic worth preserving.

Referencing John Paul Jones, Teresa recalled: “When John Paul Jones was in the heat of battle in close quarters and asked to surrender, he said, ‘We have not yet begun to fight.’” She continued: “We owe our very lives and freedoms to those ordinary men.
They shed blood so that we may be free today.” The fight facing Americans today, Teresa said, is different.
“Today we must fight, not a revolution of musket and cannon, but of ideas and renewed effort.
Today we must do our part to keep the Republic.” That message presents voters in Washington’s 6th Congressional District with a clear contrast.

While Congresswoman Emily Randall has publicly celebrated support from activist organizations, including endorsements from Indivisible groups, Teresa Fox spent the afternoon standing with Puget Sound Patriots and speaking directly to citizens committed to constitutional liberty, individual rights, limited government, public safety, and preserving the freedoms generations of Americans sacrificed to secure.
Teresa summarized that choice in some of the strongest words of her speech: “This election is not a contract with America, this election is a contrast FOR America.
And the contrast could not be more clear.
Law and order or chaos on the streets.
It’s our choice in November.” Her campaign, she told the crowd, is a campaign for the people, with People over Politics as a cornerstone.
Teresa also spoke about the energy she sees beyond political models and conventional predictions.
“A lot of great patriots in this room, a lot in Oly.
I want to do great things in Washington, D.C.” And as she looked toward the future, Teresa returned to the responsibility inherited from those who founded and defended this nation.
“Together we can give our dear America a 500th birthday.
We are ordinary men, as our founding fathers were ordinary.
We here today come from that stock.” Her closing words captured the spirit of the afternoon: “We are blessed to live in the greatest country ever born.
A beacon of shining light and hope to the rest of the world.” The contrast Teresa presented is one voters will decide for themselves in November: Law and order or chaos on the streets.
People over Politics.
A campaign for the people.
A Republic worth preserving.
“May we be forever free.
God bless America.” Back to all articles Show Your Support Get your official Fox for Congress yard sign and put it proudly on display.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Press Release Teresa Fox Announces Congressional Campaign Kickoff On April 19, Teresa Fox, local occupational safety professional and emergency manager, will officially launch her campaign for Congress in Washington State’s 6th Congressional District.

April 13, 2026 Campaign Staff FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE April 13, 2026 info@foxforwa.com foxforwa.com Teresa Fox Announces Congressional Campaign Kickoff Public Event for District 6 Featuring Dave Reichert in Bremerton Bremerton, WA - On Apirl 19, Teresa Fox, local occupational safety professional and emergency manager, will officially launch her campaign for Congress in Washington State’s 6th Congressional District.
The kickoff event will be held at the Kitsap Golf & Country Club at 2pm.

Teresa Fox will be joined by former Sheriff and Congressman Dave Reichert and current Washington State Republican Party Chair Jim Walsh to outline a vision for the district that places the priorities of working families over divisive ideological activism.

“While our communities are working hard to keep shipyards operating, timber moving, and small businesses alive, our current representative has been focused on building a national political brand and aligning herself with the most extreme faction of Congress,” Fox said.

“The people of the district deserve better than a member of Congress who spends more time chasing national headlines than fighting for the industries that sustain our communities.” Event Details What: Teresa Fox Congressional Campaign Kickoff When: April 19, 2026, 2pm Where: 3885 NW Golf Club Hill Rd, Bremerton, WA 98312 Who: Teresa Fox, Dave Reichert, Jim Walsh, and community supporters Since filing for candidacy in March, Teresa Fox has already garnered an early endorsement from the Kitsap County Republican Party.

The kickoff marks the transition into the next phase of the grassroots powered campaign aimed at bringing responsibility, accountability, and true representation back to the 6th Congressional District.
Members of the press are invited to attend.
Teresa Fox will be available for brief interviews immediately following speaking events.
About Teresa Fox: Fox enters the race with more than two decades of experience leading safety and emergency management programs in maritime, industrial, and government settings.
She has worked in shipyards, naval facilities, and offshore operations where the stakes are high and leadership requires accountability.

Her career includes seven years overseeing environmental and safety operations for the Naval Inactive Ships Maintenance Office in Bremerton, leadership roles at Olympic College and the Washington State Department of Labor and Industries, and service as Environmental, Health, Safety and Emergency Manager aboard a 380-foot fish processing vessel in the Gulf of Alaska responsible for the safety and medical readiness of a 232-member crew.
Fox said her decision to run was driven by frustration that Washington’s 6th District has lost its voice in Congress.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Campaign Update Teresa Fox Takes Her Case Directly to Northwest Detention Center Protesters Teresa Fox went directly to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, engaging protesters face-to-face and drawing a sharp contrast with Rep.
Emily Randall over immigration, public safety and the role of a congressional representative.
August 14, 2026 Campaign Staff WA-06 challenger engages activists face-to-face as sharp contrast with Rep.

Emily Randall emerges over immigration, public safety and the role of a congressional representative TACOMA, Wash. — Teresa Fox, candidate for Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District, went directly to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma to do something increasingly rare in American politics: walk into a crowd that did not agree with her, ask questions, listen to the answers and explain exactly how she believes a member of Congress should make decisions.
The resulting exchange presents a striking contrast between Fox and incumbent Rep.
Emily Randall over immigration enforcement, political rhetoric and what it means to represent Washington’s 6th District.

Randall has made the Northwest Detention Center a recurring focus of her tenure in Congress, visiting the facility 9 times in her first term and publicly accusing the Trump administration of waging a “war on brown people” and calling ICE agents “masked murderers.” Fox arrived with a different question: What do the people gathered there actually want Congress to do?
“As your representative, it’s going to be my job to represent all of the voices in our district,” Fox says at the beginning of the video .

“I want to hear what they have to say, if they have any proposed legislation.” Fox also made clear that she wanted the conversation to include something she believes is too often missing from the national immigration debate: crime victims.
And the experience of families and communities whose loved ones have been victims of preventable crimes committed by criminals in the country illegally.
She then walked into the demonstration.
Rather than delivering remarks from a distance, Fox approached activists and introduced herself as a candidate for the United States House of Representatives.
“I’m running for Congress, and I want to hear what you have to say,” Fox told members of the group.
“What’s your objective?” When protesters described alleged conditions inside the detention facility, Fox did not end the conversation.
She asked them what they wanted their congressional representative to do.
“What kind of legislation would you propose?” Fox asked.
“What kind of changes would you like to actually see?
I was elected, what could I do in office?” That exchange quickly became more confrontational.
Fox stuck with it even as a man with plate armor marched confrontationally toward her team, and then circled her team menacingly.
Some demonstrators compared the detention facility to a concentration camp.
One participant invoked the Holocaust.
Others repeatedly pressed Fox to declare whether she personally believed the facility should exist and challenged her when she declined to answer the question on their terms.
Fox instead returned to the principle she says is a cornerstone of her campaign.
“Here’s the deal, and this is a cornerstone of my campaign,” Fox said.
“I’m going to represent the people.” She then described the standard she says will guide her in Congress: “Number one, I’m going to do what’s legal under the Constitution.
And number two, I’m going to represent the majority of the voices in our district.

That’s my job.” When activists continued pressing Fox for her personal opinion, she rejected the idea that the personal preferences of a member of Congress should override the people that member was elected to represent.
“My personal opinion is absolutely zero in this,” Fox said.
“I have no dog in the fight.

Because I’m supposed to represent the citizens of my district.” She repeated the point moments later: “What the majority of people in our district want to do is what I’m going to do.” The encounter underscores a fundamental difference emerging in the race for Washington’s 6th Congressional District.
Randall has repeatedly used her congressional office to obstruct federal immigration enforcement and scrutinize conditions at federal facilities across the country.
Randall recently stated she has been to the Tacoma facility nine times while she fanned the flames of violent political rhetoric.
Randall calls for the abolishment of ICE and accuses immigration authorities of targeting people based on the color of their skin.
Fox is presenting voters with a very different conception of the job.
Her message at the detention center was not that a member of Congress should arrive with all the answers already decided.
It was that a representative should ask questions, listen to competing voices, stay within the Constitution and ultimately represent the citizens of the District.
The differences were visible in real time.
Fox asked the activists where they were from.
All in the group were from Oregon.
One protestor described the demonstration as an expression of solidarity across the Pacific Northwest.
Fox continued the conversation anyway.
“I’m crossing the aisles,” Fox said during the encounter.
“My platform is people over politics.
I’m here to represent the citizens in my district.
And I want to hear the voices of everybody.” Even as the discussion became increasingly hostile, Fox continued answering questions and asking for specific policy proposals.
Near the end of the exchange, protesters again demanded that she take their position on the detention facility.
Fox gave them the same answer.
“As a representative in the federal Congress, I am going to do what’s legal under the Constitution, first and foremost.” That may be the clearest distinction in the race.
One candidate has characterized current immigration enforcement in sweeping terms involving race, fascism and a war against immigrant communities.

The other walked directly into a protest, asked what people wanted their government to do, listened while they challenged her and refused to substitute political pressure for the obligations she believes come with representative government.
For Fox, the contrast between the Fox for Washington Campaign for the People and the incumbent could not be more clear.
Law and order, with justice for victims or chaos on the streets.
The choice is yours in November.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News In the News Washington State Republican Party Endorses Teresa Fox for Congress The Washington State Republican Party has endorsed Teresa Fox for Congress in Washington’s 6th District, building on support from all six county Republican parties.
August 16, 2026 Campaign Staff The Washington State Republican Party has endorsed Teresa Fox for U.S.
Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District , adding statewide Republican support to a campaign already backed by Republican organizations across all six counties of the district.

The endorsement marks another important step forward for the Fox for Washington campaign as it enters the general election and continues building support across Clallam, Grays Harbor, Jefferson, Kitsap, Mason, and Pierce counties.
Teresa has already earned the support of the Republican Party organizations in all six counties that make up Washington’s 6th Congressional District.
The Washington State Republican Party endorsement now adds the support of the state party as Teresa takes her campaign directly to voters throughout the district.
“I am deeply grateful for the support of Republicans across this district and now from the Washington State Republican Party,” Teresa said.

“This campaign has always been about the people we represent, the communities we serve, and making sure their voices are heard in Washington, D.C.” The endorsement comes as Teresa continues emphasizing public safety, constitutional rights, responsible government, strong representation for all six counties, and a campaign centered on People over Politics .

Her message throughout the district has been consistent: Washington’s 6th Congressional District deserves a representative who will listen to its communities, defend individual liberty, and put the people of the district ahead of political interests.
The growing Republican support also reflects the campaign’s expanding organization heading into the general election.
Six counties.
One district.
A campaign for the people.

Teresa Fox and the Fox for Washington campaign are grateful for the confidence placed in her by Republican leaders and organizations throughout Washington and look forward to carrying that momentum into November.
About Teresa Fox Teresa Fox is the Republican candidate for U.S.
Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District, representing Clallam, Grays Harbor, Jefferson, Kitsap, Mason, and portions of Pierce County.
Learn more about Teresa, her campaign, and upcoming events at foxforwa.com .

added: Counterfeit pills made to look like real prescriptions, some laced with fentanyl, are reaching our young people, and opioid deaths in South Dakota went up last year.
Teach kids the facts about opioids.

Make sure every public school student, at least once between 6th and 12th grade, learns how addiction develops, how to recognize and respond to an overdose, where to find treatment, and why counterfeit pills are so dangerous.

Set clear statewide rules for license plate readers so data is used only for active criminal investigations, deleted on a firm deadline, and protected with real privacy accountability. ✅Progress So Far Publicly supported the new prison proposal in Sioux Falls with contract caps and accountability to control costs.
Backed legislation to impose stronger penalties on repeat violent offenders . 💡Why This Matters Public safety is government’s first responsibility.
A modern prison protects citizens, keeps staff safe, and saves money long term.
State health officials found that in more than 60% of overdose deaths, someone had a chance to step in and save a life.
When a student knows what an overdose looks like and what to do, a friend can live.
License plate readers have helped solve real crimes, including finding a 9-year-old girl abducted in Clark County in 2023.
But South Dakota has no state law on how that data is used, how long it’s kept, or who can see it.

I’ll work with Attorney General Jackley to set real limits: legitimate investigations only, a deletion deadline, a warrant for anything beyond a short window, and consequences if the rules are broken.
Public safety and privacy aren’t opposites.

removed: Set clear, tight statewide rules for license plate reader (ALPR) technology — data used only for active criminal investigations, a hard deadline to delete footage and real accountability about privacy. ✅Progress So Far Publicly supported the new prison proposal in Sioux Falls with contract caps and accountability to control costs.
Backed legislation to impose stronger penalties on repeat violent offenders . 💡Why This Matters Public safety is government's first responsibility.
A modern prison protects citizens, ensures staff safety, and saves money long term.
This isn't just about new walls, it's about protecting lives and defending South Dakota's future.
Automatic license plate readers have helped solve real crimes, including a case right here in District 4.
In 2023, this technology helped find a 9-year-old girl abducted in Clark County.
Just this September, it helped Highway Patrol troopers locate a suspect vehicle near Plankinton within an hour of being notified, leading to the safe recovery of an abducted 15-year-old girl.
That matters.
If we eliminate them instead of regulate them, what do we say to the families of these children?
I have very real privacy concerns.
South Dakota currently has no state law governing how this data is used, how long it's kept, or who can access it.

This isn't hypothetical: nationally, officers have been fired and arrested for using this exact technology to track ex-partners, and agencies have shared this data for immigration cases that have nothing to do with why the public was told these cameras existed.

Courts are already weighing in, with a federal judge in a Norfolk, Virginia case finding that networked plate-reader searches could raise the same concerns the Supreme Court flagged in a case where extended location tracking was found to require a warrant.
That's the gap South Dakota law needs to close before it becomes our story too.

As Attorney General Jackley develops statewide ALPR legislation, I'll work with him to ensure there are real limits, such as legitimate investigations only, a deletion deadline, a warrant requirement for anything beyond a short window, and accountability if the rules are broken.
Public safety and privacy aren't opposites.

added: Meet Andrew Issues Endorsements News Contribute Policy Information Privacy is important to us.
Welcome to the official website of Fudge 4 Oregon.
We understand that your right to privacy is important, especially online.
This privacy policy has been created to answer any questions you may have regarding our protection and privacy policies.
What information is being collected at www.fudge4oregon.org The only personal information collected is information you give us.
In an effort to grow our community online, we may ask you to submit information.
This information will be used to inform you about online events, campaign activities, TV appearances, and other Fudge 4 Oregon news.
We will never require you to give us personal information in order to visit this site – we only ask that you do so that we can better communicate with you.
When you offer your personal information or choose to participate in our efforts, we will use your information to personalize and customize Web pages and emails to you.
Some information must be collected when you make a contribution.
When you make contributions to Fudge 4 Oregon, federal law requires us to collect your name, mailing address, employer, and occupation.
We ask that children under 18 do not submit their information.
In accordance with the Federal Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA), Fudge 4 Oregon does not knowingly collect information from children.
How is the information collected at www.fudge4oregon.org used?
We will not sell your personal information.
Sms opt-in consent and data will not be shared with third parties.
Under no circumstances will Fudge 4 Oregon sell your information to third parties or any commercial entities.
Fudge 4 Oregon may provide your email address or other personal information to authorized third parties required to deliver a particular service.
These third parties may not use said information for any other purpose than to carry out the services they are performing on our behalf.
Fudge4oregon.org links to other sites: Our site may contain links to other websites and servers.
Fudge 4 Oregon does not bear responsibility for privacy policies or content on linked websites.

Because we have no control over the websites we link to, you agree and acknowledge that Fudge 4 Oregon is not responsible for the availability of resources or external sites and does not endorse and is not responsible or liable for any content provided therein.
We encourage you to read the privacy statements on each website you visit.
Fudge 4 Oregon provides links to original articles written and maintained by third parties.
These links are provided as a convenience and do not imply a claim of ownership in that content.
If you have any questions, comments or concerns please contact Fudge 4 Oregon at info@fudge4oregon.org .

added: Follow the Campaign in Real Time Facebook Used for the like, share, comment, and reaction icons Jared Gapinski For MN Senate 13 #ago What a great day at the Sauk Rapids Fire Department Open House this past Saturday! 🚒🍂 This event is always a special one for me.
I spent nearly 20 years serving with the Sauk Rapids Fire Department as a firefighter and captain, and it was great to be back catching up with old friends and fellow firefighters!
We couldn’t have asked for better weather, and the turnout was incredible!
From the free pumpkins and vehicle extrication demonstrations to the kids getting to climb inside the fire trucks and explore all the equipment, there was something for everyone to enjoy.
Having spent so many years in the fire service, I know firsthand the time, dedication, and sacrifice that go into protecting our communities.
It’s wonderful to see so many families come out to support these men and women and learn more about what they do.
A huge thank you to the Sauk Rapids Fire Department and everyone who helped put on another fantastic open house.

I’m proud to have been part of this department and will always appreciate the people who continue to serve our community! 🇺🇸🚒 www.gapinskiformnsenate.com #MNLeg #MNSenate #District13 #FirstResponders #SaukRapidsMN #Community #MNPolitics #Vote2026 #MNVotes #GOP #GapinskiforMNSenate ...

Whether you're a chili recipe master or you just love to eat the stuff, come on out this Sunday starting at 1 for Sunday Funday with Mike, Rose and us.
There's loads of fun things going on all day.

(See comments below for chili cook-off rules!) 📍 The Vikes don't play, but other games will be shown starting at noon. 📍 Chili sampling begins at 1pm. 📍 Judging will be complete at 3pm - we need your help with this! 📍 Speaking of judging, we will have some sweet guest judges joining us - Tanja Goering for MN and Jared Gapinski For MN Senate 13! 📍 Starting at 3pm, the Lions will be slinging meat raffle meat plus we'll be running horse races for BIG CASH and $5 tip boards for $25 and $90 prizes every round.
To sign up to participate in the Chili Cook-Off, please text Jenny at 320-223-3602.
And honestly, if you have not yet become a massive fan of the hand-crafted cocktails that Mike and Rose have made famous, one sip and you'll be HOOKED.
Old Fashioneds, Bee's Knees and more, handcrafted right in front of you.

See More See Less View on Facebook · Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email View Comments likes love 57 Shares: 2 Comments: 3 3 Comments Comment on Facebook Jared Gapinski For MN Senate 13 #ago We need to take a serious look at ALL programs at the state level.
Minnesotans who need help are looking for a hand up, not a handout.
At the same time, we need to dig deeper into funded and unfunded mandates pushed down to local governments.
Those mandates have real consequences for taxpayers when local levies are set each year.
Under the DFL-led trifecta, Minnesota has seen an $18 billion surplus disappear, billions lost to fraud, the cost of government increase by 40%, and now we face a substantial upcoming deficit.
Whether you’re red, blue, or independent, Minnesotans simply cannot afford more of the same.
We need to tighten the purse strings.
We need to cut wasteful spending.
We need to get serious about taxes.
And we need to recognize that while people sometimes need a hand up, taxpayers deserve accountability for where their hard-earned dollars are going.
Government may not be a business, but it still has a responsibility to operate within its means.
If a local business continually spent beyond what it could sustain, ignored inefficiencies, and failed to properly account for its money, eventually there would be serious consequences.
State government should be held to a high standard of fiscal responsibility as well.
This doesn’t have to be complicated.
We need to bring some common sense and accountability back to state government.
If money were no object, we could fund everything.
Unfortunately, that isn’t reality.

It’s time for a serious conversation about our priorities, our spending, and what Minnesota taxpayers can actually afford. www.gapinskiformnsenate.com #MNLeg #MNSenate #District13 #BloatedGovernment #MNPolitics #Vote2026 #MNVotes #GOP #GapinskiforMNSenate ...

View on Facebook · Share Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email View Comments likes love 31 Shares: 2 Comments: 0 0 Comments Comment on Facebook Jared Gapinski For MN Senate 13 is with Lisa Demuth.
#ago Last week, I had the opportunity to participate in the Association of Minnesota Counties (AMC) Fall Policy Conference in Bemidji.
As a Benton County Commissioner and Chair of AMC’s Public Safety Policy Committee, I spend a great deal of time working on issues that affect counties across Minnesota.
The Fall Policy Conference brings county officials together for important conversations and presentations on policies that affect Minnesotans, their communities, and their wallets.
I was also grateful to AMC for asking me to participate in a panel on legislative engagement.
Counties work with legislators on a regular basis, often navigating challenging policy discussions while explaining how decisions made in St.
Paul affect the people and communities we serve.
The panel was a great opportunity to share some of what I’ve learned through that work and hear perspectives from county leaders across Minnesota.
We also had the opportunity to hear from gubernatorial candidate Lisa Demuth .
She has real vision on addressing these topics and restoring MN.
Thank you to her, and I look forward to serving with her in St Paul, helping change the trajectory of the state of MInnesota.

Conferences like this are valuable because they bring local leaders together to have serious conversations about the issues we deal with every day—from public safety and county services to state mandates, funding, and the relationship between counties and the Legislature.
I appreciate AMC and everyone who took part in this year’s conference.

I’m grateful for the opportunity to represent Benton County in these statewide discussions and to continue learning from county leaders throughout Minnesota. www.gapinskiformnsenate.com #MNLeg #MNSenate #District13 #MNPolitics #Vote2026 #MNVotes #GOP #GapinskiforMNSenate ...

added: Home About Platform Accomplishments Media Radio Scripts Endorsements Volunteer Donate Accomplishments These are just some of the bills I’ve championed since taking office last year.
Many have passed the Senate and I will continue to push this agenda forward.

We have the right to bear arms and defend ourselves, especially in a time of rising crime.
SF 442: Defense of Dwelling Act 2021 Pending: Defense of Dwelling Act 2022 SF 2328: Amendment to the Minnesota State Constitution protecting the right to bear arms.
We can’t depend on future legislators to stop anti-gun legislation, so I have co-authored this bill to make it clear: we have the RIGHT to bear arms.
SF 1202: Prohibiting the closure of shooting ranges during a state of emergency.
We saw states shut down shooting ranges for COVID!
They are looking for any excuse to limit our right to bear arms.
The passion I see with high school shooting teams needs to continue and will with this bill.
IMPORTANT FLOOR VOTES BY SENATOR DORNINK YES , on SF 1589 , banning vaccine mandates and passports.
This bill passed the Senate on May 14, 2021, and must now be passed by the House. — ELECTION INTEGRITY — YES , on Voter ID.
Everyone must feel like their vote counts.
Do they think people are too dumb to get an ID?
These will help ensure everyone gets ONE vote. — EMERGENCY POWERS — YES , on ending Governor’s emergency powers.
The governor should never have the extended control Governor Walz took!
The “Never again bill” would be tied up in court and would likely be considered unconstitutional.
It is poorly written and has zero chance of passing.
YES , on a bill that requires legislative approval for the extension of emergency powers.
It’s easy to say only the legislature should have control but the legislature is slow, and it would take us a week just to get together.
WE can’t organize in an hour to address an emergency.
That is why our constitution allows for emergency powers.
YES , on eliminating the Governor’s authority to close schools and restrict learning.
The legislature needs to be a part of any decision regarding our children as we are the closest to the people.
TAX RELIEF FOR MINNESOTANS SF 56: Unlimited Social Security income tax subtraction.
SF 273: Income tax subtraction for retirement income.
SF 1822: Butcher shop machinery tax exemption.
We continue to see the average age of farmers increase and there is very little opportunity for young people who have the passion to farm.
This will help beginning farmers have the financial stability necessary to operate successfully.
SF 676: Senior citizen property tax credit.
Should we just continue to chase our senior citizens out of Minnesota, or should we keep the most important people in our lives here?
I think we need them with us!
This allows our local bars, Eagles club, and VFW clubs to support under-privileged kids or support the community in other ways.
SF 245: Tax reduction holidays for firearms and fishing equipment.
SF 2643: Purple Heart special plates fee exemption.
PUBLIC SAFETY AND LAW ENFORCEMENT SF 82: Increased penalties for assault on peace officers, judges, prosecuting attorneys, and correctional employees.
It’s time to support our public servants.
They are our neighbors and friends.
PASSED ☑ SF 208: Law enforcement hiring information access expansion.
SF 686: Hometown Hero’s Act; providing support to those who sacrifice so much for our communities.
PASSED ☑ SF 820: Sex trafficking cases model policies adoption.
SF 952: Allowing for emergency medical care to police dogs.
Our police dogs are protecting us and our police officers.
They put their lives on the line for us and we need to give them the best care possible.
PASSED ☑ SF 2650: Police use of deadly force modification.
SF 3015: Body cam systems grants for rural MN.
This will protect the public and law enforcement.
SF 3042: Additional school safety specialists appropriation.
I want to protect our children from people who may try to harm them in our schools.
The carjackers are putting our friends, neighbors, and our families in danger.
SF 3151: Increased penalties for fleeing police in a car.
Why is it criminals can run from the police and endanger our families?
We need to keep increasing the penalties until they stop endangering other people.
OTHER NOTABLE BILLS I’VE SIGNED ON TO SF 754: Imposing term limits of legislators.
From the beginning, I have said I will abide by term limits and have pushed legislation to impose term limits.
We all know career politicians that need to go.
SF 1264: Prohibiting employers from having vaccination requirements.
No one should be told what to put in their bodies!
Medical treatments are a personal decision not for an employer to decide.
It’s a slippery slope and you can imagine what else an employer could ask us to do if we let them.
SF 1979: Reopening our DVS testing locations.
With the increase in gas costs due to the Biden administration why do they want us to drive even further for basic services?
PASSED ☑ SF 2450: Prohibiting youth sport masking requirements.
The chance of our youth dying from COVID-19 is no more than the flu.
Stop pretending that masks work for children.
The Democratic party wants to control our lives.
One way is with Vaccine Passports.
SF 2474: SF 2729: Protecting parents’ right to speak at school board meetings.
Who’s in control of your children?
The democratic party thinks you should sit down and be quiet!
I think you are in control, and I voted YES on this legislation.
PASSED ☑ SF 3208: Call for a Convention of States to impose fiscal restraints on the federal government and impose term limits on members of congress.

added: Back in January I joked about running against Tom Emmer but once I realized there was already a strong candidate running against him, I figured it wasn’t the right time.
We attended an Indivisible meeting where we heard from Joe Shephard that no one was running against the incumbent in our district, so I decided it was time to throw my hat into the ring.
I was already angry about the way that both the federal and state governments were being run.
I needed a constructive outlet for my anger.
What better way than to go and make working class voices heard.
For too long our elected officials have sat in their offices and have lost touch with what the needs of what the average Minnesotan are.
I’m running because things need to change and it’s time for working folk to be heard.

added.text: 2026 Proposed Constitutional Amendment – What You Need to Know | League of Women Voters of MN
Elk River Economic and Development Business Resource

added: I know that to achieve free health care for all there will be many steps to get there, so I propose that we start with making sure our children are covered first, from ages newborn all the way up to 26.
This will help give them the healthcare they need without the added costs that come with copays and insurance prices through parents work.
At the same time healthcare doesn’t just cover a trip to the doctors, it should also cover sight, hearing, dental, and mental health as well.
We should not have several different insurances when it is all healthcare.
As well as making sure everything is covered, I believe we should put a cap on drug prices.
For too long insurance prices have continued to go up, as well as drug prices.
Low-income families continue to struggle while pharmaceutical companies continue to make more and more money.
This November you can find a constitutional amendment on the ballot that does just this.
It is proposing increasing the permanent school fund payout from 2.5% to 4.5%.
This will not increase your taxes.
For more information you can check out 2026 Proposed Constitutional Amendment – What You Need to Know | League of Women Voters of MN .
The #1 cause of death for children is gun violence.
As a gun owner myself and someone who has the training on how to properly store and use them myself, I know that protection is important.
I stand up for our 2nd amendment rights, but I also stand up for the protection of children and those that are most vulnerable when it comes to gun violence.
Government accountability Elected officials should be held to a higher standard when it comes to upholding the law.
No member of government should get a slap on the wrist when they break the law.
Everyone, whether an elected official or not, should be held accountable for their actions, be it through the government itself or the people they represent.
Repeat offenders should no longer be able to hold office.
Fraud has been a large talking point lately, each accusation should be investigated thoroughly.
We have the newly established Office of Inspector General, this office should receive the full support of both the house and senate and given any tools and resources they need to do their job.
Which is rooting out fraud in every corner of the state.
Small and Local Business Small and local businesses are the backbone of any community.
We need to support them in becoming successful.
This will have to be a bit of give and take by giving tax breaks to small and new businesses and increasing taxes of big corporations.
Elk River is home to roughly 2500 small businesses and each of those employ on average around 11 employees.
We need to strive to increase minimum wage so those employees can have livable wages while at the same time bringing cost down so employers do not struggle to pay those livable wages.
According to Elk River Economic and Development Business Resource this area thrives on small businesses.
And that’s just Elk River; Otsego is home to several small businesses as well and they deserve to have the means to thrive too.
By giving small businesses, a leg up then we can work towards increasing their long-term success.
Housing Affordable housing is an issue that is not just statewide but country wide.
Everyone should have the opportunity to achieve homeownership.
And those that do not wish to own a home should also be able to rent without predatory increases and on one income, as well as not cost more than 30% of someone’s income.
To lower costs, we can build more and smaller starter homes as well as renovate older homes to reduce the shortage.
We could also look into using older abandoned buildings and bring them up to code to convert them into low-cost apartments.
Corporations and real estate investment companies should be limited on how many single families homes they can own.
They should also be required to sell those homes after 5-10 years.
Energy Sources I support lifting the moratorium on nuclear energy.
We have 2 existing plants in Minnesota that are currently producing over 30% of the state’s current energy needs.
The Xcel Energy plant is over 50 years old and with current technology I believe that nuclear energy is much safer and more reliable.
I do still believe that we should invest in solar, wind, and hydroelectricity.
We should make strides to move away from the Sherco power plant as it is far too outdated.

added: Gina Hinojosa is running for Governor of Texas to help families thrive and give every child a brighter future.

The thing is, he has the power to do it today.” Austin, TX – Today, Democratic nominee for Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa called on Greg Abbott to sign an emergency executive order putting a moratorium on data centers until the legislature meets to give Texans a seat at the table.
“The people of Texas are being taken advantage of, in a big way, by corporations who are operating under no rules,” Hinojosa said.
“Data centers are coming in and doing as they please – they are guzzling up all our water, guzzling up all our electricity – and the people have no say.
That is the Wild West of data centers that Greg Abbott has created in Texas.

People need relief.” “I’m calling for a moratorium until a legislative session that puts Texans first so that we don’t have any more communities in Texas who are powerless against these global corporations,” Hinojosa added.
Hinojosa was joined by impacted Texans to discuss their first-hand experiences and how Greg Abbott’s policies have put billionaires first and left them behind.
Cheryl Shadden , a nurse practitioner who lives across from a Granbury data center, said, “We are bombarded with noise 24/7.
My entire community is sick, and [data centers] are taking 2.5 million gallons of water per day off the Brazos River and Lake Granbury.

This is what my community has lived through for three years.” Hinojosa outlined her Texans First Data Center Priorities for the next legislative session, which Abbott could call today: Requiring American union jobs so operators hire skilled, licensed, union labor, and undoing the fast-track rollbacks that let corporations cut safety corners.
When corners get cut on builds this size, workers die.
Giving Texans a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come to their communities.
Creating full transparency by stopping data center companies from using NDAs.

Lowering costs for Texans by ensuring data center companies prove households won’t pay more for electricity or water, including the hidden costs passed through for grid upgrades, transmission, and new capacity.
Make data centers pay for themselves by stopping subsidies.
These data centers are owned by the richest men in the world; Texans shouldn’t foot the bill.
Putting water and power for Texans first by ensuring any water contract with data centers becomes unenforceable if it threatens a community’s water supply.

The event follows Hinojosa’s recent swing in the Panhandle, where she met with rural Texans about their concerns on data centers at a series of roundtables, a town hall, and by visiting one of the world’s largest planned data center sites.

The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex is the number one data center market in the world, with the highest concentration of data centers in Texas, including 132 operational, under construction, or planned in Dallas County alone.

At the press conference, Hinojosa called out Abbott’s data center theatrics as nothing more than a lame campaign promise, as nothing has changed for Texans suffering the consequences of unfettered data centers coming into their communities.
“Greg Abbott’s moratorium on data centers is just words,” said Hinojosa.

“We still have Texans who are against big economic powers in our communities that are having to fend for themselves because Greg Abbott invited the data centers into Texas with the richest tax breaks in the country.” “The [Danik data center] went online December 19, 2025, the same day that we were giving out Toys for Tots in our neighborhood,” said Claudia Fowler, a Joppa resident fighting the Danik data center, which got approval from the city and state by disguising its project as “utility company/utility use.” Fowler added, “Our question since day one is: ‘When are we going to be included in the conversation on data centers?’” Unlike Abbott, Hinojosa is fighting to protect all Texans.
In July, she called on Greg Abbott to call a special session to create real laws that protect Texans and give them a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into their communities.
An overwhelming number of voters don’t support data centers in their communities, and they know Abbott’s election-year lies and hypocrisy are just more false promises.
Texans are ready for change, which is why multiple recent independent polls in the last month show Hinojosa beating Abbott.
Voters are sick of Abbott letting data centers harm their communities, and they’ll make that clear at the ballot box this November.

Since starting her campaign, Hinojosa has traveled more than 75,000 miles crisscrossing the state and met with thousands of Texans, regardless of party, to outline her plan to end Greg Abbott’s corruption and secure the American Dream for Texans.
With multiple independent polls showing her ahead of Abbott in the governor’s race, the tour will underscore Hinojosa’s momentum in the lead-up to Election Day.
“There’s One Fight this year: Is Texas a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaire’s world and we just live in it?” said Hinojosa.
“This campaign has always been about listening to the needs of working Texans in every corner of the state, regardless of party.
In those conversations, I built my plan to secure the American Dream by saving Texas public schools and putting money in your pockets.
I’m excited to continue meeting new voters, outlining our plans to create a Texas built for the people, not the billionaires, and turning out the vote ahead of Election Day.

Don’t let them tell you it can’t happen in Texas, because it already is.” “One Fight” GOTV Tour: Sunday, October 18th: Houston Monday, October 19th: San Antonio Tuesday, October 20th: Laredo Thursday, October 22nd MORNING: Fort Bend, Houston EVENING: Midland-Odessa Friday, October 23rd: Denton Saturday, October 24th MORNING: Dallas AFTERNOON: Austin Sunday, October 25th MORNING: College Station AFTERNOON: Weslaco Monday, October 26th MORNING: Brownsville AFTERNOON: Corpus Christi Tuesday, October 27th MORNING: Waco AFTERNOON: Fort Worth Wednesday, October 28th: El Paso Thursday, October 29th: Collin More dates and stops to be announced!

added: Find Your Early Voting Location: https://gregabbott.com/vote Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Governor Abbott Calls For Tougher Crackdown on Career Criminals Oct 14, 2026 ROCKWALL – Governor Greg Abbott today outlined his plan to crack down on violent repeat offenders, strengthen criminal prosecutions, and keep dangerous criminals off Texas streets during a roundtable with law enforcement leaders.
The Governor also honored officers who put their lives on the line to protect Texans in recognition of Law Enforcement Appreciation Month.

Governor Abbott was joined by Senator Bob Hall, Representative Katrina Pierson, Rockwall County Sheriff Terry Garrett, Hunt County Sheriff Terry Jones, Heath Department of Public Safety Chief Brandon Seery, Royse City Police Department Chief Kirk Aldridge, and members of the Combined Law Enforcement Association of Texas (CLEAT), Texas Municipal Police Association (TMPA), and Texas Department of Public Safety Officers Association (DPSOA).
“Law Enforcement is common sense,” said Governor Abbott.
It also happens to be a necessity.
Some people are running for office who are against our law enforcement officers and public safety.

I know that when the time comes, voters will vote in favor of common sense.” During the roundtable, Governor Abbott discussed his proposal to establish a statewide prosecutor to support overburdened local prosecutors and ensure criminals are held accountable.
Additionally, Governor Abbott highlighted the expansion of the Texas Repeat Offender Task Force to Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio, and Austin to target and arrest dangerous repeat offenders.
Governor Abbott also drew a sharp contrast with Gina Hinojosa’s anti-law enforcement voting record .
While Hinojosa claims to support law enforcement, she in fact voted to defund the police and opposed legislation to strengthen protections for officers assaulted in the line of duty.
Click here to read more about Governor Abbott’s Public Safety Initiatives.
Additional photos of today’s events will be provided here when available.

added: About Meet Greg Ballard Podcast Meet Greg News & Updates Greg’s Plan Voters Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer CONTRIBUTE Meet Greg Ballard Greg’s Plan Voter’s Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission News and Updates Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer Subscribe Contribute Oct 14, 2026 Letter: Ballard would make Secretary of State job less partisan River Karner, Lafayette Journal & Courier After spending much of my life teaching and being involved in my community, I've become increasingly concerned about how deeply partisan politics has seeped into nearly every aspect of public life.
That's one reason I'm supporting Greg Ballard for Indiana secretary of state.
I have always believed that institutions work best when they serve the people they are intended to serve, not a particular political interest.
I think our elections deserve that same kind of independence.
The person responsible for administering our elections should be independent of the candidates and political parties competing in those elections.
Former Mayor Ballard has said that if elected, he would not endorse, donate or raise money for candidates.
Further, he has said that he would seek to make that standard part of the law.
This takes partisan politics out of this office.
Another and perhaps more important reason I support Ballard is that I appreciate his proposal for a personalized statewide voters' guide.
Democracy works better when people have the opportunity to become informed before they are filling out their ballots.
And Ballard says the guide would be nonpartisan, with candidate statements supplied by the candidates themselves rather than political messaging from the secretary of state's office.
Finally, I believe Ballard's experience as the mayor of Indianapolis is invaluable.
He is the only candidate running for this office who has led a large and complicated government.
The secretary of state belongs to the people of Indiana — not to a political party.
Greg Ballard has earned my vote, and I urge other voters to give him serious consideration.
River Karner is a Lafayette resident.
This article originally appeared in the Lafayette Journal & Courier .

removed: About Meet Greg Ballard Podcast Meet Greg News & Updates Greg’s Plan Voters Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer CONTRIBUTE Meet Greg Ballard Greg’s Plan Voter’s Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission News and Updates Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer Subscribe Contribute Jul 14, 2026 Signature Delivery Day Speech The following is the transcript from Greg Ballard's speech on Signature Delivery Day, as he and Hoosiers from across the state delivered over 41,000 verified signatures to get his name on the ballot for Indiana Secretary of State this fall.
Hello!
Thank you for being here today.
The status quo is over.
For too long, our government has been conducted behind closed doors by the same insiders, the same parties, and the same rules written to protect the same people.
They continue to treat our elections like a private club and then hand Hoosier taxpayers the bill.
This is not consent of the governed.
This is not the Indiana Hoosiers deserve.
Our current political system asks for your vote, but ignores your voice.
We have politicians who fight to empower our parties, while what Hoosiers really want is accountability, honesty, and results.
The two-party stranglehold on Indiana politics is a relic.
A political dinosaur long overdue for extinction.
Our campaign is bigger than one candidate.
It is bigger than one office.
And insiders from both establishment parties know it.
They fought hard to keep us off the ballot.
In fact, both Republicans and Democrats tried to convince me not to run or to drop out.
Trust me, that’s not happening.
They tried to make the rules so difficult, the threshold so hard to meet, and so unfair that ordinary citizens would give up.
But tens of thousands of Hoosiers stood up and said, “No more.
We want another choice.
We want real competition.
We want our state back!” The Republican and Democrat in this race were each nominated at closed party conventions by about one thousand party insiders.
Today, I am delivering more than 42,000 verified signatures from Hoosiers who signed petitions because they are fed up, frustrated, and angry.
Now we are on the ballot.
We are not here to whisper.
We are here to break open this system and give Indiana back to her people.
For those of you who don’t know, I’m a two-term former mayor of Indianapolis, who won against all odds.
As well as a 23-year Marine, Lieutenant Colonel, and Persian Gulf War veteran.
I’m different.
I have always been an outsider, but I do know how the government should work.
As mayor of Indianapolis for eight years, I had to solve problems.
I had to bring people together.
I had to deliver, and we did.
This campaign, however, is not just about me.
It is about a movement.
It is about opening the door for more good candidates around Indiana.
Candidates with good judgment and character.
Candidates with courage.
Candidates who can win and who want to serve voters instead of parties.
The Secretary of State oversees our elections.
The Secretary of State must protect every voter, every candidate, and every ballot, not merely mark time until the next, higher political position comes along.
So let me be clear: I will neither endorse, nor fundraise for, nor donate to, nor accept donations from candidates in Hoosier elections.
Let that sink in.
I will serve the voters of Indiana.
Period.
This should not be controversial.
In this race, however, I am the only candidate willing to make this pledge, because I am the only candidate not owned by a political party.
My opponents are offering more of the same because they are part of the same.
They will want to protect the rules that protect them.
They will want to keep power exactly where it is.
Unfortunately, the establishment parties built a system that pushes good people out and pulls extreme voices in.
The candidates who are nominated make it clear: their priority is to serve the party first and the people second.
This is backward.
It should be easier to run for office.
The rules should be fair.
The playing field should be level.
So to every Hoosier who has been shut out or taken for granted: this campaign is for you - you are in charge.
To every independent who has been told your vote does not matter: this campaign is for you.
To every Republican and Democrat who still believes public service should matter more than party loyalty: this campaign is for you.
To every Hoosier who is sick and tired of politics as usual: this campaign is for you.
To the thousands of Hoosiers who supported our historic, unprecedented effort to get us on the ballot— I thank you.
The status quo is over.
The stranglehold is broken.
The insiders have had their turn.
Now it’s the people’s turn!
This campaign, and the thousands of Hoosiers who support it, have already achieved two main goals, goals a few months ago everyone said couldn’t be achieved.
Number one: The incumbent is out of this race.
Number two: We are taking this step today to be on the ballot with the potential to open up ballot access into the future for scores of qualified Hoosiers who can serve their communities.
There is one more goal to go.
Winning.
Working together, we will win this fight.
Let’s take back our elections and put power back in the hands of the people – where it belongs!
Today, I’m asking you, the people, for your vote, just as I asked for your signatures - the signatures we are about to turn in to the State.
Thank you for being here today, please join me as we walk to take the next step toward being on the ballot, the signature delivery!

added: Donate Here Endorsed by Beyond Party Endorsement On behalf of Beyond Party – Montana First, I am pleased to let you know that our Board of Directors has voted to endorse your candidacy for the Montana Legislature.
As a new organization, Beyond Party has taken great care to approach endorsements thoughtfully and selectively.
This election cycle, we focused our attention on races where the outcome is likely to be particularly close or especially consequential to the future of our communities and our state.

Our endorsement process is grounded in our mission to support leaders who are committed to strengthening democracy, improving civic discourse, and putting the public interest ahead of partisan division.

After careful review and discussion, we believe you demonstrate the qualities that align with our mission and values, as well as the leadership, integrity, and commitment to democratic principles that Montana needs.
We are proud to add our support to your campaign.
We have shared our endorsement with our members and supporters in our latest newsletter, which is attached.
We will continue to promote our endorsed candidates through social media and other communications between now and Election Day.
We want our support to be helpful and aligned with your campaign’s needs.
If there is anything you’d like us to know about messaging, timing, or how we share our endorsement, we would be glad to hear from you.
Please feel free to share this endorsement with your supporters.
You will also find our logo attached for your use.
If there are additional ways we can help amplify your campaign, we would be happy to discuss them.
Thank you for your willingness to serve and for your commitment to strengthening Montana.
Congratulations, and best wishes for a successful campaign.
