title.after: It’s time we make creeps afraid again | Jim McGovern for Congress

added: Home | Menu | Sign Up | Donate Jim McGovern for Congress - https://www.jimmcgovern.com Meet Jim News Volunteer Contact Donate It’s time we make creeps afraid again Doesn't this guy ever get tired of being a creep?
I mean, every time we blink, our moronic president has found another way to screw over the American people.
For months, we've seen Flock cameras across the country be used to stalk Americans, aid ICE thugs in illegal raids, and trample our Fourth Amendment rights.
Now, Trump and the federal government are using Flock camera data to sell us out to his buddies in Big Tech.

I mean, come on, I can't remember Americans on either side of the political spectrum ever saying, "You know what'll solve all of our problems and bring down the cost of eggs, gas, and housing: a surveillance state." Why is it that on the rare occasions when Trump actually puts in the work, it's to do stuff nobody, and I mean nobody, asks for?
The bigger picture here is that his technology poses a clear threat to the privacy rights of everyone in the country.
We've seen this administration ignore the rule of law time and again — as long as he or his billionaire big-tech friends can profit from it.
We can't let this fall by the wayside.
I won't stop fighting and sounding the alarm until it ends.
One way to end this federally funded peepshow is to elect people with the guts to reject every clear violation of civil rights.
I need your help to get back to Congress so I can work to end this disgusting violation of our privacy.
Can I count on you to chip in today to help me get reelected this November?
This grassroots movement goes as far as people like you take me!
I promise you this — I'll never lie to you, and I'll NEVER take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Yours in the fight, Jim Posted on October 14, 2026 .
Learn More In Congress, Jim works to defend human rights, reform our campaign finance system, end hunger, and create an economy where everyone can thrive.
Join this effort to support Massachusetts families.
Together we can make it happen.
Donate Now Meet Jim Jim McGovern represents the 2nd District of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
He has earned a national reputation as a tireless advocate for his district and as a champion for food security, human rights, campaign finance reform, social justice and peace.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Press Releases FACT CHECK: Juan Ciscomani Lies about Taxes, Veterans in AZ-06 Debate September 14, 2026 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE September 14, 2026 Contact : [email protected] Multiple Outlets Fact Check Ciscomani Claims, Ads RED ROCK, AZ – On Thursday, JoAnna Mendoza participated in Arizona Clean Elections Commission’s debate for Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District, showing voters why she is the independent leader that Southern Arizonans deserve in Congress.
According to Arizona Public Media , during the debate, Representative Juan Ciscomani made false claims about Mendoza’s taxes and denied personally supporting policy changes that hurt veterans.

Additionally, according to American Journal News , dark money groups supporting the Ciscomani campaign are running ads with Mendoza comments about tax cuts clipped and intentionally taken out of context–from six years ago .
“JoAnna is a battle-tested Marine veteran who served our country for two decades,” said Kyle McCarthy, campaign spokesperson.
“In Congress, she’ll be focused on honoring our veterans and on lowering costs and tax cuts for Arizona families–not tax breaks for the wealthy and big corporations.
JoAnna is running an honest race.

We just wish our opponent would do the same.” GET THE FACTS: Veteran healthcare According to AZPM : “The claim: Mendoza blamed Ciscomani’s policies for staffing cuts at the Department of Veteran Affairs.

The verdict: True .” “In December 2024, Ciscomani said in a press release that, in light of the national debt surpassing $36 trillion, he was thrilled to join the DOGE Caucus to reduce waste and streamline government bureaucracy.
“When we talk about staff getting cut, no doctors were let go,” Ciscomani said.
That’s a fact.” Policy changes tied to DOGE, however, did lead to a net loss of physicians and medical staff, according to the VA.
The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities reports that the Trump Administration cut nearly 28,000 VA employees in 2025.

VA staffing cuts included 2,700 nurses, more than 1,000 medical officers, and more than 1,000 psychologists and social workers, as well as over 1,800 people tasked with evaluating veterans’ claims for benefits.

VA health centers and offices in every state have seen staffing declines, with Arizona’s VA workforce losing 575 employees.” Mendoza Personal Taxes According to AZPM : “The claim: Ciscomani cited a report from the Arizona Daily Star to accuse JoAnna Mendoza of “cheating” on her taxes.
The verdict: False .” “Mendoza acknowledged the error to the Republic and her campaign characterized that as a filing mistake.
Records reviewed by the Republic showed she contacted Pima County on Aug.

10 to correct the property’s classification.” Dirty ads Ads by the Congressional Leadership Fund and the National Republican Campaign Commission–spending on behalf of Juan Ciscomani–claim Mendoza wanted, “no new tax cuts, no new tax credits, or sale tax exemptions” for working Arizonans.
But here’s the full context of Jo’s quote being distorted by CLF , where Mendoza talks about her opposition to more tax breaks for the wealthy and corporations in a time of severe budget cuts.
Full quote: “We know that there have been enormous tax breaks and tax cuts for wealthy folks and for corporations.
So moving forward, there should be no new tax cuts, no new tax credits, or sale tax exemptions.

We need to ensure that we work on securing additional federal fiscal relief to balance the state budget and explore new ways to modernize the tax code to ensure that everyone is paying their fair share of taxes.
Now, it’s been reported that 73% of Arizona’s corporations paid $50 or less in state income taxes last year.
I’m sure you pay your taxes.
Shouldn’t Arizona’s corporations pay their taxes too?” Read the full fact check by American Journal News .

Juan Ciscomani is a fight over what things cost ”, detailing how JoAnna Mendoza is the candidate who voters should elect to bring down prices.

The piece describes the actions of her opponent, Juan Ciscomani, to support tariffs that jack up prices, vote for the so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” that knocked Arizonans off their health insurance and SNAP coverage, cut clean energy tax cuts that supported thousands of jobs in Arizona, voted to DOGE the VA and lay off staff, increasing wait times, and voted six times in support of the Iran War, a senseless conflict that has sent gas and diesel prices skyrocketing.

The article detailed Mendoza’s commitment to end reckless tariffs, reverse Medicaid and SNAP cuts, expand apprenticeships and technical education programs, and reverse tax cuts for billionaires and the ultrawealthy.

“JoAnna can speak to voters about affordability because she grew up in rural poverty, and knows what it means to struggle to get by, even if that means accepting some help from social safety net programs,” said campaign spokesperson Kyle McCarthy.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Press Releases Arizonans Voice Frustration with Juan Ciscomani October 14, 2026 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 14, 2026 Contact : [email protected] RED ROCK, AZ – Arizonans across Congressional District Six are sharing their anger, disappointment, and frustration with Juan Ciscomani in opinion pieces and letters to the editor in local publications.
“Arizonans are fed up with Ciscomani’s broken promises and staunch refusal to put the needs of his constituents over his desire to please Donald Trump,” said campaign spokesperson Kyle McCarthy.

What they are saying: Arizona Daily Star Opinion Columnist: Tim Steller’s column: Ciscomani ‘bipartisan’ except when it mattered most “…when it has mattered most, Ciscomani has fallen in line with Trump, supporting his most consequential and damaging policies.
Even when other Republicans dared to break ranks on key issues, Ciscomani toed the Trump line.

“On the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, on tariffs and on the war in Iran — votes that have defined the last two years — Ciscomani even raised concerns at times, but in the end voted with Trump anyway.” Green Valley News: OPINION: No, Juan, this isn’t ‘small potatoes’ “Rep.
Ciscomani did a good job his freshman term in Congress, but all of that evaporated with Donald Trump’s return to the White House in 2025.
Juan stopped thinking for himself and went along with anything the president wanted.
“There’s a high cost to being weak-kneed.
For Ciscomani, it should be his House seat.

Regardless of your politics, CD6 doesn’t need a follower, and Ciscomani has proven he’s not a leader.” Arizona Daily Star: Letter: Ciscomanian “Dirty Tricks” “The desperation of Juan Ciscoimani’s reelection campaign is increasingly evident.
Currently, bright yellow signs with absurd lies about Ms.
Mendoza are appearing beside signs for Joanna Mendoza for Congress.
Intended to mislead voters, such “dirty tricks” are the same practice used by the infamous Joe McCarthy, Roy Cohn, and Richard Nixon nearly a century ago.
Ciscomani: have you no sense of decency?” Copper Courier: A Tucson mom lost SNAP for 2 months.
Ciscomani “For months, Garcia, a single mother, lived on potatoes, beans, rice, and other cheap staples.

Struggling to find a job and without SNAP food assistance, she had to ration the little money she and her oldest daughter had to afford groceries, which have increased by about 2.7% in the last year under President Donald Trump’s administration.
She relied on her family to help afford meals, promising to pay them back when she could, and even visited a local food bank for help.
“It’s harming people like me,” Garcia said face-to-face with Ciscomani.

In a brief reply before closing the elevator doors, Ciscomani said, “No, what it did is–” “For Garcia, the moment was about looking eye to eye with her representative and speaking up about her experience.

But she said she was instead met with a “dismissive” congressman, who she said did not stop to talk with her but rather “dodged” the questions and spoke over her.” Arizona Daily Star: Letter: Who Backs Ciscomani?
“Here’s an elected official who, for a year-and-a-half, would not even hold an open public meeting because he’d have been drown out in boos.
These Ciscomani ads claim he’s been a champion of working families.

Ciscomani voted nearly one hundred percent of the time to please his wealthy donors and to enable Trump’s corruption—a violation of his oath to protect the Constitution.” ### Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Terms & Conditions Privacy Policy Mailing Address: Mendoza for Congress P.O.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Jo's Positions Bring Good-Paying Jobs to Southern Arizona & Protecting Workers Growing up in rural poverty and the proud daughter of farmworkers, JoAnna saw how hard her parents worked and (still) struggled to make ends meet.
She believes working one job should allow you to provide for your family through a livable wage, benefits, and the ability to retire with dignity.
JoAnna also understands that a 4-year college degree isn’t the only path to success.
She supports workforce training, apprenticeships, and technical education that prepare Arizonans for good-paying jobs in the trades and growing industries.

In Congress, JoAnna will work to support small businesses, bring good-paying jobs back to our cities and towns, and ensure that companies who put roots down in Arizona hire and retain workers from our communities.
JoAnna also strongly supports the right to unionize and believes workers should be treated with dignity and have a fair shot at the American Dream.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Jo's Positions Lowering Costs & Protecting Our Families and Seniors As a working mom, JoAnna knows what it’s like to stretch a dollar and worry about rising costs.
Right now, families are paying too much – for groceries, gas, healthcare, housing, and utilities.
Instead of getting ahead, families are falling further behind.

In Congress, JoAnna will work to lower costs by cracking down on price gouging costing families an extra $2,000 a year by strengthening consumer protections and stopping unfair price disparities in rural communities.
A nursing mom should be able to afford a can of formula.
She will work to modernize the Child Tax Credit to deliver relief to working families and oppose reckless tariffs that drive up costs.
JoAnna is committed to delivering real-practical solutions because our families deserve a stable healthy future.
Social Security is a lifeline for older Arizonans who have worked their entire lives, paid into the system, and deserve to retire with dignity.
And as someone with an aging parent, she knows that the social security benefit isn’t enough to cover basic necessities.
JoAnna will oppose any efforts to cut seniors’ hard-earned benefits.
She strongly supports strengthening Social Security and exploring ways to increase benefits, especially for seniors living on fixed incomes.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Jo's Positions Restoring Trust and Accountability in Government JoAnna isn’t a politician; she’s a retired Marine and a mom who believes that public service is about accountability, integrity, and looking out for ordinary people.
Too many politicians in D.C. use their positions to benefit themselves instead of the people they serve.
JoAnna has zero tolerance for corruption.
JoAnna supports banning members of Congress, their families, and other top government officials from trading individual stocks while in office.
She will work to strengthen transparency laws, and ensure that the public can clearly see how decisions are made and how taxpayer dollars are spent.
Restoring trust in government means making Congress accessible to the people it serves.

In her first 100 days, JoAnna will bring Congress back to the community by reinstating town halls and launching “Congress in Your Community” events across AZ-06 – including rural and underserved areas – so that every Arizonan has a direct line to their representative.

JoAnna will also work to modernize how Congress connects with constituents by adopting a mobile-first constituent engagement platform to provide real-time updates on legislation, explain how decisions impact families, and give constituents a direct way to raise concerns, report issues, and share their experiences.

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Safe Communities, Strong Borders & Real Immigration Solutions As a single mother, JoAnna worries about her child, and wants every child to grow up in a safe, crime-free community.
People who break the law must be held accountable, including and especially those that commit violent crimes or smuggle illicit drugs like fentanyl and dangerous weapons into our neighborhoods.
As a retired Marine, JoAnna understands the call to serve and has deep respect for men and women in law enforcement who do their difficult jobs with honor.
It’s why she supports funding for law enforcement and ensuring officers have the critical resources to keep every Arizonan safe, including training and body cameras.

JoAnna does not support slashing police budgets, and she also believes that public safety is stronger when we invest in hiring more crisis response professionals, improve transparency, and build trust between law enforcement and the communities they serve.

In Congress, JoAnna will work with both parties to strengthen border security at ports of entry, deporting violent criminals, holding cartels accountable, and ensuring that immigration enforcement is professional, properly trained, and consistent with the law.
JoAnna believes in a fair immigration system that reflects our values as Americans.
She supports creating legal pathways to citizenship for people who work hard, follow the law, and contribute to their communities.
She supports legislation to strengthen oversight of detention facilities and restore independent audits.
JoAnna also supports Senator Kelly and Senator Gallego’s bicameral Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act .

title.after: Protecting our Water, Energy, and Climate Security - JoAnna Mendoza

added: Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Meet Jo On the Issues Endorsements News Get Involved Donate Contact Store Contribute Jo's Positions Climate, Water & Energy Security for Rural Arizona Having grown up in rural Arizona, JoAnna knows that rising energy costs and water shortages put real pressure on families, farmers, and rural communities.
She believes Arizona can lead the way in building a more affordable, reliable, and self-sufficient future.
In Congress, JoAnna will support investments in American-made energy, including clean energy, which will save money for ratepayers.

While Ciscomani has sided with utility companies and voted to roll back clean energy investments, JoAnna will stand up and protect local solar projects that bring energy online faster, lower costs, and reduce harmful pollution in our air. .
As new industries like data centers expand, JoAnna will fight to make sure that these industries bring their own energy and don’t drive up costs for Arizonans.
Her priority will be to keep utility costs from rising, protect workers and consumers, and safeguard our limited water supply.
JoAnna understands that water security is critical to Arizona’s future.
She will fight to strengthen water infrastructure, secure Arizona’s fair share of Colorado River resources, protect groundwater, and clean up contaminants like PFAS to ensure safe drinking water.
As the daughter of farmworkers, JoAnna grew up working Southern Arizona’s cotton fields.
She has a deep respect for the state’s agricultural economy, which is essential to providing for and feeding the nation.
JoAnna will push for a five year Farm Bill that provides certainty to farmers and ranchers, invests in rural communities, and ensures a healthy food supply for our families.

Stability and consistency for farmers, also means stopping reckless tariffs that jack up prices on equipment and fertilizer and make it difficult for farmers and other small business owners to plan ahead.
JoAnna will also fight to restore funding for programs that help farmers, including enhanced ACA subsidies.

added: PRESS RELEASE WATCH: Jocelyn Benson Slams John James For Repeatedly Voting to Raise Prices Amid Affordability Crisis Today, Secretary of State and Democratic nominee for Governor Jocelyn Benson joined CNN’s Dana Bash on Inside Politics and slammed John James for rubber-stamping Trump’s price-hiking agenda in Congress.

Jocelyn is the only candidate in this race that works for the people and is prepared to stand up to anyone — no matter how wealthy or powerful — who tries to raise costs or threatens the rights and safety of Michiganders.

In the final weeks before the election, Jocelyn will be campaigning alongside downballot candidates in crucial battleground districts, to protect and flip seats across the state and win back the Democratic trifecta in November.

“President Obama knows what’s at stake for Michigan families, and I’m grateful to have his support,” said Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson.
“My campaign is about three things: costs down, wages up, and ending the corruption that is hurting working Michigan families.

You need a governor like Jocelyn Benson.

Now she’s running for governor to lower healthcare costs, build more homes, and fight for every child’s right to a quality education.
Jocelyn has real answers to the problems keeping families up at night.

Capitol Police Officers Endorse Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Jocelyn Benson Statement on Donald Trump Pausing Federal Dollars for Thousands of Working of Michiganders PRESS RELEASE ICYMI: Jocelyn Benson Launches Gubernatorial Campaign with Momentum and Support Across Michigan PRESS RELEASE End Citizens United Endorses Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE EMILYs List Endorses Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Michigan State Lawmakers Endorse Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson Announces Run for Governor Oct 14 2026 PRESS RELEASE WATCH: Jocelyn Benson Slams John James For Repeatedly Voting to Raise Prices Amid Affordability Crisis Today, Secretary of State and Democratic nominee for Governor Jocelyn Benson joined CNN’s Dana Bash on Inside Politics and slammed John James for rubber-stamping Trump’s price-hiking agenda in Congress.

Jocelyn is the only candidate in this race that works for the people and is prepared to stand up to anyone — no matter how wealthy or powerful — who tries to raise costs or threatens the rights and safety of Michiganders.
Key point: “When [John James] went to Washington, he did not fight for people.

He fought for the highest bidder and did whatever Donald Trump asked: raising costs on all of us, voting three times to increase health care costs on the people of Michigan, supporting tariffs that have taxed Michiganders more than any other state, and voting six times to support a war in Iran that has directly impacted gas prices in Michigan.

So what people are looking for in Michigan right now — and what Democrats are unified around delivering — are lowering costs, increasing wages, growing our economy, and frankly, ending the type of corruption at the federal level that has got us here.” In case you missed it… WATCH HERE Dana Bash: …What do you say to voters who may have supported President Trump two years ago, and now are trying to figure out who to vote for for governor?
Jocelyn Benson: Look, in 2024, Donald Trump made a lot of promises to the people of Michigan: promises to lower costs, promises to make life more affordable.
And then he failed to deliver on those promises.
And not only that, here we are in 2026 and we're seeing not just failure to deliver, but also cost going up on just about everything.
If it's a reckless war in Iran, it is causing our gas prices to increase.
The reckless tariffs with Canada, that he and my opponent John James both support, have driven up costs on Michiganders and Michigan households more than any other state in the nation.
And the people of Michigan are feeling that.
We see our prices go up at the gas pump, at the grocery store, everywhere else and people are looking for leaders who will actually deliver results.
I've done that as Secretary of State: reforming our office to actually save people time and money.
And that track record, that results-oriented record, is ultimately what people are looking for in elections like this.
Bash: …What do you make of James’ comments about your party in Michigan?
Benson: Our party is the party of the Voting Rights Act.
We are the party of the Civil Rights Act, the party of Medicaid, Medicare, the party that does big transformational things and actually drives down costs for the people.
And my opponent, when he went to Washington, did not fight for people.

He fought for the highest bidder and did whatever Donald Trump asked: raising costs on all of us, voting three times to increase health care costs on the people of Michigan, supporting tariffs that have taxed Michiganders more than any other state, and voting six times to support a war in Iran that has directly impacted gas prices in Michigan.

So what people are looking for in Michigan right now — and what Democrats are unified around delivering — are lowering costs, increasing wages, growing our economy, and frankly, ending the type of corruption at the federal level that has got us here.
I talk a lot about how governments kind of, at the federal level, showing up everywhere we don't want it and nowhere we actually need it.
But here in Michigan, Democrats are united around showing up for people, actually delivering results, lowering costs, increasing wages, and making life better for everyone.
Bash: You mentioned tariffs…Would you be able to work with [Donald Trump] to try to lower the trade war’s burden on Michiganders?
Benson: My job as governor will be to fight for and represent the people of Michigan on all sides, in every county.
And that's what I've done as Secretary of State.

I'll always stand up to anyone who tries to interfere with our rights, our freedoms, and abuse their authority…But I also know that growing our economy, increasing access to well-paying jobs, is critical to ensuring everyone in Michigan can thrive.
And I will work with the President and anyone else who is committed to those same goals.
However, the President has to recognize that the tariffs he's imposed in this war with Canada has hurt Michiganders more than any other state.
Households are paying $6,400 more as a result of these tariffs.
So, as governor, I'll also work to negotiate agreements with Canada: subnational agreements that can carve out exceptions to these tariff wars to help protect Michiganders.
And I hope the President would support that work.

title.after: Joe de la Cruz, a 'breath of fresh air' in Hartford

added: top of page ABOUT PRIORITIES PRESS Menu Close All Posts Joe de la Cruz, a 'breath of fresh air' in Hartford Alisha Rayner Dec 14, 2024 9 min read Updated: Apr 24 State Rep.
Joe de la Cruz, D-Groton, speaks during a legislative town hall event Monday, April 18, 2022, at the Groton Senior Center.
(Sarah Gordon/The Day) By Kimberly Drelich Groton — When state Rep.
Joe de la Cruz, D-Groton, looks back on his six years as a legislator in Hartford, he hopes he inspired people to put themselves in others' shoes.

“If I have a superpower, it’s learned from my grandmother and my mother and my huge family, and it’s empathy," he said, "and to really try to understand where someone else is coming from to understand how to fix a problem.” De la Cruz, 51, a union sheet metal worker and the vice president of Hillery Co., a metal fabricator in Groton, rose through the ranks of local politics, serving six years on the Groton Representative Town Meeting and three years on the Town Council, before being elected in 2016 to his first term as state representative for the 41st District covering parts of New London and Groton.
He was motivated by the opioid crisis to run for state office.

De la Cruz and his wife, Tammy, are among the co-founders of the nonprofit organization Community Speaks Out that helps families and individuals struggling with opioid addiction find treatment and recover, after their son Joey Gingerella faced addiction struggles.
Gingerella, who spoke about his story and was in recovery, was fatally shot in December 2016 when he went to help a woman being assaulted.
De la Cruz will be wrapping up his final legislative session in Hartford on Wednesday.
He said his proudest accomplishments in the General Assembly include helping pass legislation to raise the minimum wage and legislation for a registry system for sober homes.
De la Cruz had announced at the start of the session that he would not run for reelection.

While he has worked long hours his whole life and juggled his business responsibilities with a full schedule in the legislature, he said it's "all hands on deck" now with a jump in business at Hillery Co., and he has to be there at the mom-and-pop business.
"The $35,000 we make for this illustrious job is truly not enough to live on or retire on," he said during his speech on his work as a representative in Hartford.

"I want to remind you of all the voices that never made it here that would sound like my voice ... because of the limitations we have.” De la Cruz, who has said he is fighting for the next generation and so his 3-year-old grandson can have the same opportunities he did, said he feels like he could offer a lot more in Hartford, but, after considering different options to try to make it work, he ultimately thinks he is making the right decision.
He supports raising salaries for legislators to bring in more people, from school teachers to construction workers, whose voices are needed in the legislature but who simply can’t afford it.
A ringside view of the American worker De la Cruz said he always reminds himself of where he came from, which he said makes him a better legislator and a better person.
He grew up in public housing in New London and graduated from New London High School before starting a career as a sheet metal worker.
In the 1990s, he worked on the duct work for the Legislative Office Building in Hartford.

As de la Cruz spoke on April 21 on the House floor in the Connecticut State Capitol in support of the State Employees Bargaining Agent Coalition agreement with the state, which ultimately passed, he said he’s had a ringside view of what’s happened to the American worker.

He started by reminding people where they were two years ago at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic as they grocery shopped for elderly parents and neighbors and recognized there were workers on the buses, walking to work and stocking shelves.
He said people “started to realize that not everybody that’s a hero wears a uniform or a badge,” and the SEBAC agreement was an opportunity to show appreciation for about 46,000 state employees.
He then shared a personal story about how he joined the United States Air Force when he was a junior in high school and recruited two of his classmates.

He graduated from high school and was supposed to leave for the Air Force in August 1989 — he had had a job to become a physician’s assistant on a helicopter — but he ended up getting arrested, so he couldn’t go.
De la Cruz, then a teenager, was supposed to spend six months in jail but was released after six days due to overcrowding.

But because of all the work done on labor rights in decades past, despite his criminal record, he was able to get a job in the sheet metal industry with health care, paid holidays and a week’s paid vacation.
His wages were raised after he completed his apprenticeship.

He then told the story about how he was able to afford, through his insurance as a member of the sheet metal workers union, to get his son the treatment he needed when he was addicted to the painkiller Percocet.
But a friend of his, who worked in a different field and whose child also needed help, was quoted an unaffordable price.
De la Cruz said for a lot of people in this country and state, things aren’t working out.
He mentioned a 22-year-old local police officer who wishes he was born a few years earlier so he could have a pension.
“When I’m speaking about Connecticut and how we’re going to make it better, better can’t mean that we’re ripping down the people that are doing all the work for us,” de la Cruz said.

“Better can’t mean that our future generations can’t retire.” As he walked around the Capitol and the Legislative Office Building with a reporter after the speech, people, from lobbyists to staff to legislators, enthusiastically greeted him and complimented him on his speech, with state Rep.
Anne Hughes, D-Easton, calling him a "rock star." “It was awesome,” said state Rep.
“You shared so much that was so relevant to why people should vote for this.

I’m proud of you.” In the halls of Hartford, de la Cruz smiles and jokes at times with colleagues to share a moment of levity, but also takes time to listen to serious issues and offer his support to proposed bills.
House Speaker Matthew Ritter said de la Cruz brings life experience on labor issues and manufacturing and construction to the legislature, and that diversity of perspective is really important.
Ritter said everybody smiles when they see de la Cruz, and he’s probably one of the most popular members of the chamber and well-liked by all sides.
“He’s a breath of fresh air,” Ritter said.
“He’s about as honest as they come, and we’re going to miss him.” Continuing his work At a recent town hall-style meeting at the Thrive55+ Active Living Center in Groton with state Reps.

Christine Conley, D-Groton, and Anthony Nolan, D-New London, and a small group of residents, de la Cruz reflected that this will be the last year the 41st District will include parts of Groton and New London.
Next year, it will include parts of Groton and Stonington, and he’s not running again for the seat.
But he said he’s not here to talk about that: he’s here to talk about his work on the Veterans Affairs, Aging and Housing committees.
He spoke about how even in communities such as New London and Groton, that have met the state’s affordable housing goal, what's considered affordable doesn’t seem to match up with people’s salaries.

The Housing Committee is working so that Connecticut's communities don't become like San Diego, where people who grew up there can't afford to live next door to their parents or send their kids to the same school they had attended.
He also encouraged people who know a veteran in need to reach out.
He then answered residents' questions, from his thoughts on tolls to how to best keep up to date on legislative votes.
De la Cruz told The Day that as he leaves the legislature, he hopes to leave the impression to look at things from other people's points of view.
For example, rather than increasing penalties for crime, he thinks it's important to get to the root issue and try to solve problems early on in a person's life.

Speaking from a place of truth Cheryl Biekert, vice president of Community Speaks Out, said de la Cruz speaks from a place of truth and a place of passion, whether he’s on the floor in session or facilitating a Community Speaks Out family support group meeting.
“He just represents everyday people and the struggles and triumphs that we each have in our daily lives,” she said.
Linda Labbe, another Community Speaks Out board member and co-founder, said de la Cruz has spread awareness about the reality of how many people are affected by the opioid crisis.
“He’s just a down-to-earth person, and he just gets things across to people and makes them see things in a different way,” she said.
During support group meetings, men sometimes have a harder time opening up, but de la Cruz is really good at talking to the fathers because he lived the same experience with his son, Labbe added.
His wife, Tammy, said people rely on him for his honesty in the room on how their family was affected by addiction.
"He wants to support and encourage and be that lifeline to people in that support group," she said.

De la Cruz said when he first found out his son was addicted and started learning about how deep addiction was in the community, he was horrified to see conditions at some of the sober homes, without the opioid overdose-reversal medication Narcan or things such as fire extinguishers and proper lighting.
In addition to de la Cruz's work in Hartford on sober homes, Community Speaks Out became a certifying body for such facilities to ensure they were meeting basic standards.
At a recent event, Community Speaks Out received a $# check from Holmgren Subaru.
De la Cruz reflected for a moment on how the donation will help cover sober living expenses for many people or costs of youth group meetings.
As one of the faces and voices of Community Speaks Out, de la Cruz has raised awareness about the opioid crisis in Hartford, Tammy de la Cruz said.
While a bill he proposed to label opioid prescriptions as addictive on a 1 through 10 rating system did not pass, it still raised awareness, she said.
He’s also a regular person who speaks his mind and didn’t vote on what he thought would help him get reelected, but on what he thinks is right, she said.

“One thing I love about him is when there’s a really tough vote, he will call me, and he struggles because he understands that every vote matters, and all I would tell him is ‘you have to put your head down at night and sleep on your pillow, and as long as you can live with yourself, you know that you did the right thing,’ and that’s how he voted every time,” she said.
Nolan said the conversation around opioids is de la Cruz’s legacy.
He brought a tragic issue that happened in his family not only to Hartford, but also breathes it daily in the community.
He and his wife and Community Speaks Out educate people to understand why it’s so necessary to help fight the opioid issue.

With their son being a victim of violence, they also lend their support to other victims, said Nolan, who recalled seeing Joe and Tammy de la Cruz at a candlelight vigil held by Safe Futures, a regional organization that assists victims of domestic violence.
“They were there crying, but yet they were there being helpful to those other victims who were recently inundated with violent crimes, and it’s just amazing to watch them be there,” Nolan said.
“How they can work through their own personal pain to help other families is huge, and they’re not going to stop doing that at all,” Conley added.
De la Cruz said he may run again for the legislature when he’s retired in the future.
But when this term ends, he will take a step back from politics for the time being and continue being involved in the community he loves.
He said everywhere he goes in Groton, he sees someone he knows, and his love for his community was solidified by the outpouring of support for his family when his son was murdered.
De la Cruz’s hobbies include bowling and he hosts a TV show, called “Born Political,” in which he interviews different people in the community.
He is interested in getting involved with coaching youth baseball again.
He also will focus on Community Speaks Out — “That’s something that will never leave me,” de la Cruz said.
The organization is a part of him and his wife and keeps them close to their son as they help other people through him.

De la Cruz said people come up to them and say they’re still sober because of the night at Fitch High School that Joey Gingerella told his story. k.drelich@theday.com The original article can be found at: https://theday.com/news/493303/joe-de-la-cruz-a-breath-of-fresh-air-in-hartford/# Recent Posts See All Can Dems oust Somers and claim another Senate seat?

PAUL – The Minnesota Chamber of Commerce Leadership Fund PAC recently endorsed Jon Koznick for the Minnesota House in the November 3 general election.

“Employers and employees are facing uncertain times, and need support from Minnesota’s decision makers to ensure our economy returns to full strength,” said Laura Bordelon, treasurer of the Leadership Fund PAC.
“Jon understands what it takes to grow Minnesota in today’s challenging economy.

This endorsement reflects his willingness to support Minnesota employers and employees in House District 58A and around the state.” The Leadership Fund PAC Board uses specific criteria to determine its endorsements including responses to its candidate questionnaire, leadership on key business issues and voting records of incumbent candidates.
Click here for a list of all candidates endorsed by the Minnesota Chamber of Commerce Leadership Fund PAC.
The Minnesota Chamber of Commerce Leadership Fund PAC is a state-registered political action committee.
The PAC represents supporters from across Minnesota organized to promote the election of pro-business, pro-jobs candidates to offices in Minnesota state government.

added: Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT More Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT AM I IN NEW YORK'S 6TH CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT?
Short answer: check by your address, not by your neighborhood.
Queens is split across several congressional districts, and the lines run between streets rather than around neighborhoods.
It is common for two people who would both say they live in the same part of Queens to be in different districts.
Zip codes do not settle it either.
A single zip code in Queens can fall across more than one congressional district, so a zip code lookup will sometimes give you an answer that is close but not correct.
How to check properly Use the voter lookup at voterlookup.elections.ny.gov and enter your address.
It will return your congressional district along with your state senate, assembly and city council districts.
If you are registered to vote, this is also the fastest way to confirm your registration is current.

Neighborhoods in the 6th District The district takes in Flushing, Forest Hills, Rego Park, Elmhurst, Fresh Meadows, Jackson Heights, Kew Gardens Hills, Bayside, Auburndale, Oakland Gardens, Maspeth, Middle Village and Woodside, along with Briarwood, East Flushing, Electchester, Hillcrest, Hollis Hills, Jamaica Hills, Pomonok, Queensboro Hill, Utopia and Willets Point.
If your address comes back as New York's 6th Congressional District , Joseph Chou is running to represent you.

added: Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT More Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT How to contact your representative in Queens If you need help with a federal matter, a passport, immigration paperwork, Social Security, veterans' benefits or a problem with a federal agency, your representative's district office is the place to start.
That service is free and it is available to everyone in the district, whoever they voted for.
Finding the right office First find your district by entering your address at voterlookup.elections.ny.gov.
Then look up your representative in the House directory at house.gov, which lists a Washington office and one or more district offices for every member.
For a case that needs local help, the district office is usually the faster one.
What to have ready Your full address, so the office can confirm you are a constituent.
A short written summary of the problem and what you have already tried.
Offices handle a high volume of requests, and the clearer the first message is, the quicker it moves.

Contacting the Joseph Chou campaign If you live in New York's 6th Congressional District and you want to reach the campaign directly, with a question, an offer to help or a problem you think is not being heard, you can get in touch through the contact page.

This link leads off-site. es October 8, 2026 Governor Josh Shapiro Decisively Wins Gubernatorial Debate, Highlighting His Track Record of Getting Stuff Done and Commitment to Fighting for All Pennsylvanians HARRISBURG, PA – Tonight on the debate stage, Governor Josh Shapiro won a decisive victory as he delivered a strong performance, highlighted his record of getting stuff done for our Commonwealth, and made clear that he will always keep fighting for all Pennsylvanians.

“Governor Shapiro delivered a clear win tonight on the debate stage — highlighting his record of listening, showing up, and getting stuff done for our working families all across our Commonwealth,” said Shapiro for Pennsylvania Campaign Manager Lisa Swanson .

“Tonight’s debate demonstrated the real contrast in this race – a choice between a Governor who fights for all Pennsylvanians, and a 100% MAGA loyalist like Stacy Garrity who will continue to support Donald Trump no matter how much it hurts our Commonwealth.

As we head into the final month of this race, the Governor will continue to drive the growing momentum and strength behind this campaign as we keep working to earn every vote and win up and down the ballot in November.” From creating nearly 29,000 jobs and cutting taxes 10 times for our seniors, small businesses, and working families, to supporting law enforcement and putting public safety first, to securing historic funding for public education and apprenticeships, Governor Shapiro has delivered real results to move Pennsylvania forward.
The Governor is fighting for all Pennsylvanians to have the freedom to chart their own course and the opportunity to succeed — and tonight’s debate underscored that commitment.

This link leads off-site. es October 14, 2026 Governor Shapiro Fired Up Democrats at the Lackawanna County Democrats Pre-Election Dinner PENNSYLVANIA – Last night, Governor Josh Shapiro delivered the keynote address at the Lackawanna County Democrats’ pre-election dinner, where he laid out the stakes of this year’s midterm election and highlighted his record of delivering for working families across Pennsylvania.
During his address, Governor Shapiro thanked Lackawanna Democrats for their work to elect Democratic leaders — like Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti — up and down the ballot this November.
In these midterms, Pennsylvanians have an opportunity to put a check on Donald Trump and his enablers’ disastrous agenda that is making everything more expensive.

The Governor also spoke to what more his Administration will be able to deliver — from raising the minimum wage, to building more housing, to codifying abortion access in Pennsylvania — by electing Brian Wrightson to the state Senate.

The Governor has been clear that these midterm elections will be a referendum on the chaos, cruelty, and corruption coming from Washington, D.C. — and here in Pennsylvania, Governor Shapiro is leading the fight to win up and down the ballot this November to get even more stuff done and keep moving the Commonwealth forward.
Read below for highlights from Governor Shapiro’s keynote address at the Lackawanna County Democrats’ pre-election dinner and watch here : “Chaos and cruelty and corruption.
You see the corruption play out every day in Washington.

The kind of corruption we see from your Congressman, where he’s quite literally trading stocks on private information that is available only to him as a congressman… The kind of corruption we see from a president who’s put $2 billion in his pocket during his time as president… He has this privilege to sit behind the desk in the Oval Office, and instead of thinking about how to put money in your pocket, instead of thinking about how to make sure you have access to healthcare, instead of figuring out ways to make you safer and better off in your community, he’s thinking about how to enrich himself and his spoiled kids.
“This room has the power to be that check on Donald Trump’s chaos and cruelty and corruption.
Everything he’s been able to do, the damage that he has inflicted upon us is because he’s had a rubber stamp in Congress.

The people who know better, but look the other way… Republicans have the majority down there in the Congress by about four seats, and we have four competitive congressional seats right here in Pennsylvania, and I’m working my tail off to make sure all four of them win.

“You’ve got someone who’s turned Scranton around, someone who has stepped into messy situations and figured out how to make them better, someone who has led with integrity, and someone who I know knows how to get the job done, and most importantly, someone who will go to Washington prepared to be that check on Trump’s chaos and cruelty and corruption… That’s a lot of power that all of you have to bring a trifecta to Harrisburg, to make sure we got a check in Washington, and maybe even a reelected governor while you’re at it.
And I would argue that it’s a power you have and a responsibility on your shoulders to do this work… Let’s not let Donald Trump steal our hope, take away our optimism.
I believe that brighter days are ahead.

“It starts on November 3rd with the decisions that we make, and over the next 21 days, it matters how much work you put into this… The Pennsylvania way is to step up and do our part, and I know you can.” ### Donate By Mail Shapiro for Pennsylvania PO Box 22635 Philadelphia, PA 19110 Paid for by Shapiro for Pennsylvania By participating, you agree to the terms & privacy policy for recurring autodialed marketing messages from Josh Shapiro to the phone number you provide.

added: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/720874113_122133122373156370_8072487203416253360_n.jpg|My senior year I was with a group of friends–the Top 10 students at Olympus High school in academics. They all decided to go sledding on baking sheets off the roof of the pagoda church. They got arrested! I didn’t go because I knew it was against the law. I regret it to this day. That slopey roof tempts me every time I drive past it. Anyone else have great memories of the pagoda church?

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/725860763_122133994803156370_6605839905600577267_n.jpg|A neighbor just shared dropping off their ballot with a friend. Love this idea! What a great reminder that voting plans are often easier when we help each other remember. So remind a friend, family member or colleague! Have you made your voting plan yet? To be sure your vote arrives, for USPS, mail by Thursday, June 18th. Or place your ballot by 8pm on Tuesday, June 23rd at any official voting location or ballot box.
alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/726964031_122134065705156370_3864716267310539945_n.jpg|This is the kind of tough I want to be.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/729784946_122134352733156370_6558106583707996862_n.jpg|ELECTION DAY is happening tomorrow (6/23) from 7:00 am - 8:00 pm! Your vote matters—this election will determine who represents Utah House District 34. You can drop off your completed ballot at any official ballot drop box or city hall location. If you'd prefer to vote in person, nearby voting locations include: • Holladay Library • Millcreek Library • Murray City Hall Bring your kids—it only takes a few minutes, and it's a great opportunity to show them how civic participation works. Don't forget to pick up an "I Voted" sticker! If you need a Democratic primary ballot, you can request one when voting in person. https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/clerk/elections/vote-in-person/vote-centers/

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/729889757_122134509333156370_5175868400197705484_n.jpg|It will be an honor to represent you in the Utah State Legislature. Thank you for participating in Utah’s primary election and the democratic process. Thank you to my opponent, Erin, for running a positive and respectful campaign. She has a strong record of working on important issues, and I look forward to opportunities to work together in serving our community. I’m deeply grateful to the hundreds of people who contributed to the success of this campaign. Your support has meant so much to me. You showed me once again what is possible when people come together around a shared purpose. When each of us helps, even in small ways, it can add up to something great. I ran because I believe we can solve Utah’s toughest challenges when we listen to each other, work together, and invest wisely in our future. I am a product of my community’s investment in me, and I’m honored by the trust you have given me. Together, we can do real good for our community and for the state of Utah.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/729988337_122134601073156370_6007462276806037196_n.jpg|This campaign would not have been possible without the incredible volunteers, friends, family members, and neighbors who gave their time, energy, and support along the way. These photos capture just a small part of the effort that so many people put into this campaign. I am grateful for every conversation, every hour volunteered, and every person who helped make this journey possible. Thank you for being part of it.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/723126196_1043722368602776_2204617650329259691_n.jpg|I knew exactly what each person did for me. I felt that gratitude deeply and hope you felt it too. I wish every person could get the experience of asking people to show up for them in a big way, and having people answer the call. Surreal. Thank you to everyone who helped. Now let’s go solve the problems of the world! 😉. Thanks to @steinwayutah for donating this absolutly gorgeous space and to Mark Cheney for bringing the greatest jazz trio on Utah!
alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/830612756_1387437697789561_3700057037594409156_n.jpg|Seriously—how can you NOT want to care for it?
alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/722956143_17885866269603379_9177022523377245697_n.jpg|One of the many times when a student email turned into a full blown movement!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/725226880_17885526849603379_4500026497649169622_n.jpg|Since 40% of our taxes go to k-12 education, understanding the state budget became crucial for me as a school board member. When I really looked at the budget as a whole, I started to understand why legislators were trying to dip their hands into education funding. A close study revealed that the revenue sources for our state were changing, which means we really need to restructure our budget planning in general.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/725946751_17885866278603379_3080018628440497471_n.jpg|This campaign is about bringing people together. I've focused on issues that matter to District 34, including affordability, water, education, and ensuring our community has a voice in important decisions. More information is available at JulieJacksonForUtah.com. Please vote for me on June 23!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/726838744_17886293979603379_1615221614946012809_n.jpg|I loved problem solving with the Millcreek Youth Council about how we can get our younger voters out to the ballot box. They had great ideas and are so well-informed. Now to see if we can make some headway on this Tuesday! Everyone go vote!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/728795015_17886067032603379_4282897175978374070_n.jpg|I cannot say enough about how much I love Voices for Utah Children. The goal of this organization is to be a voice for kids. They speak through the eyes of kids in each Utah community, in their unique circumstances, using strong data. added: Kitchen Table Solutions Tour Media Blog Issues Volunteer Yard Sign Request Newsletter Sign Up Donate Buller Launches New Ad “Abuse” Oct 14, 2026 Back to Blog October 14, 2026 Syracuse, NY — Kailee Buller for Congress today released “Abuse,” a new :30 TV ad contrasting John Mannion’s record with Buller’s plan to lower taxes and energy bills.
“We can’t take any more of John Mannion’s abuse,” Buller says in the ad.

“I’ll cut your taxes and lower your energy bills.” WATCH THE AD HERE Mannion’s Record In 2024, three former staffers published a letter accusing Mannion of creating a hostile work environment in his State Senate office.
The investigator’s report has never been made public .
In Albany, Mannion voted to fast-track industrial wind and solar projects , phase out gas-powered cars , curtail natural gas service , and ban gas hookups in new buildings .
New York’s own energy officials now say those mandates could add more than $4,000 a year to household energy bills, yet Mannion still backs the “lofty energy goals” behind them.
POLITICO has highlighted NY-22 as a race where energy costs have become the defining issue.
In Washington, Mannion voted against the 2025 tax law that stopped a scheduled tax increase on middle-class families and cut taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
Kailee’s Plan Kailee Buller has signed a no new taxes pledge and released a five-point energy plan to repeal Albany’s mandates, expand reliable American energy, and bring utility bills down.

removed: Kitchen Table Solutions Tour Media Blog Issues Volunteer Yard Sign Request Newsletter Sign Up Donate Kailee Buller Agrees to Second Debate with Central Current & WAER August 24, 2026 Auburn, NY — Kailee Buller , candidate for New York’s 22nd Congressional District, has accepted an invitation to participate in a second congressional debate, this one hosted by Central Current and WAER.
The organizations have proposed Monday, October 19th at 6:00 pm for the debate.
“Voters keep asking whether John Mannion will actually debate me.
He should.
After years of backing policies that have driven up energy bills and taxes on New Yorkers, he has an atrocious record to defend,” said Buller.
“I’m ready to stand on a stage, answer tough questions and defend exactly where I stand.
John Mannion should have to do the same.” Organizations and media outlets interested in hosting a debate should contact [email protected] .
Background: Kailee Buller is an Auburn native, working mother of three, and former Chief of Staff at the U.S.
Department of Agriculture, where she helped lead a department of more than 100,000 employees and a budget exceeding $200 billion.
She is running for Congress to lower costs, support working families and farmers, and bring accountability and common sense back to Washington.

added: Kitchen Table Solutions Tour Media Blog Issues Volunteer Yard Sign Request Newsletter Sign Up Donate POLITICO Puts Spotlight on NY-22 as Mannion’s Costly Climate Record Becomes Key Issue Jul 16, 2026 Back to Blog Auburn, NY — In a new report , POLITICO highlights New York’s 22nd Congressional District as a race where costly energy and climate policies have become the defining issue.
The article cites Kailee Buller’s push to overrule New York’s costly climate laws, stop forced wind and solar projects on rural land, fast-track nuclear power, and lower utility bills.

The report noted Buller’s recent message from the site of a proposed wind farm, where she warned that New York Democrats are putting “pet projects over our pocketbooks.” “John Mannion owns this costly climate agenda,” Buller said.
“He sided with Albany Democrats and their “lofty goals” while families got crushed by higher bills and rural communities got targeted for wind and solar projects.

I’ll fight against these climate laws, protect our farmland, and lower energy costs.” Read the excerpt below: 5 New York House races where energy policy could matter Candidates across the Empire State are battling over rising utility bills and the future of nuclear, wind and solar energy projects.
22nd District Oberacker isn’t the only Republican challenger running against New York’s renewable energy policies.

Kailee Buller, a former Department of Agriculture official in the Trump administration, is promising to protect rural areas from wind and solar development, which has been a USDA priority under Secretary Brooke Rollins.
“Wondering why your energy bills are up over $4,000 annually this year,” she said in a recent video standing at the site of a planned wind farm.
The figure comes from a state estimate published this year of potential impacts from New York’s Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act in the next decade.
“Democrats in New York are putting their pet projects over our pocketbooks.

“Let’s vote New York Democrats out of office this November, repeal the climate law, stop these windmills and lower energy costs.” In a statement, Buller said she’d push in Congress for laws to override the state’s climate law, fast-track nuclear power and reform permitting for infrastructure like natural gas pipelines.

title.after: Standing at NY-22 Wind Farm, Kailee Buller Calls for Repeal of the New York Climate Law Which Has Sent CNY Energy Costs Soaring - Kailee Buller for Congress

added: Kitchen Table Solutions Tour Media Blog Issues Volunteer Yard Sign Request Newsletter Sign Up Donate Standing at NY-22 Wind Farm, Kailee Buller Calls for Repeal of the New York Climate Law Which Has Sent CNY Energy Costs Soaring Apr 29, 2026 Back to Blog AUBURN, NY — In a video released today , congressional candidate Kailee Buller (NY-22) blasted New York’s Climate Law, which is causing Central New York families to face unprecedented utility bills at a time when the state is already having an affordability crisis.
According to a recent New York State memo , the law is projected to increase energy bills an additional $4,000 per household.
Buller drew a sharp contrast with her opponent John Mannion, who maintained the Climate Law while in Albany and has continued to defend it as a Congressional Representative.

At a recent town hall, Mannion doubled down, praising the climate law’s “lofty goals.” Buller said, “Utility bills are out of control in New York because Albany politicians like John Mannion and Kathy Hochul have put their pet projects over our pocketbooks by striping us of energy options which have resulted in higher costs, more reliance on foreign energy sources, and weaker grids.
Unless we act, the financial strain facing CNY families will only get worse.
We don’t want bans and mandates, we want reliable energy options and lower costs.

As your representative I will use common sense, honesty, and call out politicians- regardless of party when they are wrong.” Kailee Buller laid out the following 5 actions to lower costs for consumers and ensure our New York energy supply is controlled by Americans not foreign entities: 1.) Albany politicians must repeal the broken climate law including foreign wind and solar projects that were recently mandated by Albany in Scipio and Venice 2.) Albany politicians must revisit their reckless bans on fracking and natural gas.
If the state fails to lift these bans, Congress should pass legislation that Buller will support to stop Albany from stripping energy options away from consumers.
3.) Fast track nuclear expansion at the local, state, and federal levels.
4.) Reform permitting at the local, state, and federal levels to bring on new energy infrastructure like natural gas pipelines as quickly as possible while protecting people and the environment.
5.) Full transparency into our current energy suppliers is needed coupled with a long-term plan to invest in key American and New York energy sources through tax incentives.
Unfortunately, the two leading utility providers in CNY – National Grid and NYSEG have significant interests in foreign governments.
Foreign corporations and foreign governments should not own American utility companies – this results in higher costs and less reliability for us.
These actions that are both short and long term measures coupled together will help lower costs for families, strengthen our American energy infrastructure, and support good-paying union jobs.
Kailee Buller, an Auburn native and working mom of three is focused on driving results and lowering costs to the community she grew up in.

added: Re-Elect Karilyn Brown Contact Donate Re-Elect Karilyn Brown Contact Donate Privacy Policy Thank you for interacting with Karilyn Brown for Arkansas State Representative (“we,” “us,” or “our”).
We are committed to protecting your personal information and your right to privacy.
If you have any questions or concerns about our policy, or our practices regarding your personal information, please contact us at karillynbrownar.com/contact/.
When you visit our website coleforcommissioner.com and use our services, you trust us with your personal information.
We take your privacy very seriously.
In this privacy policy, we explain what information we collect, how we use it, and what rights you have in relation to it.
If there are any terms in this privacy policy that you do not agree with, please discontinue use of our Sites and services.
This privacy policy applies to all information collected through our website karilynbrownar.com and/or any related services, sales, marketing, or events (collectively, the “Services”).
Please read this privacy policy carefully, as it will help you make informed decisions about providing your personal information to us.
We collect personal information that you voluntarily provide when you request information about us or our products and services, participate in activities on the Services, or otherwise contact us.
The personal information we collect depends on how you interact with us and the Services.
It can include: Publicly Available Personal Information.
We may collect first name, last name, phone numbers, email addresses, current and former addresses, and other similar data.
We collect passwords, password hints, and similar security information for authentication and account access.
All personal information that you provide must be true, complete, and accurate, and you must notify us of any changes.
Information automatically collected We automatically collect certain information when you visit, use, or navigate the Services.

This information does not reveal your specific identity (like your name or contact details), but may include device and usage information (e.g., IP address, browser/device characteristics, operating system, language preferences, referring URLs, device name, country, location, and information about when and how you use our Services).
This information is needed for security, internal analytics, and reporting.
HOW DO WE USE YOUR INFORMATION?
We use personal information collected via our Services for the following purposes, relying on the appropriate legal bases indicated: To send you marketing and promotional communications.
We may use the personal information you provide for our own marketing purposes, in accordance with your marketing preferences.
You can opt out of our marketing emails at any time (see “WHAT ARE YOUR PRIVACY RIGHTS” below).
We may use your information to develop and display content and advertising tailored to your interests and/or location, and to measure its effectiveness.
We may use your information to request feedback and to contact you about your experience with our Services.
As a political organization, we may also use your information to provide you with information about candidates, elections, and issues we support.
We may need to disclose or process personal information under specific circumstances, such as: Consent: If you have given us specific consent for a particular use.
Legitimate Interests: When it is necessary to achieve our legitimate business interests.
Performance of a Contract: Where we have entered a contract with you and need your data to fulfill its terms.
Legal Obligations: Where we are legally required to comply with law (e.g., in response to a court order or subpoena).

Vital Interests: Where we believe it is necessary to investigate, prevent, or take action regarding potential policy violations, fraud, or illegal activities, or as evidence in litigation in which we are involved.
Text messaging opt-in data (including consent and related personal information) will not be sold or otherwise shared, except if required by law.
HOW LONG DO WE KEEP YOUR INFORMATION?

We only keep your personal information for as long as it is necessary for the purposes described in this privacy policy, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law (e.g., for tax, accounting, or other legal requirements).
When we have no ongoing legitimate business need to process your personal information, we will delete or anonymize it.

If deletion or anonymization is not possible (e.g., because it is stored in backup archives), we will store your personal information securely and isolate it from any further processing until deletion is feasible.
HOW DO WE KEEP YOUR INFORMATION SAFE?
We have implemented appropriate security measures designed to protect your personal information.
However, no electronic transmission over the internet or information storage technology can be guaranteed to be 100% secure, so please only access our Services within a secure environment.
DO WE COLLECT INFORMATION FROM MINORS?
By using the Services, you represent that you are at least 18 years old or the parent/guardian of a minor who is using our Services with your consent.
If we learn we have collected personal information from a user under 18 without verification of parental consent, we will deactivate the account and delete such data.
If you become aware of any data we have collected from children under 18, please contact us at karilynbrownar.com/contact/.

If you have questions about your personal information or wish to update, correct, or delete it, please contact us at karilynbrownar.com/contact/ CONTROLS FOR DO-NOT-TRACK FEATURES Most web browsers and some mobile operating systems/apps include a Do-Not-Track (“DNT”) feature you can activate to signal your privacy preference not to have data about your online browsing monitored and collected.
No uniform standard for recognizing and implementing DNT signals currently exists.
We do not respond to DNT browser signals at this time.
If a future standard is adopted, we will follow it and update this privacy policy accordingly.
Third-Party Services Text opt-in consent data will not be sold or shared with third parties for promotional or marketing purposes.
Except as otherwise stated in this Privacy Policy, we don’t sell, trade, rent, or otherwise share for marketing purposes your Personal Information with third parties without your consent.
Our website may contain links to third-party websites or services.
We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of such third parties.
We encourage you to review the privacy policies of those third parties when accessing their websites or services.

Compliance with Applicable Laws and Guidelines Our practices for collecting and processing opt-in data—including phone numbers and (if applicable) email addresses—are designed to comply with all applicable laws, rules, and industry guidelines, such as the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), CTIA guidelines, and carrier requirements for 10DLC, toll-free, and short code messaging.

By opting in and providing your personal information, you acknowledge that our methods for obtaining, processing, and storing your data adhere to these regulatory standards, ensuring transparency and compliance in our communications.

EMAIL COMMUNICATIONS TERMS & CONDITIONS If you provide your email address through our website or other Services, you are opting in to receive recurring email communications from Karilyn Brown for Arkansas State Representative.
These emails may include newsletters, updates, donation requests, event invitations, and promotional information.
By providing your email address, you consent to the collection and use of your email in accordance with this policy.
You may opt out of receiving marketing and promotional emails at any time by following the unsubscribe instructions included in each email.
We do not share, rent, or sell your email address with third parties, except as required by law.
DO WE MAKE UPDATES TO THIS POLICY?
We may update this privacy policy from time to time.
The updated version will be indicated by an updated “Revised” date and will be effective as soon as it’s posted.
If we make material changes, we may notify you by prominently posting a notice of such changes or by sending a notification.
We encourage you to review this privacy policy frequently.
If you have any questions or comments about this policy, you may contact us at: karilynbrownar.com/contact/ Donate Paid for by Karilyn Brown for State Representative

The message was loud and clear: No branch of government should be above oversight, accountability, or the will of the people.
Elected officials work for the people, not the other way around.
When an overwhelming majority of voters demand transparency, Beacon Hill has a responsibility to listen and act.
If elected, I will always follow the will of the voters—regardless of my personal opinions or party affiliation.
My responsibility will be to represent the people of this district and honor their voice.
And the will of the voters must NEVER be ignored. — Kari MacRae Republican Candidate for State Senate Plymouth & Barnstable District C.T.E.

added.text: SB0632/HB0709 – Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - Small Business and Nonprofit Health Insurance Subsidies Program - Workgroup
SB357/HB424 – Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for All Marylanders Now Act
SB802/HB814 – Protect Maryland Health Care Act of 2019

added: Show Menu About Priorities Services Volunteer Donate Yard Sign Spanish | Korean | Chinese twitter facebook instagram Skip to main content Healthcare The pandemic years underscored the necessity of improving healthcare access, affordability, and quality for every Marylander.
Still, 1-in-20 Marylanders are uninsured, and prescription drugs remain inaccessible to many seniors and low-income families.
I have fought to establish a Prescription Drug Affordability Board to prevent dramatic price increases, and voted to cap insulin copays at $30/month.

I sponsored legislation that required the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to draft a strategy to scale our Small Business Health Options (SHOP) program to provide affordable insurance coverage for small employers and their employees.

Legislation I have passed includes: ** SB357/HB424 – Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for All Marylanders Now Act (2025) Strengthens the authority of Maryland’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board and requires the Board to establish a process for setting upper payment limits on certain high-cost prescription drugs in special circumstances, like when a drug enters a shortage. ** SB165/HB204 – Student-Athlete Mental Health Training (2024) Requires coaches at Maryland public schools to complete mental health training in addition to existing physical health training to help coaches recognize signs of mental illness, behavioral distress, and substance abuse among student-athletes.

SB705/HB728 – Access to Care Act (2024) Establishes the Qualified Resident Enrollment Program to help eligible Maryland residents enroll in qualified health insurance plans through the Maryland Health Benefits Exchange, expanding access to affordable health coverage for residents who may otherwise face barriers to enrollment. ** SB0341/HB0477 – Reproductive Health Services Plans (2023) Requires health insurers to provide coverage for reproductive health services and establishes requirements designed to protect access to covered reproductive care. ** SB0632/HB0709 – Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - Small Business and Nonprofit Health Insurance Subsidies Program - Workgroup (2022) Required the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to draft a strategy to scale our Small Business Health Options (SHOP) program to provide affordable insurance coverage for small employers and their employees.

SB802/HB814 – Protect Maryland Health Care Act of 2019 (2019) Makes it easier for uninsured Marylanders to access affordable health coverage by creating the Maryland Easy Enrollment Health Insurance Program, which allows residents to check a box when filing their taxes to see if they qualify for health insurance or financial assistance. (**Denotes Legislation I Sponsored) Friends of Katie Fry Hester, Treasurer: Margaret E.

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases Katie Hobbs and John Giles Tour Ironworkers Local 75 Wednesday, October 14, 2026 [CLICK FOR HIGH-QUALITY PHOTOS] PHOENIX – Today, Gov.

Katie Hobbs and her running mate, former Mesa Mayor John Giles, toured the Ironworkers 75 facility, spoke with President of the Arizona Building Trades Council Jason Sangster and Apprenticeship Coordinator Aaron McDonald, met with several apprentices, and tried their hand at welding.
“As a proud union member, making sure that working families have a real voice in their government is personal to me,” said Gov.

“By partnering with organized labor, we have delivered historic results for Arizona’s workers, investing in efforts to double state apprenticeships, creating Arizona’s first Workplace Heat Stress State Emphasis Plan, and blocking legislative attempts to erode labor protections.

I’ll always stand with workers who keep our state running, because they deserve a government that works for them.” Since taking office, Katie has delivered on the issues that matter most to working Arizonans: lowering costs and expanding access to necessities like healthcare and childcare.
This year, she signed a bipartisan budget that provides $1.4 billion in tax relief for hardworking Arizonans, including eliminating taxes on tips and overtime pay.
She has delivered paid parental leave , childcare investments , and healthcare expansions for working families , and canceled $1 billion in medical debt for nearly 700,000 Arizonans.

She has worked to deliver for Arizona workers and ensure labor has a seat at the table, investing in efforts to double state apprenticeships through the BuildItAZ initiative, launching a first-in-the-nation Workplace Heat Stress State Emphasis Plan to protect outdoor workers from Arizona’s extreme heat, and blocking legislative efforts to erode workers’ protections.

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases Katie Hobbs Launches Multi-Million Dollar Statewide Ad Campaign With English- and Spanish-Language Ads Wednesday, May 27, 2026 PHOENIX – Today, Gov.

Katie Hobbs launched the first television, radio, and digital ads of her reelection campaign as part of a multi-million dollar statewide media campaign focused on lowering costs and fighting for working families across Arizona.

The campaign’s first major paid media push includes both English- and Spanish-language ads across all platforms, reflecting an aggressive and historically early investment in communicating directly with Arizonans in every corner of the state.
This robust communication nearly six months before the November election demonstrates the strength of Katie Hobbs’ campaign and the broad support behind her Arizona First leadership.
Katie has outraised the entire Republican field combined over five consecutive filing periods and holds nearly seven times as much cash on hand as her closest Republican opponent.
Alongside “Work,” the campaign is also launching “No Se Rinde,” the campaign’s first Spanish-language ad.

Both spots highlight how Katie Hobbs’ working-class background — from driving for Uber to support her family to helping domestic violence survivors rebuild their lives through social work — motivates her as governor to fight to lower costs, erase medical debt, reduce prescription drug prices, and create good-paying jobs across Arizona.

“From working fast-food jobs and driving for Uber to helping families in need as a social worker, Katie Hobbs understands what Arizona families are going through because she’s lived it herself,” said Michael Beyer, Communications Director for Elect Katie Hobbs.
“That’s why, as governor, Katie has focused on lowering costs by expanding school meals, reducing utility bills, and making housing more affordable across the state.
