El anuncio celebra la ética de trabajo, las ganas de superarse y la determinación de las familias trabajadoras de Arizona, y explica por qué la gobernadora Hobbs ha hecho de su misión apoyar a quienes son el motor de la economía de Arizona.

Los esfuerzos de la gobernadora se traducen en ahorros reales que ayudan a las familias a hacer rendir su presupuesto, al trabajar con ambos partidos para recortar impuestos a las pequeñas empresas, eliminar los impuestos sobre las propinas, las horas extra y el alquiler, financiar los almuerzos escolares para que ningún niño pase hambre y cancelar mil millones de dólares en deudas médicas para casi 700,000 arizonenses.

“Katie Hobbs entiende que cada dólar cuenta para las familias en Arizona, y ha trabajado con ambos partidos para ayudarles a quedarse con una mayor parte del dinero que tanto les cuesta ganar,” dijo Michael Beyer, director de comunicaciones de la campaña de Hobbs.

Estos nuevos anuncios se suman a la compra multimillonaria en español anunciada previamente, que destaca cómo el origen de clase trabajadora de Katie Hobbs —desde manejar Uber para sostener a su familia hasta ayudar a sobrevivientes de violencia doméstica a reconstruir sus vidas como trabajadora social— la motiva como gobernadora a luchar por bajar costos, cancelar deudas médicas, reducir el precio de los medicamentos recetados y crear empleos bien remunerados en todo Arizona.
También lanzó Familias Primero , una coalición de líderes latinos, miembros de la comunidad y funcionarios electos locales que trabajan para lograr su reelección.

title.after: ROUNDUP: Katie Hobbs Crisscrosses State on Arizona First Tour, Meeting with Families, Farmers, Small Businesses, and Healthcare Providers - Katie Hobbs for Governor

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - In the News ROUNDUP: Katie Hobbs Crisscrosses State on Arizona First Tour, Meeting with Families, Farmers, Small Businesses, and Healthcare Providers Wednesday, July 29, 2026 PHOENIX – Last week, Gov.
Katie Hobbs embarked on her Arizona First Tour , crisscrossing the state to hear firsthand the challenges people are facing and share her vision for moving Arizona forward.

From making tortillas at a family-owned restaurant in Yuma to visiting a seventh-generation farm in Cochise County, opening campaign offices, listening to healthcare providers, and meeting with local business owners and supporters, Katie Hobbs traveled across the state to hear directly from Arizonans and highlight her record of lowering costs and growing Arizona’s economy.

The Arizona First Tour brought her to Gilbert , Prescott , Yuma , Scottsdale , Pearce , Sierra Vista , and Tucson , where she met with healthcare professionals, social workers, farmers, restaurant owners, brewers, volunteers, and working families.

Along the way, she heard firsthand how Washington’s cost-hiking agenda—from tariffs driving up the price of essential goods to rising healthcare costs—is affecting Arizona families and small businesses.

Throughout the week, Hobbs visited Alliance Behavioral Care in Gilbert to discuss expanding access to affordable healthcare; met with the owners of Wild Iris Coffee, The Chile Pepper, Tombstone Brewing Company, and the New York Pizza Department to hear how Washington’s tariffs and misguided policies are affecting local businesses; toured Curry Seed & Chile Company with seventh-generation farmer Ed Curry to discuss water security and agriculture; celebrated National Drive-Thru Day at the Burger King where she worked in high school; and opened Copper State Victory coordinated campaign offices in Prescott, Yuma, Scottsdale, and Sierra Vista, continuing to build the grassroots infrastructure needed to win in November.

The tour concluded in Tucson, where Hobbs launched a weekend of action canvass, visited another local small business, and rallied nearly 700 supporters alongside Senator Mark Kelly, former Congresswoman Gabby Giffords, Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva, Mayor Regina Romero, and congressional candidate JoAnna Mendoza, emphasizing the campaign’s momentum and her commitment to continuing to lower costs and deliver for Arizona families.

She met with psychologists, social workers, and administrators there to discuss Medicaid cuts and keep mental health services accessible for Arizonans.
Katie Hobbs: I think these stories just really reinforce why we need to keep fighting for access to care and ensuring that we’re protecting that health care for so many Arizonans who need it.

House candidate Jonathan Nez spoke Wednesday at the grand opening of the Copper State Victory Prescott campaign office.

Copper State Victory describes itself as a coordinated campaign effort focused on reelecting Hobbs, Secretary of State Adrian Fontes and Attorney General Kris Mayes, while supporting Democratic candidates across Arizona.
The Prescott stop is the second on Hobbs’ statewide campaign tour.
“I know you’re here because you know what’s at stake in this election,” Hobbs told the crowd.
“I didn’t leave social work when I ran for office.
I ran for office because too often, as a social worker, I didn’t see our elected leaders fighting for the right people and the right things.

And I realized that if you can’t change policy, you have to change who’s making policy.” Hobbs noted that she is one of two Democratic governors seeking reelection in states carried by President Donald Trump.
“I’m sure you all know he won Arizona with the largest margin of any swing state, 5.5%,” Hobbs said.
“I’m also the only Democratic governor in a toss-up race in 2022.
We know this race is going to be just as close.
Our electorate here is plus-nine Republican, so that’s a lot to overcome.
I know we can do it.” Nez also criticized Crane and Republican gubernatorial candidate Andy Biggs.
“Both Crane and Biggs voted to reduce taxes for elites in the Big Ugly Bill,” Nez said.
“Crane and Biggs backed budget cuts to Medicaid, making health care more expensive.
And Crane and Biggs voted against a housing bill to make housing cheaper.
“Those two voted against ending the Iran war, making gasoline more expensive, and goods and services prices are skyrocketing as well,” he continued.
“They both supported tariffs, hurting small businesses in and around the state.” KSWT: Gov.
Hobbs hits the campaign trail Anchor: Arizona Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs made her way to Yuma today to rally supporters.
Governor Hobbs made a special stop in Yuma today to speak with a local small business and Yuma County leaders.
Anchor: Her first stop today was at a local restaurant, at The Chile Pepper.
Hobbs spoke with the owners about how rising costs brought on by Washington D.C. have affected their day-to-day operations and their ability to thrive.
Anchor: We had the chance to ask her about her opponent Andy Biggs winning the primary election.
She says the choice on who people would vote for couldn’t be any clearer.

Katie Hobbs: I mean, it’s not really a surprise, and I think Arizonans have a real choice in this election: someone who is focused on delivering for Arizonans, lowering costs, securing the border, creating good-paying jobs, or someone who continues to champion Washington’s agenda and vote against Arizonans every chance he gets.
Telemundo 3 Noticias: Gobernadora Katie Hobbs visita la ciudad Anchor 1: La gobernadora demócrata de Arizona, Katie Hobbs, viajó hoy a Yuma para movilizar a sus simpatizantes.
Nuestro reportero Abraham Retana habló con ella y nos tiene los detalles.

Anchor 2: La gobernadora Hobbs hizo una parada especial hoy en Yuma para conversar con una pequeña empresa local y con líderes del condado de Yuma, su primera parada de hoy fue en el restaurante Chile Pepper, donde habló con los propietarios sobre el aumento de costos provocado por las decisiones de Washington.
Katie Hobbs: No es ninguna sorpresa.

Los habitantes de Arizona tienen una opción real en estas elecciones, alguien que se centra en dar resultados para Arizona, reduciendo costos, asegurando la frontera, creando empleos bien remunerados y alguien que se esté defendiendo de la agenda de Washington.
Anchor 2: Tuvimos la oportunidad de preguntarle sobre la victoria de su oponente Andy Biggs, ella afirma que la elección sobre por quién votar no podría ser más clara.
Katie Hobbs: Lo que he escuchado de los residentes de Arizona es que las alzas de los precios han sido un reto.
Ellos quieren buena educación para sus hijos, una frontera segura, y yo me he enfocado en eso.
Anchor 2: La mandataria estatal también abrió las puertas de su oficina de campaña en Yuma, donde diversos candidatos tendrán un lugar para reunirse con la comunidad.
Kris Mayes: La gobernadora y yo, necesitamos a Yuma que vote.
Necesitamos a los independientes y a los republicanos que voten por nosotros.
Así que vamos a tener gente aquí en la oficina para que impulsen el voto.
Anchor 2: La gobernadora Hobbs enfrentará directamente al representante Andy Biggs en las elecciones generales de noviembre.
Katie Hobbs visits Yuma to rally supporters Gov.
Katie Hobbs (D-Ariz.) visted [sic] Yuma Thursday afternoon to rally supporters.

Hobbs stopped at and toured the Chile Pepper, where she spoke with the owners “about how rising costs brought on by Washington, D.C. policies have affected their day-to-day operations and their ability to thrive.” The governor then attended the grand opening of the Yuma Copper State Victory Office , where she was joined by Charlene Fernandez, chair of the Arizona Democratic Party, and Yuma County Board of Supervisors Chairman Martin Porchas.
Hobbs, who is running for reelection, will face off against Republican candidate Andy Biggs (R-Ariz.) in the November midterm election.
KAWC: Hobbs highlights education priorities, rising costs during Yuma campaign stop Ahead of the opening of her campaign’s Copper State Victory Office in Yuma, Arizona Gov.
Katie Hobbs stopped at Chile Pepper Thursday, where she discussed education priorities, rising costs and other issues facing the state.
Before getting down to business, Hobbs stepped into the kitchen to prepare tortillas, then sat down for lunch with the Gutierrez family, founders of the restaurant.
Over the meal, she listened to their perspectives as small business owners.
Hobbs told the press that some of that conversation focused on how the White House’s tariff policies are driving up the restaurant’s supply costs.
“They employ 170 people here in Yuma, and it’s affecting their customers,” she said.
They’re seeing that in the customer base, and it’s a challenge.” Hobbs used those concerns to pivot to the governor’s race and her Republican opponent, Andy Biggs.
“That’s really the contrast in this election,” she said.

“My opponent is someone who continues to support Washington’s agenda, including tariffs that are raising costs everywhere.” “When I ran for governor, and the way I’ve governed — I’m focused on working with anyone to solve real problems to deliver for Arizonans,” she said.
But I also said, ‘Look, I’m going to be a backstop.
I’m going to stop bills that take away people’s rights, that attack our right to vote, reproductive freedom — things like that.
And that’s what I’ve done.” With the election approaching, Hobbs is taking her case — on education and otherwise — to voters.
Yuma Sun: Governor visits the Chile Pepper, new field office Gov.
Katie Hobbs made a couple of stops in Yuma on Thursday in her bid to retain her public office.
The Democratic is seeking reelection in a race against her Republican opponent, U.S.
Andy Biggs of Arizona’s Fifth Congressional District.
Hobbs’ first stop was at the Chile Pepper, located at 2401 S.
4th Ave, a family-owned restaurant which has been a Yuma staple since 1956.
Andrea Huff of B & G Family Ltd. was ecstatic to have Hobbs visit their restaurant.
“We’re so excited, we’re huge supporters,” Huff said.
“We love that she supports small businesses.” While at the restaurant, Hobbs learned to make some of the restaurant’s food in the kitchen.

Briefly mentioning that she once worked at Burger King, Hobbs washed her hands, put on the Chile Pepper hat and apron, and was shown how to make various Mexican dishes such as beans and cheese by restaurant staff.

Afterward, Hobbs sat down with the Gutierrez family, the founders and long-time owners of the restaurant, to discuss the effects of federal policies out of Washington, D.C., such as tariffs, and how they have affected day-to-day operations of Yuma businesses such as the Chile Pepper.
“We talked about how Washington’s policies are really hurting small businesses,” Hobbs said.
“They’re being hit really hard with their spending because of the tariffs.

And they’re having to make really hard decisions as an employer.” After her stop at the Chile Pepper, Hobbs made her way over to the opening of the Yuma Copper State Victory Office to speak alongside Arizona Democratic Party Chair Charlene Fernandez and Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes.
Hobbs, who only won her previous election by 17,000 votes, stresses that the upcoming race will be close.
“This is going to be a tough race,” Hobbs said to the crowd at the opening.
“I am the only Democratic governor in a toss-up race.” Sierra Herald/Review: Hobbs talks to Herald/Review about rural concerns, Lt.

Katie Hobbs was in Cochise County last Saturday to meet with the owners of two small businesses before recognizing the opening of the Sierra Vista office of Copper State Victory, a statewide get-out-the-vote effort promoted by the Democratic Party.

The governor first stopped at the family-owned Curry Seed & Chile Company farm in Pearce where she met several FFA officers and took part in discussions about water concerns and the impacts of tariffs on farmers and ranchers.
She then visited Tombstone Brewing Company in Sierra Vista to hear from the owners about how rising costs driven by federal policies are affecting their day-to-day operations.

Hobbs finished her time in Cochise County with a short speech to local Democrats gathered to celebrate Copper State Victory’s new headquarters in Sierra Vista, where she also talked about the importance of grassroots volunteer efforts.
Before leaving Cochise County, Hobbs spoke with the Herald/Review about two critical topics ahead of the Nov.
3 General Election: picking her lieutenant governor and addressing the challenges of rural economic development.
Herald/Review Media: You have a big decision coming up – Sept.
4 is the deadline for you to announce your lieutenant governor pick.
Do you have any front runners?
And if not, what are you looking for?

Katie Hobbs: Well, I’m not ready to share specifics today, but I do know that Arizonans are really excited about this because it’s the first time in our state’s history that the governor and lieutenant governor will be running on the same ticket together and the first time we have a lieutenant governor.
Hobbs: I’ve heard from a lot of Arizonans about what they’re looking for.

And I certainly want to have someone who shares my approach to governing, working across the aisle, focusing on the issues rather than the partisan politics and tackling the tough challenges that so many Arizonans are facing.
Herald/Review: One of the biggest issues in Cochise County this election happens to be economic development in rural Arizona. […] How do you see the balance?
Hobbs: Economic development across the state is so critical to helping ensure that every Arizonan can thrive.

The more that we can ensure there’s economic opportunity in communities around Cochise County, the more folks are going to want to be able to stay here and provide for their families here and continue living in the place they grew up and their family might have called home for generations.
Hobbs: So, I really focus on bringing opportunity across the state and not just focusing on the urban areas like Pima and Maricopa County.
And our Arizona Commerce Authority is focused on rural community development or economic development specifically.
Hobbs: We also have a big focus on small business support because I know that, especially in our smaller communities, small businesses really are the economic backbone.
Hobbs: We’re trying to provide all kinds of tools so that those folks can thrive as well.

And we have to address issues like quality education and affordable housing and childcare and all the things that create barriers to economic development in order for all of those other things to happen.
Hobbs and allies rally in Tucson Anchor: Governor Katie Hobbs is currently in Tucson, holding a rally with several other prominent state officials as we are now # days from the general election.
Anchor: Senator Mark Kelly took the podium in support of the governor’s platform, speaking about the importance of every vote in the coming election.
Mark Kelly: At the end of the day, it means that our kids can dream about their future, and know that their hard work will actually pay off like it did for all of us.
Anchor: That wasn’t the only event that the governor held during her time in Tucson today.
Governor Hobbs also launched a canvassing operation in the city as she’s now putting her campaign into action.

Katie Hobbs: When you have someone who spent the last decade in congress building one of the most extreme partisan records in the country, and who has voted time and again for these policies that are raising costs for Arizonans, how can you trust him to actually then work to tackle those costs and bring them down?

We are an even # days out from Election Day this fall, Tuesday, November 3rd, and this afternoon here in Tucson, Governor Katie Hobbs and other Arizona Democrats, rallied supporters in midtown at La Rosa.

Anchor: She spent yesterday in Cochise County .
She was joined today for that rally by Arizona Senator Mark Kelly and former Congresswoman Gabby Giffords, Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva, and Democratic hopeful CD6 candidate JoAnna Mendoza.

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - In the News ROUNDUP: Katie Hobbs Launches Familias Primero Coalition Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PHOENIX – Last week, Gov.

Katie Hobbs launched Familias Primero , a coalition consisting of over sixty Latino leaders, community members, and local elected officials working to re-elect her, including Maricopa County Supervisor Steve Gallardo, former Maricopa County Supervisor Mary Rose Wilcox, former State Sen.
Raquel Terán, President and CEO of the Arizona Hispanic Chamber Monica Villalobos, and President of Arizona Carpenters Local 1912 Fabian Sandez.

On the eve of the start of the general election, Familias Primero was the first coalition the Hobbs campaign launched, underscoring her commitment to earning the vote of every Arizonan and building a broad coalition of support.
Engaging Latino voters has been a top priority since day one of the Hobbs campaign.

Hobbs has consistently communicated directly with Spanish-language media about her efforts to lower costs for working families; the campaign began a historically early investment in Spanish-language television, radio, and digital advertising back in May; and Hobbs has met with Latino Arizonans and community leaders across the state from cultural celebrations to conversations with small business owners about the impact of rising costs brought on by Washington’s misguided policies.
Hobbs ramping up her campaign for November Anchor: Governor Katie Hobbs is ramping up her campaign for November.
Anchor: Hobbs launched the Familias Primero coalition Monday, bringing together more than 60 Latino leaders to support her re-election.
Katie Hobbs: We know it’s going to be close.
We’re here on the ground […] I’m not listening to the pundits.
I’m doing what I need to win.
We know it’s going to be close; I’m not taking a single vote for granted.

Univision Arizona/KTVW: Coalición latina para la reeclección de Katie Hobbs Anchor 1: Cambiamos de tema y es que la gobernadora Katie Hobbes busca fortalecer el apoyo del electorado hispano de cara a la próxima contienda electoral, y ayer en la mañana presentó una nueva coalición que reúne a líderes comunitarios, pero también figuras políticas de todo nuestro estado.
Anchor 2: Aunque todavía no está definido quién será su rival en noviembre, la gobernadora Katie Hobbes ya comenzó a impulsar su campaña de reelección.
Hoy lanzó Familias Primero , una nueva coalición con la que busca sumar el apoyo de votantes latinos en Arizona.
La presentación contó con más de 50 líderes latinos y autoridades locales que forman parte de esta coalición.

Según la campaña de Hobbs, Familias Primero será una plataforma para escuchar las preocupaciones de las familias latinas y promover temas como el costo de vida, la economía, la educación y el acceso a oportunidades.
Katie Hobbs: Seguiré trabajando todos los días para ganarme la confianza y el apoyo de los habitantes de Arizona, incluyendo las familias latinas, en los próximos meses.

Y voy a necesitar su ayuda porque esta será una contienda difícil… Anchor 2: La campaña también destacó que continuará invirtiendo en comunicación en español y en actividades comunitarias para acercarse a los votantes latinos en todo el estado.
Un sector que considera clave para las próximas elecciones.
Raquel Terán: Ha protegido el seguro de salud médico. [Se] ha asegurado de que haya recursos para las familias y que tengan comida sobre la mesa.

Y también ha rechazado leyes antimigrantes que… Anchor 2: A través de su cuenta de X, Hobbs, aseguró que su administración ha estado enfocada en reducir los costos y los impuestos para las familias del estado.
También criticó medidas impulsadas por políticos en Washington que, según dijo, han aumentado los costos para los latinos.
Petra Falcón: La importancia del voto es que podemos expresar la importancia de tener una persona como gobernadora que va a pelear por sus hijos.
Katie Hobbs launches campaign coalition Familias Primero Anchor: Incumbent for governor, Katie Hobbs , already has a spot on the general election ballot.
Today she launched a campaign coalition Familias Primero or Families First to drum up support from Latino voters.
Anchor: Maricopa County Supervisor Steve Gallardo is among multiple Hispanic leaders championing Hobbs’ re-election bid.
Maricopa County Supervisor Steve Gallardo: Today we come together to kick off Familias Primero campaign here in 2026 to get Katie Hobbs re-elected to the Ninth Floor of the Governor’s Office.
We want to keep her there.
Anchor: Gallardo says that the election will be tight and Hobbs needs the support of the Latino community, but that she is the right candidate for the job.

Arizona Daily Star: Latino voters could hold key to Arizona’s governor race The road for Katie Hobbs to keep the governor’s office in the November election could lead through the Hispanic community in Arizona.

Hobbs acknowledges that means convincing those who voted for Donald Trump in 2024 — and gave him a winning margin here — that they should support her versus presumed Republican nominee Andy Biggs “I am focused on doing everything I can to deliver for Arizonans.
That includes Latino families,” Hobbs said Monday when her campaign unveiled Familias Primero — Families First — its coalition of Latino leaders, community members and local elected officials.

As she has at virtually every event, the governor clicked off what she says are her bipartisan goals like addressing high costs for consumers, securing the border, creating good-paying jobs and protecting the state’s water supply.
“Trump-endorsed Andy Biggs is one of the most extreme MAGA politicians in the entire country,” the governor told her Latino coalition members.
She claimed Trump is pushing Biggs to be governor in this swing state specifically to give him a role in overseeing the 2028 election.
Teran said that is the kind of message the Latino community, crucial to the governor’s victory, needs to hear.
“The Republicans have worked to purge people from the permanent early voting list,” Teran said.
“Who are the people most impacted when you have that type of anti-democracy legislation?” she asked.

“It’s communities of color, communities that usually don’t come out and vote.” “We’ve been working for over a year on this campaign and building the coalitions in support we need to win,” the governor said.
“So I’m confident that we’re running the campaign I need to win.
And I’m really proud of the coalition of folks here supporting my reelection.” In May, UnidosUS said its bipartisan poll showed 67% of Latino voters in Arizona disapproved of Trump’s job performance.
More to the point, 19% who said they voted for the president in 2024 said if they could do it over they would not vote for him again.
State Affairs: Hobbs launches campaign to court Latino voters Gov.
Katie Hobbs’ reelection campaign launched its “ Familias Primero ” coalition on Monday, an effort meant to drive Latino turnout in Arizona ’s top-of-the-ticket race in November.
“I am focused on doing everything I can to deliver for Arizonans, and that includes Latino families,” Hobbs told reporters after the event.

“When I go across the state, whether I’m talking to Democrats or Republicans, whites or Latinos, rural or urban communities, I’m hearing the concerns about higher costs, about securing the border, about protecting our water, creating good-paying jobs, and those are the things I’m focused on delivering on.” Polls estimate that anywhere from 34 to 41% of Arizona’s Latino voters, who make up one-fourth of the state’s eligible voters, cast ballots for Trump in 2024.

But more recent numbers from UnidosUS show those voters are souring on the Trump administration, with 19% of Arizona Latinos who voted for the president saying they would not vote for him knowing what they know now.
Speakers at Hobbs’ event on Monday attribute that to the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown and what they see as its failure to move the needle on kitchen table issues.
All said Hobbs is the best candidate to win Latino voters back because of her record on both topics.

“She refused to let Arizona become a testing ground for immigration policies that divide our families and distract law enforcement from doing its job,” said Raquel Terán, a former state lawmaker and Arizona Democratic Party chair.
KTAR: ‘We know it’s gonna be close,’ Gov.
Katie Hobbs says as likely Andy Biggs matchup looms “We know it’s gonna be close.
We’re here on the ground…” Hobbs told reporters during a Monday campaign event.

Hobbs, described by The Associated Press as “the most vulnerable Democratic governor in the country,” spoke at a reelection event where she launched “ Familias Primero ,” a new coalition aimed at rallying Latino voters behind her bid for a second term.
“Look, I’m not listening to the pundits.
I am doing what I need to win.
We know it’s going to be close.
I’m not taking a single vote for granted,” Hobbs said.
During Monday’s event, Hobbs pitched herself as a bipartisan alternative to Biggs.
“Andy Biggs had one of the most extreme partisan records in the state Legislature and continues to do that over his decade in Congress,” Hobbs said.
“I am focused on reaching across the aisle.

I did that many times in the Legislature, while Andy Biggs blocked bipartisan solutions like my bill to end the backlog of untested rape kits, and he continues to vote in the extreme minority in Congress.” “When I talk to Arizonans across the state, they well and full understand that the cost hikes we’re seeing are a result of Washington’s agenda and tariffs and the war in Iran,” she said.

“They’re seeing costs go up everywhere from the grocery store, gas station, doctor’s office, everywhere in between.” She described Biggs as a Trump loyalist and said he has repeatedly backed the president’s agenda over Arizona’s interests.
“Andy Biggs, every chance he had to not support that agenda, he has taken the opposite approach, supported that agenda and put that agenda above Arizonans,” she said.

Home About Kelly Accomplishments News Join Team Kelly Donate Join Team Kelly Donate August 19, 2026 | News Sen.

Jeb Bradley: Ayotte delivers results, Warmington offers excuses – Union Leader In this morning’s Union Leader , former Congressman and New Hampshire Senate President Jeb Bradley highlighted that while Governor Ayotte continues to deliver for all of New Hampshire, Opioid Lobbyist Cinde Warmington still refuses to come clean about her disqualifying record: Jeb Bradley: Ayotte delivers results, Warmington offers excuses Kelly Ayotte has earned a second term based on her record alone!
But, it’s also time for Cinde Warmington and the Democrats to come clean about Warmington’s long history of working for the opioid industry and bad actors like Purdue Pharma.
In a recent op-ed (“Before you judge Warmington on Purdue, look at Ayotte’s own pharma money,” Aug.
7), former Democratic Party Chairwoman Kathy Sullivan conveniently left out quite a bit of information about Warmington’s record.
Worried about Warmington pushing Purdue Pharma’s lies and calling OxyContin a “miracle drug” with “few side effects” — Sullivan thinks voters should move on.
She claims Warmington’s work for the opioid industry ended “almost #ago.” Unfortunately, the facts tell a different story, and until recently, Sullivan said so herself.
For more than a decade, Warmington was the registered agent for Dr.

Michael O’Connell and his PainCare clinic network, which gained notoriety for its role in worsening the opioid crisis in New Hampshire when a provider was convicted of accepting illegal kickbacks for prescribing opioids.

Warmington continued representing PainCare and its interests for years — including representing O’Connell after he surrendered his medical license, helping negotiate a settlement for a doctor tied to the scandal, advocating against legislation that would prevent doctors with revoked licenses from owning a medical practice, and even meeting with NHPR to defend PainCare’s public image.
After Warmington fought for PainCare and its founder for years, O’Connell returned the favor by donating $49,000 to her political campaigns.

During the 2024 Democratic primary, Joyce Craig described Warmington as a business agent for “a notorious pill mill in Somersworth that pushed pills into all of our communities.” Now, Craig refuses to endorse Warmington while Kathy Sullivan embraces her excuses and misrepresentations.
Sullivan also repeats Warmington’s claim that “no one knew” about Purdue Pharma’s lies or the dangers of OxyContin.
Recently on WMUR’s CloseUp, Adam Sexton confronted Warmington with evidence to the contrary.

At the same hearing where Warmington called OxyContin a miracle drug, New Hampshire State Police and then Health and Human Services Commissioner Don Shumway were sounding the alarm about the dangers of opioids.
Sexton also pressed Warmington on her work for O’Connell.
Her response was that PainCare was just “one of hundreds of doctors” she represented.
O’Connell is not just some doctor.
Warmington brushing it off as just another client shows how little she regrets the work.
Ironically, Kathy Sullivan herself called out this exact defense during Warmington’s failed 2024 campaign for governor.
These are Sullivan’s own words on social media: “One of the defenses from Cinde’s campaign is that the opioid problem wasn’t known when Cinde lobbied for Purdue Pharma.
That just is not correct.
Cinde testified Oxy was a miracle drug in April, 2002, several months after that congressional hearing.
That is also a fact.” The facts haven’t changed since Sullivan’s tweet.
The only thing that has changed is that New Hampshire Democrats couldn’t recruit a better candidate than an opioid lobbyist to challenge Governor Kelly Ayotte.
Now, they’re parroting the same excuses Sullivan herself once called out.
Remember that it was Sullivan who said “suck it up buttercup” after President Joe Biden’s 2024 debate disaster.
Voters aren’t forgetting that excuse either.
The opioid crisis has devastated our state, yet Cinde Warmington still refuses to take responsibility for her work for the opioid industry.
Instead of being honest with New Hampshire voters, she continues to double down on excuses and misrepresentations about her record.
When someone can excuse away and misrepresent so often and so easily about something this serious, that should terrify every Granite Stater.
While Warmington doubles down on defending her disqualifying record, Governor Kelly Ayotte continues to show why she has earned another term in the corner office.

With record per-student funding for education, large increases of funding for cities and towns, a bell-to-bell cell phone ban in our schools, fixing lenient bail laws that allowed violent offenders back on the streets — New Hampshire once again ranks #1 for public safety — and the most ambitious housing legislation in state history, Kelly Ayotte has delivered a successful first term.
Also critical to the Granite State’s future, Kelly will continue to oppose an income tax or a new state homeowner tax on top of local property taxes.
Voters should look at their records: Governor Ayotte’s numerous successes vs Warmington’s lobbying for a disgraced opioid manufacturer.
The choice is easy: Kelly Ayotte in 2026.

This year, Governor Ayotte also signed a new law giving local communities a voice in the siting process for new landfills, helping to protect the North Country and natural beauty all across New Hampshire.

Our natural beauty is what makes the North Country so special, and I look forward to working together to protect it for generations to come.” New TV Ad: “Protecting Forest Lake” Transcript: “Protecting Forest Lake” WMUR Anchor: Governor Kelly Ayotte doubling down today on her stance, saying there is no way there is going to be a landfill at Forest Lake.

Governor Ayotte: The North Country is what makes New Hampshire so special.
That’s why I fought to stop the landfill at Forest Lake.
I’ll always do what’s best for New Hampshire.

added: Skip to content Ryan Michael Kelly For Congress • NJ-03 About Issues Updates Get Involved Media Register to Vote EN ▾ Donate ← Back to updates October 15, 2026 A 2008 NYPD Disciplinary Decision: Records and Open Questions A 2008 NYPD disciplinary decision naming an officer Michael McGuire is being discussed in connection with the NJ-03 congressional race.
Here are the original sources, documented findings, and questions that remain open.
The video was scheduled for October 15, 2026.
If the player is unavailable, it may not yet be public.
Watch on YouTube ↗ The identity question The NYPD decision names Police Officer Michael McGuire, Tax Registry No.
Central Jersey Newswire separately reported speaking with congressional candidate Michael McGuire about an NYPD investigation.
Its correction does not identify the officer by tax registry number.
The available documents alone do not conclusively establish that the candidate is officer 929410.
What the official record says The March 31, 2008 memorandum concerns four disciplinary cases and eleven specifications.
Pages 3–4 record nine guilty pleas and two guilty findings on contested specifications in an administrative proceeding.

Nine guilty pleas Five unauthorized absences, including one full missed shift; failure to safeguard an NYPD identification card; failure to maintain a valid driver's license and report its suspension; and two failures to follow instructions.
Two contested findings One concerned an emergency-leave request and court notification.
The other concerned slapping a woman and causing swelling around her right eye.
The disciplinary proceeding found him guilty.
Criminal case The memorandum states that the related criminal case was dismissed.
The disciplinary finding was not a criminal conviction.
The underlying criminal-court order has not been independently reviewed here.
Approved penalty Dismissal was held in abeyance for one year, with dismissal probation April 21, 2008 through April 20, 2009.
The penalty also included forfeiture of 14 vacation days and 16 previously served suspension days.
The document does not establish that the officer was ultimately fired.
The published correction and response On February 15, 2026, Central Jersey Newswire corrected an earlier article about congressional candidate Michael McGuire and an NYPD investigation.
The publisher said it spoke with McGuire, concluded its earlier account was mistaken, and published a statement attributed to his former wife denying their disagreements were physical.
The correction does not include an NYPD order reversing the disciplinary findings.
October 14 request for clarification On October 14, 2026, at 6:24 a.m.
EDT, Ryan Michael Kelly emailed candidate Michael McGuire asking whether he is officer 929410, whether the findings were ever modified or overturned, and how his NYPD employment ended.
The sent email documents the request, not whether it was read or answered.
As of October 15, 2026, at 3:19 AM EDT, no response had been received.
Additional responses or official records will be reviewed and reflected in a dated update.
What remains unverified An independent identity match between the candidate and officer 929410.
Any later official order changing the disciplinary findings.
The officer's final NYPD employment separation record and reason for leaving.
Original sources NYPD disciplinary decision (March 31, 2008; 19-page PDF) ↗ Central Jersey Newswire correction (February 15, 2026) ↗ YouTube video ↗ The NYPD decision is an administrative record.
The publisher's correction and attributed response are different kinds of evidence.
Corrections and updates This page can be updated with a date and explanation if a response, later official record, or material correction becomes available.

added: top of page HOME ABOUT ISSUES CONNECT Menu Close DONATE About Kevin Knoke Raised with Midwest Values and a Passion to Serve Others Why I'm Running for State Assembly I am running for the Wisconsin Assembly because I believe our state needs practical, principled leadership that puts people ahead of politics and problem-solving ahead of partisanship.

My life experiences—as a teacher, veteran, outdoorsman, and parent—have shaped a clear understanding of what works, what doesn’t, and what Wisconsin families actually need from their government. ​ I identify as a Democrat, but I have long believed that both sides of the aisle are made up of good people with legitimate concerns.
Spending my childhood summers on a family farm taught me that hard work, responsibility, and respect for the land are not partisan values.

That perspective drives my belief that government should be thoughtful, limited, and effective—stepping in where it truly helps and staying out where it doesn’t belong. ​ I am fiscally conservative and socially progressive.
I believe government should stay out of people’s wallets as much as possible and out of their personal lives entirely.
I am unequivocally opposed to shifting taxes onto working families or squeezing the middle class, which I see as the engine of Wisconsin’s economy.
Every tax dollar must be spent wisely and transparently. ​ Education is deeply personal to me.
As a schoolteacher, I have seen firsthand how declining enrollment and underfunding strain public schools across Wisconsin—especially special education services.

I am committed to strengthening public education through smarter resource allocation, expanded mental health services, early screening and intervention, and broader access to early childhood education.

I believe public education is the most effective and cost-efficient investment Wisconsin can make, and I have serious concerns about private school vouchers undermining funding equity and evading accountability. ​ My commitment to veterans is personal.
During my deployment in 2002, I saw firsthand the sacrifices Americans make every day to protect and serve our country.
My father-in-law, a Vietnam veteran and dairy farmer, died from Agent Orange exposure.
That loss reinforced my belief that Wisconsin must honor veterans not just with words, but with real support and accountability. ​ My connection to Wisconsin’s land and water runs deep.
My family owns hunting land in Cumberland and actively participates in the DNR’s DMAP program.
My wife and I spend much of our time on Beaver Dam Lake, which makes water quality and conservation issues personal, not theoretical.

I believe the DNR should be guided by expert science, public input, and legislative oversight—while remaining mindful of the financial realities faced by small municipalities. ​ I am running for the Wisconsin Assembly to help move our state forward—by building consensus, respecting differences, protecting freedoms, and ensuring government works for the people it serves.
Click Here to See My Endorsements There is an old saying to judge people by the company they keep.
Well... there is some truth to that point.
That's why I'm so proud to receive the endorsement of these organizations.
This election will shape the direction of our District and state for years to come.
Electing the right person is critical, and that is why Kevin is running.
If you have a specific question for Kevin, he would be happy to answer you personally.

Kevin Knoke was a former member of the United States Army Reserve.
Use of his military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the United States Army, the Department of Defense or any branch of U.S. government.
Kevin Knoke is proud to receive the endorsement of 314 Action.
314 Action is the only national organization working to elect scientists across all levels of government—from the Senate down to local school boards.

The organization is powered by a grassroots community of over six million people supporting scientists, doctors, and STEM professionals who will use science and facts to address our most pressing issues like climate change and health care.
Climate Cabinet has endorsed Kevin Knoke for WI Assembly District 30.

Climate Cabinet is a U.S. nonprofit that uses data-driven analysis to identify high-impact state and local elections, supporting pro-climate candidates and policymakers to advance clean energy, reduce emissions, and improve affordability.
They recognize Kevin's commitment to the environment.
Kevin is grateful for the support of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee.
The DLCC Target Races are a core part of our national strategy to protect, expand, and build Democratic principled leadership across America’s state legislatures.
The DLCC view this race as one of the most important state legislative races across the country.
Kevin Knoke is very proud to receive the endorsement of LiUNA.

LIUNA Wisconsin, formally the Wisconsin Laborers’ District Council, represents about 10,000 construction laborers, advocating for higher wages, benefits, workplace safety, apprenticeship training, and skilled workforce development across Wisconsin’s infrastructure and construction industries.
Kevin is honored to receive the endorsement of the AFL-CIO because it represents Wisconsin working families across countless industries and communities.
Their support reflects a shared commitment to good-paying jobs, workplace safety, economic opportunity, and strong communities.
Kevin looks forward to working together to ensure Wisconsin’s workers have a strong voice in Madison.
Kevin Knoke is pleased to receive GROWW’s endorsement because it represents the power of people coming together to create meaningful change in their communities.
Their support reflects a shared commitment to local voices, economic security, strong communities, and government that works for working families—not corporate interests.
Kevin is proud to stand with GROWW.
Kevin Knoke is honored to receive the Wisconsin Conservation Voters’ endorsement because protecting Wisconsin’s clean water, air, land, and natural resources is essential to our state’s future.

Their support reflects a shared commitment to healthy communities, responsible stewardship, and practical conservation policies that protect Wisconsin’s environment while strengthening our economy and quality of life.

Kevin Knoke is pleased to receive the endorsement from The Committee to Protect Health Care because it reflects trusted support from physicians and health care advocates who recognize his commitment to protecting affordable, accessible care.
The endorsement reinforces his campaign’s focus on patients, public health, and strengthening health care for every community.
The endorsement from the Northern Midwest Regional Council of Carpenters reflects Kevin Knoke’s commitment to supporting working families, creating good-paying jobs, and protecting workers’ rights.
He is honored to earn the trust of skilled trades professionals who build Wisconsin and looks forward to fighting for economic opportunity and strong communities.
Kevin Knoke is honored to receive the endorsement of the Bricklayers & Allied Craftworkers District Council of Wisconsin.
Their support reflects a shared commitment to protecting good-paying union jobs, investing in skilled trades, and strengthening opportunities for working families.
Together, they will continue building a stronger, more prosperous future for Wisconsin.
Kevin is honored to receive the endorsement of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee.
Their commitment to fair representation, protecting voters’ voices, and strengthening democracy aligns with his belief that every community deserves a meaningful voice in our government.
He is grateful for their support and proud to stand with those working to protect representative government.
Kevin Knoke proud to receive the endorsement of OPCMIA Local 599, an organization representing skilled tradespeople whose hard work helps build and strengthen our communities.
Their support reflects a shared commitment to good-paying jobs, strong labor standards, safe workplaces, and ensuring Wisconsin’s hardworking families have opportunities to succeed.
Kevin is grateful to receive the endorsement of Planned Parenthood, an organization dedicated to protecting reproductive freedom and expanding access to essential healthcare.

Their support reflects our shared commitment to ensuring every Wisconsinite can make personal healthcare decisions, access affordable and quality care, and receive the services they need without political interference.

Anderson's record isn't hard to read.
On the issues that shape daily life in Granby, New Hartford, Barkhamsted and Hartland, his answer is almost always no .
Affordability : Free child care for families earning under $100,000.
Protection from price gouging after emergencies.
Anderson voted no on all of it.
Ideology : Four straight state budgets, including the one with the largest middle-class tax cut in Connecticut history: no .
Emergency aid for a local hospital and children's nonprofits: no .
And in 2021, he didn't vote on the budget at all.
Healthcare & Public Wellness : Insurance coverage for kids with PANDAS, chemotherapy patients and families facing infertility: no.
Protections that keep kids safe online: no.
When only eight legislators opposed expanding health coverage , he was one of them.
Civil Rights : In 2024, Connecticut voters approved absentee voting for all.
When the legislature wrote it into law, he voted no .
He also opposed protecting nursing home residents from discrimination and keeping bail arrests out of schools, hospitals and churches.
The Environment : Lower-cost solar, climate action and clean energy jobs: no , no and no .
His CT League of Conservation Voters score fell to 36% this year.
Affordability Scored 30% from the Connecticut AFL-CIO The AFL-CIO scored Rep.
Anderson 30% for 2025–26 , with a 23% lifetime score.

He voted against PA 26-12 , which waives state college tuition and offers mortgage help for police, firefighters and EMTs who live where they serve, strengthens workers' comp for teachers and healthcare workers assaulted on the job, and guarantees break time for nursing mothers.
He also voted against extending the state's retirement savings program to home care aides ( PA 25-30 ).
The Connecticut Education Association gave him a 50% for 2026 .
Anderson was one of 34 legislators to vote no .

added: top of page KIM DAILEY * HOUSE DISTRICT 85 * REPUBLICAN HOME MEET KIM ON THE ISSUES EVENTS UPDATES GET INVOLVED CONTACT MEDIA KIT DONATE ENDORSED BY: Endorsed by: Montanans for Limited Government, Montana Conservative Alliance, Montana Freedom Caucus PAC, and the Americans for Prosperity- Montana All Posts In the News Campaign Updates On the Issues Voter Resources Endorsements Legislative Insights Events Kim Dailey Receives A+ Endorsement from Montana Conservative Alliance Editor Apr 28 2 min read Kim Dailey has received an A+ endorsement from the Montana Conservative Alliance (MCA) as part of its 2026 Legislative Candidate Endorsements.
The MCA recently released its long-awaited endorsement report, highlighting candidates across Montana who align with its principles-based evaluation process.

According to the organization, this year’s endorsements were delayed due to unforeseen circumstances, but were carefully developed to provide voters with what they describe as a more reliable measure of a candidate’s values and likely decision-making.
Unlike some endorsement lists that may reflect political alliances or specific interest groups, MCA emphasizes a different approach.
Their process centers on evaluating each candidate’s core principles, philosophies, and instincts, which they believe are the strongest indicators of how an elected official will vote once in office.

At the heart of MCA’s evaluation is a 58-question Principles Questionnaire, designed to uncover a candidate’s positions on key issues related to constitutional government, individual liberty, and the role of government.

The organization states that this method prioritizes principles over promises, aiming to identify candidates who will consistently support policies aligned with limited government and pro-freedom values.

MCA also notes that its system allows for multiple endorsements within the same race, acknowledging that while candidates may share alignment on key principles, their overall ratings can still vary based on depth and consistency of those convictions.
Kim Dailey’s A+ rating places her among the top-tier candidates recognized in this report, reflecting strong alignment with the criteria outlined by the Montana Conservative Alliance.

The organization encourages voters to review the full report and its methodology to better understand how candidates were evaluated, and to use the information as one of many tools when considering their choices in the upcoming election.

Logan Dozier Sep 29, 2020 2 min read Voters of the 16th Legislative District are the clear winners in the race to replace Rep.
Bill Jenkin, R-Prosser, in the state House.
Republican Mark Klicker and Democrat Frances Chvatal, both of Walla Walla, are outstanding candidates.
Klicker and Chvatal are extremely bright and articulate with the skills needed to serve in the Legislature.
Still, there is a clear difference in the candidates — Klicker is conservative and Chvatal is liberal.

Beyond that, Klicker has a breadth and depth of knowledge on agriculture and environmental issues, as well as a clear understanding of how the Legislature really works (as in hardball politics), that is impressive.
Klicker has been a farmer in several capacities with his farming family.
He worked for 17 years as a regional director for the Washington State Farm Bureau followed by a stint as a project coordinator for Monson Fruit Company.
Klicker now operates and owns a forest management business.
His years with the Farm Bureau brought him in touch with government officials, and he spent a lot of time in Olympia working on agricultural issues.
His views on business, agriculture and environmental protection are pragmatic.
He comes from the perspective of a need to protect the environment so farms — particularly small farms — will survive.
His approach to business is similar in that he believes it is critical to establish a business-friendly environment so small and large employers can stay in business.
Chvatal, who is also from a farm family (in the Touchet area), has similar sensibilities when it comes to agriculture.
Her overriding focus, however, is health care.
She has had a long and successful career as a nurse and hospital administrator in Walla Walla.
When it comes to talking health care, and understanding the nuances of issues, it would be difficult to find anyone more fluent.
Again, voters can’t go wrong.
We see Klicker as the stronger candidate in this race because of his wide array of experiences.
His conservative politics are also more in line with the conservative 16th Legislative District.
However, Chvatal is sharp and understands the District and, if elected, would certainly be responsive to all regardless of their political views.
Klicker would too.
What stands out most about both candidates is their sincere willingness to work across the political aisle seeking collaborative solutions.
They understand that won’t be easy in the hyper-partisan Legislature, but they both contend this is how they roll in their careers and personal lives.
We don’t doubt them for a second.
Both candidates have many strengths, but in the end we recommend Klicker for the state House, Position 1.

removed: Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact Donate Donate Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact 💖 We need your help to power our campaign, chip in today! $10 $100 $250 Meet Kristina Gabriel Kristina Gabriel is an Oklahoman, a community advocate, and citizen of the Cherokee Nation who believes public service should be rooted in integrity, lived experience, and accountability to the people.
Kristina has dedicated her career to improving the health and well-being of communities across Oklahoma and Indian Country.

Before running for office, she worked as a public health researcher focused on strengthening health outcomes in Indigenous communities, helping inform state, federal and tribal policy to restore Food Sovereignty and expand access to culturally grounded, community-driven solutions.

Kristina holds a Master of Science in Forensic Investigation and a graduate certificate in Public Health from Oklahoma State University, a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Fort Lewis College, and an Associate of Arts from Tulsa Community College.
She is trained in Community-Based Participatory Research and has published peer-reviewed research on Indigenous health.
Her work has been supported by national institutions including the National Institutes of Health and the U.S.
Department of Health and Human Services, and she has partnered with tribes and community organizations across the country.
But Kristina's path to public service didn't begin in academia, it began in community.

She has a background in grassroots organizing, has volunteered with Planned Parenthood, and has supported local progressive campaigns focused on expanding healthcare access, protecting voting rights, and building a more equitable Oklahoma.
Kristina lives in Tulsa's White City neighborhood.
She is a renter who understands firsthand the pressures families face, rising costs, access to healthcare, and the need for thriving communities.
Kristina is running because she believes Oklahoma deserves leadership that listens, collaborates, and delivers real results.
She is committed to strengthening tribal-state relationships, expanding healthcare access, protecting fundamental rights, and ensuring every community has the opportunity to thrive.

removed: Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact Donate Donate Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact 💖 We need your help to power our campaign, chip in today! $10 $100 $250 Priorities Affordability Oklahoma families are working harder than ever, yet too many are still struggling to keep up.
Housing costs in the Tulsa area have risen significantly, putting pressure on renters and first-time homebuyers alike.
U.S.
Census data show that median gross rent in Oklahoma has steadily increased over the past decade, while wages have not kept pace for many working families.
1 Oklahoma ranks near the bottom nationally in median household income.
2 When housing, childcare, groceries, and utilities rise faster than paychecks, families are forced to make impossible choices.
I support: Expanding affordable housing through smart incentives and zoning reform - We don't have a housing shortage because we lack land.
We have a housing shortage because we've made it too hard to build the kinds of homes regular people can afford.
I support reforms that make it easier to build starter homes while protecting existing neighborhoods and preventing predatory practices.
Lowering childcare costs through state-supported partnerships - Childcare is one of the biggest monthly expenses families face.
If we want parents to work and businesses to grow, we have to make sure childcare is accessible and affordable.
That means partnering with employers, strengthening subsidies, and supporting providers so they can keep their doors open.
Protecting consumers from predatory fees and utility rate spikes - When your electric bill spikes, you don't get to shop around.
You don't get to negotiate.
That's why oversight matters.
If utilities want guaranteed profits, they also need guaranteed accountability Healthcare Accessibility Oklahoma consistently ranks near the bottom nationally in overall health outcomes.
3 The state also has one of the highest uninsured rates in the country.
4 Mental health services, maternal healthcare, and specialty care remain strained.
The Oklahoma Maternal Mortality Review Committee continues to document preventable pregnancy-related deaths.
5 We must: Invest in community-based mental health and substance use services - Prevention and early treatment save lives and save taxpayer dollars.
Community-based care is the smart, humane way to address mental health and addiction in Oklahoma.
Strengthen maternal healthcare access - Maternal healthcare isn't just about babies, it's about families, communities, and equity.
Strengthening access saves lives and builds stronger Oklahoma families.
Tribal-State Partnerships Oklahoma is home to 39 federally recognized Tribal Nations.
Tribal governments are major employers and contribute billions annually to the state's economy.
6 Following the U.S.
Supreme Court's decision in McGirt v.
Oklahoma (2020), strong government-to-government cooperation is more important than ever.
7 Public safety, infrastructure, healthcare delivery, and economic development all depend on respectful collaboration.
When Tribal Nations thrive, Oklahoma thrives.

I am committed to: Protecting tribal sovereignty and honoring treaty obligations - Tribal sovereignty is not just a legal principle, it's the foundation for strong communities, safe neighborhoods, and economic growth.
Honoring treaties and partnering with Tribal Nations benefits everyone in Oklahoma.
Increasing collaboration on infrastructure and broadband - Collaboration is key.
When the state and Tribal Nations plan and invest together, we can close gaps in roads, utilities, and broadband, bringing opportunity, safety, and prosperity to every neighborhood.
Strengthening partnerships in healthcare, education, and workforce development - Our state thrives when we work together.

By strengthening partnerships in healthcare, education, and workforce development with Tribal Nations, we create opportunities for all Oklahomans, better schools, stronger healthcare, and jobs that support families.
AI Data Centers Artificial intelligence and data infrastructure are expanding rapidly, including in Oklahoma.
While data centers bring economic opportunity, they also require significant electricity and water resources.
The U.S.
Department of Energy reports that data centers account for roughly 2 percent of total U.S. electricity consumption, with demand projected to grow due to AI expansion.
8 Large facilities can also consume millions of gallons of water annually for cooling.

As Oklahoma attracts technological investment, we must ensure: Transparent economic incentive agreements - If we're going to offer incentives for high-tech development, everyone deserves to know the cost, the benefit, and the timeline.
Transparency isn't optional, it's smart governance.
Responsible water and energy use standards - Innovation shouldn't come at the expense of our neighbors.
Responsible energy and water standards make sure high-tech development benefits everyone, not just corporate bottom lines.
Grid reliability protections for residential consumers - We want tech companies to bring jobs and investment, but not at the expense of your electricity bill or power reliability.
Grid protections make sure the community comes first.
Workforce training so Oklahomans benefit from job growth - We want tech growth in our state, but it has to work for Oklahomans.
Training and apprenticeships ensure that new jobs stay in our communities and lift up our people.

added: Say hi when you spot her out there 🧡 kuisforyou.com #weekend #photodump #community ##Newtown #newtownct #door 8 1 Open post by michelleku4newtown with ID 17917074921245406 Load More Follow on Instagram The latest on Facebook: Used for the like, share, comment, and reaction icons Michelle Embree Ku for Newtown #ago View on Facebook (opens in a new tab) Proud to have the support of organizations standing up for science, our educators, working families, reproductive freedom, gun safety, and the environment.

But because of the way income taxes work, here’s how that claim is not unusual.
At the state level, revenue grows automatically as prices and incomes rise.
Connecticut collects more through income tax, sales tax, and investment funds without ever changing a rate.
The Legislature may not have voted for it, but you’re likely paying more income and sales tax each year.
Costs rise with inflation, but property-tax revenue doesn’t keep pace on its own.
Every budget has to go through a local process and voter approval.
Michelle evaluates budgets based on needs and resources, not ideology.
Some years that means cuts, some years an increase, and some years no increase at all.

But because of the way income taxes work, here’s how that claim is not unusual.
At the state level, revenue grows automatically as prices and incomes rise.
Connecticut collects more through income tax, sales tax, and investment funds without ever changing a rate.
The Legislature may not have voted for it, but you’re likely paying more income and sales tax each year.
Costs rise with inflation, but property-tax revenue doesn’t keep pace on its own.
Every budget has to go through a local process and voter approval.
Michelle evaluates budgets based on needs and resources, not ideology.
Some years that means cuts, some years an increase, and some years no increase at all.
Vote Michelle Embree Ku, Democrat for State Representative, 106th District. 🗳️ Vote early October 19–November 1 or on Election Day, November 3.

removed: top of page Home ABOUT PLATFORM GET INVOLVED BLOG DONATE DONATE NOW All Posts 314 Action Official Endorsement Lauren Cole Mar 19 1 min read I am proud to share that my campaign has been officially endorsed by 314 Action Fund, a national organization dedicated to electing leaders who believe in science, evidence-based policy, and stronger communities.
This endorsement means a lot.
Not just for our campaign, but for what it represents.
As someone with a background in biochemistry, this recognition is especially meaningful to me.

I've always believed that the best decisions, especially when it comes to healthcare, public policy, and our communities, should be grounded in evidence and a commitment to understanding real world impacts.
My experience in science has shaped how I approach problem solving.
I have learned to ask questions, listen first and focus on solutions that actually work.
Those are the same values I will bring to the Statehouse.
I'm grateful for this endorsement and excited to keep connecting with people across District 37 as we continue this campaign.

added: top of page Home ABOUT PLATFORM GET INVOLVED BLOG DONATE DONATE NOW All Posts Where Lauren Stands: Endorsements, Campaign Updates & How You Can Help Lauren Cole #ago 2 min read Hi everyone, One piece of feedback we’ve heard from voters is that they want to know more about where Lauren stands on the issues that matter to them.
We want to make sure you have that information, too!
Lauren is a scientist, a neighbor, and an advocate for our community.

Her campaign is focused on putting people first, protecting access to healthcare, supporting public education, strengthening local businesses, and building a future where Hoosiers have the opportunity to thrive.
We’re proud to share the organizations that have recognized Lauren’s work and the priorities she brings to this race.

Here’s who is standing with Lauren: Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates endorsed Lauren for the 2026 election cycle in recognition of her commitment to advancing reproductive healthcare, protecting reproductive rights, and promoting reproductive justice.

Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC (IRFPAC) IRFPAC endorsed Lauren for the 2026 election cycle and works to educate Hoosiers about reproductive freedom, the impact of abortion restrictions, and the importance of reproductive rights in Indiana.

Indiana Young Democrats — 2026 Priority Endorsement Indiana Young Democrats named Lauren a 2026 Priority Endorsement, committing additional resources to her campaign, including a $1,000 contribution, in recognition of her work to strengthen communities across Indiana.

3.14 Action As a scientist with experience in clinical trials, Lauren is backed by 3.14 Action, an organization that works to elect scientists who bring evidence-based thinking to public policy, healthcare, and climate issues.

Voters for a Green Indiana — 2026 Green Voters Guide Lauren was recognized as an environmentally friendly candidate in the 2026 Green Voters Guide, which examines candidates’ records and campaign priorities on utility affordability, data centers, renewable energy, and environmental protection, alongside their responses to an environmental questionnaire.
MADVoters — Verified Politician Lauren received the MADVoters-Verified Politician designation.

As a MADVoters-Verified Politician, she is dedicated to fighting for a better life for all Hoosiers through affordable and accessible healthcare, fully funded public education, making housing, utilities, childcare, and everyday essentials more affordable, s afeguarding voting access and protecting our freedoms, building safe and inclusive communities for all Hoosiers.

Indiana Coalition for Public Education (ICPE) — Candidate Pledge Lauren signed ICPE’s pledge addressing public education, including support for traditional public schools, local school board authority, and accountability for schools receiving public funds.
These recognitions reflect important issues in this race, but we know there is still more work to do to get Lauren’s name and priorities in front of voters.
We have come so far, and we’re not slowing down now.
Let’s keep building our future together!

added: Dear Friends, It has been a privilege to serve you over the past two years.
When I first ran, I made a commitment to represent you with professionalism, integrity, and statesmanship.
I have worked every day to uphold that standard while delivering results grounded in our shared conservative values.
Delivering Results Through Leadership and Collaboration With the increasing polarization in today’s political environment, this past session at times became contentious.
Despite that, I was able to navigate those challenges and work collaboratively with a wide range of legislators to advance meaningful legislation.
That ability to build coalitions—without compromising core principles—is how real work gets done in Cheyenne.
Much of the most important work in the Legislature happens outside of the spotlight.
One example is the $15 million appropriation for Sheridan College’s science building renovation, a shovel-ready project critical to our community.

After my amendment to fund this project narrowly failed by a single vote during the first round of budget amendments, we built a coalition by incorporating additional priorities, successfully passed the amendment, and ensured that the funding remained intact through conference committee.
This is the approach I bring to the Legislature: persistence, coalitionbuilding, and results.
Committee Leadership and Impact Because of my professional background and 16 years of experience in public policy, I was assigned to two very important committees: Judiciary and Education.

Notable legislative accomplishments include: Judiciary Committee: • Passed legislation on the stalking and grooming of minors, crimes that can lead to human trafficking • Passed legislation to address Wyoming Chamber of Commerce concerns regarding retail theft Education Committee: • I successfully introduced two late interim bills strengthening protections for parental rights and homeschooled students that were signed into law by Governor Gordon • Increased funding for Hathaway Scholarships, Career and Technical Education School Funding Recalibration • Recalibration was completed and fully implemented for the first time in 20 years • I worked to incorporate amendments specifically requested by our local school districts • Funding model salaries for teachers will increase by 20.7%, a statewide average increase of $13,133 Property Tax Relief After years of inaction, we were able to provide some relief from the excessive increases we’ve experienced in property taxes.
Now the focus is turning to property tax reform for the long term.
The Budget The budget process began in 2025, when state agencies submitted their budget requests to the governor.
Each agency request includes three primary components: 1.
The funding needed to maintain current service levels (the “standard budget”) 3.

Any requested increases or decreases (“exception requests”) HOUSE DISTRICT 51 • 1004 Big Goose Road • Sheridan, Wyoming 82801 TELEPHONE (307) 683-1788 • E-MAIL Laurie.Bratten@wyoleg.gov • WEBSITE www.wyoleg.gov The governor reviews agency requests and submits recommendations to the Joint Appropriations Committee (JAC), which then conducts its own detailed review before producing the final budget bill.
That bill is introduced simultaneously in the House and the Senate.
At that point, legislators begin debating the bill, offering amendments, and working toward passage in their respective chambers.
Ultimately, the House and the Senate passed their versions of the budget bill, coming within $170 million of each other (out of $11 billion).
The final budget was resolved by the Joint Conference Committee in a matter of hours.
After the last two budgets increased state spending by 24%, the final budget for FY27-28 limited the spending increase to 0.8%.
Local Funding We stabilized the funding of Direct Distributions from the state with a formula to provide predictable funding levels that counties and municipalities can depend on in the future.
The result for the FY27-28 budget is that local governments will receive an increase in funding from the state.
A Consistent Conservative Framework My work is guided by a clear and consistent set of principles.
I approach every issue with several key perspectives: the state and federal constitutions, the Wyoming Republican Party Platform, and input from constituents.
Those foundations guide every vote I take.
I evaluate every issue on its merits and remain committed to thoughtful, disciplined decisionmaking rather than political rhetoric.
I am always happy to visit with anyone to talk about issues, share my extensive research, and discuss the decision-making process behind my votes.
I will also be posting issue information on my website addressing questions I frequently receive.
Please feel free to reach out to me to have a conversation.

Priorities Moving Forward Include: • Pursue long-term structural property tax reform • Ensure sufficient, stable, sustainable funding for essential services • Strengthen economic development by helping local communities with infrastructure • Build on progress we’ve made on funding for education • Continue advancing legislation to provide fiscal accountability and transparency • Protect our public lands • Continue defending our Second Amendment rights • Support a culture of life Constituent Services I am honored to represent you, and I work for you.

One of the most rewarding aspects of this position has been the opportunity to help constituents with all sorts of issues, whether it’s helping you open a case at the federal level, connecting you with the right people or organizations locally, or helping resolve an issue at the state level.
My experience and involvement within the community has given me the chance to work with so many people, not just in HD51, but in all of Sheridan County and throughout the state.
Together, we can continue building on the progress we have made while staying true to the principles that make Wyoming strong.

Sincerely, Representative Laurie Bratten House District 51 HOUSE DISTRICT 51 • 1004 Big Goose Road • Sheridan, Wyoming 82801 TELEPHONE (307) 683-1788 • E-MAIL Laurie.Bratten@wyoleg.gov • WEBSITE www.wyoleg.gov

CAMPAIGN MAILERS LETTERS & COMMENTARY CONSTITUENT MAILER 5-6-26 NEWS Laurie Bratten Announces Campaign for Re-Election to Wyoming House District 51 “My strengths include finding areas of common ground and collaboratively working together for solutions.
The relationships I’ve developed in both the House and the Senate will be incredibly valuable in the next session.

I have earned a reputation as being well prepared, thoughtful, and ready to approach every issue on its merits – even if that means going against the grain at times when I felt it was the right thing to do.” READ ARTICLE CAMPAIGN FINANCE REPORTS Campaign Finance Report - August 13, 2026 ​ This week, campaign finance reports revealed something I think you should know before Tuesday.
I have never taken a dime from a PAC or another political committee, not in this campaign, and not when I ran in 2024.
My opponent has accepted more than $5,000 from PACs this year.
That difference shows up in your mailbox.
I'm sure we're all ready for campaign season to end; the onslaught of political mail has been overwhelming, and every piece of it costs money.
I've sent two mailers this entire election.
That's what a campaign looks like when it's funded by the people who live here.
The first was about my record, what I've accomplished as your State Representative for House District 51.
The second laid out a few clear policy differences between my opponent and me, because you deserve to know what your choices are.
No vague platitudes, just real differences on the issues.
I think voters deserve the facts, and then they can decide for themselves.
I work for the people of House District 51.
I work hard to represent everyone in this district, especially the individual citizen and taxpayer who doesn't have a lobbyist in Cheyenne.
I've been honored to be your representative in Cheyenne, and I would be honored to continue to represent you.
Both mailers are on my campaign website if you'd like to read them.
I'm Laurie Bratten, and I'm asking for your vote in the Republican Primary this Tuesday, August 18th.
