removed: top of page Home About Lex Social Media Platform News Yard Signs Voter Education Donate Voter Education All information listed comes directly from the Kansas Secretary of State website: sos.ks.gov Click on any blue text to be taken to the appropriate page.
What are the requirements to vote in Kansas?
Anyone who is a US citizen, 18 years or older, a resident of Kansas, and has completed the terms of any sentence from a felony conviction, is legally qualified to vote.
(Voting rights are restored upon completion of the terms of a felony sentence, including all supervised release.
Registration is not automatic - the ex-offender must act to register to vote.
Unpaid criminal fines, restitution, or court costs may make you ineligible to vote.
Verify with the court if any amounts owed prevent the restoration of your civil rights.) Per state law, the voter registration books close 21 days before an election until the election is completed.
This means for 2026, all voter registrations must be completed by October 18th to be considered valid.
Any registrations received in that period will not be processed until after the election.
Always make sure to double check your voter registration before the deadline to ensure your voting eligibility for the election. ​ What are the Photo ID requirements?
State law requires voters to show photographic identification when casting a vote in person.
If the photo ID has an expiration date on it, the ID must not have expired at the time of voting.
An acceptable photo ID does not have to have an expiration date on the document in order to be valid.

Acceptable forms of photo ID include: A driver’s license or nondriver’s identification card issued by Kansas or by another state or district of the United States; A concealed carry of handgun license issued by Kansas or a concealed carry of handgun or weapon license issued by another state or district of the United States; A United States passport; An employee badge or identification document issued by a municipal, county, state, or federal government office; A military identification document issued by the United States; A student identification card issued by an accredited postsecondary institution of education in the state of Kansas; A public assistance identification card issued by a municipal, county, state or federal government office; and An identification card issued by an Indian tribe.
Exemptions exist for individuals 65 years of age or older who may use expired photo IDs or individuals whose religious beliefs prohibit photographic identification.

Voters with religious objections may sign an affidavit before the election or at the poll on election day to be exempt. ​ Registered voters who do not have an approved government-issued photo ID and would like one to vote may apply for a free nondriver identification card with the Kansas Division of Motor Vehicles.
To get a free photo ID, individual must fill out a Certification Requesting Fee Waiver for Nondriver Identification Card.
This form is available at all driver’s licenses offices, all county election offices and online. ​ How do I register to vote?

You can go to your county election office and fill out a paper form in person. ​ If you have a valid Kansas ID, you can register online . ​ How do I check my voter registration status? ​ Check your voter registration status HERE ​ When do I vote? ​ Election dates can be found HERE ​ How do I vote early?
Individuals can vote early in person at the county election office or at a satellite location, and must show photo ID.
If an advance voter does not provide identification, the county election officer will issue a provisional ballot to the voter.
The provisional ballot will not be considered valid until the voter submits their photo ID before the county canvass.
Apply for an Advanced Ballot ​ What is the county canvass?

The canvassing process includes counting ballots, tabulating votes by election district and certifying the results of all official primary and general elections and question submitted elections held pursuant to federal or state law.

It is the process which produces official election results, whether it is the official number of valid votes cast for each candidate for each elected office, or the official number of valid Yes and No votes cast on an issue in a question submitted election.
For local elections, there are always two canvasses: the original canvass and the final canvass.
For national and state elections, there are always three canvasses: the original, intermediate and final canvass. ​ How do I vote by mail?
Voters may vote by mail prior to election day in the state of Kansas.

To do so, you must complete an application for an advance ballot and include your driver’s license number or a copy of your photo identification. ​ Under Kansas statute, the deadline to return your ballot is the close of the polls on Election Day.

A district court in Douglas County entered a statewide injunction requiring ballots postmarked by election day to be counted if a ballot arrives by the last postal delivery on Friday after the election.
The Kansas Court of Appeals rejected the Secretary of State’s appeal to stay the injunction.
Regardless of the decision, voters are urged to return their ballots by the close of polls on Election Day.

Doing so will ensure that their ballots will be counted. ​ Military and overseas citizens: Uniform and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) allows for overseas voting , or federal services voting, for active duty military and family members and individuals, living abroad.
To qualify, voters must meet the criteria set out in the Federal Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.
Absentee voters who qualify under this act should apply for a ballot in the county election office in the Kansas County where their residence is located.
It is not necessary for qualifying individuals to be registered to vote in the county which they vote (K.S.A.
25-1215 ). ​ The Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) provides a ballot application HERE called the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA).
Voters who file the application before a primary election will automatically receive a ballot for the general election that year (K.S.A.

Although there is no statutory deadline for applications to be submitted, they must be submitted with enough time to allow transmittal time to and from the voter. ​ Submit a ballot application to the county election office that you consider your residence.
Complete your ballot.
Starting # days prior to an election, ballots will be sent to all voters with an active federal post card application.
Return your ballot to the county election office by mail, fax, or email.
Verify your ballot was received and counted by contacting your county election office. ​ How are mail in ballots verified?
K.S.A.

25-1122(e)(1) requires county election offices compare the signature on the advance by mail ballot application with the signature on voter registration records to verify the voter, and not a third party, requested the advance by mail ballot.

If the signatures do not match, the signature may be challenged, and the county election office will contact the voter to verify the signature. ​ Voters must provide the number of their photo identification (e,g., driver’s license) on the advance by mail ballot application.
In the event identification information cannot be verified, K.S.A.

25-1122(c) states the applicant must provide a copy of an acceptable form of photographic identification. ​ When a voter has completed their advance by mail ballot, they must sign the outside of the ballot envelope.
That signature is then reviewed with voter registration records.
If the signatures do not match, the signature may be challenged, and the county election office will contact the voter to verify the signature. ​ How do I know if I need a provisional ballot?
Provisional voting provides individuals with the opportunity to vote even though questions exist on their eligibility.
Kansas law encourages individuals to participate in an election by allowing any individual with an eligibility issue to cast a provisional ballot.
There are a number of instances where an individual may be provided with a provisional ballot.

The most common include: -Failure to provide photographic identification -Address change -Name change -Already issued a ballot ​ How do I find out where to vote? ​ Find my voting location ​ Where do I vote if I just moved?
If you move to a new county in Kansas before the registration deadline, you must complete a new voter registration application.
If you move after the registration deadline, you can still vote at the precinct assigned to your old address, but you will be required to complete a new voter registration application.
If you moved from another state, you should register to vote in Kansas as soon as possible after moving.
If 45 days before an election and the deadline to register has passed, you may vote a president-only ballot.

To vote a president-only ballot, you must go to your local election office by noon on the day before the election and complete voter registration forms. ​ ​ ​ ​ © # by The Goff Family, Powered and secured by Liberty and Justice for All bottom of page

House candidate Lindsay James brings Crowded Table Town Hall Tour to Tama County NEWS ARTICLE Lindsay James on protecting Social Security, preventing benefit cuts NEWS ARTICLE Candidates cite corruption as key issue in Iowa’s 2nd Congressional District race PRESS RELEASE Lindsay James Decisively Wins Final IA-02 Debate Against Lobbyist Joe Mitchell PRESS RELEASE “Toss Up” - Cook Political Report Moves IA-02 toward Lindsay James PRESS RELEASE Must See: Joe Mitchell’s Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Debate Night PRESS RELEASE Lindsay James Releases New TV Ad Focusing on the Healthcare Crisis Facing Everyday Iowans PRESS RELEASE Lindsay James Touts Labor Support with AFSCME National and Council 61 Presidents Oct 14 2026 PRESS RELEASE Lindsay James Touts Labor Support with AFSCME National and Council 61 Presidents CEDAR RAPIDS, IA - Today, Lindsay James hosted a press conference with American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) National President Patrick Moran and Council 61 AFSCME President Todd Copley to tout her strong labor support as the only labor-endorsed candidate in the race for Iowa’s second congressional district.
“Public employees are the lifeblood of our Iowan communities,” said Lindsay James .
“Too many Iowans are making impossible choices living paycheck to paycheck.
There is a disproportionately loud voice for special interests, the ultra-wealthy, and the big corporations in our policy making places while our hard working families get left behind.
Our workers, our unions, and our families deserve a leader that will give them an equal voice in our policy making.

I’m ready to be that leader in Washington and I’m so grateful for the support of AFSCME in this race.” “We know it’s a tough economic environment for regular working people,” said AFSCME National President Patrick Moran .
“Executives are making hand over fist while everyday people are experiencing an affordability crisis from groceries to rent to healthcare to diesel fuel.
That’s why we need champions in Congress who will take on billionaires, tech bros, and the people that are making so much more on the backs of everyone else.
Lindsay James is a champion for working people.

We’re going to send her to Congress to fight for us and for the life that Iowans deserve.” “We need leaders who will stand with workers, respect organized labor, and fight for an economy that works for everyone, not just those at the top,” said Council 61 AFSCME President Todd Copley.
“Joe Mitchell voted for rollbacks to unemployment, against raising the minimum wage, and against restoring collective bargaining for Iowa workers.

Lindsay James will be a leader that fights for workers, not the ultra-wealthy, and that’s why we need her in Congress.” Lindsay James has built broad coalition support across IA-02 and is the only labor endorsed candidate in the race.

She is proud to have the support of The Iowa Federation of Labor, Laborers’ International Union of North America, Iowa Building and Construction Trades Council, Iowa State Council of Machinists, Iowa Teamsters, Iowa State Building & Construction Trades, AFSCME Council 61, Carpenters, IBEW, UAW, AFGE, NALC, UA, NALC, NEA, Iron Workers Local 89, and Operating Engineers Local 150.
Lindsay is also endorsed by End Citizens United, the largest anti-corruption organization in Washington D.C fighting to end money in politics.

added: To the Editor, As our upcoming election approaches, I am writing to express my enthusiastic support for Mary Shannon Lindstrom for Maine State house Representative District 124.
In a time when finding true leadership can feel challenging, Shannon stands out as a person of exceptional character, dedication, and proven service to our community.

I have had the privilege of watching from the sidelines as she has served our town for years, most notably through her impactful tenure on the school board and her tireless work on various volunteer committees.
In every role she takes on, she proves herself to be remarkably hardworking.
She doesn't just show up to meetings; she does the heavy lifting, thoroughly researches the issues, and listens intently to the concerns of residents.
Shannon is a highly ethical individual who treats every person with respect and approaches governance with complete transparency.
With her, what you see is what you get.
Her authenticity in both her words and her actions is a breath of fresh air.
She makes promises she intends to keep, and she never compromises her values for political expediency.
Our community needs a leader in the legislature who understands our local values, possesses a deep-rooted commitment to public service, and commands the work ethic to deliver real results.
I urge my fellow neighbors to join me in voting for Mary Shannon Lindstrom this November.
We deserve a representative who works hard, acts ethically, and speaks with genuine authenticity.

DONATE SUBSCRIBE Green Campaign Pledge ​ Lorig has pledged to run a green campaign.

This gives concrete evidence of her commitment to climate change action, shows she can “walk the walk,” and challenges other candidates to do so, too. ​ Lorig’s campaign has pledged to: ​ Print campaign literature on recycled paper with soy-based inks.
Eliminate campaign swag that is not recyclable (such as plastic items and bags, balloons).
Locate campaign events, when possible, to be accessible by public transit (or biking or walking), and advertise that fact (with directions).
Carpool volunteers to events and field work, when possible.
Drive a Prius or small, energy efficient car with good mileage rating, when necessary.
Hold events with sustainable supplies, using compostable, recyclable, or reusable and Styrofoam-free products, and offering a non-meat options.
Serve food prepared by local businesses with short food supply chains, whenever possible.
Eliminate one-serving plastic water bottles at campaign events and for volunteer events.

added: REP LYNN HOLLAND COPELAND Home Meet Lynn Profile Accomplishments Issues Endorsements Contact Top Three Priorities AFFORDABILITY: Needed are opportunities to work hard, earn a living wage, access affordable housing, food, healthcare and transportation.
Tax burdens must be shared equitably.
Divisions are human constructs of those seeking free labor/superiority.
YOUTH & OLDER PEOPLE: With the lack of living wages, families can be stressed and can lead to the inability to raise their children in a safe and loving environment.
The foster care system is there to give children an opportunity to thrive.
Connecting youth and older people works for both.

I am running to continue supporting families, youth, and older Mainers to be meaningful contributors in their communities by enacting laws to support families with good paying jobs, equality, reproductive freedom, healthcare, mental healthcare, housing, food security, quality education, childcare, while ensuring gun safety, social security nets, tribal sovereignty, addressing climate change, supporting renewable energy, and leaving a clean environment to pass on to the next generations.
What is one way Maine is on the right track?
What is one way the state is on the wrong track?
Supporting our schools by funding 55% of education costs and revenue sharing to our communities, without which our property tax bills would be much higher.
As one of several dozen legislators in your chamber, how would you make a measurable difference for your constituents?
Work together with all interested parties.
Surveys show the economy is the top concern of voters.
What is a specific proposal addressing Maine voters’ economic anxieties that you’d work to make law?
We need to bring businesses to Maine – and we need a younger workforce.
I have proposed a bill to bring serious film production to Maine.
This would give a place for the students graduating from Maine’s secondary education schools a place to work and a reason to stay in Maine and raise a family.

For the first time, two traditional Navajo women are running for the Arizona Legislature.
Each bring essential experience and has deep roots as longtime residents of Legislative District 6.
Together, they have lived in and traveled throughout the largest legislative district in Arizona.
Jamescita Peshlakai will be serving as your State Senator and Mae Peshlakai as your State Representative.
Elect these 2 highly qualified women to the 2 Open Seats!

She served as the tribal liaison for the U.S.
Department of the Interior under President Biden and, in 2025, was appointed by Governor Hobbs to the Arizona State Transportation Board.
Representative Mae Peshlakai is seeking a third term in the State House.
Overcoming her experience as a federal boarding school survivor, she has become an internationally celebrated artist and a revered elder dedicated to preserving and sharing Indigenous knowledge.

removed: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Jamescita Peshlakai Matriarch I am Navajo of the Tangle People Clan, born for the Red House clan, maternal grandfathers are of the Deer Water clan, and paternal grandfathers are of the Cliff Dweller clan.
I was born north of the sacred mountain of the west, Doo'ko'osliid (the San Francisco Peaks).
Combat War Veteran I am a combat veteran of the Persian Gulf War.
I previously served in the Arizona legislature as a Representative and a Senator for this district.
I earned my bachelor's and master's degrees at NAU in Flagstaff, and I am currently a student at ASU's Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law.
Knowledge of policies and the legislative process is essential for representing Arizona's citizens.

Proud Democrat Protect our Democracy: Countering extremism Protect our fundamental rights Protect social security and healthcare Lower food and energy costs Job creation and stability Climate change solutions Gun violence prevention Home ownership and housing affordability Protect reproductive rights Immigration and humanity Tribal sovereignty and inclusion Veterans benefits and services Who is Arizona?
We are!
Established Navajo Code Talkers Day in Arizona in 2021 Taking Care of our Home I am committed to civil rights, equity, and justice in Arizona.
This includes educating our citizens about living together.
Arizona needs a leader who can lead by educating and building bridges.
In 2021, I sponsored the legislation (SB1802) that established August 14th as "Arizona Navajo Code Talkers Day", an official state holiday.
My work ensured the recognition of Navajo Code Talkers' contributions to world stability during World War II.
I am one of thousands of federal employees who have lost their jobs.
Many in rural Arizona are finding fewer job opportunities in their home communities.
Some folks are seeing their homes valued less than they had hoped in prior years.
Essentially, their nestegg and savings are dwindling before their eyes.
The American Dream seems lost to us.
It is not lost; we need to elect people who represent the citizens of our amazing state.

LD 6 includes some of the most beautiful parks and natural wonders in the world, including the Grand Canyon, the San Francisco Peaks, Monument Valley and the White Mountains, and the Colorado and Little Colorado Rivers.

Eight tribes make up the majority of district’s constituents; Hualapai, Havasupai, Kaibab Paiute, San Juan Southern Paiute, Navajo, Hopi, White Mountain Apache, San Carlos Apache and some Zuni Pueblo.
The district spans 7 counties and includes Flagstaff, Winslow, Page, Holbrook, Pinetop, Fredonia, and more!

removed: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Mae Peshlakai Experienced Advocate As a Precinct and State Committee Member of the Arizona Democratic Party, Mae has worked or volunteered on the majority of tribal, county, state and federal elections since 1974.

She has traveled all of Arizona’s Legislative District 6 to register voters, collect signatures for candidate petitions, referendums, and educate constituents on the US census and the 2021 redistricting.
Mae is committed to be the voice of the people of rural and tribal Arizona.

Leader and Elder Representative Mae Peshlakai is Diné - Tangle People Clan and born for the Deer Water Clan, maternal grandfathers are of the Salt clan and paternal grandfathers are of the Rock Gap clan.
She is a boarding school survivor.
Mae attended a U.S.
Federal Bureau of Indian Affairs Boarding School in Tolani Lake, Arizona, 100 miles northeast of Flagstaff, Arizona..
Mae was married to James Peshlakai, an accomplished silver and goldsmith.
She took up silversmithing and, to this day, makes jewelry every day as well as weaves.
She and her husband worked with prestigious colleges and universities across the nation sharing the Navajo culture and assisting scholarly research.
Mae knows the issues and challenges of District 6 and has worked tirelessly for two terms representing all the communities of District 6.

Budget Champion Missing and Murdered Indigenous People Hope and Opportunity In 2025, Representative Peshlakai fought and voted for a budget that made historic investments in Indigenous Tribal healthcare and traditional healing practices.
Rep.

Peshlakai was elated to support an opportunity to leverage $100,000 from the state to secure more than $220 million in federal matching funds to cover culturally relevant traditional healing practices that are vital to our way of life and well-being.
Representative Peshlakai co-sponsored Emily's Law, HB2281, which created the new statewide "Turquoise alert" system for missing indigenous people.
The new law was named for Emily Pike, a 14-year-old Indigenous girl who went missing and was murdered in 2024.
Mae has the knowledge and experience to work for our citizens by representing your values, and needs.
Infrastructure investment is a priority for our rural district.
In the 2025 budget Mae also supported $30 million for fire suppression and better pay and training facilities for Northern Arizona firefighters.
Representative Peshlakai understands change in laws and policies are key to creating a home of hope and opportunities.

removed: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Policy Platform Veterans Advocacy Jamescita Peshlakai joined the military for a job at the age of 20 years old and to be able to afford school, just as many young people in our country do.
Jamescita is a combat war veteran of the Persian Gulf War, Desert Storm and she knows the United States government has failed veterans.
Indigenous people serve at the highest percentage in the military, more than any other population.
The Trump administration's cuts to the VA and healthcare, the massive lack of mental healthcare, and lack of support in general has led to the millions of veterans living on the street.
These are policy failures from our Government that must be addressed.
Protecting the Environment Our world is a living being and all life is tethered to Mother Earth.
We are all in this together.
We must focus on de-growth and slowing gas production.
The best solution is to switch to renewables immediately.
Nuclear energy is a false climate solution.
The burden should not be on Indigenous, low income communities, but Indigenous and low income communities should be at the forefront of planning the solutions.

Missing & Murdered As indigenous women our candidates know that Missing and Murdered Indigenous People issues are directly connected to lack of housing, lack of economic opportunities, loss of culture, domestic violence, and just surviving.
Representative Mae Peshlakai is extremely proud to co-sponsor and pass Emily’s bill into law creating the “Turquoise Alert System”.
Emily’s bill was named after Emily Pike, a 14 year old who went missing from a group home and was later found murdered.
Despite the passing of Emily’s Bill there is still so much that needs to be addressed to protect vulnerable people.
The Republicans in control of the legislature have stopped creative legislation addressing this epidemic.
Save Public Education Public Education is the most important investment we can make as a state.
Our youth are our future and a strong public education system is needed to set our young people on the right path.
Over the last few decades in Arizona we’ve seen the result of our underfunded public school system.
We rank near last in the nation in most categories and that is because we’ve refused to properly invest in our children.
With the recent expansion of the ESA program to allow for universal vouchers we are now seeing; 1.
Schools closing around the state 2.
Over $1 billion being looted out of the system.
Over $124 million of these dollars are approved with 0 oversight and have been used to pay for luxury items like diamond rings and electric bikes .
This will have the most negative impact to our rural communities where our public schools have been dealing with decades of budget cuts and under-funding.
This is the wealthy stealing and ensuring that the majority of public schools students in Arizona have less opportunity for a decent future.
We must repeal the universal voucher program, pay teachers and staff a fair wage, and support our students' mental health.
We must once again prioritize public education in our state.
Our legislature is one of the only guardrails to this injustice.
Tribal Sovereignty Arizona has 23 indigenous tribes.
Arizona must recognize the authority and sovereignty of the tribes to govern themselves.
For far too long the federal and state governments have exploited indigenous people.
If the state legislature plans to sell state lands, it should be first offered to indigenous tribes for $1 (which is more than what the US Government paid to tribes).
Medicare for All Healthcare is a human right, and providing that care is the responsibility of the government.
Healthcare on Tribal lands is mandated by treaties and we must respect those treaties.
Additionally, let us expand on that idea.
Healthcare should be a right for everyone.
Legislative oversight is key to ensuring Federal commitments are adhered to.
We will raise our voices and ensure that allocation of funds meet the guidelines of Federal commitments.
Angela, Mae, and Jamescita will also push our state towards Medicare-For-All in any way they can at the state level.
Human Rights Regardless of gender, race, religion, or sexual orientation you should be treated with equality and respect.
The trailblazers are committed to honoring our values and protecting our communities.
Abolish ICE Immigration Customs Enforcement (ICE) is a new agency, it was only created in the last 25 years.
It has become a cruel, broken way to engage in immigration enforcement.
The agency is rotten to its core.
We must completely abolish ICE and create a humane immigration policy.
Being a border state, Arizona has a key role in the national conversation.
We must support our immigrant neighbors.
Remember that you live on stolen land.

Here are notable votes: ​ Taxes & Budget Voted for a constitutional amendment banning any income tax (CACR 10, 2026) Voted for cutting business taxes (HB 155, 2025) Voted against a tax on non-primary residences (HB 1580, 2026) Voted for late budget amendments restoring some police/fire retirement benefits (HB 282, 2025) ​ Education & Parental Rights Voted for a Parental Bill of Rights (HB 10, 2025) Voted for removing some home-school notification/evaluation requirements (HB 1268, 2026) Voted for requiring a local school tax cap vote and limiting admin expenses (HB 1300, 2026) Voted for open enrollment across public schools (SB 101, 2025) Voted for the CHARLIE Act limiting certain teachings on race/sexuality (HB 1792, 2026) Voted for banning "harmful to minors" sexual material in schools (HB 324, 2025) Voted for voter ID requirements and absentee ballot verification ​ Social & Health Issues Voted for biological sex-based classifications in bathrooms, sports, prisons, etc.

(HB 1442 & HB 148) Voted for conscience rights for medical professionals on abortion (HB 232, 2025) Voted against extreme risk protection orders ("red flag" law; HB 1642, 2026) Voted for banning hormone treatments/puberty blockers for minors (with exceptions; HB 377, 2025) Voted to keep school immunization requirements (HB 1811, 2026) Voted against home-growing medical marijuana (HB 53, 2025) Voted to keep penalties for marijuana possession/use (HB 198, 2025) ​ Guns & Criminal Justice Voted against expanded background checks + waiting periods (HB 56, 2025) Voted for banning public colleges from regulating firearms (HB 1793, 2026) ​ Other Voted for repealing Housing Champion program (HB 1196, 2026) Voted for no-cause evictions after lease term (HB 60, 2025) Voted for banning state refugee resettlement involvement (HB 1706, 2026) Voted against sanctuary policies / for local immigration enforcement Voted for allowing utilities to invest in natural gas/nuclear (HB 1775, 2026) ​ Recent Specific Roll Call Examples (May 2025) Yes on HB 1442 (biological sex classifications) Yes on HB 232 (conscience rights) No on HB 1681 (tiny houses/yurts) ​ Paid for by Dennis Mannion 1 Muse Terrace Salem, NH 03079 Treasurer: Dennis Mannion mannion4nh@comcast.net Salem, New Hampshire bottom of page

added: Press Releases ICYMI: Gabe Evans Spends Exorbitant Amount of Taxpayer Money for Hotels and Dining October 14, 2026 · Read the full release Evans Spent the Most Taxpayer Dollars Out of Entire CO Congressional Delegation THORNTON, CO – While Coloradans are struggling to make ends meet, Gabe Evans uses his constituents’ hard earned money to wine and dine out in DC.

A new article by Colorado Public Radio reports that from January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, Evans spent $43,471 from his Members’ Representational Allowance (MRA), a taxpayer funded resource that can be used to “expense housing, whether it be hotels or rent, as well as meals and incidentals without providing receipts.” During that time period, Evans expensed the most out of the entire Colorado Congressional Delegation.
In case you missed it: “According to House data that was released during the time period covering January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, Republican Rep.
Gabe Evans expensed the most of the Colorado delegation.
Evans spent $43,471, with $31,421 going towards housing from January 2025 to May 2026.

An additional $12,050 went towards meals and incidentals during that same time period.” While Evans squeezed out every dime out of his constituents to fund his time in the least effective Congress ever , he made life unaffordable in CD-8.

Gas and diesel prices are climbing with no end in sight because he continues to vote for the reckless war in Iran and his 100% voting record for Donald Trump’s corrupt, chaotic tariffs have made everything from housing to groceries expensive.
“Gabe Evans talks a lot about how Coloradans need to be more fiscally responsible," said Alex Terr, spokesperson for Manny for Colorado .
“But he is totally fine with spending his constituents' money on his lifestyle.

It’s time to elect Manny Rutinel who will work for Colorado’s working families, not bankrupt them for his own gain.” Manny Rutinel Releases New TV Ads: “The Pump” and “The Truth” October 13, 2026 · Read the full release Rutinel highlights Evans’ support of Trump’s Iran War that has raised gas prices, work to prevent the release of the Epstein Files THORNTON, CO – This week, Manny Rutinel for Congress released two new TV ads, “ The Pump ” and “ The Truth .” “The Pump” is a $350,000 initial buy and “The Truth” is a $400,000 initial buy.

removed: About Issues District Map Get Involved Donate Donate About Issues District Get Involved Donate TEXAS SENATE DISTRICT 19 Fighting for the Heart of Texas Marcus Cardenas is a proven small business owner who understands what it takes to create jobs, support families, and keep our communities safe.
Join Our Campaign Our Priorities Texas families deserve a senator who will fight for economic opportunity, public safety, and the values that make our state great.

Together, we'll build a stronger future for District 19. — Marcus Cardenas MEET MARCUS A Leader Who Cares About Texas A True Texas Success Story Marcus Cardenas was born and raised on the Southside of San Antonio, where family, faith, and community shaped every part of his life.
Marcus grew up learning the values of hard work, integrity, and service to community.
As a small business owner Marcus has created jobs, supported families, and contributed to the economic vitality of District 19.
Building a Life Through Perseverance After attending St.
Joseph's Catholic School, Kazen Middle School, and South San High School—where he played basketball—Marcus began his studies at Palo Alto College.
In 2007, tragedy struck when his older brother passed away in a motorcycle accident.
Marcus made the difficult decision to set aside his education and step into the family plumbing business to help support his loved ones.
Through hard work and determination, Marcus built Vertex Concrete, a thriving business that has served District 19 for over a decade.
As a proud father to his daughter Isabella and uncle to his nieces and nephews, Marcus understands what Texas families need: opportunity, safety, and a brighter future.
Invest in Texas' Future Your contribution helps us reach more voters, spread our message, and win this critical race.
Every dollar makes a difference in building a stronger District 19. $25 $50 $100 $250 $500 Cover the processing fee? +$ 1.06 Contribute Now Paid for by Marcus for Texas.
Contributions are not tax-deductible.
OUR PRIORITIES Fighting for What Matters Marcus is focused on the issues that impact District 19 families every single day Economic Development Creating Jobs.
Growing Businesses.
Building Prosperity.
As a successful small business owner, Marcus knows what it takes to create jobs and drive economic growth.
He'll work to attract new businesses to District 19, reduce regulatory burdens on job creators, and ensure Texas remains the best state in America for entrepreneurs and workers alike.
Marcus will fight for policies that support small businesses, lower taxes, and create high-paying career opportunities for Texas families.
Economic prosperity isn't just about numbers—it's about giving every Texan the chance to achieve their dreams.
Public Safety Backing the Blue.
Protecting Families.
Securing Communities.
Every family deserves to feel safe in their home and neighborhood.
Marcus will be a strong voice for law enforcement, fighting to ensure our police have the resources and support they need to keep our communities safe from crime and violence.
Marcus opposes any effort to defund the police and will work to strengthen penalties for violent criminals.
He believes in smart, effective policies that protect law-abiding citizens while holding criminals accountable.
Public safety is not negotiable.
Education & Opportunity Investing in Our Future.
Empowering Parents.
Supporting Teachers.
Quality education is the foundation of opportunity.
Marcus supports increased funding for schools, better pay for teachers, and empowering parents to make the best decisions for their children's education.
Every child in District 19 deserves access to excellent schools.
Infrastructure & Growth Building Better Roads.
Modernizing Systems.
Planning for Tomorrow.
District 19 is growing, and our infrastructure needs to keep pace.
Marcus will fight for investments in roads, bridges, water systems, and broadband internet to ensure our communities can thrive now and in the future.
Smart infrastructure investment means better quality of life for all Texans.

added: Mark will be a strong voice for Sanford's working families in the State Senate, and I hope you will join me in voting for him this November.
Anne-Marie Mastraccio (State Representative for Sanford): I have lived in Sanford for nearly 45 years.
Serving as your Town Councilor, Mayor, and State Representative has been the honor of a lifetime, and it taught me a great deal about our community and how Augusta works.
I know the people of Sanford are struggling: prices are rising rapidly while wages stay the same.
Gas, health care, housing — these costs are forcing families across our state to choose between heating their homes and putting food on the table.
Sanford deserves a state senator who understands these struggles personally, knows how to fight for solutions, and cares enough to do it.
For too long, Matt Harrington has put his own political career ahead of the everyday needs of people in his district.
Sanford needs a fighter, and Mark's years as a union leader at the bargaining table make him the best candidate in this race.

I enthusiastically endorse Mark Vigliotta for State Senate, and I hope you will vote for him on or before November 3rd. markformaine@gmail.com Powered by RUN! website builder Paid for and authorized by Mark Vigliotta for Senate You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.

On October 12th we release our first ad.

PLEASE post this link on social media and forward the link to every third district voter you know.
October 10 - Mark Wins Democratic Support at Hastings Town Hall On October 10th I held a town hall in Hastings that was attended by several prominent Democrats.
One asked about my concerns with the Democratic party, and I responded with two main points.
First, as someone who lives in a rural area, I don’t think people in New York and San Francisco should dictate gun policy in Nebraska.
Second, I felt there were too many in the Democratic party who would rather be right than win an election.
They took MARK FOR NEBRASKA yard signs when the they left.
I really enjoyed meeting them and others who attended.
October 10 - Mark attends Banned Book Protest in Grand Island On October 10th I attended a banned book protest in Grand Island.
As a veteran who swore to uphold the Constitution, and as an author, the idea of book bans repulses me.
I don’t need the government telling me what to read..
When I swear to uphold the Constitution, I won’t just pay lip service to it like Adrian Smith who remains silent while our freedoms are under assault.

Fiction: Jim Desmond's False Attack on Marni von Wilpert Jim Desmond is 100% MAGA, and he is attacking Marni von Wilpert over a paperwork matter the San Diego Ethics Commission fully resolved in 2023.

He is doing it to distract from his own record of pay-to-play politics, including an ongoing state investigation into a developer who donated money after Desmond voted to give that same developer's company county funding.
FICTION: “27 Ethics Violations” FACT: The San Diego Ethics Commission fined the professional campaign treasurer, not Marni.
The treasurer took full responsibility for the late filing of supplemental forms for 27 contributions to Marni’s legal defense fund.
These forms, called Disclosure of Pending Matters forms, are filed with the City Clerk on top of a fund's regular campaign finance reports.
The commission resolved the matter in 2023, after the treasurer agreed to a fine.
FICTION: “Undisclosed donations” FACT: Every contribution was reported on time.
The settlement notes that the legal defense fund filed its regular campaign finance reports, which list all contributions, by the deadline.

For five of the late forms, the Commission also found that the same information "was available to the public through the lobbyist disclosure forms." FICTION: “Fined by the ethics commission” FACT: The Ethics Commission's own settlement says otherwise.

It states that Marni, "a first-time candidate for elective office, reasonably relied on" her professional treasurer to file the forms on time, and that the treasurer "has, therefore, taken full responsibility for the violations." Marni and her treasurer "fully cooperated with the Ethics Commission investigation." THE FACTS ABOUT JIM DESMOND Jim Desmond is a multi-millionaire who has cozied up to developers, and he is under an ongoing investigation for multiple alleged violations of the California Political Reform Act.

A sworn complaint filed with the California Fair Political Practices Commission in 2024 claimed that Desmond failed to properly report his role in a ballot measure committee, and violated conflict-of-interest rules when that committee received a $5,000 contribution from a developer who also leased property Desmond had voted to fund months earlier.
As of this month, the case remained listed as “opened and pending” on the FPPC’s complaint and case information portal.
Desmond is funded by real estate developers, who have given him more than $144,000.

He has faced multiple ethics complaints for allegedly voting to benefit donors, going back to 2018, when he was mayor of San Marcos and a local realtor filed a complaint over council votes on issues affecting donors to his supervisor campaign.
Desmond also faced criticism for budgeting $240,000 to “remodel and renovate his downtown and district office space” shortly after he took office at the county.
Marni von Wilpert has spent her career fighting for working people.

She served as a civil prosecutor in the City Attorney’s Office, where she sued special interests ripping us off – price gougers during the pandemic, corporate polluters for toxic dumping, and the opioid industry for the addiction and devastation they caused.

added.text: Creating a Terms and Conditions Policy

title.after: Terms & Conditions | Marygrunning4in

added: top of page Marygrunning4in.org Menu Close Home Event Details Service List About Blog Feed Contact Events Program List Notifications Groups Members Book Online Blog Terms & Conditions A legal disclaimer The explanations and information provided on this page are only general and high-level explanations and information on how to write your own document of Terms & Conditions.

You should not rely on this article as legal advice or as recommendations regarding what you should actually do, because we cannot know in advance what are the specific terms you wish to establish between your business and your customers and visitors.
We recommend that you seek legal advice to help you understand and to assist you in the creation of your own Terms & Conditions.
Terms & Conditions - the basics Having said that, Terms and Conditions (“T&C”) are a set of legally binding terms defined by you, as the owner of this website.
The T&C set forth the legal boundaries governing the activities of the website visitors, or your customers, while they visit or engage with this website.
The T&C are meant to establish the legal relationship between the site visitors and you as the website owner.
T&C should be defined according to the specific needs and nature of each website.

For example, a website offering products to customers in e-commerce transactions requires T&C that are different from the T&C of a website only providing information (like a blog, a landing page, and so on).

T&C provide you as the website owner the ability to protect yourself from potential legal exposure, but this may differ from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, so make sure to receive local legal advice if you are trying to protect yourself from legal exposure.

What to include in the T&C document Generally speaking, T&C often address these types of issues: Who is allowed to use the website; the possible payment methods; a declaration that the website owner may change his or her offering in the future; the types of warranties the website owner gives his or her customers; a reference to issues of intellectual property or copyrights, where relevant; the website owner’s right to suspend or cancel a member’s account; and much, much more.
To learn more about this, check out our article “ Creating a Terms and Conditions Policy ”.

title.after: Privacy Policy | Marygrunning4in

added: top of page Marygrunning4in.org Menu Close Home Event Details Service List About Blog Feed Contact Events Program List Notifications Groups Members Book Online Blog Privacy Policy A legal disclaimer The explanations and information provided on this page are only general and high-level explanations and information on how to write your own document of a Privacy Policy.

You should not rely on this article as legal advice or as recommendations regarding what you should actually do, because we cannot know in advance what are the specific privacy policies you wish to establish between your business and your customers and visitors.
We recommend that you seek legal advice to help you understand and to assist you in the creation of your own Privacy Policy.

Privacy Policy - the basics Having said that, a privacy policy is a statement that discloses some or all of the ways a website collects, uses, discloses, processes, and manages the data of its visitors and customers.

It usually also includes a statement regarding the website’s commitment to protecting its visitors’ or customers’ privacy, and an explanation about the different mechanisms the website is implementing in order to protect privacy.
Different jurisdictions have different legal obligations of what must be included in a Privacy Policy.
You are responsible to make sure you are following the relevant legislation to your activities and location.

What to include in the Privacy Policy Generally speaking, a Privacy Policy often addresses these types of issues: the types of information the website is collecting and the manner in which it collects the data; an explanation about why is the website collecting these types of information; what are the website’s practices on sharing the information with third parties; ways in which your visitors and customers can exercise their rights according to the relevant privacy legislation; the specific practices regarding minors’ data collection; and much, much more.
To learn more about this, check out our article “ Creating a Privacy Policy ”.

added: top of page Marygrunning4in.org Menu Close Home Event Details Service List About Blog Feed Contact Events Program List Notifications Groups Members Book Online Blog Home Groups Marygrunning4in.org Group Marygrunning4in.org Group Public · 2 members Join Discussion Media Files Members About Back amol shinde March 9, 2026 Unlocking the Potential of Multiplex Assays in Modern Diagnostics In recent years, the field of diagnostics has witnessed remarkable innovations, and multiplex assays have emerged as one of the most transformative tools for researchers and clinicians alike.
Unlike traditional single-target testing methods, multiplex assays allow the simultaneous detection of multiple analytes in a single experiment.
This capability not only saves time but also conserves precious sample material, which is particularly important when dealing with limited patient specimens.
Multiplex Assays The principle behind multiplex assays is relatively straightforward yet powerful.
By using specialized probes or antibodies, these assays can identify and quantify several biomarkers or molecules at once.

This multi-target approach is especially valuable in complex disease conditions such as autoimmune disorders, infectious diseases, and cancer, where multiple pathways or indicators need to be assessed concurrently.
Researchers can obtain a comprehensive snapshot of a patient’s biological state, facilitating earlier and more accurate diagnoses.
One of the key advantages of multiplex assays is their efficiency.
Performing multiple tests in a single run reduces the workload in laboratories and minimizes variability between separate assays.
Additionally, multiplexing can significantly lower costs by reducing the amount of reagents and consumables needed.
This makes it an appealing option for both clinical diagnostics and research settings, where large sample volumes or high-throughput testing are common.
Another important benefit is the ability to detect subtle interactions between biomarkers.
Diseases often manifest through complex biological networks rather than isolated molecular changes.
Multiplex assays provide a more holistic view of these interactions, allowing researchers to identify patterns that might otherwise go unnoticed in single-analyte testing.
This holistic approach can improve our understanding of disease mechanisms and guide the development of more targeted therapies.
Despite these advantages, multiplex assays come with certain challenges.
Designing an assay that maintains sensitivity and specificity for multiple targets simultaneously requires careful optimization.
Cross-reactivity between assay components and interference from complex sample matrices can pose difficulties, making rigorous validation essential.
However, advances in assay design, automation, and analytical software have steadily improved reliability and ease of use.
Looking ahead, multiplex assays are poised to play an increasingly central role in personalized medicine.
By enabling comprehensive profiling of a patient’s molecular landscape, these assays can help clinicians tailor treatment strategies to individual needs.
Furthermore, they offer significant potential in epidemiology and public health, allowing rapid screening for multiple pathogens or immune responses in large populations.

added: top of page Marygrunning4in.org Menu Close Home Event Details Service List About Blog Feed Contact Events Program List Notifications Groups Members Book Online Blog Home Groups Marygrunning4in.org Group Marygrunning4in.org Group Public · 2 members Join Discussion Media Files Members About Back amol shinde March 14, 2026 Understanding the Large Bore Extension Kit and Its Applications A Large Bore Extension Kit is an essential tool used in medical, laboratory, and industrial settings where high-volume fluid transfer or extended reach is required.
Unlike standard tubing or small-bore kits, large bore extensions are designed to handle greater flow rates efficiently, reducing the risk of pressure drops or blockages.
They are particularly valued for their durability, flexibility, and adaptability across multiple applications.
Large Bore Extension Kit In medical environments, these kits often play a crucial role in intravenous therapies, blood transfusions, or surgical procedures where rapid fluid delivery is needed.
The large diameter ensures that fluids move smoothly and consistently, minimizing the chance of hemolysis or turbulence.
Additionally, these kits are often compatible with a variety of medical devices, including infusion pumps, catheters, and drainage systems, making them versatile in critical care scenarios.
For laboratory use, large bore extension kits are instrumental in experiments that require precise fluid handling.
Researchers rely on them when working with viscous liquids, chemical reagents, or biological samples.
Their robust design prevents leaks and ensures accuracy in measurements, which is vital for reproducibility in experiments.
Moreover, the modular nature of many kits allows users to extend or shorten connections without compromising safety or performance.
Industrial applications also benefit from large bore extension kits, particularly in processes involving the transfer of chemicals, water, or other fluids in high volumes.
The reinforced tubing materials resist wear and chemical corrosion, ensuring longevity even under continuous use.
Many kits are designed with easy-to-connect fittings, allowing operators to quickly assemble or disassemble systems as needed.
Another key advantage of these kits is their user-friendly design.
Most kits are lightweight, flexible, and resistant to kinking, which makes them easier to manage in confined or complex spaces.
Some also feature color-coded connectors to prevent misconnection, enhancing operational safety and efficiency.

From our local small businesses and coastal estuaries to the rivers where our kids swim, fish, and grow up, clean water is the lifeblood of our community.
When I first came to Congress, I made a promise that fighting toxic discharges and restoring our waterways would be my mission every single day.
We’ve made incredible strides since then, but I want to make sure everyone in our community sees the tangible results we’ve delivered together.

Today, our campaign launched a new 30-second broadcast TV ad across the Palm Beach media market titled “Major Progress.” In the spot, I take my son, Major, up in a helicopter to show him from the air what years of unrelenting pressure and hard work have accomplished right here in South Florida.
Major Victories for Our Waterways We didn’t just talk about fixing our water problems—we wrote the bills, passed the laws, and secured the funding to get it done.

Here is what we’ve accomplished so far: Fighting Toxic Algae head-on: I authored the South Florida Clean Coastal Waters Act (signed into law in 2022), requiring the first-ever federal assessment and action plan to fight harmful algal blooms in South Florida.
Finishing the Herbert Hoover Dike: We secured full funding to accelerate the rehabilitation project, finishing the work three years early and coming in $300 million under budget .
Fixing Lake Okeechobee Operations: I forced the U.S.
Army Corps of Engineers through legislation to rewrite their outdated lake management schedule.
Under the new plan, discharges into the St.
Lucie Estuary are projected to be stopped 95% of the time under normal operations—up from a miserable 37% under the old schedule.
Fast-Tracking the EAA Reservoir: I wrote the law authorizing the Everglades Agricultural Area (EAA) Reservoir at the federal level and secured over $2 billion to speed up construction.
We pushed the finish line up by 5 full years—moving completion from 2034 to 2029 .

Delivering Record Everglades Funding: We secured a historic $461 million in federal funding for FY2026 to restore natural water flows south, elevate water quality, and protect our coastal communities.
The Mission Isn’t Finished We aren’t taking our foot off the gas.
Just recently, we passed the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 through the House by a 415 to 9 vote.
It includes key provisions I wrote to push more clean water south, hold officials accountable for harmful discharges, and address long-standing navigation safety issues at the Jupiter Inlet.
Protecting Florida’s water has been my mission since day one, and we have major results to show for it.
We’ve improved the way Lake Okeechobee is managed to reduce discharges, fought toxic algae, and accelerated completion of the EAA Reservoir.
We’ve made tremendous progress, but the mission isn’t finished.
As your representative in Congress, I’ll keep fighting until we achieve zero discharges ever again.
Watch the New Ad Thank you for standing with me in this fight.

added: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/848734106_122125675113364925_8940033421710521823_n.jpg|Who needs a debate? A representative's job is to represent the people, all the people, not just the ones who vote for them. That means being willing to engage with them publicly. There's no way to take a question from everyone, but a crowd can get a lot out of listening to an exchange, particularly when that exchange is between candidates. There is no debate planned in the 2nd District this cycle. The Hampton Roads Chamber hosted one in 2024. And in Northern Virginia, the League of Women Voters held an 8th District debate this fall even though the incumbent declined. Bottom line, a debate can be done. So here's my ask to the Hampton Roads Chamber, WHRO Public Media, WAVY TV 10 and The Virginian-Pilot: host one for the candidates willing to attend. I'll be there. Any date, any format, before November 3. Our district isn't alone. Virginia has 11 House races and a Senate race on the ballot. As far as I can find, only the 10th District has put both major-party nominees on the same stage. This from the state that gave the country Washington, Jefferson and Madison. Without debates, voters get millions of dollars in PAC-funded ads instead. I don't take that money. I'd rather earn your vote in front of you. #VA02 #virginiabeach #suffolkva #chesapeake #easternshoreva

title.after: Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY – Delegate Marvin E.

added: Skip to content Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Menu Close Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Blog Home / Latest News / Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY Post author: admin Post published: July 8, 2021 Post category: Latest News The sudden collapse of the 12-story Champlain Towers South condominium building in Surfside, Florida, was a tragedy of a scale normally associated with natural disasters or terrorist attacks.
The exact cause is not yet known and may not be well understood for months yet.

But while the investigation, cleanup and search for missing people efforts continue, the circumstances strongly point to deterioration in the concrete structure that for several years had not been sufficiently addressed by the governing board of the building’s condominium association .
As recently as April, condo owners had been warned that a major renovation was needed in response to serious water damage evident in the basement garage at a cost of more than $15 million.

While few communities have witnessed a sudden building failure of this magnitude, what is far more commonplace is a condominium development — whether a high-rise, collection of townhouses or low-rise apartments — facing insufficient investment in maintenance and replacement of common assets.
Civil lawsuits arise from these circumstances fairly routinely.
Someone’s roof leaks, and the board is alleged not to have kept up with repairs.
The costs add up quickly: Siding needs to be replaced periodically, outdoor spaces replanted, pools resurfaced.
Cracks in the foundation or support columns might be the most expensive (and scariest) possibility of all.
Yet for many condo boards, the focus is always on keeping fees to the minimum.
After all, the higher the fee, the lower the resale price of the unit as buyers look at the total monthly cost of ownership.
In Maryland, government has always treated such arrangements with a relatively light regulatory hand.
Only two counties, Prince George’s and Montgomery, formally review condominium documents, and only Montgomery has the authority to enforce them.
Prince George’s County has taken a slightly different tack that is especially instructive, however.

Since last year, the county requires condo associations and similar bodies to conduct a review every five years to see if they’re collecting enough money (and holding enough in reserves) to meet their projected maintenance costs.
The governing boards must then set fees based on meeting those anticipated needs.
In other words: If your roof needs to be replaced in 10 years, you had better be collecting sufficient money to cover that cost between now and then.
And such studies can’t be conducted by just any Tom, Dick or Harry.
The law requires the contractor to be well-qualified and experienced, recognized by the state board of architects or engineers, for example.
In the wake of the Florida disaster, this appears to be an excellent idea.
Holmes Jr., a Prince George’s Democrat, offered legislation to take his home county’s approach statewide .
It passed the House of Delegates by a 2-to-1 margin but never got serious consideration in the state Senate.
It needs to become a much higher priority in the next legislative session in early 2022.
As Assistant Maryland Attorney General Karen S.

Straughn testified in a House committee in January, such assessments may raise fees in the short-term, but they spare homeowners major increases in the long-term when the bill suddenly comes due for major repairs that had not been properly anticipated.
The measure even allows condo associations to raise fees higher than whatever local cap may exist.
Again, that’s because it’s in the owners’ collective financial interest.
Some developers may oppose the measure.

But during testimony on House Bill 313 , builders did not object to the periodic studies, only asking that there ought to be an exemption for smaller developments with few common assets that are unlikely to generate major new costs.
That seems a reasonable point, particularly for projects where the only common spaces are walkways, parking lots and signs.
There is certainly no reason to make this unduly burdensome.
Indeed, it’s likely that the folks who will appreciate this level of protection most may be the homeowners who volunteer to serve on the governing boards of common ownership communities.
Few enter such arrangements with a deep background in construction, engineering or property management.
The more guardrails the better for these potentially fraught circumstances, particularly for projects like beachfront high-rises where the risks are so high, as the Surfside disaster demonstrated.
Surely, the owners will sleep better knowing that there are periodic assessments of maintenance needs — and the funds to cover them are going to be there when needed.
Baltimore Sun editorial writers offer opinions and analysis on news and issues relevant to readers.
They operate separately from the newsroom.

added: Skip to content Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Menu Close Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Blog Home / Latest News / Today is day-one of the Maryland General Assembly Today is day-one of the Maryland General Assembly Post author: admin Post published: January 14, 2021 Post category: Latest News Today is day-one of the Maryland General Assembly.
In my 18 years of “Day-Ones” this day-one is like no other.
We spent this session primarily adopting the Modified Procedures During a Public Safety Emergency.
These procedures adopted a series of rule changes to allow us to function as a body while simultaneously staying safe and keeping each other safe.
This will be a General Assembly session like no other.

added: Download Map Contact the Campaign District Overview Understanding Georgia House District 157 District Quick Facts Legislative Body: Georgia House of Representatives Region: Southeast Georgia (Coastal Plain) Counties Represented: Appling, Candler, Evans, Jeff Davis, Tattnall Primary Economic Sectors: Agriculture, Forestry & Timber, Healthcare General Election Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 2026 General Election District 157 has an open legislative race following the retirement of long-serving Representative Bill Werkheiser.
Voters in the November 2026 election will choose between Democratic nominee Micah King of Glennville and Republican nominee Bradley B.
Read the 2026 Candidate Guide View County Early Voting Hours & Locations Frequently Asked Questions About District 157 What counties are in Georgia House District 157?
Georgia House District 157 represents communities across Southeast Georgia, including Tattnall County, Jeff Davis County, Appling County, Evans County, and Candler County.
What cities and towns are in District 157?

Major communities include Glennville, Reidsville, Collins, Cobbtown, and Manassas in Tattnall County; Hazlehurst and Denton in Jeff Davis County; Baxley and Surrency in Appling County; Claxton, Hagan, Bellville, and Daisy in Evans County; and Metter and Pulaski in Candler County.
How do I check if my address is in District 157?

You can verify your exact state legislative districts by entering your voter registration information into the official Georgia Secretary of State My Voter Page (mvp.sos.ga.gov) or by downloading our official district map.
What does a Georgia State Representative do?
Members of the Georgia House of Representatives serve two-year terms in the Georgia General Assembly in Atlanta.

Representatives author, debate, and vote on the annual state budget, state tax policy, healthcare appropriations, infrastructure funding, and rural economic policies directly affecting local communities.

Below are the official physical locations and contact details for each county: County Designated Early Voting Facility Physical Address & Directions Regular Weekday Hours Office Phone Appling County Board of Elections Office 83 South Oak Street Baxley, GA 31513 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 367-8113 Evans County Courthouse Annex (Suite 8) 201 Freeman Street Claxton, GA 30417 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 739-0708 Jeff Davis County Public Safety Facility 15 Public Safety Drive Hazlehurst, GA 31539 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 375-6635 Tattnall County Central Elections Office 114 W Brazell Street Reidsville, GA 30453 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 557-6417 Note for Tattnall County voters: Advance early voting is conducted at the Board of Elections central office in Reidsville.

Priority Line Accommodations During Advance Voting Under Georgia law ( O.C.G.A. § 21-2-385.1 ), electors who are 75 years of age or older, electors who have a physical disability, or electors accompanied by a child two years of age or younger are entitled upon request to poll officials to vote without waiting in line during advance in-person voting.

(Note: On Election Day, a similar provision under O.C.G.A. § 21-2-409.1 entitles electors aged 75 or older or those with physical disabilities to vote without waiting in line between 9:30 AM and 4:30 PM).

Statewide Constitutional Amendments Your ballot includes three proposed constitutional amendments: Amendment 1 (HR 32): Increasing the Conservation Use Value Assessment (CUVA) farm and timber property tax cap from 2,000 to 4,000 acres.
Amendment 2 (HR 251): Requiring nonpartisan elections for all probate court judges statewide.

Constituent Access & Town Halls • District 157 Voting Logistics & Dates • The Choice for District 157 When voters across Appling, Evans, Jeff Davis, and Tattnall Counties cast their ballots in the 2026 General Election, they will decide who represents Southeast Georgia in the Georgia House of Representatives for the next two years.
This seat has seen significant political transition this year.
After ten years of service, incumbent Republican Representative Bill Werkheiser was defeated in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary by challenger Bradley Anderson.
Voters now face a clear choice between two local residents with distinct backgrounds, experiences, and legislative visions: Micah King and Bradley B.

To help voters make an informed decision at the ballot box, this guide provides an objective, side-by-side comparison of the candidates, their professional backgrounds, and their approaches to the most urgent issues facing rural Southeast Georgia.
Quick Race Overview Detail Micah King Bradley B.

Anderson Party Nomination Democratic Party Republican Party Hometown Glennville, GA (Tattnall County) Reidsville, GA (Tattnall County) Primary Background Former City Councilman, Educator, Financial Counselor (AFC®) Small Business Owner, Funeral Director, Former Police Chief & Coroner Key Issues Rural hospital stabilization, utility rate reform, family farm tax protection Small business deregulation, public safety support, traditional conservative values Campaign Website votega157.com electbradleyb.com The Candidates: Background & Public Service Bradley B.
Anderson is a lifelong resident of Tattnall County and a well-known local business owner in Reidsville.
Business & Community Roots: Anderson is a licensed funeral director and the owner and operator of Bradley B.
Through his business, he has served families across Tattnall and neighboring rural counties for decades during times of loss.

Law Enforcement & Public Service: Prior to his legislative campaign, Anderson’s public service career included work in local law enforcement, where he served as a municipal police chief and as Tattnall County Coroner.

Primary Victory: In the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, Anderson mounted an active challenge against incumbent Representative Bill Werkheiser, securing the Republican nomination on a platform centered on business experience, public safety, and conservative community values.
Micah King (Democratic Nominee) Micah King is a former Glennville City Councilman, educator, and financial professional rooted in Tattnall County.
Municipal Governance: As a member of the Glennville City Council, King worked directly on municipal budgeting, infrastructure maintenance, public works, and community services.
His local government service centered on fiscal responsibility and making city hall responsive to daily constituent needs.
Financial & Educational Background: Professionally, King works as an Accredited Financial Counselor (AFC®) and educator.
His career has focused on helping working families, rural workers, and young adults navigate debt, kitchen-table budgeting, utility costs, and career transitions.

Community Advocacy: King launched his legislative campaign to bring proactive, accessible representation to the Gold Dome, emphasizing constituent service, transparent communication, and quarterly open town halls across all four district counties.
Where the Candidates Stand on Key Issues District 157 faces challenges that transcend national partisan talking points.
From hospital solvency and utility rates to timber preservation and local school funding, here is how the race frames the central questions facing Southeast Georgia.
Rural Healthcare & Hospital Solvency Southeast Georgia has experienced significant strain on its healthcare infrastructure.
Facilities like Evans Memorial Hospital in Claxton and Appling Healthcare in Baxley provide essential emergency care, local jobs, and maternal health services, but operate under tight margins.
Micah King’s Approach: King views rural healthcare preservation as an urgent economic and public safety priority.

He advocates for targeted state stabilization funds for rural independent hospitals, higher Medicaid reimbursement rates for rural healthcare providers, and incentives to recruit and retain doctors and nurses in Appling, Evans, Jeff Davis, and Tattnall Counties.

Bradley Anderson’s Approach: Drawing from his business background, Anderson emphasizes reducing bureaucratic burdens, lowering state healthcare mandates, and supporting free-market options to expand access while maintaining fiscal discipline in state budget appropriations.

Utility Bills, Power Rates & Data Center Growth Georgia power bills have climbed sharply due to multi-billion-dollar infrastructure buildouts and an unprecedented surge in commercial electricity demand from high-load data centers across the state.
Micah King’s Approach: King has called for aggressive consumer ratepayer protection.

He supports legislation to ensure large industrial power consumers (such as massive AI data centers) pay their fair share of new power generation costs, rather than having utility monopolies shift grid expansion costs onto rural homeowners, small businesses, and church electricity bills.

Bradley Anderson’s Approach: Anderson aligns with pro-growth economic development, emphasizing that Georgia’s competitive energy sector and business-friendly regulatory climate attract capital investment, create commercial tax revenue, and support statewide job creation.
Agriculture, Timber & Family Farm Taxes Agriculture and forestry are the economic lifeblood of District 157.
Local onion growers in Glennville, timber tract owners across Appling and Jeff Davis, and poultry producers face rising input costs, unpredictable weather events, and property reassessments.

Micah King’s Approach: King strongly supports Georgia Constitutional Amendment 1 on the 2026 ballot to increase the Conservation Use Value Assessment (CUVA) acreage cap from 2,000 to 4,000 acres, ensuring family farms and multi-generational timber growers are not taxed out of their land.
He supports targeted tax exemptions for agricultural equipment and fertilizer inputs.

Bradley Anderson’s Approach: Anderson supports protecting agricultural property rights, reducing state regulations on farm operations, and maintaining low statewide income and business tax rates to keep Georgia agribusiness globally competitive.
Constituent Access & Town Halls Representation in the Georgia General Assembly requires staying connected to the people back home throughout the legislative session.
Micah King’s Approach: King has pledged a strict open-door policy, promising to hold regular, quarterly town halls across Appling, Evans, Jeff Davis, and Tattnall Counties.

The campaign formally invited Bradley Anderson to a joint candidate debate at the Glennville Town Hall on Saturday, October 17, 2026, keeping a reserved podium open for him to engage directly with constituents.

Bradley Anderson’s Approach: Anderson has conducted traditional grassroots campaigning, meeting with constituents at community events, civic club meetings, and local small businesses throughout the district, emphasizing his established reputation and deep personal ties as a trusted local businessman.

District 157 Voting Logistics & Dates Whether voting early or on Election Day, all registered voters across the district have multiple options to cast their ballots: In-Person Advance Voting Window: Tuesday, October 13 - Friday, October 30, 2026 Mandatory Saturday Voting Days: Saturday, October 17 & Saturday, October 24, 2026 Absentee Application Deadline: Friday, October 23, 2026 General Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 (7:00 AM - 7:00 PM) For detailed polling locations, contact information for county election boards, and voter identification rules, review our comprehensive District 157 Early Voting Guide .
To verify your registration status and view your official precinct sample ballot, visit the official Georgia Secretary of State My Voter Page (mvp.sos.ga.gov) .

The Choice for District 157 The representative elected to House District 157 will cast votes on the state budget, tax policy, healthcare access, and rural development that directly affect families in Baxley, Claxton, Glennville, Hazlehurst, Reidsville, and every community in between.
Voters have a meaningful choice between two dedicated local leaders.
Make your voice heard by participating in advance voting or casting your ballot on Tuesday, November 3.

Why Showing Up Matters – Key Community & Election Resources On Saturday, October 17, 2026 , our campaign is hosting an open, public District 157 Community Town Hall at the South Tattnall Middle School Gym in Glennville , starting at 6:00 PM .
Earlier that same day, all four counties across District 157 will open their doors for Mandatory Saturday Early Voting .

Whether you cast your ballot on Saturday morning or plan to vote later in the advance window, this guide provides practical logistics for Saturday’s polling hours, driving directions, event details, and an objective breakdown of the three statewide constitutional amendments on the 2026 general election ballot.
District 157 Community Town Hall (Saturday, October 17) Public service begins with showing up where people live and listening to their real concerns.
Our campaign formally invited Republican nominee Bradley Anderson to join us on stage for a joint debate.
While he declined that invitation, our invitation remains open should he choose to attend.

The evening will proceed as an open-floor constituent forum where questions will be taken directly from the floor regarding rural healthcare, agricultural policy, living costs, and local infrastructure: Event: District 157 Community Town Hall & Open Q&A Date & Time: Saturday, October 17, 2026 | Starting at 6:00 PM Location & Directions: South Tattnall Middle School Gym, 721 E Barnard St, Glennville, GA 30427 (Tap for driving directions) Add to Calendar: Add to Google Calendar | Download iCal / Outlook (.ics) Format: Open-floor microphone for direct constituent questions with Micah King.
Questions will be taken directly from the floor.
Admission: 100% free and open to the public.
All voters from Appling, Evans, Jeff Davis, and Tattnall Counties are welcome.

Come ask direct questions about the future of Evans Memorial Hospital, staffing and infrastructure challenges surrounding Smith State Prison, agricultural protections, living costs, or how state tax dollars are distributed back to rural roads and trade schools.

Mandatory Saturday Early Voting: Where & When to Vote (October 17) For residents across Southeast Georgia - including shift workers at Plant Hatch, timber haulers, poultry processing employees, and busy farm families - voting between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM on weekdays can be difficult.
Georgia election law ( O.C.G.A. § 21-2-385 ) requires every county in the state to provide two mandatory Saturday voting days during the advance voting window.
The first mandatory Saturday is October 17, 2026 .
During advance voting, you do not have to travel to an assigned neighborhood precinct.

Registered voters may cast a ballot at any designated early voting location within their county of residence: County-by-County Advance Polling Locations County Designated Advance Polling Site Address & Driving Directions Saturday Hours Office Phone Appling County Board of Elections Office 83 South Oak Street Baxley, GA 31513 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 367-8113 Evans County Courthouse Annex (Suite 8) 201 Freeman Street Claxton, GA 30417 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 739-0708 Jeff Davis County Public Safety Facility 15 Public Safety Drive Hazlehurst, GA 31539 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 375-6635 Tattnall County Central Elections Office 114 W Brazell Street Reidsville, GA 30453 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (912) 557-6417 Note for Tattnall County voters: Advance early voting is conducted at the Board of Elections central office in Reidsville.
Glennville voters can take advantage of Saturday voting in Reidsville during the day, then join neighbors in Glennville at the gym that evening.
