added: HB 94 September 17, 2019 admin Criminal Law and Courts Comments are Closed 0 This Act will increase payments of child support arrears or retroactive support from payments for settlements and awards from negligence, personal injury, and workers compensation cases by requiring that all insurers share information with an insurance claim data collection organization.

The Division of Child Support Services (“Division”) uses an insurance claim data collection organization to match individuals who are in arrears on child support or who owe retroactive child support with individuals with insurance claims based upon negligence, personal injury, or workers’ compensation cases.
The data collection organization performs a data match of the claimants provided by insurers and child support obligors provided by the Division.

The data collection organization provides reports of matches to the Division so that the Division can issue a lien against the insurance claim to collect the child support arrears or retroactive support.
Currently, some insurers voluntarily submit claim information to the insurance claim data collection organization and in 2018, $424,977 in unpaid child support was collected through this process.
This Act requires that all insurers submit claim information to the insurance claim data collection organization and is expected to collect an additional $150,000 – $200,000 in unpaid child support.
This Act also allows written notice of a lien or action to perfect the lien to be sent by electronically or by first class mail to conform to industry practices.
This Act also makes technical corrections to conform existing law to the standards of the Delaware Legislative Drafting Manual.

Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed HB 102 September 17, 2019 admin Criminal Law and Courts Comments are Closed 0 This bill allows a person who is arrested or convicted of any crime, except a violent felony, which was a direct result of being a victim of human trafficking may file an application or for a pardon or expungement or make a motion to vacate judgment.
This bill also makes changes to the Human Trafficking Interagency coordinating by adding another member of the judicial branch and a representative of the Department of Education.
This bill also adds locations where a public awareness sign must be placed.

Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed SB 57 September 17, 2019 admin Consumer Protection Comments are Closed 0 This Act makes clear that a retail licensee may only purchase authorized product from an importer, also known as wholesaler, except that a retail licensee may purchase up to 20 gallons a day from a premises licensed to sell for off-premises consumption.
This Act also clarifies that off-premises licensees may sell untapped kegs for off-premises consumption.
Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed Prev.
removed: HS 1 for HB 105 September 17, 2019 admin Health and Social Services Comments are Closed 0 Step therapy protocols are a mechanism by which health insurance companies require patients to try one or more prescriptions drugs before coverage is provided for the actual drug prescribed by the patient’s health care provider.

This Act creates a Step Therapy Exception Process whereby patients who are required by their insurance company to go through step therapy protocols can, under certain circumstances, bypass step therapy to obtain the initially-prescribed medication.
This Act does not apply to state or federal governmental plans.

Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed HB 40 September 17, 2019 admin Open Government/Government Operations Comments are Closed 0 This bill: (1) increases the number of directors on the Board and allows the Board to appoint four additional directors; (2) implements clarifying language; (3) sunsets the former Advisory Council to replace it with a subcommittee structure to allow greater participation from members of the public and to allow the Corporation to appoint and receive assistance and expertise from a greater variety of experts; and (4) allows the Board of Directors to amend the Certificate of Incorporation with approval from the General Assembly.
Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed HCR 34 September 17, 2019 admin Social Policy Comments are Closed 0 This resolution recognizes April 29, 2019 as World Wish Day in Delaware.

All Posts Search FOR Immediate RELEASE nikkigronli Jun 30 1 min read This past Thursday, the U.S.
Supreme Court made a reckless decision by siding with Bayer-Monsanto, making it harder for Americans to hold the company accountable in state courts.
Elected and appointed officials have a duty to protect the people they serve.

That's why it was deeply disappointing to see my opponent, Marty Jackley, use his office to sign an amicus brief supporting Bayer-Monsanto and its Roundup weed killer instead of standing with the people of South Dakota.
Our neighboring state of Iowa is expected to see more than 22,000 new cancer diagnoses this year, many linked to agricultural chemical exposure.
This ruling makes it even more difficult for farmers and families to seek justice in their own state courts.
My opponent talks about states' rights and limiting federal power, but when it mattered, his actions told a different story.

Listen.

Do the Work. nikkigronli Jun 18 3 min read An Important Weekend on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation On Saturday, June 13, I attended a candidate forum at Thunder Valley Community Development Corporation in the Porcupine community on the Pine Ridge Reservation.
Thunder Valley is an Indigenous-led nonprofit organization that addresses a wide range of issues on the reservation.
I was excited to join other federal, state, and tribal candidates for an afternoon of introductions, conversation, and listening.
Community members shared their perspectives on issues affecting the Oglala Sioux Tribe.
We also discussed the constitutional amendments that will be on November’s ballot and concerns related to voter access and engagement.
Most important to me was hearing, first-hand, about tribal members’ priorities and experiences.
Over the last nine months, I’ve learned how truly valuable the opportunity to listen is to this campaign.
Every community in South Dakota has its own unique strengths, challenges, perspectives, and those on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation are no different.
I believe meaningful representation begins with showing up, asking questions, and taking time to understand experiences different from your own.
It is where policy should begin.
It was an important and informative afternoon.

I left the gathering with a deeper understanding of the challenges facing this community and a renewed commitment to building the trust and relationships necessary to effectively represent this and similar communities across our state.

A specific thanks to Elaine MatoTamHecha and Andrew Cisneros of Oceti Sakowin Ho Was’te, who organized the TVCDC event, as well as those from the community, and other democratic candidates who participated.
DAY TWO The following day, June 14 - Flag Day, the same delegation and I had the opportunity and honor to speak with Oglala Lakota veterans at a wacipi held in their honor.
Our candidate delegation once again made introductions, this time via KILI Radio’s tribal vets radio hour.
We also had the opportunity to share our perspectives on a range of important issues.
I specifically spoke about health care for our veterans, school lunch programs, and a few other relevant topics.
Later that afternoon, the delegation and I had the privilege of an impromptu conversation with Tribal President Frank Star Comes Out.
It was an important opportunity to hear directly from tribal leadership about the challenges, priorities, and opportunities facing the Oglala Sioux Tribe.
The President also invited us to share our ideas and goals as elected officials.
As our conversation wound down, President Star Comes Out presented each of us with a challenge coin, a meaningful and unexpected honor.
For those not familiar, a challenge coin is often given by military leaders, elected officials, and other dignitaries to recognize service, achievement, or partnership.
I viewed this gesture as a sign of respect and an encouraging start to our relationship with tribal leadership.
One of my favorite parts of the day was watching tribal members of all ages prepare for and participate in a wacipi honoring their veterans.
As I observed all the pride and pageantry, I reflected on the many wacipis I have attended over the years and found myself drawn to the same conclusion.
These gatherings are a powerful expression of living culture deeply rooted in generational tradition, resilience, and deep pride.

The wacipi also reminded me about the importance of ensuring that tribal nations have the resources and support necessary to preserve and strengthen their languages, traditions, and cultural practices for future generations.
One final note...
The Indian Taco I had for lunch was bigger than my head, and the picture below doesn’t do justice to how large the fry bread was.
If you’re wondering, it was delicious.

title.after: The Big, Epic Road Trip: 1,400 Miles of Listening to South Dakota

added: top of page NIKKI G FOR SD DONATE HOME PRIORITIES ABOUT EVENTS NEWS ENDORSEMENTS CONTACT More Use tab to navigate through the menu items.

All Posts Search The Big, Epic Road Trip: 1,400 Miles of Listening to South Dakota press2950 #ago 2 min read Last week, I traveled more than 1,400 miles across South Dakota, starting at my home near Dell Rapids and winding through communities from De Smet and Clark to Herreid and Lemmon, Hot Springs, Martin, and Wanblee.
Jenny Sampson, Sioux Falls resident and campaign volunteer, joined me for five days on the road.
We met with farmers, ranchers, educators, healthcare professionals, small business owners, retirees, and people from all walks of life.
We visited coffee shops, a hospital, wacipi, livestock auction, and Main Streets.
We knocked on doors, delivered yard signs, and had conversations with Republicans, Independents, and Democrats.
Every stop reinforced something I’ve believed throughout my career: You can’t represent people you aren’t willing to listen to.
The conversations were as diverse as the communities themselves, and common concerns emerged.
In De Smet, we talked about supporting education and the importance of protecting federal support for children with disabilities and special needs.
In Aberdeen, we discussed accountability in government.
In Herreid, I revisited my time at USDA Rural Development and the creative approaches to housing and maintaining essential services in small towns.
In Mobridge, we toured the new regional hospital and discussed the future of rural healthcare.
In McIntosh, we stopped by the school and daycare, both projects from my USDA days.
In Lemmon, we saw how investments in art and local leadership can breathe new life into downtown.
From the Martin Livestock Auction to the small businesses of Hot Springs, I heard concerns about affordability, access to services, and the future of rural communities.
They are everyday challenges that deserve practical solutions.
The Black Hills brought another set of important conversations about protecting public lands, water, wildlife, and the natural beauty that belongs to all of us.
We also joined the Native American Day celebrations and the Black Hills Powwow, opportunities to connect with Tribal communities and honor their cultures and traditions.
In Rapid City, I was encouraged to see people from different political backgrounds come together and recognize that their voices and votes matter.
Along the way, I was reminded that South Dakota’s economy isn’t one-size-fits-all.
What matters to a rancher near Martin may be different from what matters to a young family in Aberdeen or a teacher in De Smet.
Good representation requires understanding those differences, finding common ground, and making sure no community is overlooked.
During my time leading USDA Rural Development in South Dakota, I came to know many of these communities and the people who work tirelessly to keep them strong.
This trip reminded me why I value this experience so much.
South Dakota is filled with hidden gems, remarkable people, and communities finding creative ways to meet their challenges.
I came home tired, inspired, and more determined than ever to bring their voices to Washington.

Whether you live in our largest city or at the end of a gravel road, whether you’re a farmer, a business owner, a teacher, a retiree, or someone just trying to make ends meet, you deserve a representative who shows up, listens, and does the work.
That’s the kind of leadership I believe in, and that’s the commitment I’m making to South Dakota.

title.before: When Disaster Strikes, South Dakotans Come Together

removed: top of page NIKKI G FOR SD DONATE HOME PRIORITIES ABOUT EVENTS NEWS ENDORSEMENTS CONTACT More Use tab to navigate through the menu items.
All Posts Search When Disaster Strikes, South Dakotans Come Together nikkigronli Jun 30 2 min read Just last week, I was in Highmore celebrating Old Settler Days.
I had planned to use this week’s News from the Road to reflect on the thoughtful conversations I had there about the future of public education.
Then everything changed.
On Monday, June 29, straight-line winds devastated the Highmore community.
Gusts reaching 131 mph ripped roofs from homes, flattened farm buildings, and crushed grain bins like tin cans.
According to various local news sources, these may have been the second strongest directly measured straight-line thunderstorm wind gusts ever recorded.
One of the things I have always admired about South Dakota is how neighbors respond in moments like these.
People don’t wait to be asked.
They simple show up.
They share generators, clear debris, cut fallen trees, and check on one another.
I’ve witnessed that spirit since I was a child, and it remains one of the greatest strengths of our state.
That generosity gets recovery started, but rebuilding homes, farms, and businesses requires more than volunteer labor.
Families and business owners need insurance companies to honor the commitments they’ve made, and they need disaster assistance programs that work efficiently when disaster strikes.
Whether it’s severe storms, flooding, wildfires, or damaging winds, communities across South Dakota are experiencing more frequent and more costly weather events.
We cannot ignore what is happening, and we have a responsibility to prepare for it.
Preparation begins at home.
Every homeowner, renter, farmer, and business owner should review their insurance coverage and understand what is, and isn’t, protected before disaster strikes.
Insurance only works when the promises made in a policy are honored.
Families and businesses that have faithfully paid their premiums deserve timely, fair claims processing when they need it most.
Holding insurance companies accountable for the coverage they have sold is essential to protecting working families and rural communities.
Government also has an important responsibility.
When disasters overwhelm local resources, FEMA exists to help communities recover.
Too often, however, its response has been slow, difficult to navigate, and inconsistent for the people depending on it.
Disaster assistance should be efficient, transparent, and focused on getting people back on their feet, not buried in paperwork and delays.

As South Dakota’s representative in Congress, I will work to strengthen disaster preparedness, improve coordination between local, state, and federal partners, and ensure FEMA delivers the timely, accountable service taxpayers expect.
Our communities deserve a recovery system that works when lives, homes, farms, and small businesses are on the line.
My thoughts are with everyone in Highmore as they begin the difficult work of recovery.
South Dakotans have always taken care of one another in times of need.
Now it’s up to our public institutions and private partners to do the same.
To see drone footage of the damage, check out AeroAg Drone Services video.
Want to help the community of Highmore recover?
You can find information here .

added: top of page Home About Norma Endorsements Priorities Get Involved Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Media Photos Videos Photos Videos Menu Close DONATE About Norma Torres Congresswoman Norma Torres is a mom, Nani, and community servant dedicated to working families in the Inland Empire.
Congresswoman Torres moved to Pomona in 1990 to raise a family and call the Inland Empire home.
Congresswoman Torres believes the working families in our communities know what’s needed: safer streets, stronger schools, good jobs, and a government that actually responds.
That’s why Congresswoman Torres stepped up to serve and has worked to deliver for the Inland Empire.
Now, Congresswoman Torres is running to keep pushing for our communities’ priorities and making sure working families aren’t left behind.
That includes defending them from the Trump Administration’s immigration abuses and attempts to gut our healthcare and educational systems.
1990 - 2008 911 Dispatcher Norma started her career as a 911 dispatcher for the LAPD, serving the community for 17 years.
She often worked the graveyard shift, sitting four floors below ground, taking calls every day from people from all walks of life, often in their most vulnerable moments.
After a particularly tragic 911 call, Norma reached out to the Los Angeles City Council to improve access to emergency services.

As a result, Norma led the successful fight to recruit and hire more bilingual operators and ensure that bilingual operators were on call for every work shift, as well as improved training for all dispatchers, securing a $350,000.00 grant to upgrade the computer system and founding the Community Outreach Program to teach the general public how to properly use the 911 emergency system.
2000 - 2006 City Council Member While working at the 911 dispatch center, Norma was an active member of AFSCME, which challenged its members to become more involved and run for local office.
She rose to the challenge and unseated a long-time incumbent for City Council in Pomona who had long stopped being responsive to the needs of the community.

As a City Councilmember, Norma led many initiatives to improve the quality of life in Pomona and combat crime, including the Neighbors for Pomona Committee, which was dedicated to reducing crime and graffiti in the community.
2006 - 2008 Mayor of Pomona Norma was sworn in as the first Latina Mayor of Pomona in February 2006 after winning an 11-way primary for the seat.

As the Mayor of Pomona, Norma continued to fight to keep Pomona safe by imposing gang injunctions limiting gang member activities, which substantially reduced the severity of Pomona’s gang violence problem.
In 2008, she was selected to serve as the Treasurer of the National Conference of Democratic Mayors.

2008 - 2012 Member of the California State Assembly Serving as the Assemblywoman representing California’s 61st district, Norma served as the Chair of the Committee on Housing and Community Development at a time when the recession and housing crisis had left thousands of families struggling financially.
In response to the crisis, she successfully led an effort to secure $2 billion in federal funds for the “Keep Your Home California” program.
The Keep Your Home California Program helped nearly 100,000 families stay in their homes and kept them from becoming homeless.
Norma also helped pass the Homeowner’s Bill of Rights to protect consumers from foreclosure and worked to make it easier for returning veterans to purchase homes.
2011 The Order of the Great Congress of Guatemala Norma was born in Guatemala, but moved to the United States because of instability in the country.

Norma has been an honored guest in Guatemala, where she toured the country, met with Heads of State, and received the country’s highest honor — the Order of the Great Congress of Guatemala, in the rank of Knight.
In 2011 while serving in the State Assembly, Norma was invited by the President of the Guatemalan Congress to speak before congress during their plenary session.

During a ceremony the Guatemalan National Palace, Norma was also awarded with the " Cambio de la Rosa de la Paz ," which honors individuals or organizations for their contributions to human rights, justice, and peace-building.

2013 - 2014 Member of the California State Senate After winning a hard-fought special election for the California State Senate, Norma represented California’s 32nd District where she fought to create jobs in the Inland Empire at a time when families were still recovering from the recession.
She advocated for job training programs, access to higher education, and other tools to improve the skills people need to get better-paying jobs.
She also strongly advocated for services and programs to help families transition out of the recession, keep their homes and ensure quality education is available for our children.
During her time in the Legislature, Torres also made significant contributions to successfully implementing the Affordable Care Act for California’s patients and consumers.
She also took on public corruption, introducing legislation to strengthen California’s anti-bribery laws, close loopholes, and hold those involved in corruption accountable.

January 2016 Visit to Guatemala with Joe Biden In January 2016, Norma was invited by Vice President Biden to represent Congress and join him at the swearing-in of the new President of Guatemala, Jimmy Morales.

Prior to the swearing-in, Norma founded the bipartisan Congressional Central America Caucus, which focuses on the root causes of instability in Central America and in particular, the Northern Triangle countries, supporting a strategy of governance, security, and prosperity in the region.
Through these efforts, Norma worked closely with the Vice President on rooting out public corruption.
2015 - Present Member of Congress As the Congresswoman representing California’s 35th district, Norma has been a powerful advocate for the working families of the Inland Empire.
Norma is a member of the House Committee on Appropriations, one of the most influential committees in Congress, which funds the federal government.
Her top priority has been fighting for funding and programs that are critical to the development of the Inland Empire.
On this Committee, she has secured improvements in our communities when it comes to housing, transportation, protecting fair elections, and job creation.

She has also introduced legislation to spur investment in our infrastructure and was instrumental in achieving local control for the Ontario Airport, which has seen the airport grow by 10% in recent years.

Congresswoman Torres has been dedicated to making sure working families in the Inland Empire aren’t left behind, fighting to lower our cost of living, build more housing and protect our communities from the Trump Administration’s attempts to gut our healthcare and educational systems.

While Congresswoman Torres has been actively working to pass comprehensive immigration reform while supporting the development of neighboring countries to address the root causes of immigration, she is strongly opposed to the barbaric immigration practices of the Trump Administration.

Whether its family separations at our nation’s southern border, Trump’s indiscriminate mass deportation program, or his attempts to gut immigration judges or limit oversight of detention centers, Norma has been fighting tooth and nail to hold this Administration accountable for the damage it has done to families.

Norma Torres secures $100,000 in federal funding for WesternU’s Health Career Ladder programs Health Care is a Human Right Congresswoman Torres strongly believes that health care is a human right.
The United States is one of the wealthiest countries in the world, and no one should go without affordable and comprehensive health insurance.

During her tenure in Congress, she has fought to strengthen the Affordable Care Act, expand community health centers in the Inland Empire, and eliminate the barriers preventing Americans from accessing the care they deserve.
She strongly opposed the Medicaid cuts in the Republican Big Ugly bill, and is fighting to restore these critical health services to millions of Americans.

added: top of page Home About Norma Endorsements Priorities Get Involved Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Media Photos Videos Photos Videos Menu Close DONATE NORMA'S PRIORITIES HOUSING Housing is a critical issue that resonates across our nation, but it is especially pressing in our communities, where the demand for safe and affordable homes continues to outpace supply. ​ Congresswoman Torres is a recognized leader in Congress, tirelessly advocating for policies that promote the construction of new housing and the preservation of affordable options.

As Chair of the New Democrat Coalition Working Group on Housing, Infrastructure, and Transportation, she understands that stable, affordable housing is the foundation for thriving families and communities, and she is committed to ensuring that everyone has a place to call home.

And, as a senior Member of the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Subcommittee of Appropriations, Congresswoman Torres has successfully fought against Trump Administration funding cuts to critical affordable housing and homelessness prevention programs. ​ In addition to advocating for increased funding for affordable housing initiatives, Congresswoman Torres works to remove barriers to homeownership and support innovative housing solutions.
These efforts are essential to tackling the housing crisis head-on, creating pathways for families to secure their futures and build strong, vibrant neighborhoods.

added: top of page Home About Norma Endorsements Priorities Get Involved Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Media Photos Videos Photos Videos Menu Close DONATE NORMA'S PRIORITIES IMMIGRATION IN THE NEWS Three-day, 40-mile walk held in support of immigration bill authored by Congresswoman Norma Torres The Fairness to Freedom Act Will Save Lives House Registry Bill Would Help Millions of Documented, Undocumented Immigrants IE Congresswoman: Trump’s New Immigration Rules Are an ‘Excuse to Rid the Country of People Who Look Like Me’ Building a Compassionate Immigration System Congresswoman Torres recognizes the essential need to address the root causes of migration forcing so many from Latin America to flee violence and lack of opportunity in their home countries.

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Central America Caucus and the New Americans Caucus, she is focused on reforming our immigration system to be more compassionate, flexible, and responsive to the needs of those who simply want to pursue the American Dream.

She has authored the Fairness to Freedom Act, which would guarantee a right to a lawyer in deportation cases, and the Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929, which would update our immigration laws to allow millions of immigrants to adjust their status and start on a path to citizenship.
She understands that we can secure our border and deliver the empathy and humanity that so many of our southern neighbors need right now.

removed: Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE In the News Alliance for Retired Americans Endorses Norma Torres for Congress Seniors Honoring our seniors with dignity, care, and lasting security.
Seniors in our community deserve dignity, respect, and the resources to age comfortably.

As the population of older adults in the Inland Empire continues to grow, Congresswoman Torres is dedicated to ensuring that seniors have access to the healthcare, retirement security, and support services they need.

On the Appropriations Committee, she has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare, ensuring these vital programs remain strong for current and future generations, and voted to lower the cost of prescription drugs, so seniors no longer have to choose between medication and other necessities.
She has introduced legislation to help seniors affected by DOGE cuts at the Social Security Administration so that our seniors can receive all the benefits they earned from years of hard work.
Beyond healthcare, Congresswoman Torres is working to make sure seniors can live independently and remain connected to their communities.
She secured federal funding for the City of Ontario’s Active Seniors on the Go program, expanding transportation options and mobile nutrition services for seniors.

By supporting these initiatives, Congresswoman Torres is committed to enhancing the quality of life for seniors across our communities, ensuring that they have the security and resources to thrive." Powered by Squarespace

With average commute times in the Inland Empire averaging nearly twice the national average, addressing our transportation challenges has never been more urgent.
Congresswoman Torres is committed to connecting our communities and creating high-quality, good-paying jobs through reliable transportation infrastructure.

That’s why she voted for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law which invested billions of dollars into the Inland Empire’s infrastructure, creating safe routes to school for students, improving our communities’ roads and highways, developing Ontario and Chino airports, and bringing high-speed rail from Rancho Cucamonga to Las Vegas.
These investments are not only about reducing traffic and improving safety but also about sustainability and economic growth.

By expanding public transit options, upgrading bridges and tunnels, and investing in green technologies like electric vehicle infrastructure, Congresswoman Torres is working to build a transportation system that meets the needs of today while preparing for the future.

removed: Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE In the News Women’s Rights Upholding women’s rights and reproductive freedom is vital to building a just and equitable future for all.

In the wake of the Dobbs decision, which rolled back decades of hard-fought protections for reproductive rights, it is more crucial than ever to ensure that women have access to the healthcare they need.
Congresswoman Torres, is a dedicated advocate for protecting a woman’s right to choose and expanding access to essential reproductive healthcare services.

As a Vice-Chair of the Reproductive Freedom Caucus, she stands firmly against any attempts to undermine these rights and is committed to fighting for healthcare equity, particularly for marginalized communities.

Beyond reproductive rights, Congresswoman Torres is focused on creating economic opportunities for women by working to lower the cost of childcare, advocating for paid family leave, and supporting initiatives that advance women in leadership positions.
By empowering women in the workplace and in government, she aims to break down barriers and create a society where every woman has the resources and support necessary to thrive.

added: top of page Home About Norma Endorsements Priorities Get Involved Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Volunteer Endorse Newsletter Media Photos Videos Photos Videos Menu Close DONATE NORMA'S PRIORITIES SENIORS Honoring our seniors with dignity, care, and lasting security Seniors in our community deserve dignity, respect, and the resources to age comfortably.

As the population of older adults in the Inland Empire continues to grow, Congresswoman Torres is dedicated to ensuring that seniors have access to the healthcare, retirement security, and support services they need.

On the Appropriations Committee, she has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare, ensuring these vital programs remain strong for current and future generations, and voted to lower the cost of prescription drugs, so seniors no longer have to choose between medication and other necessities.

She has introduced legislation to help seniors affected by DOGE cuts at the Social Security Administration so that our seniors can receive all the benefits they earned from years of hard work. ​ Beyond healthcare, Congresswoman Torres is working to make sure seniors can live independently and remain connected to their communities.
She secured federal funding for the City of Ontario’s Active Seniors on the Go program, expanding transportation options and mobile nutrition services for seniors.
By supporting these initiatives, Congresswoman Torres is committed to enhancing the quality of life for seniors across our communities, ensuring that they have the security and resources to thrive.

removed: Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE Home Donate Issues Endorsements Media Volunteer Newsletter ICE Scroll Congresswoman Norma Torres is a mom, grandma, and community servant dedicated to working families in the Inland Empire.
Along with her husband Louis, Congresswoman Torres moved to Pomona in 1986 to raise a family and call the Inland Empire home.
Congresswoman Torres believes the working families in our communities know what’s needed, safer streets, stronger schools, good jobs, and a government that actually responds.
That’s why Congresswoman Torres stepped up to serve and has worked to deliver for the Inland Empire.
Now, Congresswoman Torres is running to keep pushing for our communities’ priorities and making sure working families aren’t left behind.
911 Dispatcher 1990-2008 Norma started her career as a 911 dispatcher for LAPD, serving the community for 17 years.
She often worked the graveyard shift, sitting four floors below ground, taking calls every day from people from all walks of life, often in their most vulnerable moments.
After a particularly tragic 911 call, Norma worked with the Los Angeles City Council to improve access to emergency services.

As a result, Norma led the successful fight to recruit and hire more bilingual operators and to ensure that bilingual operators were on call for every work shift, she improved training for all dispatchers, secured a $350,000.00 grant to upgrade the computer system and founded the Community Outreach Program to teach the general public how to properly use the 9-1-1 emergency system.
City Council Member 2000-2006 While working at the 911 dispatch center, Norma was an active member of AFSCME which challenged its members to become more involved and run for local office.
She rose to the challenge, and unseated a long-time incumbent for City Council in Pomona who had long stopped being responsive to the needs of the community.

As a City Councilmember, Norma led many initiatives to improve the quality of life in Pomona and combat crime, including the Neighbors for Pomona Committee, which was dedicated to reducing crime and graffiti in the community.
Mayor of Pomona 2006-2008 Norma was sworn in as the first Latina Mayor of Pomona in February 2006 after winning an 11 way primary for the seat.

As the Mayor of Pomona, Norma continued to fight to keep Pomona safe by imposing gang injunctions limiting gang member activities which substantially reduced the severity of Pomona’s gang violence problem.
In 2008, she was selected to serve as the Treasurer of the National Conference of Democratic Mayors.
The Order of the Great Congress of Guatemala 2008 Norma was born in Guatemala, but moved to the United States because of instability in the country.

Norma has been an honored guest in Guatemala, where she toured the country, met with Heads-of-State, and received the country’s highest honor—the Order of the Great Congress of Guatemala, in the rank of Knight.

Member of the California State Assembly 2008-2012 Serving as the Assemblywoman representing California’s 61st district, Norma served as the Chair of the Committee on Housing and Community Development at a time when the recession and housing crisis had left thousands of families struggling financially.
In response to the crisis, she successfully led an effort to secure $2 billion in federal funds for the “Keep Your Home California” program.
The Keep Your Home California Program helped nearly 100,000 families stay in their homes and kept them from becoming homeless.
Norma also helped pass the Homeowner’s Bill of Rights to protect consumers from foreclosure and worked to make it easier for returning veterans to purchase homes.

Member of the California State Senate 2013-2014 After winning a hard fought special election for the California State Senate, Norma represented California’s 32nd District where she fought to create jobs in the Inland Empire at a time when families were still recovering from the recession.
She advocated for job training programs, access to higher education, and other tools to improve the skills people need to get better paying jobs.
She also strongly advocated for services and programs to help families transition out of the recession, keep their homes and ensure quality education is available for our children.
Member of Congress 2015-Present As the Congresswoman representing California’s 35th district, Norma has been an advocate for the working families of the Inland Empire.
Norma is a member of the Powerful House Committee on Appropriations, one of the most powerful Committees in Congress, which funds the federal government.
Her top priority is to fight for funding and programs that are important to the Inland Empire.
On this Committee, she has advocated and secured improvements for our communities for housing, transportation, , protecting fair elections, and job creation.
She has also introduced legislation to spur investment in our infrastructure and direct resources to training facilities for local law enforcement agencies.
Norma was instrumental in achieving local control for the Ontario Airport, which has seen the airport grow by 10% in the past year.
Norma also sits on the Foreign Affairs Committee where she has become a leader on Western Hemisphere policy.
During her time on the Committee she has successfully passed legislation to root out corruption in foreign governments, while supporting fair elections and open and free democracies.
She is actively working to pass comprehensive immigration reform while addressing the root causes of immigration by supporting the development of neighboring countries.
She is strongly opposed to barbaric practice of family separations at our nation’s southern border and continues to hold the Administration accountable for the damage they have done to families.

Visit to Guatemala with Joe Biden January 2016 In January 2016, Norma was invited by Vice President Biden to represent Congress and join him at the swearing in of the new President of Guatemala, Jimmy Morales.
She also delivered remarks to a plenary session of the Guatemalan Congress.

Prior to the swearing-in, Norma founded the bipartisan Congressional Central America Caucus which focuses on the root causes of instability in Central America and in particular, the Northern Triangle countries, supporting a strategy of governance, security, and prosperity in the region.

With average commute times in the Inland Empire averaging nearly twice the national average, addressing our transportation challenges has never been more urgent.
Congresswoman Torres is committed to connecting our communities and creating high-quality, good-paying jobs through reliable transportation infrastructure.

That’s why she voted for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law which invested billions of dollars into the Inland Empire’s infrastructure, creating safe routes to school for students, improving our communities’ roads and highways, developing Ontario and Chino airports, and bringing high-speed rail from Rancho Cucamonga to Las Vegas. ​ These investments are not only about reducing traffic and improving safety but also about sustainability and economic growth.

By expanding public transit options, upgrading bridges and tunnels, and investing in green technologies like electric vehicle infrastructure, Congresswoman Torres is working to build a transportation system that meets the needs of today while preparing for the future.

Seniors in our community deserve dignity, respect, and the resources to age comfortably.

As the population of older adults in the Inland Empire continues to grow, Congresswoman Torres is dedicated to ensuring that seniors have access to the healthcare, retirement security, and support services they need.

On the Appropriations Committee, she has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare, ensuring these vital programs remain strong for current and future generations, and voted to lower the cost of prescription drugs, so seniors no longer have to choose between medication and other necessities.

She has introduced legislation to help seniors affected by DOGE cuts at the Social Security Administration so that our seniors can receive all the benefits they earned from years of hard work. ​ Beyond healthcare, Congresswoman Torres is working to make sure seniors can live independently and remain connected to their communities.
She secured federal funding for the City of Ontario’s Active Seniors on the Go program, expanding transportation options and mobile nutrition services for seniors.
By supporting these initiatives, Congresswoman Torres is committed to enhancing the quality of life for seniors across our communities, ensuring that they have the security and resources to thrive.

The event will feature Democratic candidates seeking to represent the 9th Bristol District in the Massachusetts House of Representatives.
This seat will be a vacant seat for the first time in over 14 years!

Ed will participate in the forum and welcomes the opportunity to continue to speak directly with residents about the future of the district, the priorities facing local communities, and the issues affecting families throughout Dartmouth and New Bedford.

The forum is designed to give voters the opportunity to hear directly from the candidates, learn about their positions on key issues, and gain a better understanding of their vision for the 9th Bristol District and the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

The evening's program will include: Candidate introductions and opening statements Questions focused on priorities for the communities of the 9th Bristol District Discussion of statewide issues affecting Massachusetts residents Audience questions Candidate-to-candidate questions The event will also be recorded and broadcast by Dartmouth Community Television, giving residents across the district the opportunity to watch and stay informed.
Community members are encouraged to attend, engage in the discussion, and learn more about the candidates seeking to represent the 9th Bristol District .

title.after: Green Energy is Energy Sovereignty – Time For A Change

added: Skip to content Time For A Change Home September 30, 2026 energy policy , politics , public health Green Energy is Energy Sovereignty If there is one thing the Iran war has taught us, it is that having lots of oil in your country does not shield you from the consequences of a global shortage.
We are a major oil- EXPORTING nation.
But for one reason or another, we don’t have the refined products we need.
We export one grade of crude and import a different one.
Our refineries have been allowed to age and close instead of being upgraded, because that takes capital ($$$) and companies are averse to spending it.
The sun doesn’t have to go through a strait on the other side of the world.
And we all live on a gigantic ball of superhot rock that won’t run out of heat for billions of years.
There are also locally available resources like hydropower, tidal energy, and more.
Energy generated in our own locale is the safest, cheapest way to power our future.
We should be promoting the renewable energy industries in every way possible.
While we in Idaho cannot do a lot about federal policies, we can: Restore a fair export credit to promote solar and wind installation.
Allow “balcony solar” as several other states already have, so that renters and people with less capital to spend can also generate some power.
Promote agrovoltaics, where solar panels and row crops or pasture share the same land, to the benefit of the crops.
Panels also pair very well with pollinator meadows and bee keeping.
Streamline permitting for smaller-scale wind projects.
We also have the local ability to promote energy efficient buildings and public transportation to save fuel.
Electric school busses not only cost less to run, but save the children riding on them from diesel fumes that cause respiratory problems.
Induction stoves in place of gas stoves cut the rate of asthma attacks by a lot.
Heat pumps are the most efficient way to heat and cool a building, and buildings can be far better insulated than is currently common.
Clean energy is a win-win situation.
Except for the fossil fuel barons currently gouging us for every penny.
They can go jump in a lake.

removed: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate About Howard Pearl My Story As a lifelong resident of Loudon and a sixth-generation farmer operating Pearl and Sons Farm on Loudon Ridge, I believe in New Hampshire's traditional “Common Sense” values.
My strong business ethic is deeply rooted and has steadily grown since I took over the farm at age 20.
I've made real strides in improving and growing the farm, utilizing a strong commitment to sound business principles combined with sensible financial strategies.
And I've also worked hard to successfully promote collaboration within our local business community.
My three terms in the N.H.
House of Representatives provided me withgreat insights, a working knowledge of how to get things done, and countless new positive relationships.
I successfully sponsored many bills aimed at preserving a way of life that families like mine have enjoyed for generations.
It was an honor to be entrusted by legislative leadership with the chairmanship of the House Environment and Agriculture Committee.
It was similarly an honor to be entrusted with the position of Loudon Town Moderator by the folks who know me best.
The experiences and knowledge I gained from serving in these roles readied me for new opportunities to serve my fellow Granite Staters.
My commitment to agriculture and to the greater New Hampshire community remains profound.
I still serve on the N.H.

Farm Bureau's state board of directors as treasurer, on the Executive Committee of the Concord Grange Chapter, and as a member of two statutory committees relating to solid waste and weights and measures.
Over the last 20 years I've held many different positions within community and trade-based organizations to include the Loudon Zoning Board, the Loudon Trust Fund Committee, the N.H.
Maple Producers, the Merrimack County Farm Bureau, the Speedway Childrens Charities, and the Farm Credit East Customer Service Council.
With the full support of my fiancé Heather, I remain deeply committed to continue to serve constituents as well as the greater Granite State community.

My beliefs in hard work, a positive attitude, and compassion have served me well in all my roles as I seek to continue to make a difference for the better for my family, my community, and our wonderful Granite State.
Endorsements ”Count me in as an enthusiastic supporter of Howard Pearl for State Senator.
As a State Representative, Howard is a proven leader who gets the job done and always fights to protect our New Hampshire Advantage.

The families and small businesses of Senate District 17 will be well served by Howard, and I urge everyone to vote for him.“ Chris Sununu Governor Can You Help?​ We need Howard Pearl in the Senate to stop the Washington socialist agenda from impacting New Hampshire!
Donate to Howard today!
Donate Now Your contribution will benefit Friends of Howard Pearl.

removed: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate Issues My Priorities No Income or Sales Tax We have what is called the "New Hampshire Advantage" over other states because we have no income or sales tax.
Democrats have tried to pass one for years but it would dramatically increase the tax burden for everyone Granite Stater and I will fight tooth and nail against one.
Lowering High Prices Howard Pearl understands that rising prices are squeezing New Hampshire families and small businesses.

He is committed to keeping taxes low, cutting unnecessary regulations, expanding housing opportunities, supporting local agriculture, and creating an environment where businesses can grow, compete, and create good-paying jobs.
Strong fiscal leadership helps keep everyday costs affordable for Granite Staters.
Work to Lower Property Taxes The best way to stop higher property taxes is to control government spending.

As President Ronald Reagan said, "The problem is not that people are taxed too little, the problem is that government spends too much." Protect Our Constitutional Rights There is a full on assault of our Constitutional rights.
Whether it's the freedom of speech, or our right to bear arms, the Constitution is being trampled by radicals.
I am a Constitutional conservative and will fight to protect and preserve our Constitutional rights.
Fight the Status Quo Howard Pearl believes New Hampshire succeeds when leaders challenge outdated ideas and pursue practical solutions.
He isn't afraid to ask tough questions, reform government where needed, and stand up to special interests.
Howard will continue fighting for transparent, accountable government that puts taxpayers, families, and local communities first.

removed: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate Privacy Policy Last updated: October 28, 2022 Overview Welcome to the official web site (the “Site”) of Howard Pearl for State Senate.
This Privacy Policy outlines our practices for collection, use, and disclosure of your information that you provide to us when you use our Site and see or engage with our advertisements.
By using this Site, you agree that your use of the Site is governed by this Privacy Policy and our Terms of Service.
From time to time, we may update this Privacy Policy.
We encourage you to periodically check this Site for updates.
Your continued use of the Site affirms your agreement to any changes we make to this Privacy Policy.
Please note the distinction between our privacy practices in connection with your visit to the Site, and our Terms of Service.

Information Collected and how it is Collected Voluntary Information : We may collect personal information you voluntarily provide to us including your name, e-mail address, postal address, phone number, mobile number and geographic location.
You may provide this information when you request information, register, make a purchase or for other purposes.
We may also collect demographic information such as gender, date of birth, occupation, employer name and zip code.
In limited circumstances, we may collect payment information such as credit card number where needed to complete a requested service or transaction.

By requesting information to your mobile phone, we may obtain the following information from you in connection with our SMS service: your cell phone number, your carrier's name, and the date, time and content of your messages, as well as other information that you provide.
We will use such information in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

Automatically Generated Information : We may also collect non-personally identifiable information that is generated automatically while you are visiting the Site or elsewhere on the Internet when our advertisements are served, also known as log files.

This data includes, but is not limited to, information such as IP address, web pages visited before and after visiting the Site, date and time, domain type, type of mobile device you use, your device’s unique ID, web pages you view and links you click on within the Site and interactions with our advertisements delivered by us or advertisements delivered by a third party advertising technology vendor.
This type of information may be collected using different types of technologies, such as cookies and pixels.
An IP address, for example, is a unique identifier that certain electronic devices use to identify and communicate with each other on the Internet.
When you visit our Site, we may view the IP address of the device you use to connect to the Internet.
We use this information to determine the general physical location of the device and understand from what regions of the world our Site visitors come.
We also may use your non-personally identifiable information to enhance our Site.
All Site users remain anonymous unless they choose to give us their personal information.
You may elect not to allow us to collect and use this non-personally identifiable data as part of our Service by following the Opt Out procedures described below.

Overview : Currently, we do not use our own cookies to obtain certain types of information when your web browser accesses the Site or advertisement or visits a web site in our network, but rather, we may use other companies to set cookies on our Site and advertisements to gather non-personally identifiable information for us.
“Cookies” are small pieces of information that are stored by your browser.
In some cases, we may also use another company to operate web servers or process credit card purchases for our Site.

The Site may use cookies and other technology to speed navigation and keep track of items and to gather anonymous traffic data that we may use to enhance the Site, our Services, marketing, and other internal purposes.

Remember me : If you select “remember me” on your computer when logging on to the Site, Howard Pearl for State Senate will set a persistent cookie to retrieve your username and password when you return to the site so that you do not have to enter it more than once.
It also allows us to send confirmations, receipts, updates, alerts and support and administrative messages and otherwise facilitate your use of and our administration and operation of the Site.
The persistent cookie also enables Howard Pearl for State Senate to track and target the interests of users to enhance the experience on the Site.
The persistent cookie is removed when you uncheck the “remember me” check box.
Google Analytics collects information anonymously.
Google will not associate your IP address with any other data held by Google.
Neither Howard Pearl for State Senate nor Google will link, or seek to link, an IP address with the identity of a computer user.
We will not associate any data gathered from this site with any Personally Identifiable Information from any source, unless you explicitly submit that information via a fill-in form on our website.
It reports website trends without identifying individual visitors.

You can opt out of Google Analytics without affecting how you visit our site – for more information on opting out of being tracked by Google Analytics across all websites you use, visit Web Beacons : Pages of our Site, advertisements, and/or e-mails may contain small electronic files known as web beacons (also referred to as clear gifs, pixel tags, and single-pixel gifs) that permit us, for example, to count users who have visited those pages, engaged in our advertisement or opened an e-mail and for other related web site statistics (for example, recording the popularity of certain web site content and verifying system and server integrity).

In connection with any contests, sweepstakes and other promotions that we may offer from time to time via our Site, we use the information you provide to administer the contests, sweepstakes and other promotions.

Subject to applicable contractual or legal restrictions, we also may use the information to communicate with you, or the other people you select, about our ’ products and services or our service providers or agents partners may use such information to communicate with you about the contests, sweepstakes or other promotions or their products and services.

Social Media Platforms and Web sites : Any information, communications, or material of any type or nature that you submit to our Site (including, but not limited to any of our pages contained on a social media platform or web site such as Facebook or Twitter) by e-mail, posting, messaging, uploading, downloading, or otherwise (collectively, a “Submission”), is done at your own risk and without any expectation of privacy.

We may archive your message for a certain period of time or discard it, but your e-mail address and message will only be used in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

Submitting your e-mail : Submitting your address anywhere on the Site may result in your e-mail address being added to the Howard Pearl for State Senate e-mail list, in addition to the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy.

Suggesting the Site to a Friend : If you elect to use any feature that includes suggesting a page to a friend or to inform a friend about the Site or solicit donations or pledges or otherwise communicate, Howard Pearl for State Senate may ask for your friend's name and e-mail address.

Your friend may contact Howard Pearl for State Senate to request the removal of this information from our databases.
Security We employ and maintain technology and security measures designed to protect your personal information.
However, no data transmission over the Internet can be guaranteed as 100% secure.
As a result, while we strive to protect your information, we cannot ensure or warrant the security of any information you transmit to us or receive from us.
This portion of our Privacy Policy describes specific rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”).
Please note that we will seek to verify your identity when we receive an individual rights request from you in order to ensure the security of your information.

Please direct any rights requests (as further described below) or additional questions you may have regarding this Privacy Policy via email to: hpearl56@gmail.com​ If you do, we will need to collect your information such as your name, email or transaction history in order to verify your identity.

Federal law also requires us to report this information to the Federal Election Commission if an individual’s contributions aggregate in excess of $200 in a single calendar year.
Any credit card information provided is only used to immediately process your donation.
All contributions made to the Site are considered final unless the donation is not in compliance with federal election law and/or Federal Election Commission regulations.
All purchases from the online store are considered contributions to Howard Pearl for State Senate.

Special Statement for Job Applicants Any personal information that you provide to us when applying for a career position with Howard Pearl for State Senate will be used solely to consider and act upon your application.
We may retain your personal information for a period of time, but only for as long as necessary for such purposes or as otherwise required by law.

We may disclose your personal information to our agents for the purpose of evaluating your qualifications for the particular position you applied for, for other available positions or as otherwise required by law.
We may also disclose your personal information to third parties hired by us to collect, maintain, and analyze candidates for career positions or as otherwise required by law.

Visiting our Site from outside of the United States If you are visiting our Site from outside of the United States of America, please be aware that your information may be transferred to, stored or processed in the United States, where our servers are located and our central database is operated.
The data protection and other laws of the United States and other countries might not be as comprehensive as those in your country, but please be assured that we take steps to protect your privacy.
By using our Site, you understand that your information may be transferred to our facilities and those third parties with whom we share it as described in this Privacy Policy.

added: Contact Information: Miranda Jenkins, Press & Communications Cell: 480.216.2164 miranda@petercrosbyforcongress.org PRESS RELEASE For Immediate Release PETER CROSBY SHOWS VOTERS HE’S DEDICATED TO FIXING THE ISSUES THEY CARE ABOUT MOST IN DEBATE FOR UTAH’S 2nd CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT Peter Crosby showed he was a professional problem solver in his debate with Blake Moore last night at Utah State University in Logan, Utah, covering solutions he’ll champion from issues as far afield as cost of living, preservation of the Great Salt Lake and the inefficiencies of our current Congress.
Salt Lake City, UT, October 14, 2026 – Peter Crosby routed incumbent Blake Moore in the debate for Utah’s Second Congressional District last night at Utah State University.
Crosby spoke to the people of Northern Utah about the actions he will take once elected on the issues they care about most.

“I have a moral obligation to my district before a political party, before anybody else, and I need to vote in a way that's going to solve these problems,” Crosby said in response to reining in inflation and strengthening the job market.

Among the priorities Crosby laid out are reinvesting in federal housing affordability programs the Trump administration has disinvested in, investing in upgrading Utah’s aging water infrastructure, securing real funding for water rights to save the Great Salt Lake, tax code changes that close loopholes for corporations, securing a right to privacy for all citizens, legal and humane immigration policy, passing legislation ensuring local review and approval of data center development, ending the Trump administration's tariffs and stopping the War in Iran.
“We could vote to end the war in Iran.
It would only take 1 or 2 Republicans to cross the aisle.
The House is that close right now.
We could vote to end a broad tariff regime.

Again, it only takes 1 or 2 Republicans to cross the aisle and say, ‘I'm going to put the needs of my district before political party or loyalty to an executive,” Crosby went on, “It doesn't take committee work.

It just takes courage.” When asked about representing Northern Utah’s diverse 2nd Congressional District, Crosby highlighted his thousands of conversations with voters across Northern Utah, emphasizing his focus on the concerns they raised directly to him, “I think the most important thing that I need to remember is first, do no harm and then second, help as many as I possibly can.
And when I look at our existing policy right now - a policy that Mr.

Moore has voted six times to maintain - tariffs are harming everybody – harming farmers or harming ranchers or harming small business owners, or they're harming families.” When asked to respond on the topic of tariffs, Moore mentioned taking a private call from Proctor and Gamble to help solve their tariff challenges rather than mentioning any concrete action he’s taken to ease the pain for small businesses and working families.

To which Crosby replied, “none of the small business owners seem to receive the same attention.” In his almost six years in office, Blake Moore has supported bills that focus on special interests and has done little to counteract the work of the current administration - despite constituent concerns.
His inaction was apparent in his talking points last night. • When asked about reliable affordable energy Moore side stepped by talking about unpassed legislation.

He neglected to mention that the One Big Beautiful Bill – which he voted for – phased out tax credits for industrial and residential solar projects. • When asked about how he could help the unaffordability crisis facing young people Moore again touted a piece of legislation that hasn’t left committee and another that passed which critics say could drive students away from affordable federal education loans and towards more expensive private loans. • Moore stood behind President Donald Trump for a photo op as he gutted protections for 90% of Utah’s beloved national monuments, Bears Ears and Grand Staircase Escalante.

Moore later defended his presence at the signing, “I’m not in charge of leasing” the land. • Moore co-chairs the DOGE Caucus driving agency cuts, but admitted at his town hall that DOGE "didn't consult" Congress.
Crosby closed with a clear vision, “There's a vision of our country that's different than the path that we're headed down now.

It is a country where the economy works for regular people, where we have access to things that we need, like health care and housing, where the Great Salt Lake is healthy, where our public lands are protected and available not just for our kids, but every future generation.
And that's a future that happens when we elect people who are transparent and honest in their dealings in government.

That's the future that we're fighting for.” Independent polling from the Utah Debate Commission showed Crosby, whose grassroots campaign has taken no funding from Corporate PACs, in striking distance of Moore.
About Peter Crosby for Congress Peter Crosby is the Democratic nominee for Utah’s U.S.
Congressional District 2, a first-time political candidate, and a girl-dad.

He is running a strictly clean-money, grassroots campaign: Peter is not accepting corporate PAC donations or funding from PACs aligned with foreign interests, and has raised over $125,000 from small-dollar and individual donors, with over 94% coming from right here in Utah.
The campaign is fully volunteer-supported with over 400 registered campaign volunteers.
Peter believes citizens of Northern Utah deserve a representative that lives in the district, listens to their concerns, and puts the people of Utah ahead of party or the pursuit of personal power.
He is holding public town halls throughout the district, with at least one in Cache, Box Elder, Davis, and Weber counties each month.

item_pages.value: ENDORSED BY John Carlson New Haven RTC Chairman "I endorse Peter Lumaj as Secretary of the State for several reasons.
To begin with, he has the qualifications required to do the job.
His familiarity with law and running a business will no doubt be a huge boon in running SOTS.
Secondly, he has the character to ensure the job gets done without bias, and with honesty and integrity.
As we’ve seen from recent events, not only in BPT, but elsewhere, we need someone who will take the appointment seriously and without fear of political backlash from any party or backers.
“Fear not”, Peter is the candidate who is not afraid to let everyone know what he stands for and what he won’t stand for.
Lastly, he is an experienced candidate which will aid him in this run." View all endorsements →

DONATE My Polling Place "Protecting Parental Rights and protecting children from social agendas." Standing up for the unborn and valuing every stage of life.
Safeguarding your right to keep and bear arms, which defends all other rights.
Supporting parents and protecting childhood from harmful agendas.
Promoting trade schools, small businesses, and entrepreneurship to help families thrive.
Backing law enforcement, strong borders, and policies that protect our neighborhoods.
KEY ISSUES Life I believe every life has value, and I will work to defend the unborn while also supporting policies that honor life at every stage.
Strengthen Support for Mothers and Families Pass legislation that increases access to prenatal care, parenting support, and adoption services.
Women facing unplanned pregnancies will have more resources, reducing the pressure to consider abortion and supporting life in early stages.
Promote Life-Affirming Education Programs Fund educational programs in schools and communities that teach about the value of life, alternatives to abortion, and support for families.
Encourages a cultural respect for life while giving practical alternatives for expecting parents.
2nd Amendment The right to bear arms is what protects every other freedom we enjoy.
I will fight to make sure it is never taken away.
Legislative Protection of Gun Rights Introduce bills that prevent state or federal overreach on legal gun ownership.
Ensures responsible citizens retain their right to own firearms.
Promote Responsible Gun Ownership Programs Focus on community programs for safe gun handling, storage, and training.
Reduces accidents and crime while maintaining constitutional rights.
Parenthood & Childhood Parents should have the freedom to raise their children according to their values, without government interference or harmful social agendas.
Childhood should be protected, not politicized.
Parental Choice in Education Support legislation that allows parents to choose schools, homeschool options, and curriculum transparency.
Parents gain control over their child’s education, avoiding unwanted political or ideological influence.
Strengthen Protections Against Harmful Content for Children Implement laws that restrict exposure to inappropriate media or social agendas for minors in schools and public programs.
Ensures children grow up in safe environments aligned with family values.
Economy/Expanding Opportunity The next generation deserves more than broken promises from government.

We need stronger trade schools, support for small business, and more pathways to success that don’t require crushing debt. ​ Expand Trade & Vocational Schools Increase funding for technical training, apprenticeships, and vocational education programs.
Provides alternative career paths with lower debt and strong earning potential.
Support Small Businesses and Entrepreneurship Reduce bureaucratic hurdles and provide tax incentives for small business owners.
Encourages local economic growth, job creation, and financial independence.
Safety & Security Strong community means secure neighborhoods, supporting self-defense rights and law enforcement, and real solutions for border security.
Safety is the foundation of freedom.
Strengthen Law Enforcement & Community Programs Increase funding for police training, community policing, and neighborhood watch initiatives.
Improves unity between law enforcement, crime prevention, and trust between citizens and law enforcement.

CONTRIBUTE Log In Join the Movement Campaigning is about more than just policies; it’s about people.
Our grassroots movement is fueled by neighbors like you who believe in the power of collective action.
When we stand together, we can build a Maryland that reflects our shared values and hopes for the future.
Volunteer Application Form Please fill out all required information below.

First name * Last name * Email address * Phone number * Position(s) you're interested in * Canvassing Phone banking Text banking Community events Fundraising Host a Fundraiser Social media support Other Current/previous company Work experience * Available start date * Month Day Year Submit Application Volunteering is your chance to turn your vision for District 6 into reality.
Your voice and your time are the most powerful tools we have to reach every corner of our community and ensure every Marylander is heard and represented.
Every Role Matters Whether you have six minutes or six hours, there is a place for you in this movement.
Every door knocked and every conversation held brings us closer to a brighter future for all of us.
Canvassing: Door-knocking to share our mission across District 6.
Phone Banking: Calling neighbors to encourage election day turnout.
Social Advocacy: Sharing our campaign message via digital platforms.
Event Support: Representing the movement at local community gatherings.
Fundraising: Securing the resources necessary to power our outreach.
Hosting: Organizing small events to raise essential campaign funds.
Resource Support: Helping neighbors access housing and health services.
General Support: Providing adaptive help wherever the team needs it most.
This is a campaign built on the belief that everyone deserves a fair shot.
We are fighting for a Maryland defined by second chances, strong schools, fair wages, safe neighborhoods, and equitable access to the resources our families need to thrive.
Join Us Ready to make an impact?
Sign up to join our team of dedicated volunteers and help us drive real change in District 6.

added: Skip to content Rebecca Bennett for Congress Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Facebook X-twitter Threads Instagram Youtube Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Donate with ActBlue Donate with Numero New Jersey State Association of Pipe Trades Endorses Rebecca Bennett for Congress The union previously endorsed Kean Jr. in 2024 SOMERVILLE, NJ — Today, the New Jersey State Association of Pipe Trades (NJSAPT) announced their endorsement of Rebecca Bennett for Congress in New Jersey’s seventh district.
The Pipe Trades represents over 12,000 members and includes the United Association (UA) Locals 9, 24, 274, 322, 475, 669, 692, 696, and 855.

The group cited Rebecca’s commitment to working across the aisle, investing in apprenticeship programs, and her understanding of the importance of creating good paying union jobs that strengthen the middle class as reasons for the endorsement.
The NJSAPT had previously been part of a Building Trades endorsement for Congressman Tom Kean Jr.’s campaign in 2024.
“I am grateful to have the support of Pipe Trades in this race.
While touring the Local 9 facility, I saw firsthand how the Pipe Trades is building the next generation of union labor while ensuring that members can continue to grow in their trade.

I look forward to working together to make sure that we can connect veterans with these important programs, stand up for collective bargaining, and ensure that New Jersey families can break into the middle class with a good union job,” said Rebecca Bennett .
“The Pipe Trades are looking to endorse leaders who are willing to fight for our values and have the tough conversations and we don’t base our support on politics or party affiliation.
We’re proud to endorse Rebecca Bennett because we know that she’ll fight for us.
Rebecca will stand up for collective bargaining rights and make sure that we have the resources we need to expand apprenticeship programs and recruit veterans to the trades.
We will have a seat at the table as we pursue an “all of the above” energy approach to help lower utility bills for New Jerseyans.

The Pipe Trades will work to ensure that Rebecca wins in November so that we have a leader we can count on in Congress to help us grow the middle class,” said Mike Tranberg, President of the New Jersey State Association of Pipe Trades .

added: Skip to content Rebecca Bennett for Congress Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Facebook X-twitter Threads Instagram Youtube Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Donate with ActBlue Donate with Numero Rebecca Bennett Announces NJ-07 Deckplate Leadership Tour Rebecca’s showing up despite Kean Jr. declining her debate challenge SOMERVILLE, NJ — Over the summer, Rebecca Bennett challenged Tom Kean Jr. to six debates — one in each county covered by the district.
Rebecca and Tom debated in Union County last weekend, but he never responded to the rest of the challenge .
Today, she’s announcing a Deckplate Leadership Tour in the five remaining counties in the district.

Over the next few weeks, Rebecca will speak directly with voters about what’s on their minds and share her vision for lowering costs in NJ-07, getting corruption out of Washington, and putting country over party.
“Throughout his time in Congress, Tom Kean Jr. has failed to show up for us.
He was nowhere to be found when his party started a reckless war with Iran, gutted healthcare, or tried to cancel Gateway Tunnel funding.
Since taking office, he’s failed to hold a single public event and consistently runs away from the media who try to hold him accountable,” said Rebecca Bennett .
“I learned to lead in the Navy, and my leadership is deckplate leadership, which means that you have to show up and listen to the people you serve to hear what the issues are.

I’m excited to launch this Deckplate Leadership Tour because my campaign is about listening to New Jerseyans and bringing a new generation of leadership to create real change in Washington.” Members of the media interested in attending can RSVP HERE .
Participants (NON-MEDIA) can sign up using the links below: HACKETTSTOWN CALIFON BRIDGEWATER SPARTA MT.
