added: The Ohio Supreme Court ruled five times that state legislative maps—drawn by politicians in power—are unconstitutional.
Gerrymandering isn’t in anyone’s best interest other than the people who want to stay in power.
Manipulating voting maps to serve a political party rather than serving the voters is undemocratic.
As your next State Senator, I will prioritize impartial, citizen-drawn voting districts.
Ohio ranks 42nd in the nation for school funding support.

And while state leaders tell us they’ve never spent more on education, when you adjust for inflation, the increased number of specialized education needs being identified and an increase in state mandates on public schools, Ohio’s per-pupil spending is not nearly enough.
However, the current state budget is not fully funding schools per the plan—the last statehouse budget was $2.75 billion less than expected, leaving districts across the state severely underfunded.
Affordable, High-Quality Healthcare, Dependent Care & Housing The state of our economy is a lot more nuanced than what the S&P and DOW tell us each day.
HEALTHCARE Recent cuts and increased restrictions for Medicaid and insurance coverage through the ACA has led to more than 207,000 Ohioans losing health coverage.
But just because Ohioans lose coverage, their health needs don’t go away.
When uninsured patients can no longer wait to address their health needs and head to ERs, those uninsured patients are unlikely to have the resources to pay for costly ER bills.
Uncompensated care leads to healthcare providers trying to make up for losses by cutting services, closing facilities, or increasing billing in other areas, which affects commercial insurance plans.
The cost of our insurance premiums goes up when the number of uninsured Ohioans goes up.
In fact, ACA Marketplace premiums are expected to rise another 15% in 2027, which is on top of this year’s increases.
Rising healthcare costs are not only straining Ohio patients and providers, but also Ohio employers.
The average employer contribution to a health care plan for employees has risen 30% in the last decade.
Currently, Ohio is ranked 35th in the nation for healthcare access.
We need to do better, especially for underserved rural areas like those in our district.
removed: As your next State Senator, I will prioritize impartial, citizen-led voting districts.
Ohio ranks 42nd in the nation for school funding.

And while state leaders tell us they’ve never spent more on education, when you adjust for inflation, the increased number of specialized education needs being identified and an increase in state mandates on public schools, Ohio’s per-pupil spending is below average at best.
However, the current state budget is not fully funding schools per the plan—they should have provided $3 billion total for last year and this coming year combined.
The statehouse budget fell incredibly short, just $250 million and leaving districts across the state severely underfunded.
Affordable, High-Quality Health Care, Dependent Care & Housing The state of our economy is a lot more nuanced than what the S&P and DOW tell us each day.

HEALTH CARE People all across our district are having to make incredibly difficult decisions about where to allocate their limited budgets—often forgoing preventative or early-intervention health care, including critical medications.

Cuts and increased restrictions for Medicaid, SNAP benefits, and insurance through the ACA are forcing people to make difficult decisions about their health care and reducing the number of people with insurance coverage.
In fact, an analysis from the Health Policy Institute of Ohio found that Ohio public health is one of the worst funded in the country—ranking 13th lowest.

DONATE All Posts Search BIPARTISAN GROUP OF WESTCHESTER, PUTNAM HIGHWAY SUPERINTENDENTS ENDORSE MATT SLATER FOR RE-ELECTION #ago 3 min read Assemblyman Matt Slater (R,C-Yorktown) announced today that he has received the bipartisan endorsement of six highway superintendents from across Westchester and Putnam counties, citing his continued partnership with local highway departments, advocacy for increased state funding for local roads and bridges and efforts to secure greater investment in state-owned roads throughout the Hudson Valley.
“I am incredibly proud to have the support of our local highway superintendents because these are the officials who know our infrastructure needs better than anyone,” said Slater.
“They are on the front lines maintaining our roads, responding to storms and stretching every taxpayer dollar as far as it can go.
I have listened to them, worked alongside them and fought to make sure Albany provides them with the resources they need.
I am honored to have their bipartisan support.” Slater has made infrastructure investment a major focus of his work in the State Assembly.

Working with highway superintendents from across the region, he successfully advocated for consecutive increases in the Consolidated Local Street and Highway Improvement Program (CHIPS), including an additional $50 million in the 2026–27 state budget.
CHIPS funding now stands at a record $698.1 million statewide, with total state support for local highway programs reaching approximately $1.4 billion this year.
Slater has also worked directly with the New York State Department of Transportation to increase investment in state roads throughout the 94th Assembly District.

Recent investments include $15 million for improvements along the Route 202 corridor in Somers, including a $9 million repaving project, as well as millions of dollars for improvements to other state corridors across northern Westchester and Putnam counties.
“Our local highway departments do tremendous work, but residents rightly expect the state to take care of its roads too,” Slater said.
“For too long, the Hudson Valley has been asked to accept deteriorating state roads and delayed projects.
We have pushed DOT for greater investment, secured millions of dollars for our region and worked directly with state and local partners to get projects moving.

There is much more work to do, and fixing our roads will remain one of my top priorities.” That work will continue as Slater was recently selected by Putnam County to serve on the Project Steering Committee for the New York Metropolitan Transportation Council’s Northern Westchester East-West Corridors Study.

The regional planning effort is examining some of the area’s most heavily traveled corridors, including Routes 6, 35, 118 and 202, to develop actionable recommendations for future transportation investments.
“I don't want another transportation study that sits on a shelf,” Slater said.
“We need a prioritized list of real projects that improve safety, reduce congestion and fix our roads.

Having a seat at the table gives our communities another opportunity to fight for the infrastructure investments northern Westchester and Putnam deserve.” The six highway superintendents also outlined their support for Slater in a joint letter to the editor, citing his accessibility, advocacy for increased CHIPS funding and partnership with local highway departments.

Somers Highway Superintendent Nick DeVito, Yorktown Highway Superintendent Dave Paganelli, Carmel Highway Superintendent Mike Stern, Kent Highway Superintendent Rich Othmer, Southeast Highway Superintendent Mike Burdick and Putnam Valley Highway Superintendent Shawn Keeler signed the letter.
“We work with Matt, and we have seen firsthand what he brings to the table.
He listens to the people actually doing the work.
And when we tell him what our highway departments need, he goes to Albany and fights for it,” the superintendents wrote.

Pointing to consecutive $50 million increases in CHIPS funding and Slater’s efforts to secure greater investment in state roads, the superintendents said his advocacy has translated into tangible improvements for local communities while helping ease the burden on property taxpayers.
“We don't measure a partnership by press releases.
We measure it by whether someone shows up, listens and gets results.
Matt Slater has done that.” “Good roads aren’t Republican or Democrat—they are fundamental to safe communities, a strong economy and our quality of life,” Slater said.
“Our highway superintendents understand that better than anyone.

I am grateful for their partnership, grateful for their endorsement and ready to keep working with them to deliver results for the people we serve.” Recent Posts See All SLATER HOSTS 4TH ANNUAL SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN YORKTOWN SLATER RECOGNIZES YORKTOWN TIRE AUTO CARE AS AN HISTORIC BUSINESS FOR OVER 55 YEARS OF SERVICE SLATER HOSTS FIRST SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN MAHOPAC Leadership that's making a difference.

According to Enacted Budget school aid estimates, UPK funding across the school districts serving the 94th Assembly District is projected to increase from $8.84 million in the 2025–26 school year to $10.76 million in 2026–27, a net increase of $1,919,028.
“Expanding access to pre-K is an investment in our children and a direct benefit for working families,” said Slater.

“An additional $1.9 million coming into our local school districts means more opportunities for children to get a strong start and more options for parents who are balancing the demands of work and family.” The 2026–27 state budget made significant changes to New York’s UPK program.

According to the New York State Education Department (NYSED), all school districts can now access UPK funding, the program has moved to a single funding structure and per-pupil funding rates for 4-year-olds have increased.
Districts are also able to enroll eligible 4-year-olds and receive state funding for each student served, provided program requirements are met.
“Every family should have access to quality early learning opportunities regardless of their ZIP code,” Slater said.

“These investments give our school districts greater resources to meet the needs of their communities and expand opportunities where there is demand.” The estimates also project a net increase of 100 UPK seats across the districts serving the 94th Assembly District.
The largest projected seat increases include Lakeland with 40 additional seats, Brewster with 25, Mahopac with 15 and Carmel with 12.
The 2026–27 figures are preliminary estimates generated before actual student counts for the current school year were available.
NYSED will use student enrollment data reported this fall to determine final UPK payments; the department has designated Oct.
7, 2026, as Basic Education Data System Day, the day final child counts are calculated for 2026–27 payments.
“This is encouraging progress, but our work does not end with one budget,” Slater said.

“I will continue working with our local school districts and families to ensure our communities have the resources they need to give every child the opportunity to succeed.” Recent Posts See All SLATER HOSTS FIRST SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN MAHOPAC SLATER RECEIVES HELENE GOEBBELS AWARD AT PUTNAM VALLEY VOLUNTEER AMBULANCE CORPS’ 65TH ANNIVERSARY DINNER SLATER JOINS VOLUNTEER FIREFIGHTERS IN CALLING ON GOV.

DONATE All Posts Search SLATER HOSTS 4TH ANNUAL SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN YORKTOWN #ago 2 min read Assemblyman Matt Slater (R,C-Yorktown) hosted his 4th Annual Senior Resource Fair in Yorktown at the Jefferson Village Community Center, bringing together local seniors, caregivers and families with organizations and service providers from across the region.

The free event provided attendees with an opportunity to connect directly with organizations offering information and assistance on elder care, Medicare, assisted living, state and county services, Alzheimer’s and memory care and other resources available to seniors and their families.
“Each year, our Senior Resource Fair allows me to speak directly with seniors in our community and connect them with organizations that can provide valuable information and assistance,” said Slater.

“Having so many resources together in one place makes it easier for seniors, caregivers and families to get their questions answered and learn more about the programs available to them.” “Assemblyman Slater's resource fair was so well attended.
It is great to have a partner in government like him who helps bring much-needed information to our seniors,” said Yorktown Town Supervisor Ed Lachterman .

“Thank you to all who participated in making this a very informative day for our residents.” The Yorktown fair also featured a prescription medication drop-off, allowing residents to dispose of unused or expired medications safely.
Approximately 26 pounds of prescription medications were collected during the event for safe disposal.
“Collecting 26 pounds of unused and expired medications shows just how important it is to make safe disposal options accessible in our communities,” Slater continued.
“Getting these medications out of our homes helps prevent misuse and ensures they are disposed of properly.

Thank you to everyone who took advantage of this service and to all of our participating organizations for helping make this year’s Yorktown fair another success.” Slater has hosted a Senior Resource Fair for the past three years, and in response to growing demand, expanded the series this year by adding a new location in Mahopac.
The Yorktown event was the second of three Senior Resource Fairs Slater is hosting this October, with the final fair scheduled for Tuesday, Oct.
13, from 10 a.m. to noon at the Patterson Recreation Center, 65 Front St., Patterson.

HOCHUL TO SIGN TAX CREDIT INCREASE Sep 21 2 min read Assemblyman Matt Slater (R,C-Yorktown) joined members of the Firefighters Association of the State of New York (FASNY), volunteer firefighters and emergency medical personnel at the Ossining Fire Department on Saturday to call on Gov.
Kathy Hochul to sign legislation significantly increasing New York’s income tax credit for volunteer first responders.
The bipartisan legislation, A.6790-A, would increase the state personal income tax credit for eligible volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers from $200 to $800.
For married couples filing jointly where both spouses qualify, the credit would increase from $400 to $1,600.
“Our volunteer firefighters and EMS personnel answer the call at all hours of the day and night to protect their neighbors,” said Slater.

“Increasing this tax credit is a meaningful way to recognize their service while helping our local departments recruit and retain the volunteers they desperately need.” According to FASNY, New York has 20,000 fewer volunteer firefighters today than it did #ago, while volunteer firefighters save the state more than $4.7 billion each year.
The Volunteer Firefighter Recruitment and Retention Task Force, convened by the state Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services, also recommended increasing the credit.
“Volunteer fire departments are the backbone of public safety in communities across New York,” Slater continued.
“When their ranks decline, it becomes a public safety and taxpayer issue.
We should be doing everything we can to support those who step up to serve.” FASNY organized the Sept.
19 event as part of its push for the governor to act on the legislation before the end of the year.
“The Legislature has done its job, and now we need the governor to finish the job,” concluded Slater.
“Supporting the men and women who volunteer to keep our communities safe should never be a partisan issue.
I urge Gov.

Hochul to sign this bill and give our volunteer first responders the support they have earned.” Recent Posts See All SLATER HOSTS FIRST SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN MAHOPAC SLATER RECEIVES HELENE GOEBBELS AWARD AT PUTNAM VALLEY VOLUNTEER AMBULANCE CORPS’ 65TH ANNIVERSARY DINNER SLATER ANNOUNCES PROJECTED $1.9 MILLION INCREASE IN UPK FUNDING FOR LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS Leadership that's making a difference.

DONATE All Posts Search SLATER RECEIVES HELENE GOEBBELS AWARD AT PUTNAM VALLEY VOLUNTEER AMBULANCE CORPS’ 65TH ANNIVERSARY DINNER Oct 2 2 min read New York State Assemblyman Matt Slater (R,C-Yorktown) was honored with the Helene Goebbels Award during the Putnam Valley Volunteer Ambulance Corps’ (PVVAC) 65th Anniversary Dinner.
Slater joined members of the Corps, community leaders and supporters in celebrating the organization’s 65 years of service to Putnam Valley.
The award is named in honor of Helene Goebbels, whose generosity played an important role in the history of PVVAC.
Goebbels donated the land on which the Corps’ building stands today, providing a permanent home for generations of volunteers.
The award is presented in her spirit to individuals who demonstrate a strong commitment to community service and supporting others.
“For 65 years, the dedicated volunteers of the Putnam Valley Volunteer Ambulance Corps have answered the call and been there for our neighbors when they need them most,” said Slater.
“I am honored and humbled to receive an award that carries such a meaningful legacy of generosity and community service.

This recognition means a great deal to me, and I am incredibly grateful for the partnership we have built.” Slater has worked alongside PVVAC to support the organization and ensure its volunteers have the resources necessary to continue serving the community.

Most recently, Slater was instrumental in securing an $80,000 state grant to replace the Corps’ aging generator, helping ensure the organization can remain operational and respond when residents need emergency assistance.
“Our volunteer first responders dedicate countless hours to keeping our communities safe, and they deserve to know that we have their backs,” Slater continued.

“I am proud of what we have been able to accomplish together and remain committed to supporting PVVAC and the critical work its volunteers do every day.” “We are proud to recognize Assemblyman Slater with this award and thank him for his continued support of our Corps and our community,” said Sheryl Luongo, President of the Putnam Valley Volunteer Ambulance Corps.

The anniversary dinner celebrated PVVAC’s longstanding commitment to providing emergency medical services and recognized the generations of volunteers who have contributed to the organization throughout its history.
“Congratulations to the entire Putnam Valley Volunteer Ambulance Corps on 65 remarkable years of service,” concluded Slater.
“Thank you to every past and present member who has given their time to help their neighbors and strengthen Putnam Valley.

I look forward to continuing our partnership for many years to come.” Recent Posts See All SLATER HOSTS FIRST SENIOR RESOURCE FAIR IN MAHOPAC SLATER ANNOUNCES PROJECTED $1.9 MILLION INCREASE IN UPK FUNDING FOR LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS SLATER JOINS VOLUNTEER FIREFIGHTERS IN CALLING ON GOV.

DONATE All Posts Search SLATER RECOGNIZES YORKTOWN TIRE AUTO CARE AS AN HISTORIC BUSINESS FOR OVER 55 YEARS OF SERVICE #ago 2 min read Assemblyman Matt Slater (R,C-Yorktown) recently celebrated Yorktown Tire Auto Care’s recognition on the New York State Historic Business Preservation Registry, honoring the family-owned business for more than 55 years of dedicated service to motorists throughout Yorktown and the Hudson Valley.
Slater also issued a New York State Assembly proclamation recognizing the business’s longstanding commitment to quality automotive care, customer service and the local community.

For more than five decades, Yorktown Tire Auto Care has remained a family-owned, full-service auto repair shop, serving generations of residents while building lasting relationships throughout the community.

Now in its third generation of family ownership, the business has continued its tradition of dependable automotive care and customer service and has become a valued part of Yorktown’s local economy and history.
“The Froats family has been part of the fabric of Yorktown for generations, and this recognition is especially meaningful to me on a personal level.
I grew up with Ryan and his sisters, and I’ve had the privilege of seeing firsthand the pride this family takes in serving our community,” said Slater.
“Today, Ryan carries on the legacy his grandfather and father built as the third-generation owner of Yorktown Tire and Auto Center.
That kind of family tradition, hard work, and commitment to your neighbors is exactly what makes Yorktown such a special place to call home.
Small, family-owned businesses like this are the backbone of our local economy, but more importantly, they are part of the heart and soul of our community.

I was incredibly proud to nominate Yorktown Tire and Auto Center for this historic recognition by New York State, and even prouder to celebrate this well-deserved honor with a family I’ve known for years.” “As a third-generation business owner, I feel immense pride in coming to work to service the community that helped raise me and turned me into the person I am today,” s aid Ryan Froats, owner of Yorktown Tire Auto Care .
“I consider myself incredibly fortunate to love what I do, and I’m indebted to the countless family members, customers and employees that helped us achieve this honor.

I look forward to building on our legacy and am thankful to Assemblyman Slater and his staff for helping us throughout this process!” Throughout its history, Yorktown Tire Auto Care has established itself as a trusted local business, contributing to the economic vitality and character of the Town of Yorktown.

Its recognition on the statewide registry celebrates not only its longevity but also the generations of family members, employees and customers who have helped sustain the business for more than half a century.

Established by New York state in 2020, the Historic Business Preservation Registry recognizes businesses that have operated for at least 50 years and have contributed to the history, heritage and identity of their communities.
Yorktown Tire Auto Care’s inclusion honors its decades of service and enduring impact on the Hudson Valley.

added: State Representative District 122 Menu About A Better Deal Fellowship Capitol Corner Constituents Volunteer Donate About A Better Deal Fellowship Capitol Corner Constituents Volunteer Donate A Minimum Wage That Doesn’t Cover the Minimum Costs Posted April 22, 2024 By Francesca Mariano Capitol Corner Georgia’s minimum wage is $5.15, but for most employment in Georgia, the federal minimum wage of $7.25 applies due to the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).[ 1 , 2 ] This wage is even lower if one is considered a tipped employee, decreasing the number to $2.13.[ 3 ] This is also possible due to the fact that Georgia does not currently have any legislation concerning paying employees less than the standard minimum wage.[Ibid] A low minimum wage is unfortunately a commonality among southern states and is considered a historical condition constructed by Southern businesses and political leaders.

added: top of page VT HOUSE • CHITTENDEN 24 Home About Blog Videos Merch Events Donate Videos & Conversations Play Video Play Video 14:12 Stephanie Mack with Governor Jim Douglas | WVMT Morning Drive, October 12, 2026 Stephanie Mack joins former Vermont Governor Jim Douglas on The Morning Drive with Anthony Neri on WVMT Radio 103.3 FM, Monday, October 12, 2026.
The conversation explores Vermont's $9 billion FY2026 state budget, government spending, financial accountability, and the growing affordability challenges facing Vermont families and businesses.

Drawing on more than 25 years of experience in business operations and financial management, Stephanie discusses the importance of making Vermont's budget understandable to everyday taxpayers and ensuring that government spending is transparent and accountable.
Learn more about Stephanie's priorities for Vermont and read her state budget analysis at https://StephanieMackVT.com.
Stephanie Mack is a candidate for the Vermont House of Representatives, Chittenden-24, representing Essex Junction and part of Essex.
Paid for by Stephanie Mack VT.

Play Video Play Video 33:54 Meet the Candidates | Chittenden-23 & 24 On September 26, 2026, Vermont House candidates Stephanie Mack (Chittenden-24), Pearl Lucero Beckage, and Lynne Smith (Chittenden-23) participated in a community conversation at Leo & Co. in Essex, Vermont.
This candid discussion gives voters an opportunity to hear directly from the candidates about their perspectives, priorities, and the challenges facing Vermont communities.
Watch the conversation and get to know the candidates seeking to represent Essex-area residents in Montpelier.
Learn more about Stephanie Mack: https://www.stephaniemackvt.com Recorded September 26, 2026, in Essex, Vermont.

added: top of page Donate Now ABOUT Issues Press Get Involved FAQs Menu Close ABOUT Issues Press Get Involved FAQs DONATE ABOUT Issues Press Get Involved FAQs Menu Close DONATE Where I Stand On The Issues Cost | Corruption | Community As we mark the 250th anniversary of America's founding, the challenges we face are unprecedented, and yet our political parties and their representatives - on both sides - focus on fighting each other.
What if we worked together, putting aside our differences and concentrating on just fixing the problem?
That's something I learned in the U.S.
Navy and have tried to apply every day since.
These pages lay out how I think we should tackle those problems.
It is my platform, not written by a political party or wealthy donors seeking special treatment.
It's what I believe and what I will fight for.
Read it, agree with it, disagree with it - I welcome it all.

I would rather you know exactly where I stand - so we can discuss our differences, resolve them where we can, but always keep moving forward and fighting for a better life for our families, our community, and our country.
That's my pledge - I'll always talk, always listen, and always fight - for you and for us.

DEFEND PROTECT BUILD STRENGTHEN Government & Rule of Law Over the last century the United States has pushed beyond its imperfections, saved the world from fascism; sparked decades of unprecedented economic, scientific, and technical growth at home and across the globe; and established cooperative systems to protect rights while maximizing opportunity.

America's integrity and institutions were fundamental to that progress, but today cynical politicians from both parties hack away at that record, poison the electoral process, and prevent further progress for their own selfish purposes.
LEARN MORE America's Place in the World Hampton Roads has the largest concentration of veterans and active-duty military in the country.
They have served, fought, and died in dozens of conflicts and a hundred countries - all to defend and serve their country and the world.

Those efforts established America as the most successful nation in history, sparking prosperity and security at home and abroad through alliances, shared sacrifice, and a rules-based international order.
Backing away from those commitments has alienated our friends, empowered our enemies, made us less safe and less respected, and will take a generation to recover from.
LEARN MORE Jobs, Health Care, and Growth Our economy has become horribly distorted, with just 10 tech and AI companies dominating the S&P 500 for the last several years.
The speculative bets on AI that are driving record stock prices are just that - bets, and if those bets are wrong, the investor class will once again call on the American public to make them whole.
The inflation has been reignited by across-the-board tariffs and traumatizing America's undocumented - but critical - work force.
The billionaire class captures an ever-increasing share of American wealth, while paying a lower tax rate than a welder or a nurse.
For the first time ever, American children are looking at a lower standard of living than their parents.
The system has been rigged, and we owe it to them to unrig it.
LEARN MORE Jobs, Health Care, and Growth The culture wars have paid off handsomely for both political parties, their most partisan supporters, and the Anger-Industrial complex.
Keeping Americans angry at each other is good for making profits and collecting contributions, but it's not good for a healthy society.

We need to recommit ourselves to equal and fair treatment for all, protection from predatory companies and actors, being the land of opportunity the world looks up to, and creating a society that offers unlimited opportunity and steadily improving conditions for all.
Public servants must act in the public interest, not the interest of themselves and their supporters.

added: In the 2026 session I have continued my service as: Chair of the Health and Human Services Committee Member of Education and Veteran’s Affairs Committees Member of the Commission to explore the potential establishment of a medical school at URI improving the primary care pipeline.

Member of the Long-Term Care Coordinating Council and the Integrated Coordinating Council for Early Intervention Legislative Updates To read a synopsis of the legislation passed in 2026 in the General Assembly click link: https://www.rilegislature.gov/pressrelease/YearlyHighlights/2026.pdf Bills for which I was a Primary Sponsor that passed in 2026 7625 SUB A Commencing January 1, 20 27, mandates insurers provide health insurance coverage without cost-share requirements for vaccinations recommended and deemed necessary by the RI Department of Health and organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, even if the CDC does not.
It also mandates the coverage for the medical assistance program and managed care organizations.

8069 SUB A Requires shooting ranges to post signs in any area in which shooting occurs and to also enforce the standard safety practice already utilized by many facilities across the nation-- mandating that membership-based shooting ranges require non-members to be accompanied at all times by a member or a staff member while on the premises and engaging in shooting activity.
I am grateful to the 2amendment community for supporting this bill.
This bill came to me after a tragedy.
Mom Jamie Brooks came to me last year to see if we could somehow prevent another death.
She wanted to do this to honor the memory of her son JJ.
Even more heartbreaking is that it was the second such death at this range and traumatic for all involved.
7376 SUB A Allows for a special RI license plate to raise awareness for colon cancer and would be designed by the partnership to reduce cancer in RI.
This bill was the wish of Bristol couple Pam and Rusty Mirik who lost their daughter Meridyth to colon cancer after being diagnosed at the age of 28.
7163 Prohibits participation in federal school voucher tax credit for contributions to scholarship-granting organizations unless both the general assembly and the governor approve such participation.

According to the NEA, opting into the federal tax credit voucher program would divert scarce public funds to private schools with fewer standards and protections—a model historically used to evade desegregation and one that continues to undermine the inclusive mission of public education House Resolution No.

7258 BY Donovan ENTITLED, JOINT RESOLUTION MAKING AN APPROPRIATION OF $200,000 TO BE USED FOR INCENTIVES FOR FRUITS AND VEGETABLES SOLD AT PARTICIPATING BONUS BUCKS OUTLETS IN RHODE ISLAND (Authorizes the appropriation of the sum of $200,000 for incentives for the Farm Fresh Bonus Bucks Program.) This made it into the state budget.

added: Skip to main content about news volunteer Donate Susie Lee for Congress Lee, Cortez Masto Successfully Release $52 Million in Funding for Hoover Dam May 24, 2026 Back to all news WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Susie Lee and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto announced that the Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) released $52 million in funding for the Hoover Dam, as directed by their Help Hoover Dam Act .
Representatives Mark Amodei (NV-02), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06) co-led this bipartisan legislation in the House.

Shital sagare February 23, 2026 Understanding N-Formyl Peptide Receptor 2: A Key Player in Immune Regulation The human immune system is a highly intricate network designed to protect the body from pathogens, tissue damage, and inflammation.
Among its many components, receptors on immune cells play a critical role in detecting and responding to danger signals.
One such receptor, N-Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 (FPR2), has emerged as a crucial mediator in immune regulation and inflammation resolution.
Click Me FPR2 is a member of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) family, primarily expressed on neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, and certain epithelial cells.

Unlike its closely related receptor FPR1, which is mostly involved in pro-inflammatory responses, FPR2 exhibits remarkable versatility, mediating both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory pathways depending on the ligands it encounters.
This dual functionality positions FPR2 as a pivotal receptor in balancing immune responses.

Shital sagare February 23, 2026 Herpes Labialis Drugs: Effective Treatments for Cold Sores Herpes labialis, commonly known as cold sores, is a recurrent viral infection caused primarily by the herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1).
It manifests as small, painful blisters, typically around the lips and mouth, and can cause discomfort, itching, and cosmetic concerns for affected individuals.
Although there is no permanent cure for herpes labialis, various drugs and treatment strategies can help manage symptoms, reduce the duration of outbreaks, and prevent recurrences.
Herpes Labialis Drugs Market The cornerstone of treatment for herpes labialis is antiviral therapy.
Oral antiviral medications such as acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir are widely used to target HSV-1.
These drugs work by inhibiting viral replication, helping to reduce the severity and duration of outbreaks.

For patients with frequent or severe episodes, physicians may recommend suppressive therapy, which involves taking antiviral medication daily to decrease the frequency of outbreaks and reduce the risk of transmission.

added: top of page Meet Mark Endorsements Priorities Events Volunteer Donate Privacy Policy for Tedford for Congress ​ ​ Effective date: 03/11/26 ​ 1.
Introduction Tedford for Congress (“we,” “our,” or “us”) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting the personal information you provide through our website.
This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and safeguard your information. ​ 2.

Information We Collect We may collect personal information that you voluntarily provide, including but not limited to: Name Email address Phone number Mailing address Any other information submitted through forms on our website We may also collect limited technical data such as IP address, browser type, and website usage data for analytics purposes. ​ 3.

How We Use Your Information We use your information to: Communicate with you about campaign updates, events, and initiatives Respond to inquiries and requests Process donations (if applicable) Improve our website and outreach efforts Comply with applicable laws and regulations ​ 4.
Text Messaging & Opt-In Data By providing your phone number and opting in, you consent to receive campaign-related text messages.
Standard message and data rates may apply.
No mobile opt-in data will be shared with third parties for marketing or promotional purposes.
Opt-in data may only be shared with vendors, consultants, and other service providers who require access to perform services on our behalf.
Such parties are contractually obligated to use this information solely for providing services to Tedford for Congress and are prohibited from using it for any other purpose.
You may opt out of text communications at any time by replying STOP. ​ 5.
Sharing of Information We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information.

We may share information only in the following limited circumstances: With trusted vendors, consultants, and service providers who assist in campaign operations When required by law, regulation, or legal process To protect the rights, safety, and security of our campaign and supporters ​ 6.
Data Security We implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect your information.
However, no method of transmission over the Internet is 100% secure. ​ ​ 8.
Third-Party Links Our website may contain links to external websites.
We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of those sites. ​ 9.

Your Choices You may: Opt out of email communications using the unsubscribe link Opt out of text messages by replying STOP Contact us to update or request deletion of your information where applicable ​ 10.
Changes to This Policy We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time.
Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated effective date. ​ 11.

Contact Us If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at: Tedford for Congress 2448 E 81st St Suite 3100 Tulsa OK 74137 Email: Team@TedfordforCongress.com Find Your Polling Location EARLY VOTING: October 28 - 30 from 8 am - 6 pm OR October 31 from 8 am - 2 pm ELECTION DAY IS TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2026.

added: 0 Skip to Content Terri Pickens for Governor Learn More Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Get Involved Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Donate Open Menu Close Menu Terri Pickens for Governor Learn More Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Get Involved Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Donate Open Menu Close Menu Folder: Learn More Back Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Folder: Get Involved Back Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Back Donate Goodbye Idaho Wild Places Public Lands May 2 Written By Terri Pickens Hey there Idaho newcomers, Welcome to Idaho!
Now that you’re here, I know you’ll want to save it as much as I do.
I have watched this “Gem” of a state’s population double to 2 million over the last 40 years.
I may not know what brought so many people here, but I completely understand why everyone has stayed.
If you haven’t already figured it out, you need to ignore most of the inane things that a bunch of self-centered, overly ambitious political snakes and knotheads may say.
Idahoans don’t like playing anyone’s brand of politics when it comes to public lands.
In Idaho, we fight to keep what we love.
Right now our public lands are threatened like never before.
Governor Brad Little has just declared that he’s clearing the way for President Trump’s demand to turn everything over to big industries.
Now, we like loggers and miners.
But we don’t want some unhinged foreign greed-driven company destroying our public lands, under-paying Idaho workers, and then leaving a town with sacks of money and a huge mess behind them.
It’s happened before and the “great” real estate con artist and his slavish minions think Idaho is just another state shaped like a dollar sign.
I’ll say it again, Brad Little is throwing down the red carpet.
He’s much too scared of Trump and the Idaho Republican political shot callers to stand up for us.
Hey don’t let anybody fool you.
Public land is something WE ALL AGREE on.
Libertarian and liberal hearts alike love that you don’t need to be rich to tramp around where clear water percolates, animals thrive, and a human’s spirit can truly soar.
Anyone who says we’d rather have our public land sold off is lying.
I am fighting the greedy liars now and I will fight them when I am governor.
If other states want to imprison everyone in cookie-cutter suburban mazes of pointy roofs and yards too small to stretch your arms in–that’s their sad decision.

added: 0 Skip to Content Terri Pickens for Governor Learn More Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Get Involved Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Donate Open Menu Close Menu Terri Pickens for Governor Learn More Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Get Involved Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Donate Open Menu Close Menu Folder: Learn More Back Issues About Terri Terri's Blog Endorsements Media Folder: Get Involved Back Events Volunteer Voting Yard Signs Events Contact Us Store English Back Donate On the Road Across Idaho: The Final Campaign Push Oct 14 Written By Elle Casner The last campaign month is racing by and I’m doing all I can to reach out to Idaho voters.
Here’s how: TWO big campaign swings through North Idaho and now Eastern Idaho.
SIX candidate forums TWENTY interviews with reporters DOZENS of speeches at public events ONE awesome campaign ad shoot next to the awesome Snake River with the world’s cutest … my bird dog Bailey.
AND a visit from my friend Ken Martin, the Democratic National Committee Chair.
Right now we’re leaning into strategically airing ads.
I AM THANKFUL FOR FOLKS SPEPPING UP CONTRIBUTIONS!
Last month, we had nearly # donors.
One internal poll put our MAGA governor who’s too scared to meet me in debates or forums, at 37 percent for folks planning to vote for him .
That’s wildly low so close to Election Day… The odds of an upset improve with each passing day.
The ground in Idaho is practically vibrating with energy as we head into the final three weeks of this election!
AND I really wish everyone had a chance to meet Ken Martin when he visited Idaho to support my campaign.

item_pages.value: 3 I WROTE and FILED the APPEAL at the Worcester Superior Court to request the DENIAL of the 40B approval by the Millbury Board of Appeals for a developer to build 192 apartments on RICE ROAD.
During the last 2 years, we have been in court over 7 times…but the Developer has not been able to have our case dismissed.
The judges have allowed the original case that I wrote, which was based on SAFETY , to continue because our case has MERIT .
We are scheduled to make another presentation in court on October 21.
With 100% ATTENDANCE , I served HONORABLY for 33 years in the USANG, USAFR, USNR, and USMC.
I was awarded the “Air Force Airman of the Quarter” and the “Naval Reserve Sailor of the Quarter”, and with my help, my Air Force Unit was awarded the “Outstanding Unit Citation”.

I presently serve actively with the Auburn Vietnam Veterans of America, Oxford Memorial Honor Guard, Leicester American Legion, and Millbury’s Veterans of Foreign Wars, American Legion and Veterans’ Council.
I served Millbury for 18 years on its Planning Board, and wrote and helped to write many of its Zoning and Rules and Regulations bylaws.
As a Millbury Housing Partnership member, I helped to build 3 AFFORDABLE housing homes for Millbury.
I know how to do it…and have done it.
I have offered to guide a new Housing Partnership Committee when the Town reestablishes it.

I have also served on Millbury’s Electromagnetic Fields (EMF) Committee, Ponds and Lakes Commission, Youth Commission, Master Plan Committee, Water Study Committee, Fair Housing Committee, and have been the Planning Board’s delegate to the CMRPC, Central Mass.
Over the last 10 years, I have quietly donated materials to be used by organizations to earn money, without the thought of self-promotion or a photo shoot.
These organizations are in Millbury, Auburn, Oxford, Charlton and Leicester, and include churches, senior centers, historical societies, and scouts.

I have earned 4 DEGREES …a Masters Degree in Health Education, a Masters Degree in Counselling, a Bachelors Degree in Health and Physical Education with a Concentration in General Science, and an Associates Degree in Health Care Management.

I have earned the following CERTIFICATIONS : Teacher for grades 1 thru 12 in Massachusetts, Military Field Medic, Military Operating Room Technician, Military Air Transportation Specialist, EMT, and American Heart Association and Red Cross Instructor-Trainor.
Even though divorced, I was blessed and raised a wonderful daughter.
She put herself thru medical school and is now a DOCTOR OF PHYSICAL THERAPY at a local hospital.
I’ve always worked at least 2 jobs.
I bought, maintain, and OWN MY OWN HOME .
I carefully plan to pay my mortgage, and increasing real estate taxes, sewer, water, gas, electricity, and home maintenance issues.
I work FULLTIME at a local public high school HELPING students with learning challenges.
I am an INDEPENDENT candidate, and I do not beg or accept money from any individuals or organizations.
If you choose to support me…please “step up to the plate” and DO SOMETHING !
Get 10 people to the polls to VOTE for me.

added: top of page DEMOCRAT FOR SENATE HOME ABOUT TIFFANY ISSUES For The People WOMEN FOR TIFFANY WOMEN FOR TIFFANY Events GET INVOLVED Volunteer Sign Up Yard Sign Request Volunteer Sign Up Yard Sign Request Menu Close DONATE ​ PRIVACY POLICY Updated: January 1, 2026 Friends of Tiffany Alston is committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the confidentiality of your personal information.
This Privacy Policy outlines how we collect, use, and protect your information when you interact with our services. ​ 1.

Use of Information The information we collect is used to: ● Schedule and manage appointments ● Improve our services and customer experience ● Respond to your inquiries or provide customer support ● Send you updates about our services, promotions, and offers ● Communicate with you regarding appointments and other service-related matters.
SMS Privacy We value your privacy and the information you consent to share in relation to our SMS marketing service.
We use this information solely to reach out to you regarding your appointments, events, promotions, and any additional questions or concerns you may have.
You can unsubscribe at any time by replying STOP to any SMS you receive from us.
Your mobile information will not be shared with third parties under any circumstances.
Data Sharing At Friends of Tiffany Alston, we take your privacy seriously.
We do not share your personal information with third parties, except when it is necessary to deliver our services or comply with legal obligations.
In certain cases, we may share your information with trusted service providers who assist us in providing our services.
These providers are bound by strict confidentiality agreements and are only permitted to use your information in ways that support our business operations.
Please note, your mobile information is treated with the utmost confidentiality and will never be shared with third parties or affiliates under any circumstances.
Data Security We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your personal information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
Your Rights You have the right to request access to the personal information we hold about you, to correct any inaccuracies, or to request the deletion of your information.
You may also opt out of receiving marketing communications from us at any time.
Changes to this Policy Friends of Tiffany Alston may update this Privacy Policy from time to time.
Any changes will be posted on this page, and we encourage you to review this policy periodically to stay informed.

Contact Us If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy or how your information is handled, please contact us at: Friends of Tiffany Alston Email: Tiffany@AlstonGray.com Phone: 301-583-1000 CONTACT Email: TAG@TiffanyAlston.com Phone: 240.334.7607 ​ 1401 Mercantile Lane, s uite 300 Largo, Maryland 20774 ​ ​ View Privacy Policy View Terms and Conditions Copyright © # Tiffany Alston - All Rights Reserved.

Message Frequency and Charges Message frequency may vary based on campaign activity and your interactions with us.
Message and data rates may apply according to your mobile carrier plan.
Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
Opt-Out Instructions You may opt out of text messages at any time by replying STOP to a message.
You may receive a final message confirming your opt-out.
After opting out, you will no longer receive messages covered by that opt-out unless you provide consent again.
Help and Contact For help, reply HELP to a campaign text or contact us using the information in Section 9 below.
Mobile Information and Data Sharing Mobile opt-in data and consent information will not be sold or shared with third parties or affiliates for their own marketing or promotional purposes.
We may use service providers to support campaign communications and website operations, subject to applicable confidentiality and data-protection obligations.
See our Privacy Policy for additional details.

Third-Party Links This website may contain links to third-party websites or services, including donation, event, and social-media platforms.
These third parties operate independently, and we are not responsible for their content, availability, terms, or privacy practices.

Your continued use of the website after changes are posted means you acknowledge the updated Terms, to the extent permitted by law.

added: Skip to content ★ Endorsed by Gov.

Sarah Sanders and every Arkansas statewide official → Menu Home About Tom Issues News Volunteer Contact Donate Press Release American Principles Project Endorses Cotton For Standing up for Arkansas Families & Conservative Values October 14, 2026 Contact: James@TomCotton.com Today, the American Principles Project (APP), which advocates for traditional family values, pro-life policies, parental rights in education, and religious liberty has endorsed Senator Tom Cotton for re-election to the U.S.
“Senator Tom Cotton has been a consistent fighter for the American family and defender of the American Dream.
He believes that opportunities belong to those who work hard, not people who check boxes,” said Terry Schilling, President of APP.
“This year Democrats are trying to rebrand anti-family, DEI-promoting candidates like Hallie Shoffner to sneak them past voters, but we won’t let that happen.

APP is proud to endorse Senator Tom Cotton for reelection and will always stand up to radical leftists who want to undermine our families, our wages, and our country.” “I’m grateful to the American Principles Project for its endorsement and steadfast defense of American families,” said Senator Tom Cotton.
Parents should raise their children, workers should get ahead on merit, and Washington should respect both.

I’ll keep fighting for those principles and against the radical Left’s efforts to force its ideology on our families and our country.” “Democrat Hallie Shoffner has refused to take positions on many issues important to Arkansas families, including the right to life, religious liberty, and parents’ rights to choose what’s best for their kids,” said James Arnold, Cotton campaign spokesman.

“Arkansans expect their senators to share their conservative values and fight for them in Washington, not fly to Peru to lead a trans rights parade.” The endorsement comes following news that Senator Cotton’s liberal Democrat opponent, Hallie Shoffner, once flew to Peru to “lead” a trans-rights advocacy parade .
At the Hallie Shoffner wrote: “I marched in Lima’s 9th Annual Gay Pride Parade yesterday (Saturday, July 10, 2010).
Now, when I say I marched in Lima’s 9th Annual Gay Pride Parade, I marched in the FRONT of Lima’s 9th Annual Gay Pride Parade.
I mean in the very front.

My org, Promsex, funded the parade so our staff carried the opening banner.” Shoffner described her experience “celebrating being gay, lesbian, transexual, [and] bisexual” as “incredible!” ### ← All News Share ← Newer Cotton Campaign Announces More Than $# Million Raised, Funds $# Million-Plus Turnout Plan with Arkansas GOP Older → Seven Times, Hallie Shoffner Refuses to Answer Whether She Knowingly Employed Illegal Aliens, Falsified Tax Documents We depend on you Stand with Tom.

The campaign is funding a get-out-the-vote plan of more than $1 million in partnership with the Republican Party of Arkansas to turn out Republican voters for the November election.
Cotton’s campaign has received contributions from thousands of Arkansans across all 75 counties.
The investment will support efforts to get voters to the polls during early voting and on Election Day, helping elect Republicans across Arkansas.
“We are launching the most extensive turnout operation in the Arkansas Republican Party’s history to make sure that conservatives get out and vote.
We are grateful for Senator Cotton’s partnership and are ready to make sure Republicans win across the state,” said RPA Chairman Wood.

“The Cotton campaign is thrilled with this record fundraising quarter, which will finance a massive get-out-the-vote campaign to help Arkansas Republicans up and down the ballot,” said James Arnold, Cotton campaign spokesman.

You can write articles, long mission statements, company policies, executive profiles, company awards/distinctions, office locations, shareholder reports, whitepapers, media mentions and other pieces of content that don’t fit into a shorter, more succinct space.
Articles – Good topics for articles include anything related to your company – recent changes to operations, the latest company softball game – or the industry you’re in.
General business trends (think national and even international) are great article fodder, too.
Mission statements – You can tell a lot about a company by its mission statement.
Now might be a good time to create one and post it here.
A good mission statement tells you what drives a company to do what it does.
Company policies – Are there company policies that are particularly important to your business?
Perhaps your unlimited paternity/maternity leave policy has endeared you to employees across the company.
This is a good place to talk about that.
Executive profiles – A company is only as strong as its executive leadership.
This is a good place to show off who’s occupying the corner offices.
Write a nice bio about each executive that includes what they do, how long they’ve been at it, and what got them to where they are.
Learn More This is a content preview space you can use to get your audience interested in what you have to say so they can’t wait to learn and read more.
Pull out the most interesting detail that appears on the page and write it here.

My first priority is making life affordable again.
I will vote to suspend the Gas Tax, use the state's surplus to cut your taxes, and defend Proposition 13 so families aren't taxed out of their homes.
I oppose any new tax increase.
How you can help: Sign the Repeal the Death Tax petition at HJTP.com.
Education As an award-winning classroom teacher with 20+ years in public schools, I've seen the crisis up close.
California now ranks 44th in the nation — too many students graduate unable to read, write, or do basic math.
That's unacceptable.
I will fight for parental rights and school choice, defend parents' voice in their kids' education, and audit education spending so every dollar reaches the classroom.
Every student deserves the skills to succeed — in college, in a trade, or in the workforce.
Public Safety Public Safety Violent and property crime are rising, and Sacramento's soft-on-crime policies have made us less safe.
I oppose "Defunding the Police." I will fight for tougher penalties for repeat offenders, hold rogue DAs accountable, stop the refusal to prosecute, and keep dangerous felons behind bars.
It's time to put victims first.
Homelessness Protecting Kids and Parental Rights Public Safety Sacramento has spent billions on programs that only made homelessness worse.
We need real accountability.

I will call for a State Audit to track where the money went, expand mental health and addiction treatment to address the root causes, and make it easier to place people in care rather than leave them on the street.
Our neighborhoods must be cleaned up and kept safe.

Protecting Kids and Parental Rights Protecting Kids and Parental Rights Protecting Kids and Parental Rights Recent laws from Sacramento have put kids in danger and stripped parents of their right to protect them.
I'm a strong advocate for both kids and parents.
Parents must be informed if their child is at risk of self-harm.
Child removal by the state should be rare, and struggling families should get help early.
I will audit Child Protective Services, support families in crisis, and protect girls' private spaces and girls' sports.
How you can help: Sign the petition at ProtectKidsCA.com.

We are supporting Brad Trahan due to his support for: • Affordable Choices • Fewer Unfunded Mandates • Cutting Health Insurance Taxes Brad has demonstrated an understanding of complex health insurance issues and knows that the rapidly increasing cost of health insurance is a big part of what is driving the high cost of living Minnesotans are experiencing.
Brad Trahan is also committed to protecting coverage for people with pre-existing conditions.
Coverage for pre-existing conditions has existed in Minnesota’s marketplace since 1976.

About us: Minnesotans for Affordable Health Insurance represents your local health insurance agents, who are the primary advocates for consumers who purchase coverage in the individual and small group health insurance markets.

Minnesotans for Affordable Health Insurance • Bob Stein, Chair Facebook: MNforAffordableHealthInsurance Twitter: @AffordableHealthMN Website: www.affordablehealthinsmn.com Email: mnforaffordablehealthins@gmail.com 24 Sep Thursday, 9:41 AM · 2026 Brad attends the Arc Minnesota- SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council and SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota), Forum September 22nd Brad was pleased to attend this forum, sponsored by ARC Minnesota - SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council, SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota, this past Tuesday.
This event focuses on issues that impact people with disabilities in our community.

Questions asked, and addressed were questions on how candidate plan to listen to self-advocates when making decisions on waiver services/supports, Transportation, Housing, and Fraud (to make sure the fraud doesn't negatively impact people who need those services) Brad’s answer to the fraud question was, in part: “Don’t allow it to happen to begin with—in the first place!” Internal controls are designed to identify and prevent fraud before it reaches the level we have witnessed.
When state employees raise concerns about potential fraud and those concerns are not adequately addressed, that demands accountability.
Brad put it this way: “When your checking account shows unusual activity, your financial institution doesn’t simply look the other way.

It will freeze the account and contact you to determine whether the activity is legitimate or whether your account has been compromised.” The federal government took similar action when concerns arose that Minnesota funds were not being used for their intended purposes.
Minnesota has a fiduciary responsibility to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure public funds are being used as intended.
Brad believes that responsibility must be taken seriously.
Whistleblower warnings should be investigated, internal controls should be followed, and fraud should be stopped before it happens, not after taxpayers have already lost millions of dollars.
As Brad said, “FRAUD-FRAUD-FRAUD!” It should be a top priority to protect Minnesota taxpayers and the essential services that depend on those dollars.
This is not simply a federal issue, as our Democratic friends choose to blame.
Minnesota state agencies had responsibility for administering and overseeing many of these programs, and the state’s own Legislative Auditor has found significant failures in oversight.
In the Feeding Our Future case, for example, the Legislative Auditor concluded that inadequate oversight by the Minnesota Department of Education created opportunities for fraud.
The people of Minnesota deserve accountability from those responsible for overseeing these programs, including Governor Tim Walz and state agency leadership.
Minnesotans also deserve to know where elected officials stand when serious failures occur, and whether they are willing to publicly demand accountability, stronger safeguards, and meaningful reform.
Brad's opponent has mostly been silent.

Brad's opponent has spoken publicly about fraud in a newsletter, and a few media outlets, and supported anti-fraud legislation, but we have not found one, not one public press release specifically condemning the scale of Minnesota's fraud or publicly assigning responsibility for the failures to Governor Walz and his administration, nor her party, for allowing this massive fraud to occur.
Some Democrats have called for Minnesota to look forward and avoid politicizing the issue.

But accountability requires more than simply moving forward, it requires asking how these failures happened, who was responsible for oversight, and what must change to prevent them from happening again.
Minnesotans deserve transparency and accountability from their state government.
As your elected State Representative, Brad Trahan will not hesitate to ask tough questions, hold government accountable, and call out fraud, waste, and abuse when it occurs.
As many people know, Brad is the proud father of Reece, a 26-year-old with severe autism.
For the past 23 years, Brad has been not only a dedicated parent and advocate for his son, but also a passionate self-advocate for countless individuals and families facing similar challenges.

His personal experience has given him a firsthand understanding of the importance of ensuring that people with disabilities have a strong voice, access to needed services, and the opportunity to live with dignity and support.
In 2016, Brad led an initiative for 13 years, 8 months, for Mayo Clinic to provide autism therapy, benefits for their employees' dependents, diagnosed with autism.
Just recently in 2026, Brad led initiative to expand access to specialized oral care, in hospital, under anesthesia for individuals with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
There were only five (5) hospitals in the State of Minnesota that provided this case for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities, and Brad was able to add a sixth, Olmsted Medical Center.
A project he started in January 2025, and completed in June 2026.
Also, recently in late August 2026, Brad identified a gap in Mayo Clinic Insurance Policy, regarding oral anesthesia care and provider coverage.
Brad worked closely with Mayo, Medica (Plan Administrator), and MN DHS.
May0 agreed that there was a gap, and effective October 1st, they were going to add OMC as an approved Provider for this Oral anesthesia care for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
Brad achieved this task in just one-weeks time!
In 2007, Brad led an initiative to bring Project Lifesaver to Olmsted County/City of Rochester.
This technology helps those most vulnerable, if they wander away.
It helps law enforcement find those missing individuals quickly.
In 2009, Brad led efforts to raise $25,000 to help get Project Lifesaver implemented in other SE Minnesota Counties.
In 2015, Brad led efforts at the state level for “Lifesaver Technology” grant in St.
Paul, secured $80,000 for 2 years, for law enforcement to invest in this technology for the communities they serve.
Brad has not simply talked about his commitment to the disability community, he has demonstrated it through action, advocacy, and meaningful changes in legislation and insurance coverage.

15 Sep Tuesday, 11:08 AM · 2026 Brad endorsed by his 6th Grade Teacher (1979) September 15th, All candidates will tell you that the political campaign process is long and busy, but in my case, I am also having a lot of fun!
Yesterday, I came home, opened this mail, and found an endorsement from my 6th-grade teacher (1979), back in Faribault!
Needless to say, this card made my day!
I've been blessed to have many teachers and coaches impact my life during my educational years.
It's nice to see that they are proud, even decades later!
I have always strived to live by the values I have been taught at home, in the classroom, and in the workforce, and to pay them forward.
A quick THANK YOU to my past Teachers and Coaches.
You've made an impact on me, that I have never forgotten.
And, I'm certain you've made them on multiple students and athletes through your years in education.
I'll take those same life-lesson values to St.
Paul and will always put PEOPLE over POLITICS!
15 Sep Tuesday, 8:53 AM · 2026 Brad attends the Oronoco Township Board Meeting September 14th Brad took in the well-attended Oronoco Township Meeting last night for a few hours.
While sitting through the public hearings, Brad admired, and respected the readings, and the cordial public testimony, with excellent questions, and genuine thought from the Township Board.
Great job, Oronoco Township, and those you serve!
14 Sep Monday, 11:12 AM · 2026 Brad visits PACLEAR FARMS - Pagel Family in Eyota, MN.
September 11th Thank you, to Jeff Pagel, and the Paclear Farms Family, for a great 1 1/2 visit this past Friday afternoon.
Brad learned a lot and most of all, admires the passion of their family farm, now in its third-generation, have for farming and farming responsibly.
Our farmers are working 24/7/365.
Dairy cows don't take weekends off!
They don't take any days off, and neither does our American Farmer.
We hear a lot about AI these days, but AI won't be milking 150 cows at 5am and 5pm every day.
The science, nutrition, crop rotation, livestock rotation, working with other farmers, and the agricultural challenges, provided great insight.

I am very honored to have received the MINNESOTA FARM BUREAU PAC endorsement, and once elected, I promise I will work hard, and advocate to bring common-sense values and policy to our agricultural community.
You feed us.
You fuel us.
THANK YOU!

11 Sep Friday, 1:09 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester's 9/11 Ceremony September 11th A beautiful, but somber 9/11 Tribute this morning put on in partnership with Rochester Fire Department, Olmsted County Sheriff’s Office, and Rochester Police Department.
Thank you, Scott Eggert, and Broadway Plaza!
Many first responders walked the stairs to remember and honor their fallen heroes from that horrific day!
It was an honor to see the RFD, OCSO, and RPD Honor Guards accompanied by the Rochester Caledonian Pipe Band.
Great opening statements by Sheriff Torgerson, followed by a nice Benediction by George Beach of Salt and Light Partners, set the stage for then reading every first responder who lost their lives.
The ceremony paused at the times the planes struck.

WE WILL NEVER FORGET 9/11 11 Sep Friday, 1:05 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester Police Department Swearing In and Promotional Ceremony September 10th One of the awesome honors of serving on the Rochester Police Department, Police Civil Service Commission, is attending the new Police Officer Swearing-in Ceremony.

15 Jun Monday, 3:27 PM · 2026 Vehicle Registraton Costs; Wisconsin vs.
Minnesota This is unacceptable for Minnesotans.
The current formula-based system needs to be re-evaluated.
On top of the base registration tax, drivers are also paying a stack of additional costs, including plate fees, filing fees, technology surcharges, and public safety fees.

While funding roads and bridges is essential, and vehicle registration revenue is directed into the Highway User Tax Distribution Fund (HUTDF), the current structure places an uneven burden on Minnesota drivers.
There was some work done on this this year, but it doesn't take effect until January 2027, with some fees reverting back to 2023.
More work needs to be done, however.

If elected to represent MN House District 25A, I will work across the aisle to reform this system and pursue a more reasonable, transparent flat-fee model, similar to what most other states use for vehicle registration.

Questions asked, and addressed were questions on how candidate plan to listen to self-advocates when making decisions on waiver services/supports, Transportation, Housing, and Fraud (to make sure the fraud doesn't negatively impact people who need those services) Brad’s answer to the fraud question was, in part: “Don’t allow it to happen to begin with—in the first place!” Internal controls are designed to identify and prevent fraud before it reaches the level we have witnessed.
When state employees raise concerns about potential fraud and those concerns are not adequately addressed, that demands accountability.
Brad put it this way: “When your checking account shows unusual activity, your financial institution doesn’t simply look the other way.

It will freeze the account and contact you to determine whether the activity is legitimate or whether your account has been compromised.” The federal government took similar action when concerns arose that Minnesota funds were not being used for their intended purposes.
Minnesota has a fiduciary responsibility to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure public funds are being used as intended.
Brad believes that responsibility must be taken seriously.
Whistleblower warnings should be investigated, internal controls should be followed, and fraud should be stopped before it happens, not after taxpayers have already lost millions of dollars.
As Brad said, “FRAUD-FRAUD-FRAUD!” It should be a top priority to protect Minnesota taxpayers and the essential services that depend on those dollars.
This is not simply a federal issue, as our Democratic friends choose to blame.
Minnesota state agencies had responsibility for administering and overseeing many of these programs, and the state’s own Legislative Auditor has found significant failures in oversight.
In the Feeding Our Future case, for example, the Legislative Auditor concluded that inadequate oversight by the Minnesota Department of Education created opportunities for fraud.
The people of Minnesota deserve accountability from those responsible for overseeing these programs, including Governor Tim Walz and state agency leadership.
Minnesotans also deserve to know where elected officials stand when serious failures occur, and whether they are willing to publicly demand accountability, stronger safeguards, and meaningful reform.
Brad's opponent has mostly been silent.

Brad's opponent has spoken publicly about fraud in a newsletter, and a few media outlets, and supported anti-fraud legislation, but we have not found one, not one public press release specifically condemning the scale of Minnesota's fraud or publicly assigning responsibility for the failures to Governor Walz and his administration, nor her party, for allowing this massive fraud to occur.
Some Democrats have called for Minnesota to look forward and avoid politicizing the issue.

But accountability requires more than simply moving forward, it requires asking how these failures happened, who was responsible for oversight, and what must change to prevent them from happening again.
Minnesotans deserve transparency and accountability from their state government.
As your elected State Representative, Brad Trahan will not hesitate to ask tough questions, hold government accountable, and call out fraud, waste, and abuse when it occurs.

8 Sep Tuesday, 4:32 PM · 2026 Brad does a Ride-Along with the Rochester Police Department September 5th On Saturday, September 5th, Brad had the opportunity to ride along with the Rochester Police Department from 7:00 p.m. until 4:00 a.m.

Domestics, fights, weapons calls, people in crisis, and much more.

They don't always get the credit they deserve.

After responding to a serious call and getting things settled down, an RPD Sergeant noticed a 6-year-old little girl and her teddy bear nearby.
The Sergeant took the time to get police stickers for the young girl and her teddy bear.
They weren't the reason the officers were there.

We cannot continue to band-aid mental health in our communities.
We need long-term solutions that address the underlying problems and provide law enforcement with the resources and partnerships they need.
Throughout the night, I saw Rochester Police Officers demonstrate professionalism, patience, compassion and courage.

We must make sure law enforcement has the tools, resources and support they need to do their jobs effectively and safely, both for themselves and for the people they serve.
Every one of you is truly policing from the heart.
You demonstrated courage, professionalism and compassion throughout Saturday night's shift.

24 Aug Monday, 10:57 AM · 2026 Brad meet with HHS Secretary RFK Jr., FEMA Director Cameron Hamilton, DOJ and Others - Announcement of Project Lifesaver National Autism Alert System August 21st A Family, a Community, and a Commitment to Protect Our Most Vulnerable For Brad, this moment is deeply personal.

Kennedy Jr. during the announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system for individuals with autism who go missing was a powerful reminder of why this work matters.
Brad has spent years advocating for programs that help protect individuals with autism and other vulnerable members of our community.
One of those efforts began right here in Rochester and Olmsted County with Project Lifesaver, a program designed to help law enforcement locate individuals who may wander or become missing.
Brad helped bring Project Lifesaver to Rochester and Olmsted County by raising $15,000 to launch the program.

So many people have stepped up and made a difference.

When it comes to protecting our most vulnerable, we have to work together and do everything we can.” Brad is especially proud of the Rochester Police Department and Olmsted County Sheriff's Office Project Lifesaver teams, whose dedication continues to make a difference for families throughout our community.
He also recognizes the continued efforts of Rochester Autism Advocacy, including its work helping families navigate the application process and identify individuals who may benefit from the program.

Brad is grateful as well for the past support of RTAAF, and for the leadership and administrative support provided by Sheriff Borchardt, Sheriff Torgerson, and Police Chief Franklin, whose belief in the program helped make this community effort possible.
For Brad and his family, this isn't simply about policy.
And it's about making sure that when a vulnerable person goes missing, every possible resource is available to help bring them home safely.

The announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system represents an important step forward, and Brad is proud to have been part of the local effort that helped demonstrate what is possible when families, advocates, law enforcement, government, and communities work together.

27 Jul Monday, 5:49 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce Linking Leaders & Industry at Novios Cafe July 27th Brad Trahan attended the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce, Linking Leaders & Industry form at Novios Cafe, and Co-Owner, Dalton Shirley.

Brad was joined by MN House District GOP, 20-B, endorsed candidate, Sara Bertschinger. • Minnesota Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML): Dalton shared that he recently received his updated quarterly tax statement and that his taxes have more than doubled compared to what he was paying before PFML was implemented.
He also shared that, to date, none of his employees have used PFML.
It raises serious questions about whether the program is sustainable in its current form and the impact it is having on small businesses.

(My belief is that it is not sustainable in its current format – Brad) • Small business challenges: Dalton employs between 22 and 30 people, which classifies his business as a large employer under the program.
