added: Skip to content Home News & Updates Contact Us Four Years Is Long Enough to Ask – What Changed? / 151 / By Mike Four Years Is Long Enough to Ask What Changed By Michael Mason Four years is a long time in Hartford.
It is long enough to introduce legislation, build relationships, fight for your district and demonstrate what kind of representative you are.
So, I think it is fair to ask: What did you actually change?
Not how many bills you voted on or meetings you attended.
And what is better for Greenwich because you were there?
Arzeno‘s own legislative updates provide an answer.

They highlight millions of dollars in state funding for Greenwich schools and community projects, expanded education and childcare funding, tax credits and efforts to address certain costs on electric bills.
But the bigger question remains: What broader legislative agenda has he advanced for Greenwich?
A state representative’s job is not simply to vote on bills or secure funding for individual projects.
It is to identify problems, write legislation, challenge misguided mandates, protect local control and hold Hartford accountable for spending taxpayers’ money.
Connecticut needs more affordable housing, and Greenwich should do its part.
But I don’t believe the answer is imposing the same formula on every community and then allowing developers to use it to challenge local zoning decisions.
If Hartford wants more affordable housing, let’s build it intelligently.
Count existing affordable units accurately, remove the 40-year restriction on the property, and reward communities that actually produce housing.
Direct and control development where roads, sewers, schools and other infrastructure can support it.
And if the state imposes new requirements, it should help pay for the infrastructure they demand.
We must also reform 8-30g to encourage the housing Connecticut needs without unnecessarily undermining local planning.
That is not an argument against affordable housing.
It’s a demand for better policy and practical results.
In 2026, the legislature considered HB 5369, which examined the state’s 10% affordable-housing threshold.
That is precisely the kind of fundamental policy question our representative should help lead.
I don’t want to go to Hartford simply to vote on someone else’s proposal.
I want to help write a better one.
And then there is the most basic responsibility of being a legislator: Show Up.
During the November 2025 special session, the House passed HB 8002, the Housing Growth Act, by a vote of 90–56.
Arzeno was absent for the critical House votes, including the final vote.
This HB 2002 has by far more effect on our community than 830g.
Legislators can have legitimate reasons to miss votes.
But when Hartford makes consequential decisions about housing and local control, Greenwich deserves a representative who is at the table.
I intend to be there—not just to explain what happened afterward, but to help shape legislation before it becomes law.
I will pursue 8-30g and HB 2002 reform, challenge mandates that don’t make sense for Greenwich, and defend decisions that belong with our town.
I will work across party lines whenever doing so produces better results.
The same accountability must apply to state spending.
Fiscal responsibility means setting priorities, planning capital projects carefully, eliminating unnecessary spending and demanding value for every taxpayer dollar.
It also means respecting non-partisan Budget Guard rails.
Greenwich residents work hard for their money.
They deserve a representative who remembers that every dollar Hartford spends comes from someone.
When Greenwich needs legitimate state assistance, I will fight for it.
But I don’t want my definition of success to be how much money can I bring home after Hartford has already taken it.
My goal is to change the system that keeps asking taxpayers for more.
This is where I live, work and raise my family.
I know this community and understand the responsibility that comes with asking its residents for their trust.
If elected, I will show up, do the homework, write legislation, defend local control and work with anyone—Republican or Democrat—to deliver results.
Four years is long enough to ask what has changed.
I am running to make the next four years count. ← Previous Post Home News & Updates Contact Us Home News & Updates Contact Us Paid for by Elect Michael Mason 2026 Nicole Wittenberg, Treasurer.

LINK September 13, 2026 Always good to be home with our Greenwood County people in the Town o...

Always good to be home with our Greenwood County people in the Town of Hodges for the annual Lights on Main event this weekend, as we honored our first responder and military heroes in reflection of 25 years since the 9/11 attacks on our country.

MEET STEPHANIE: YOUR VOICE FOR ARIZONA Because Arizona Deserves Better My Positions Next Proven Leadership: 30+ years experience as a successful business owner, engineer, nonprofit leader Next Fiscally Responsible and Experienced Next Advocate for a Strong Public Education System Next Supports School Choice with Accountability Next People over Politics and Party Ideology WHAT OTHERS ARE SAYING For Arizona, For All of Us LATEST ENDORSEMENTS ABOUT STEPHANIE Bringing Experience to Serve You As a dedicated advocate for the people of Legislative District 14, I am committed to bringing positive progress and long-term success for Arizona.
I am an engineer with over 30 years of experience in energy, business, and creating practical solutions to difficult problems.
I'm ready to bring my experience and work ethic to the Arizona Senate. ​ Today's issues around water, our local economy, and jobs require real solutions that address competing needs.
Tomorrow's emerging challenges will be even greater--they will require strategic plans and strong decisions that will lift up everyone in our community.
I will fight for financial accountability and transparency, and for quality of life--from water rates to energy prices to quality education.
My team and supporters are driven by a passion to see progress, not division.
To see ethics and community service as the foundation for political service.
To move forward in unity and service for all constituents--not for personal gain or influenced by divisive politics.
By anchoring our actions with our core values of respect, honesty, and cooperation, my team will help create a better future for Arizona.
One that respects our past and our future, in cooperation our neighbors.

All Articles Press Announcement Search Arizonans deserve more than family name #ago 2 min read Updated: #ago By Stephanie Walsh | Gilbert OPINION — We are at a critical moment in Arizona.
We face reduced water allocations, rising costs, and rapid advances in artificial intelligence.
How we respond to these challenges will shape the future of our state and the opportunities available to our children.
We can’t continue to kick those cans down the road.
With our busy lives, it's easy to tune out elections.
I've heard the questions: Aren’t all candidates the same?
Do I just vote by party?
The truth is that local elections matter tremendously.
The decisions that most affect our daily lives are often made close to home.
And this year, voters in our district have an important choice to make.

I chose to run for the State Senate seat in Legislative District 14, which includes most of Gilbert and portions of Queen Creek and Chandler, not because politics has appealed to me (it hasn’t!), but because I believe we all have a responsibility to use our talents and experience to serve our communities.
I am an engineer, former owner and CEO of an engineering firm with 100-plus employees, and founder of a nonprofit advancing energy solutions.
I’ve received a national Congressional Small Business Award and am proud to be endorsed by the Gilbert Chamber of Commerce.
I bring a lifetime of experience in leadership, teamwork, finance, and developing smart solutions to difficult problems.
I am also the mother of two young adults, and I care deeply about the future of their generation.
Choosing to serve my community by running for the Legislature came in an unexpected way.
Last fall, I heard on national news that our district had only one choice for the State Senate — Mylie Biggs, the 25-year-old daughter of Congressman Andy Biggs.
Biggs has limited qualifications, she has name recognition.
What caught my attention more was that her announcement to run came just months after she stated on a podcast, "I don't think women should hold office in general.
That's my stance." Referring to women’s right to vote, she also remarked, "Repeal the 19th Amendment." Those statements deeply concerned me and should concern us all.
My opponent’s viewpoint didn’t come out of the blue.
There is a growing movement that society’s ills will be solved by eliminating women’s right to vote.
That extreme message is being aimed at our young women and men and Ms.
Biggs’ stated views are part of that broader movement.
Removing voting rights is a strange solution if your goal is to improve lives.
Ballots for the 2026 election are being prepared now.
The choices we make will have lasting consequences for our state's future.
I am asking for your support to strengthen Arizona's economy, strengthen our education system, secure our long-term water future, and tackle the rising costs of energy, housing, and everyday living.
Vote for a future built on practical solutions, economic opportunity, and a government that represents everyone.
Arizonans deserve integrity and experience, not a family name.

All Articles Press Announcement Search LD 14 Senate choice is crystal clear: Stephanie Walsh #ago 1 min read Updated: #ago By Carrie Goode | Gilbert OPINION — As a 16-year Gilbert resident, I’m quite concerned about the cost of, and access to, water and energy, as I’m sure many of my neighbors are.
The status of the Colorado River is getting dire, and I’ve seen it with my own eyes while driving to San Diego.
Energy and water costs continue to escalate, hurting middle-class Arizonans.
Our ballots are being delivered this week, and we Gilbert residents have a real opportunity this election.
We have a candidate for the State Senate in Legislative District 14 who has a lifetime of experience and expertise finding solutions to these critical problems.
Stephanie Walsh is an engineer who built an energy company of over 100 employees working on solving the exact issues we are dealing with.
By electing her to our state Legislature, we can help not just Gilbert, but Arizona as well.
I’m imploring voters, regardless of their party affiliation, to look at the two candidates, not just the letter next to their name.
Stephanie is running against Andy Biggs’ 26-year-old daughter, who has no experience or qualifications.
She’s running strictly on her father’s name recognition and his coattails.
She’s on the record stating that women should not hold public office.
Let’s send a real problem solver, moderate, brilliant woman to our state Senate.

[image: Risch Recognizes Walsh Engineering Services During National Women’s Small Business Month]www.sbc.senate.govRisch Recognizes Walsh Engineering Services During National Women’s Small Business MonthWashington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Jim Risch (R-ID), chairman of the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, has named Walsh Engineering Services in Idaho Falls, Idaho as the Small Business of the Month for October 2018. Walsh Engineering will be recognized in the Congressional Record of the U.S. Senate. “Walsh Engineering Services is a woman-owned design and architectural engineering firm that provides high-quality technical and design services to customers throughout Idaho and around the country,” said Chairman Risch. “Since its founding, Stephanie Walsh has grown the company from a small group of dedicated engineers and designer-drafters, to a full-service engineering and architecture firm. She is an outstanding example of Idaho’s unique entrepreneurial spirit and is an inspiration to women entrepreneurs across the great state of Idaho. During National Women’s Small Business Month, I am pleased to honor a great woman-owned small business in Walsh Engineering.” An Idaho Falls native, Stephanie Walsh graduated from the University of Idaho with a degree in mechanical engineering and returned home to work for Idaho National Lab (INL). While at INL, Stephanie recognized the emerging need for expert contractors, and in 2005 she founded Walsh Engineering Services. Owning her own business and working with INL as a contractor allowed her to continue to work to meet the needs of INL, as well as those of a growing Southeastern Idaho. Their clients have expanded over the years from INL to other DOE National Laboratories, the State of Idaho Department of Public Works, and fabrication firms located throughout the country. While Stephanie founded the company to support the changing needs of INL, Walsh Engineering Services is also focused on training the next generation of workers to continue the history of professionalism and success at INL. The firm not only offers jobs to recent graduates of Idaho universities but also develops the next generation of engineers through the firm’s internship program. The Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship oversees proposed legislation on matters relating to entrepreneurship and provides oversight of the Small Business Administration. The committee also researches, investigates and reports all problems relating to America’s small businesses to the full Senate. As Chairman, Risch will honor America’s small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Senate each month.

All Articles Press Announcement Search Walsh supports increased accountability for ESAs #ago 2 min read Updated: #ago Gilbert reader weighs in on LD 14 Senate race By Doris Karls | Gilbert OPINION — Education is foundational to our community and economy, which is why I am voting for Stephanie Walsh for State Senate to represent Legislative District 14.
She will provide a strong and consistent voice supporting our public schools.
Stephanie is endorsed by Save Our Schools Arizona and by the Gilbert Chamber of Commerce.
She clearly understands and articulates the connection between a vibrant and innovative public-education system and the positive impacts on economic development.
Stephanie is not a career politician.
She built her career for over 30 years as a mechanical engineer who was founder and former owner/CEO of an engineering firm.
As a business leader, she supports workforce training partnerships among high schools, technical and community colleges, universities and businesses.
Stephanie also is an advocate for strengthening early childhood education and school-readiness programs, such as First Things First, as early learning is foundational to school success.

Stephanie supports increased accountability in the Empowerment Scholarship Account program to carefully monitor spending of our tax dollars, as well as to ensure teacher qualifications, safety and documented student achievement.
By contrast, Mylie Biggs, her opponent, is focused on expanding the ESA program.

Stephanie states: “Arizona must continue strengthening workforce readiness and preparation for careers in technology, advanced manufacturing, healthcare, skilled trades and other high-demand industries.” Efforts in these areas will draw companies to the town of Gilbert and Arizona statewide.
The Gilbert Public School District is the largest employer in the community.
As our state senator, Stephanie is well-positioned to provide solid solutions to support public education, working in collaboration, to build bridges to the future.

Home About Platform Endorsements Vote VOLUNTEER How to Vote Your vote, your town, your plan.
Everything you need to vote in the 35th District — Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.
18 Days 23 Hours 28 Min 58 Sec Information from the Connecticut Secretary of the State and town registrars.
Always confirm your polling place at the state's lookup tool.

Pick your town Ashford Chaplin Coventry Eastford Ellington Hampton Stafford Thompson Tolland Union Vernon Willington Woodstock Or choose from the list Select your town… Ashford Chaplin Coventry Eastford Ellington Hampton Stafford Thompson Tolland Union Vernon Willington Woodstock Your options Three ways to vote 1.
Vote early in person Monday, Oct 19 through Sunday, Nov 1 , including weekends.
10am–6pm daily, extended to 8am–8pm on Tuesday, Oct 27 and Thursday, Oct 29 .
No early voting on Monday, Nov 2.
Early voting is at your town's early voting location, which is often not your usual polling place.
You can only vote early in the town where you're registered.
Vote by absentee ballot New for 2026, any Connecticut voter can vote absentee with no excuse needed.
Return it by mail, to your town's official drop box outside Town Hall, or in person to your Town Clerk.
Mailed ballots must arrive by 8pm on Election Day, so mail it early or use the drop box.
Connecticut now lets you fix (cure) a missing signature so your ballot still counts.
Vote on Election Day Tuesday, Nov 3, 6am–8pm at your assigned polling place.
If you're in line by 8pm, you can vote.

Your ballot Find Ethan on your ballot Line 3 · State Senator · Vote for one 3A Ethan Werstler Democratic 3B Other candidate — 3C Ethan Werstler Working Families Ethan appears twice on Line 3: on the Democratic row (3A) and the Working Families row (3C).

See your town's sample ballot Your town Where to vote in your town Ashford Chaplin Coventry Eastford Ellington Hampton Stafford Thompson Tolland Union Vernon Willington Woodstock Registration Not registered yet?
Register by Friday, Oct 16 to vote without extra steps: online until 11:59pm, in person at your registrar's office until 8pm, or by mail (postmarked by Oct 16).
Register online 17 and turning 18 by Nov 3?
You can register now, and you can vote early or absentee in this election.
Connecticut has Same-Day Registration every day of early voting and on Election Day.
During early voting, register and vote at your town's early voting location.
On Election Day, go to your town's Same-Day Registration location (usually Town Hall; call your registrar to confirm), not your polling place.
Bring ID and proof of address.
Arrive early, because same-day registration takes longer.
Check if I'm registered At the polls What to bring Connecticut voters are asked for ID.
Any of these works: a photo ID, a Social Security card, or a pre-printed item showing your name and address (like a utility bill, bank statement or paycheck).
If you have no ID, you can still vote by signing a statement at the polls.
First-time voters who registered by mail may need photo ID or a document showing their address.
Pick how I'll vote (early / absentee / Election Day) 3.

Wes Moore Launches New Ad Highlighting Bipartisan Support And Results Moore-Miller Campaign Continues Multi-Seven-Figure Ad Buy With New TV Ad The Moore-Miller for Maryland campaign has launched a statewide multi-seven-figure ad buy that includes a new tv ad focusing on his bipartisan support across the state and the results he’s delivered while in office.

“Marylanders are continuing to see the bipartisan work Governor Moore has accomplished to grow our economy, drop violent crime to record lows, deliver relief from skyrocketing energy bills, and build the best public schools possible,” said Senior Communications Adviser Carter Elliott, IV.
“As the campaign looks to November, Gov.

Moore continues to communicate directly with Marylanders about how he’s worked across the aisle to deliver real results for all of Maryland.” The Moore-Miller campaign just launched a new tv ad “Bringing Us Together,” highlighting support from Republican Mayor Travis Marion and Democratic Mayor Monique Ashton.
The two leaders discuss how for Governor Moore, ‘it’s not about party, it’s about Maryland,’ and when their communities needed him, he stepped up to help.
Here’s What Marylanders Are Watching: WATCH: “Bringing Us Together” Mayor Monique Ashton: I’m a Democrat.
Mayor Travis Marion: And, I’m a Republican.
Mayor Monique Ashton: We don’t agree on everything.
Mayor Travis Marion: That’s for sure.
But, we’re both supporting Wes Moore.
Mayor Monique Ashton: For Governor Moore it’s not about party, it’s about Maryland.
Mayor Travis Marion: When our town faced economic challenges, he was there for us every step of the way.
Mayor Monique Ashton: And, when federal workers were fired in my city, he was there for us too, day and night whenever we needed him.
Mayor Travis Marion: Wes Moore brings both sides together and lifts us up.
Mayor Monique Ashton: And, lord knows, we need more of that.

added: 6 rioters and investigated officers for civil rights violations; that expertise will help in Olympia Endorsed by The Stranger "It’s rare to see a serious political candidate actually pledge to challenge the tech industry in Washington’s corrupt, industry-captured political climate, and rarer still for a candidate to have the professional experience to turn such a pledge into policy.

There’s a bipartisan coalition of normal voters absolutely furious about data centers and AI, and while plenty of candidates have read the polling and promised to do something about it, the only one leading a class-action lawsuit against Apple for AI copyright infringement is Will Dreher. . . .
Dreher has showed a willingness to throw his career down the drain rather than compromise his ethics multiple times.
At the US Attorney’s Office, he gleefully volunteered to prosecute January 6 insurrectionists until Trump’s reelection sent every prosecutor involved running for the hills.

All of this means we trust him when he says he wants to rein in the tech industry. . . . [H]e’s well positioned among progressive challengers to take down an established moderate incumbent." Endorsed by Seattle City Attorney Erika Evans “I have known Will for years--he and I worked as a team to investigate and prosecute hate crimes and law enforcement officers who engage in misconduct.
removed: 6 rioters and investigated officers for civil rights violations; that expertise will help in Olympia Endorsed by The Stranger "[H]is career trajectory shows he puts his money where his mouth is. . . .
Candidates all the way down to county dogcatcher promise the SECB they’ll punish Trump’s goons, but Dreher has the rare distinction of having prosecuted 25 January 6th insurrectionists. . . .

These days he’s at a Seattle law firm suing Apple for AI copyright infringement, which is more than most other candidates who have read the polling on AI and data centers and are running on opposing tech can muster . . . .
He’s a fed, but we think he should be our fed.
Let’s unleash this blue-blooded Yankee on the billionaire tech lobby that writes our laws in Olympia.

Vote Dreher." Endorsed by Seattle City Attorney Erika Evans “I have known Will for years--he and I worked as a team to investigate and prosecute hate crimes and law enforcement officers who engage in misconduct.

added: Skip to main content Home About Jackie Events Gallery Volunteer News & Press Track AIPAT DONATE CONTACT All Press Print Jackie Auringer for Congress Kingston, New York • winwithjackie.com For Immediate Release October 14, 2026 Media Contact Jackie Auringer for Congress info@winwithjackie.com Auringer Challenges Kiryas Joel and Palm Tree Expansion Plans Pledges accountability in federal funding as check on unfettered growth Kingston, NY - October 14, 2026 - Jackie Auringer, Conservative and Republican candidate for Congress in New York’s 18th District, today voiced strong opposition to unchecked annexation and development involving Kiryas Joel and Town of Palm Tree, pledging to use congressional oversight and federal funding safeguards to protect surrounding communities.
“Today, families in Woodbury, Monroe, and across Orange County are being steamrolled by expansion of KJ and Palm Tree communities.
They deserve a meaningful say in decisions that affect their neighborhoods, infrastructure, and property taxes,” Auringer said.
“While too many elected officials have a tendency to look the other way - I will not.
Congress has a responsibility to examine how federal dollars are spent.

Federal funding should support responsible development, with full consideration of the costs imposed on neighboring communities.” Auringer outlined three priorities: Accountability for Federal Housing Funding: Auringer pledged to scrutinize the use of HUD housing assistance and Community Development Block Grants and pursue funding safeguards that promote responsible planning.
“Federal housing dollars should be spent transparently, with careful consideration of infrastructure capacity and the impact on surrounding taxpayers,” Auringer said.

Stronger Oversight of Federal Benefit Programs: Auringer called for rigorous, evidence-based oversight of Medicaid, SNAP, and other federally supported programs to identify fraud, waste, and abuse wherever they occur.
“These programs must serve eligible people and operate within the law.

Taxpayers deserve accountability, and families who depend on these benefits deserve programs they can trust.” Environmental and Infrastructure Review: Auringer pledged to press for thorough review of federally funded water and sewer projects, including applicable environmental requirements, before supporting funding for expansions serving annexed land.
“Before federal dollars support additional development, we need clear answers about water supplies, sewer capacity, environmental impacts, and who will pay.
Surrounding communities deserve to have those concerns addressed.” “Residents should not have to fight to get someone in government to listen,” Auringer said.
“I will work with local officials and state leaders, regardless of party, to protect our communities and demand responsible planning,” said Auringer.
“Every community should play by the same rules, and every federal dollar should come with accountability,” Auringer concluded.
“I will stand with the families who live here and make protecting their quality of life a priority in Congress.

Orange County deserves development that is fair, accountable, and sustainable.” ### About Jackie Auringer for Congress Jackie Auringer is running for Congress because the community she grew up in deserves a stronger voice in Washington, focused on restoring affordability, strengthening local economies, and fighting for the families and small businesses that make the Hudson Valley thrive.

added: Lora Listens, Leads, and Gets It Done Latest from the Campaign I just stepped off the forum stage, and I’m feeling more energized than ever!

Over the next few weeks, I’m looking forward to continuing the conversations I’ve been having with voters across the First Franklin District, listening to your concerns and sharing why I’m ready to lead.
This election is about more than understanding the challenges facing our communities.
It’s about having the experience, relationships, and determination to deliver real results.
I’m ready to get to work on day one, and I’m excited to keep making my case to the voters of the First Franklin District!
#TeamWondo is ready for tonight’s forum at GCTV!
removed: Lora Listens, Leads, and Gets It Done Latest from the Campaign What a great weekend enjoying fall festivities across Franklin County! 🍂🍎 We spent Sunday talking with voters in Shelburne Falls, where we were treated to a performance by the Morris dancers, before heading over to the Ashfield Fall Festival!
The dreary weather certainly didn’t dampen the spirits of festivalgoers!
I especially appreciated the opportunity to catch up with Ashfield Fire Chief Kyle Walker about much-needed improvements to the town’s fire station.
And of course, no Ashfield Fall Festival would be complete without some delicious cheddar cheese and apple pie!
Join FCCPR for a follow-up conversation about the nine ballot questions Massachusetts voters will decide on this November!
It's a space to come together to better understand the content and wording of each question, ask questions, and learn from one another.
This free, community-focused session is about understanding what’s on the ballot, not telling people how to vote.
LAVA, 324 Main Street, Greenfield October 16 at 6 PM Everyone is welcome!
Please share with your friends, family, and community networks, and join us for an evening of thoughtful conversation ahead of Election Day.

Meeting this moment will require a governor with the experience and vision to deliver results on day one.
During the hourlong debate on CNN, the campaign rolled out a new website documenting all of Steve Hilton’s precious moments with Donald Trump .

From gushing about receiving Trump’s endorsement to praising deadly ICE raids as carried out “to perfection” – voters will finally have a place to learn what Steve Hilton really thinks about Trump’s $1 trillion health care cuts, illegal war in Iran, tariffs, and more!

“Tonight’s debate made clear what’s at stake in this election and the kind of serious, experienced leadership California needs to move forward,” said Jonathan Underland, spokesperson for the Becerra Campaign .
“Donald Trump is attacking California, and he’s endorsed Steve Hilton to help him do it.

Becerra has proven that he will hold Trump’s feet to the fire, and win – that’s the kind of governor California deserves.” Becerra delivered a vision for the state – to make sure working families can afford to build their lives in California and reach for their dreams: owning a home, sending their kids to college, and getting the health care they need.

Steve Hilton made it clear that he is focused on bringing Donald Trump’s MAGA agenda to California in the form of ICE raids, attacks on voters’ rights, tax breaks for billionaires paid for by health care cuts, and a higher cost of living.
Becerra is focused on delivering results for families, protecting California’s values and building a stronger future for the state.
WHAT OTHERS ARE SAYING: David Goldberg, President, California Teachers Association “Tonight, Californians heard Xavier Becerra stand up for teachers, for students and for working families.

He made clear that the wealthy must pay their fair share so California has a steady, reliable revenue stream for our schools and communities, and he laid out his plan to bring down the cost of living so educators and families can afford to live in the communities where they teach and learn.
This November the choice is clear.

Our students and communities deserve a leader who will stand up for public education and stand with union educators, and that leader is Xavier Becerra.” Mayor Matt Mahan, San Jose “Tonight, Xavier Becerra showed Californians what thoughtful, measured leadership looks like.
He knows what’s at stake, he understands the challenges facing our state, and he has the experience to bring people together and get things done.

At a time when Washington is defined by chaos and division, California needs a governor who can lead with both conviction and common sense.” Arnulfo de La Cruz, President, SEIU California State Council & SEIU 2015 “At a time when so much is at stake — from the right to vote to the ability of working families to get ahead — we need leadership with a proven track record of getting things done.
Xavier Becerra has spent his career fighting for working people and defending our democracy, and he has the experience to deliver results for California families.

The choice is clear: when Donald Trump tries to cut health care or send ICE and Border Patrol into our communities, Xavier Becerra will stand up to him and for California values.” Speaker Robert Rivas, California State Assembly “Xavier Becerra has the experience to take on California’s toughest challenges.
Throughout his career, he has fought to expand access to health care, protect our democracy and stand up for California families.
He knows how to turn ideas into policy and policy into results.
That’s the leadership California needs from day one.” Sec.
Secretary of Energy “The fight to protect affordable care has never been more important.

Serving alongside Xavier Becerra in President Biden’s Cabinet, I saw firsthand how he helped expand coverage through the Affordable Care Act as Secretary of Health and Human Services, lowering prescription drug costs and making health care accessible and affordable for families across the country.

He knows what’s at stake and has a proven record of delivering results when it matters most.” Mayor Rex Richardson, City of Long Beach “Our health care is under attack, and California families need a governor who knows how to fight back and win.
Xavier Becerra has spent his career fighting to make sure every Californian can see a doctor and afford the care they need.
He helped write the Affordable Care Act, and when Donald Trump tried to tear it down, Xavier took him to court and won.

At a moment when access to health care is once again on the line, Xavier has the experience, the backbone, and the record to protect Californians.” Tony Hoang, Executive Director, Equality California “Xavier Becerra has spent his career standing up for California families.

As Attorney General, he took Trump to court more than 100 times to protect our health care, our rights and our immigrant neighbors, including the families who run our small businesses, care for our loved ones and strengthen our communities.
That record matters more than ever as transgender young people and their families face attacks on their health care, their rights, and their ability to feel safe and supported at school.

Steve Hilton has pledged to roll back protections for transgender students while praising Trump’s immigration crackdown as being carried out ‘to perfection.’ Tonight’s debate put those differences on full display.
Xavier will continue fighting to protect every California family.” ### Xavier Becerra has dedicated over 35 years of public service to California, serving in the State Assembly, U.S.
Congress, as California Attorney General, and as U.S.
Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Throughout his career, he has focused on delivering for Californians: from passing the Affordable Care Act and lowering costs to taking on the Trump Administration and winning lawsuits on behalf of Californians, to leading the world’s largest health agency.
Now, Becerra is running for Governor to help California build, protect our California way of life, and make sure California rises beyond the chaos in Washington.
Together, the lifelong Californians have raised their three adult daughters.

GOOD MORNING, HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY IN THE FIGHTIN’ FIFTH![image][image]Today, I’m thankful for the brave men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line every day to protect others.[image][image]Yesterday, at our beautiful People’s House in Boston, 18 police officers were honored with the 2026 Trooper George L. Hanna Memorial Awards for Extraordinary Bravery, the Commonwealth’s highest law enforcement honor.[image][image]These awards honor the memory of Massachusetts State Police Trooper George L. Hanna, who was killed in the line of duty in 1983. His family was there yesterday, as they are every year, to help keep his memory and legacy alive.[image][image]I also want to thank Governor Healey and her office, Public Safety Commissioner Kwan, and the Executive Office of Public Safety for recognizing these heroes and helping keep Trooper Hanna’s memory and legacy alive. These awards are an important reminder of the courage, sacrifice, and service of the men and women who protect us every day.[image][image]As a former police officer, the father of a police officer, and the father-in-law of a police officer, this is very personal to me. I know the sacrifices our law enforcement families make and the courage it takes to wear the badge.[image][image]Today, and every day, I’m thankful for the brave men, women, and canines in law enforcement here in Massachusetts and across our great nation.[image][image]CONGRATULATIONS to all 18 recipients. Thank you for your courage, your service, and for answering the call when others need you most![image][image]2026 TROOPER GEORGE L. HANNA MEMORIAL AWARD RECIPIENTS[image][image]MEDAL OF HONOR[image][image]• Officer Aurise Miedico, Burlington Police Department[image]• Officer José R. Valenzuela, Boston Police Department[image]• Officer Gerard Colpoys, Boston Police Department[image]• Officer Steven Negron, Holyoke Police Department[image][image]MEDAL OF VALOR[image][image]• Detective Daniel Wall, Jr., Everett Police Department[image][image]FALL RIVER POLICE DEPARTMENT[image][image]• Sgt. Shane Galus[image]• Sgt. Adam Talbot[image]• Officer Mohammed Adelakun[image]• Officer Collin Almeida[image]• Officer Brandon Andrade[image]• Officer Logan Arruda[image]• Officer Taylor Carreiro[image]• Officer Tre’Quan Gardner[image]• Officer Nicholas Kennedy[image]• Officer Jeffrey Louis[image]• Officer Jimmie J. Page[image]• Officer Christopher Silvia[image]• Officer Jacob Swenson[image][image]God bless and protect our first responders.[image]🇺🇸💙🐕🙏🏻🫡👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #CommonSenseLeadership #BackTheBlue [image]#CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli[image]Burlington Police Department[image]Boston Police Department (Official)[image]Holyoke Police Department[image]Everett MA Police[image]City of Fall River Police Department[image]Executive Office of Public Safety and Security

WHAT A DAY AT MMA![image]Marinakis Hall Dedication Day[image][image]I was so proud to be at our very own Massachusetts Maritime Academy today for the dedication of the beautiful new Marinakis Hall, a building where cadets will train, learn, and prepare to lead for generations to come.[image][image]I was honored to provide a few remarks about how special this school is, its incredible history, and the deep connection between Greece and America. I even had the opportunity to speak briefly about my son, Nicholas, and remind everyone that life is precious.[image][image]What a beautiful day celebrating an incredible $5 million donation from the Marinakis family, who traveled all the way from Greece with three van loads of family and friends to be here for this special occasion.[image][image]As a proud Greek American and state representative of the Great Fightin’ Fifth, this day meant so much to me. The Greek American tradition of service, sacrifice, fighting for what we believe in, and giving back is something I hold close to my heart. We must never forget the price of freedom and the sacrifices made by so many that allow us to gather, learn, and build a better future.[image][image]One of my special moments today was pinning Chairman Evangelos Marinakis with a pin featuring the Commonwealth of Massachusetts flag and the American flag, the same special pin we proudly wear in the People’s House. Now he will wear it on his journey back to Greece, a small token of our appreciation and a lasting connection between our Commonwealth and his family.[image][image]Thank you to the Marinakis family, Admiral Francis X. McDonald, and the entire Massachusetts Maritime Academy team for making this day possible.[image][image]We are so fortunate to have this world-renowned institution right here in our district and in the Commonwealth.[image][image]WAY TO GO, MMA! removed.text: CONGRATULATIONS, GUY![image]Thank you, Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists![image][image]This morning was extra special in the Fightin’ Fifth as I got to surprise my longtime friend, constituent, and fellow Big Nick’s Rider, Guy Cosgrove, a Midmark Veterinary Planning and Design Specialist, with a Massachusetts House of Representatives citation recognizing his 38 years of helping build and improve veterinary offices and hospitals all across America.[image][image]We met at the beautiful new addition to Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists in Buzzards Bay, right underneath the Bourne Bridge. This 24/7 animal hospital is doubling in size to care for even more sick and injured animals.[image][image]This is the hospital that saved K9 Nero and hosts the annual canine blood drive every April 12th in memory of fallen Yarmouth Police Department K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon and in honor of his dedicated partner, K9 Nero.[image][image]I’ll never forget what they’ve done for Nero and my own pets when they needed help. It was great to see this expansion firsthand and hear about what’s coming next.[image][image]Congratulations, Guy! And thank you to Dr. Louisa Rahilly and her entire dedicated team at Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists for everything you do for our four-legged family members.[image][image]Proud to see this great project happening right here in the Fightin’ Fifth![image][image]Lots more GOOD to come![image]🇺🇸😊🐕🐈👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ServiceBeforeSelf #ProudAmerican #CommonSenseLeadership #CCVS #Animals #K9Nero #Bourne #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli[image]Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists[image]Midmark Veterinary[image]Yarmouth Police Dept.[image]Nero Our K9 Hero[image]Bourne Police Department[image]Yarmouth Police Foundation

REMEMBERING MY FRIEND SEAN [image][image]Today, I attended the service for my friend Sean Andrew Whelahan at Nickerson-Bourne Funeral Home in Sandwich. It was a difficult day, but also a chance to celebrate a life that meant so much to so many people.[image][image]Sean was a devoted husband to Tara, a loving father to Kian and Rylee, a successful business owner of 6A Tours and Kian ’n Rylee’s, and a true friend. He had a great sense of humor and a special gift for bringing people together. Sean could walk into a room full of strangers and leave with a room full of friends. He was also a father figure and mentor to many.[image][image]What makes this loss especially difficult is that I last communicated with Sean just two weeks ago. He was planning to bring a van full of WW II veterans from Mashpee to Logan Airport at 4 a.m. so they could take a Hero Flight to Washington, D.C., to visit the World War II Memorial. He was also going to pick them up at 11 p.m. and bring them home. All of it as a volunteer, giving his time to honor those who served our country.[image][image]THAT WAS SEAN. Always thinking about others, always willing to help, and always showing up for those who needed him.[image][image]Sean cared deeply about our veterans and their families. I’m proud that the US Marine Corporal Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund was one of the organizations close to his heart.[image][image]My heart goes out to Tara, Kian, Rylee, and all of Sean’s family and friends. He touched so many lives, and he will be missed by all who knew him.[image][image]Rest in peace, my friend. Thank you for your friendship, your kindness, and everything you did for others.[image][image]God bless you, Sean. We’ll take it from here. 🇺🇸❤️😔🙏🏻🫡[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #CommonSenseLeadership #Sandwich #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli[image]6A Tours and Transport[image]Nickerson-Bourne Funeral Home

See More See Less Photo View on Facebook (opens in a new tab) · Share Share on Facebook (opens in a new tab) Share on Twitter (opens in a new tab) Share on LinkedIn (opens in a new tab) Share by Email (opens in a new tab) State Representative Steve Xiarhos October 15th GOOD MORNING, HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY IN THE FIGHTIN’ FIFTH!
Today, I’m thankful for the brave men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line every day to protect others.
Yesterday, at our beautiful People’s House in Boston, 18 police officers were honored with the 2026 Trooper George L.
Hanna Memorial Awards for Extraordinary Bravery, the Commonwealth’s highest law enforcement honor.
These awards honor the memory of Massachusetts State Police Trooper George L.
Hanna, who was killed in the line of duty in 1983.
His family was there yesterday, as they are every year, to help keep his memory and legacy alive.

I also want to thank Governor Healey and her office, Public Safety Commissioner Kwan, and the Executive Office of Public Safety for recognizing these heroes and helping keep Trooper Hanna’s memory and legacy alive.
These awards are an important reminder of the courage, sacrifice, and service of the men and women who protect us every day.
As a former police officer, the father of a police officer, and the father-in-law of a police officer, this is very personal to me.
I know the sacrifices our law enforcement families make and the courage it takes to wear the badge.
Today, and every day, I’m thankful for the brave men, women, and canines in law enforcement here in Massachusetts and across our great nation.
Thank you for your courage, your service, and for answering the call when others need you most!

Marinakis Hall Dedication Day I was so proud to be at our very own Massachusetts Maritime Academy today for the dedication of the beautiful new Marinakis Hall, a building where cadets will train, learn, and prepare to lead for generations to come.
I was honored to provide a few remarks about how special this school is, its incredible history, and the deep connection between Greece and America.
I even had the opportunity to speak briefly about my son, Nicholas, and remind everyone that life is precious.

What a beautiful day celebrating an incredible $5 million donation from the Marinakis family, who traveled all the way from Greece with three van loads of family and friends to be here for this special occasion.
As a proud Greek American and state representative of the Great Fightin’ Fifth, this day meant so much to me.
The Greek American tradition of service, sacrifice, fighting for what we believe in, and giving back is something I hold close to my heart.
We must never forget the price of freedom and the sacrifices made by so many that allow us to gather, learn, and build a better future.

One of my special moments today was pinning Chairman Evangelos Marinakis with a pin featuring the Commonwealth of Massachusetts flag and the American flag, the same special pin we proudly wear in the People’s House.
Now he will wear it on his journey back to Greece, a small token of our appreciation and a lasting connection between our Commonwealth and his family.
Thank you to the Marinakis family, Admiral Francis X.
McDonald, and the entire Massachusetts Maritime Academy team for making this day possible.
We are so fortunate to have this world-renowned institution right here in our district and in the Commonwealth.

See More See Less Photo View on Facebook (opens in a new tab) · Share Share on Facebook (opens in a new tab) Share on Twitter (opens in a new tab) Share on LinkedIn (opens in a new tab) Share by Email (opens in a new tab) State Representative Steve Xiarhos October 13th REMEMBERING MY FRIEND SEAN Today, I attended the service for my friend Sean Andrew Whelahan at Nickerson-Bourne Funeral Home in Sandwich.
It was a difficult day, but also a chance to celebrate a life that meant so much to so many people.
Sean was a devoted husband to Tara, a loving father to Kian and Rylee, a successful business owner of 6A Tours and Kian ’n Rylee’s, and a true friend.
He had a great sense of humor and a special gift for bringing people together.
Sean could walk into a room full of strangers and leave with a room full of friends.
He was also a father figure and mentor to many.
What makes this loss especially difficult is that I last communicated with Sean just two weeks ago.
He was planning to bring a van full of WW II veterans from Mashpee to Logan Airport at 4 a.m. so they could take a Hero Flight to Washington, D.C., to visit the World War II Memorial.
He was also going to pick them up at 11 p.m. and bring them home.
All of it as a volunteer, giving his time to honor those who served our country.
THAT WAS SEAN.
Always thinking about others, always willing to help, and always showing up for those who needed him.
Sean cared deeply about our veterans and their families.
I’m proud that the US Marine Corporal Nicholas G.
Xiarhos Memorial Fund was one of the organizations close to his heart.
My heart goes out to Tara, Kian, Rylee, and all of Sean’s family and friends.
He touched so many lives, and he will be missed by all who knew him.
Rest in peace, my friend.
Thank you for your friendship, your kindness, and everything you did for others.
God bless you, Sean.

Thank you, Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists!

This morning was extra special in the Fightin’ Fifth as I got to surprise my longtime friend, constituent, and fellow Big Nick’s Rider, Guy Cosgrove, a Midmark Veterinary Planning and Design Specialist, with a Massachusetts House of Representatives citation recognizing his 38 years of helping build and improve veterinary offices and hospitals all across America.
We met at the beautiful new addition to Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists in Buzzards Bay, right underneath the Bourne Bridge.
This 24/7 animal hospital is doubling in size to care for even more sick and injured animals.
This is the hospital that saved K9 Nero and hosts the annual canine blood drive every April 12th in memory of fallen Yarmouth Police Department K9 Sergeant Sean M.
Gannon and in honor of his dedicated partner, K9 Nero.
I’ll never forget what they’ve done for Nero and my own pets when they needed help.
It was great to see this expansion firsthand and hear about what’s coming next.
Congratulations, Guy!
And thank you to Dr.
Louisa Rahilly and her entire dedicated team at Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists for everything you do for our four-legged family members.
Proud to see this great project happening right here in the Fightin’ Fifth!

GOOD MORNING, HAPPY THANKFUL THURSDAY IN THE FIGHTIN’ FIFTH![image][image]Today, I’m thankful for the brave men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line every day to protect others.[image][image]Yesterday, at our beautiful People’s House in Boston, 18 police officers were honored with the 2026 Trooper George L. Hanna Memorial Awards for Extraordinary Bravery, the Commonwealth’s highest law enforcement honor.[image][image]These awards honor the memory of Massachusetts State Police Trooper George L. Hanna, who was killed in the line of duty in 1983. His family was there yesterday, as they are every year, to help keep his memory and legacy alive.[image][image]I also want to thank Governor Healey and her office, Public Safety Commissioner Kwan, and the Executive Office of Public Safety for recognizing these heroes and helping keep Trooper Hanna’s memory and legacy alive. These awards are an important reminder of the courage, sacrifice, and service of the men and women who protect us every day.[image][image]As a former police officer, the father of a police officer, and the father-in-law of a police officer, this is very personal to me. I know the sacrifices our law enforcement families make and the courage it takes to wear the badge.[image][image]Today, and every day, I’m thankful for the brave men, women, and canines in law enforcement here in Massachusetts and across our great nation.[image][image]CONGRATULATIONS to all 18 recipients. WHAT A DAY AT MMA![image]Marinakis Hall Dedication Day[image][image]I was so proud to be at our very own Massachusetts Maritime Academy today for the dedication of the beautiful new Marinakis Hall, a building where cadets will train, learn, and prepare to lead for generations to come.[image][image]I was honored to provide a few remarks about how special this school is, its incredible history, and the deep connection between Greece and America. I even had the opportunity to speak briefly about my son, Nicholas, and remind everyone that life is precious.[image][image]What a beautiful day celebrating an incredible $5 million donation from the Marinakis family, who traveled all the way from Greece with three van loads of family and friends to be here for this special occasion.[image][image]As a proud Greek American and state representative of the Great Fightin’ Fifth, this day meant so much to me. The Greek American tradition of service, sacrifice, fighting for what we believe in, and giving back is something I hold close to my heart. We must never forget the price of freedom and the sacrifices made by so many that allow us to gather, learn, and build a better future.[image][image]One of my special moments today was pinning Chairman Evangelos Marinakis with a pin featuring the Commonwealth of Massachusetts flag and the American flag, the same special pin we proudly wear in the People’s House. Now he will wear it on his journey back to Greece, a small token of our appreciation and a lasting connection between our Commonwealth and his family.[image][image]Thank you to the Marinakis family, Admiral Francis X. McDonald, and the entire Massachusetts Maritime Academy team for making this day possible.[image][image]We are so fortunate to have this world-renowned institution right here in our district and in the Commonwealth.[image][image]WAY TO GO, MMA! removed.text: CONGRATULATIONS, GUY![image]Thank you, Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists![image][image]This morning was extra special in the Fightin’ Fifth as I got to surprise my longtime friend, constituent, and fellow Big Nick’s Rider, Guy Cosgrove, a Midmark Veterinary Planning and Design Specialist, with a Massachusetts House of Representatives citation recognizing his 38 years of helping build and improve veterinary offices and hospitals all across America.[image][image]We met at the beautiful new addition to Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists in Buzzards Bay, right underneath the Bourne Bridge. This 24/7 animal hospital is doubling in size to care for even more sick and injured animals.[image][image]This is the hospital that saved K9 Nero and hosts the annual canine blood drive every April 12th in memory of fallen Yarmouth Police Department K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon and in honor of his dedicated partner, K9 Nero.[image][image]I’ll never forget what they’ve done for Nero and my own pets when they needed help. It was great to see this expansion firsthand and hear about what’s coming next.[image][image]Congratulations, Guy! And thank you to Dr. Louisa Rahilly and her entire dedicated team at Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists for everything you do for our four-legged family members.[image][image]Proud to see this great project happening right here in the Fightin’ Fifth![image][image]Lots more GOOD to come![image]🇺🇸😊🐕🐈👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ServiceBeforeSelf #ProudAmerican #CommonSenseLeadership #CCVS #Animals #K9Nero #Bourne #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli[image]Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists[image]Midmark Veterinary[image]Yarmouth Police Dept.[image]Nero Our K9 Hero[image]Bourne Police Department[image]Yarmouth Police Foundation

LOOK WHO’S GROWING BIGGER AND MORE HANDSOME EVERY DAY! [image][image]Zohaib Malik-Mohammed, who we affectionately nicknamed Little Z, and his family spent Columbus Day weekend up in New Hampshire enjoying the beautiful White Mountains. What a great way to end the weekend with this picture of our little buddy! Tomorrow, he’s back to school at Oak Ridge School, where this nine-year-old fourth grader continues to grow and thrive.[image][image]It’s truly amazing when you think about how far this young man has come. Four years ago, Little Z was rescued from drowning at Snake Pond thanks to the incredible citizens and first responders who stepped up, along with the doctors and nurses who helped save his life. We welcomed him home after 12 weeks in Boston-area hospitals with our Big Nick’s Ride motorcycles, police cruisers, and fire trucks, and we’ve been cheering him on ever since.[image][image]His family has stayed strong, his teachers are angels, and Little Z is an angel among us right here in the Fightin’ Fifth District. He’s strong, kind, handsome, and an inspiration to all of us.[image][image]THANK YOU to every single person who played a part in saving this young man’s life and helping him continue to grow, thrive, and enjoy being a kid.[image][image]We love you, Little Z! Keep smiling, keep growing, and keep being YOU! REMEMBERING MY FRIEND SEAN [image][image]Today, I attended the service for my friend Sean Andrew Whelahan at Nickerson-Bourne Funeral Home in Sandwich. It was a difficult day, but also a chance to celebrate a life that meant so much to so many people.[image][image]Sean was a devoted husband to Tara, a loving father to Kian and Rylee, a successful business owner of 6A Tours and Kian ’n Rylee’s, and a true friend. He had a great sense of humor and a special gift for bringing people together. Sean could walk into a room full of strangers and leave with a room full of friends. He was also a father figure and mentor to many.[image][image]What makes this loss especially difficult is that I last communicated with Sean just two weeks ago. He was planning to bring a van full of WW II veterans from Mashpee to Logan Airport at 4 a.m. so they could take a Hero Flight to Washington, D.C., to visit the World War II Memorial. He was also going to pick them up at 11 p.m. and bring them home. All of it as a volunteer, giving his time to honor those who served our country.[image][image]THAT WAS SEAN. Always thinking about others, always willing to help, and always showing up for those who needed him.[image][image]Sean cared deeply about our veterans and their families. I’m proud that the US Marine Corporal Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund was one of the organizations close to his heart.[image][image]My heart goes out to Tara, Kian, Rylee, and all of Sean’s family and friends. He touched so many lives, and he will be missed by all who knew him.[image][image]Rest in peace, my friend. Thank you for your friendship, your kindness, and everything you did for others.[image][image]God bless you, Sean. We’ll take it from here. 🇺🇸❤️😔🙏🏻🫡[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #CommonSenseLeadership #Sandwich #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli[image]6A Tours and Transport[image]Nickerson-Bourne Funeral Home

Today, I’m thankful for the brave men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line every day to protect others.
Yesterday, at our beautiful People’s House in Boston, 18 police officers were honored with the 2026 Trooper George L.
Hanna Memorial Awards for Extraordinary Bravery, the Commonwealth’s highest law enforcement honor.
These awards honor the memory of Massachusetts State Police Trooper George L.
Hanna, who was killed in the line of duty in 1983.
His family was there yesterday, as they are every year, to help keep his memory and legacy alive.

I also want to thank Governor Healey and her office, Public Safety Commissioner Kwan, and the Executive Office of Public Safety for recognizing these heroes and helping keep Trooper Hanna’s memory and legacy alive.
These awards are an important reminder of the courage, sacrifice, and service of the men and women who protect us every day.
As a former police officer, the father of a police officer, and the father-in-law of a police officer, this is very personal to me.
I know the sacrifices our law enforcement families make and the courage it takes to wear the badge.
Today, and every day, I’m thankful for the brave men, women, and canines in law enforcement here in Massachusetts and across our great nation.
Thank you for your courage, your service, and for answering the call when others need you most!

Marinakis Hall Dedication Day I was so proud to be at our very own Massachusetts Maritime Academy today for the dedication of the beautiful new Marinakis Hall, a building where cadets will train, learn, and prepare to lead for generations to come.
I was honored to provide a few remarks about how special this school is, its incredible history, and the deep connection between Greece and America.
I even had the opportunity to speak briefly about my son, Nicholas, and remind everyone that life is precious.

What a beautiful day celebrating an incredible $5 million donation from the Marinakis family, who traveled all the way from Greece with three van loads of family and friends to be here for this special occasion.
As a proud Greek American and state representative of the Great Fightin’ Fifth, this day meant so much to me.
The Greek American tradition of service, sacrifice, fighting for what we believe in, and giving back is something I hold close to my heart.
We must never forget the price of freedom and the sacrifices made by so many that allow us to gather, learn, and build a better future.

One of my special moments today was pinning Chairman Evangelos Marinakis with a pin featuring the Commonwealth of Massachusetts flag and the American flag, the same special pin we proudly wear in the People’s House.
Now he will wear it on his journey back to Greece, a small token of our appreciation and a lasting connection between our Commonwealth and his family.
Thank you to the Marinakis family, Admiral Francis X.
McDonald, and the entire Massachusetts Maritime Academy team for making this day possible.
We are so fortunate to have this world-renowned institution right here in our district and in the Commonwealth.

It was a difficult day, but also a chance to celebrate a life that meant so much to so many people.
Sean was a devoted husband to Tara, a loving father to Kian and Rylee, a successful business owner of 6A Tours and Kian ’n Rylee’s, and a true friend.
He had a great sense of humor and a special gift for bringing people together.
Sean could walk into a room full of strangers and leave with a room full of friends.
He was also a father figure and mentor to many.
What makes this loss especially difficult is that I last communicated with Sean just two weeks ago.
He was planning to bring a van full of WW II veterans from Mashpee to Logan Airport at 4 a.m. so they could take a Hero Flight to Washington, D.C., to visit the World War II Memorial.
He was also going to pick them up at 11 p.m. and bring them home.
All of it as a volunteer, giving his time to honor those who served our country.
THAT WAS SEAN.
Always thinking about others, always willing to help, and always showing up for those who needed him.
Sean cared deeply about our veterans and their families.
I’m proud that the US Marine Corporal Nicholas G.
Xiarhos Memorial Fund was one of the organizations close to his heart.
My heart goes out to Tara, Kian, Rylee, and all of Sean’s family and friends.
He touched so many lives, and he will be missed by all who knew him.
Rest in peace, my friend.
Thank you for your friendship, your kindness, and everything you did for others.
God bless you, Sean.

Thank you, Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists!

This morning was extra special in the Fightin’ Fifth as I got to surprise my longtime friend, constituent, and fellow Big Nick’s Rider, Guy Cosgrove, a Midmark Veterinary Planning and Design Specialist, with a Massachusetts House of Representatives citation recognizing his 38 years of helping build and improve veterinary offices and hospitals all across America.
We met at the beautiful new addition to Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists in Buzzards Bay, right underneath the Bourne Bridge.
This 24/7 animal hospital is doubling in size to care for even more sick and injured animals.
This is the hospital that saved K9 Nero and hosts the annual canine blood drive every April 12th in memory of fallen Yarmouth Police Department K9 Sergeant Sean M.
Gannon and in honor of his dedicated partner, K9 Nero.
I’ll never forget what they’ve done for Nero and my own pets when they needed help.
It was great to see this expansion firsthand and hear about what’s coming next.
Congratulations, Guy!
And thank you to Dr.
Louisa Rahilly and her entire dedicated team at Cape Cod Veterinary Specialists for everything you do for our four-legged family members.
Proud to see this great project happening right here in the Fightin’ Fifth!

Zohaib Malik-Mohammed, who we affectionately nicknamed Little Z, and his family spent Columbus Day weekend up in New Hampshire enjoying the beautiful White Mountains.
What a great way to end the weekend with this picture of our little buddy!
Tomorrow, he’s back to school at Oak Ridge School, where this nine-year-old fourth grader continues to grow and thrive.
It’s truly amazing when you think about how far this young man has come.
Four years ago, Little Z was rescued from drowning at Snake Pond thanks to the incredible citizens and first responders who stepped up, along with the doctors and nurses who helped save his life.
We welcomed him home after 12 weeks in Boston-area hospitals with our Big Nick’s Ride motorcycles, police cruisers, and fire trucks, and we’ve been cheering him on ever since.
His family has stayed strong, his teachers are angels, and Little Z is an angel among us right here in the Fightin’ Fifth District.
He’s strong, kind, handsome, and an inspiration to all of us.
THANK YOU to every single person who played a part in saving this young man’s life and helping him continue to grow, thrive, and enjoy being a kid.
We love you, Little Z!

Iowa should be the state where kids grow up and want to stay, because a young couple can buy a home, a young farmer can buy ground, the water is safe to drink, the schools are the best in the country, and family is close by.
Help Zach Win Iowa for You .
Every policy decision should start with one question: What will this change do to our community?
That question has been missing from politics for too long, and it’s the foundation of Zach’s Iowa First approach: think long-term, protect what makes Iowa strong, and put our communities first.
Iowa First Values We need to be able to draw the line.
Keep politics out of our schools and stop letting partisan nonsense redefine the values our communities were built on.
Make Iowa Healthy Again Too many Iowa families have a cancer story.
Zach’s published plan calls for independent safety testing of agricultural products, more Iowa-focused cancer research, and additional action on improving our water quality.
Keep Iowa Land in Iowa Hands Who owns Iowa soil twenty years from now matters.
A quarter of our land is owned by people who don’t live in Iowa – investors who treat Iowa like an annuity.

Zach will require human-level disclosure of who owns our land, tighten and enforce the laws to stop hedge funds and foreign adversaries from buying up our farms and homes, and give young Iowans a fair shot at owning a home and building a farm.
Make Education #1 Again Parents should have access to excellent schools.

Zach’s education plans include giving teachers more room to innovate, reducing reliance on standardized testing, strengthening public schools, and directing Iowa universities toward Iowa students and Iowa problems.
Keep Iowa’s Kids in Iowa Our kids should not feel like they have to leave Iowa to find opportunity.
Like many Iowa kids, Zach left, then came home.
His goal is to make sure the next generation never has to leave to find opportunity.
That means homes young families can afford, farms young Iowans can start, schools that are number one again, and an Iowa that puts Iowans first.
Count On Clean Water Clean water should be something every Iowan can count on.
Zach’s plan invests in water monitoring, targeted conservation, and proven solutions like wetlands, saturated buffers, and cover crops—while working with farmers, not against them.
Improve Affordability A great Iowa life should still be attainable.
Zach’s platform includes lowering the property tax burden on Iowans, expanding paths to homeownership, and banning hedge funds from buying single-family Iowa homes.
Expand Food Freedom Make Iowa the country’s real food capital.
Zach wants to make it easier for Iowa farmers and producers to sell directly to Iowa families and create innovation incentives for farmers who diversify into food production.

See the Food Freedom Plan Protect Iowa Culture Iowa culture should be built upon common sense principles Zach’s plan focuses on safe communities, parental rights, protecting life, supporting law enforcement, and keeping explicit material out of K–12 classrooms.
Where Does Zach Stand on Culture?
Iowa should work for the people who call Iowa home.
Zach Lahn is a husband and father, businessman, farmer, and sixth-generation Iowan.
Learn More About Zach See His Plan for Iowa You Shouldn’t Have to Wonder If Your Family Is Next.
Cancer has touched too many Iowa families.
Iowa has the fastest-growing rate of new cancers in America.
And for too long, special interests have got our leaders to look the other way.
As governor, Zach will launch independent Iowa research into agricultural products and consumer products, with no corporate influence, and publish the results publicly.
He’ll work alongside farmers to mitigate run off and clean up our drinking water, and put prevention first.
Iowans deserve answers, and Zach is committed to getting them.
Iowa should be looking for answers.
SEE ZACH'S PLAN Iowa Values vs.
Certain people want you to forget where they stand on the controversial issues of our day.
Iowa needs a leader grounded in the values that have shaped this state for generations: Faith.
Leaving something better for the next generation.
Iowa did not become Iowa by accident.
Generations before us built a culture around Midwest values that they passed down to us.
Zach’s message is that our generation has a duty too: know what we inherited, defend our way of life, and hand Iowa to the next generation stronger than we found it.
See Where Zach Stands Build an Iowa Worth Staying For.
Every year, Iowa loses thousands, as kids graduate, pack up, and build their lives somewhere else.
That’s empty seats at Friday night football games, closed shops on Main Street, and farms with no one to take them over.
Zach is running to reverse this trend.
Still Figuring Out What You Think?
You should know more about a candidate than just the letter next to his name.
BROWSE THE ISSUES MEET ZACH A Sixth-Generation Iowan Zach’s family roots in Iowa run deep.
In 1862, his great-great-great-grandfather, Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s call and rode with Iowa’s Second Cavalry in the Civil War.
Father of Seven Zach and Annie have seven kids.
He’s fighting so they, their kids, and every Iowa kid have a reason to build their life right here at home.
Farmer Zach farms the family homestead today, using regenerative practices to protect soil health and water quality.
As governor, he’ll fight to save family farms, get young Iowans back on the land, and keep Iowa land in Iowa hands.
Businessman Zach is a business owner and believes Iowa should invest in the businesses, workers, and communities that are invested here.
Investing Locally Zach and his family have worked to restore pieces of Belle Plaine’s history such as the King Theater, pictured above.
The Iowa We Love Will Not Preserve Itself.

Iowa First.
It’s about taking responsibility for what’s ours.
Our fields, our families, our future.
It’s a promise to invest in the land that feeds us and the people who make Iowa strong.
Donate Contact us Zach Lahn was endorsed by MAHA Action.
The first candidate in history to be endorsed by the org.
Watch Zach talk on MAHA Farmer Husband and Father Businessman 6th Generation Iowan About Zach Lahn Zach Lahn for Governor of Iowa I am a father, a farmer, and a businessman.
I’m investing in Iowa and I’m my own biggest donor.
I don’t answer to donors or corporations — only to God, my family, and the people of this state.
I believe Iowa can be a beacon — the safest, freest, most family-centered state in America.
That future won’t come from consultants or career politicians.
It will come from courage rooted in place, history, and duty.
Over the next months, I will be on the road, listening in church basements, VFW halls, farms, and school gyms — where Iowa’s wisdom lives.
This is Iowa.
This is our home.
And it’s worth fighting for.
Learn more about Zach I will Make Iowa Healthy Again.
Clean food.
Clean water.
Honest medicine.
I will work to defeat the cancer crisis plaguing state.
I will fight to keep Iowa land in Iowa hands.
Over 25% of Iowa land is owned by out of state investors and foreign governments.
I will fight for our birthright to own the ground under our feet.
I will Free Iowa's Farmers.
We have the best farmland in the world, but the system is rigged so the farmer always comes in last.
It’s time for a change.
I will Always Put Iowans First I promise to serve you and the people of Iowa.
Not global elites.

A Legacy of Almost 200 Years 6 Generations of Serving Iowa - Zach's Story Zach’s mission remains rooted in a deep love for his home state - its rich traditions, strong communities, rural values, and connection to the land.

1862 Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s Call Zach’s Iowa roots trace back to 1862, when his great-great-great-grandfather, Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s call by volunteering for Iowa’s Second Cavalry — one of the storied “Hawkeyes on Horseback” during the Civil War.
1880's The Boy Who Crosses an Ocean - Alone.
Twenty years later, Friedrich Lahn, left Hamburg, Germany at age 14, traveling alone in the stowage of the S.S.
Weiland.
He arrived in New York and made his way to Belle Plaine, Iowa, where he would marry Ordinancy Schluntz.
Together, they built the Iowa homestead that remained in the Lahn family for 105 years.
1917 The War to End All Wars The Lahn's legacy of stewardship and service to Iowa continued with Zach’s great-grandfather, Alfred Lahn, who serving as an elected official in Benton County.
Alfred’s older brother, John, served overseas during World War I with Iowa’s 337th Heavy Field Artillery before returning to Belle Plaine to run the local newspaper.
1940's An Affinity for the Sky Alfred and Evelyn’s sons Victor and Roger were inspired by aviation and purchased a $700 Taylorcraft and learned to fly off a runway mowed in the family’s bean field.
That experience sparked lifelong careers in aviation, including service in the U.S.
Navy flying off aircraft carriers in the Pacific.

1990's Tradition of Serving Iowans Continues Zach’s father, Jim, carried the family traditions forward, studying agronomy and working as a conservationist while also answering the call to pastoral ministry.
Zach and his siblings were raised in rural Plymouth County, Iowa and from a young age had a deep love and respect instilled in them for the beauty of God’s creation.
2005 Closing a 105-year chapter in the Lahn family’s history.
In 2005, one year after Zach graduated from Sioux City East High School, his great-grandmother Evelyn passed away.
With her passing, the family’s 105-year farming legacy came to an end when the farm was sold.
2014 Zach Lahn the Entrepreneur, Educator, and Farmer In 2016, he launched Homeplace Ventures.
Alongside his business work, Zach launched an innovative non-profit school.
Nearly a decade after the original homestead was sold, Zach was able to buy back his family property.
2020's Rebuilding a Community - Now His State.
In his hometown, he and his family are working to restore their community — including the recent purchase of the historic King Theater and the Chicago Northwestern Train Depot.
Zach’s mission remains rooted in a deep love for his home state — its rich traditions, strong communities, rural values, and connection to the land.
