added: Skip to main content Hit enter to search or ESC to close Search Close Search Menu About Issues All Issues Cancer Clean Water Affordability Farming Education Keeping Iowa’s Youth Events Debates Merch Donate Find My Polling Location Help Zach Win Iowa Is Home Zach Lahn is a sixth-generation Iowan, husband, father of seven, farmer, businessman, pilot, and Republican candidate for Governor of Iowa.
But before any of those titles, Zach sees himself as a Christian and a steward of what has been handed down to him.
For his family, Iowa is not just where they live.
Zach’s Iowa roots reach back to 1862, when his great-great-great-grandfather Hans Schluntz answered Governor Samuel Kirkwood’s call and joined the Second Iowa Cavalry during the Civil War.
Another branch of the family arrived in Iowa after Friedrich Lahn crossed the Atlantic from Germany as a teenager and eventually settled near Belle Plaine.
The family established a farm that remained in Lahn hands for more than a century.
That farm would eventually shape Zach’s life in ways he did not fully understand when he was young.
The broader idea behind the policy is that Iowa families should have a better opportunity to own homes, build wealth, and put down roots here.
Raised to Take Responsibility Zach grew up in western Iowa in a family where faith, conservation, service, and the land were closely connected.
His father, Jim, studied agronomy, worked for decades in conservation and agriculture, and now serves in pastoral ministry.
Zach has spoken about growing up alongside his dad in Iowa fields, learning about insects, crops, soil, and the responsibility that comes with caring for land.
Those early lessons stayed with him.
They helped form a conviction that still shapes Zach’s politics today: ownership creates responsibility.
When people own their homes, their farms, their businesses, and the future they are building, communities become stronger.
And when control moves farther away from the people who actually live there, something important is lost.
That belief is at the heart of Zach’s Iowa First approach.
Buying Back the Family Farm In 2005, Zach’s great-grandmother Evelyn passed away, and the family farm, which had remained in the family for 105 years, was sold.
Zach had just graduated from high school, unable to do anything about it.
Nearly a decade later, Zach bought the family property back.
Over the following years, he worked to reassemble the farm parcel by parcel and restore the homestead his family had once lost.
Today, Zach and his family live on that land near Belle Plaine.
Zach and his wife, Annie, are raising seven children together in a blended family rooted in faith and love.
For Zach, fatherhood means showing up, keeping commitments, and making family a priority.
Rooted in Faith Zach was raised in a Christian home by a father who combined pastoral ministry with work in agriculture and conservation.
He continues to speak openly about his Christian faith and has described it as foundational to the culture he wants to preserve and build upon here in Iowa.
That conviction informs Zach’s pro-life position, which is one of the clearest differences between him and his opponents in this election.
Zach believes life is a gift from God and should be protected before birth.
He has committed to standing against any and every attack on Iowa’s Heartbeat Bill, and vocally opposing the radical policies enacted in other states that permit abortion all the way until birth.
With life as the foundation, Zach also believes our faith propels us to protect life after birth.
We must actively pursue, loving our neighbors by creating a culture that prioritizes: Healthy children.
When Cancer Became Personal Zach grew up in Sioux City, riding through fields with his father, who worked around Iowa agriculture for decades, studying crops, weeds, pests, and insects.
Years later, his father developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Zach has repeatedly said that cancer is not a partisan issue.
Iowa has one of the nation’s highest cancer burdens and has experienced an unusually high rate of new cancer diagnoses.
Zach has made addressing that problem one of the central issues of his campaign.

His proposed approach includes independent state safety testing, directing more Iowa-based research toward the state’s cancer problem, incentivizing proven conservation practices to mitigate agricultural runoff, challenging agricultural monopolies, and demanding greater accountability when products may pose risks to Iowans.
For Zach, “Make Iowa Healthy Again” encompasses what we all want for ourselves, our children, and our neighbors.
It means asking harder questions about the water Iowans drink, the food they eat, the chemicals used around them, the incentives shaping agriculture, and the long-term health of Iowa children.
Iowa First Zach knows firsthand that what is worth keeping does not preserve itself.
His family lost the farm that had been theirs for more than a century.
Years later, he bought it back and began rebuilding what had been lost.
That experience shaped the way he thinks about Iowa today: protect what is worth protecting, strengthen it, and leave something better for the next generation.
That is what Iowa First means to Zach.
It means putting Iowa families first.
Iowa workers, businesses, communities, and children first.
It means building on the culture and character generations of Iowans worked to create, while standing against policies that would move our state away from the values that made it strong.
Iowa First means preserving what we love, strengthening what we have, and making sure Iowa still belongs to Iowans for generations to come.
The Iowa We Love Will Not Preserve Itself.

Zach Lahn is not a politician but another Iowan like you.
He is a father, farmer, and a businessman.
He is 6th generation Iowan, his own biggest donor, and does not answer to large corporations or special interest — only to God, his family, and the people of Iowa.

Pledge Your Support Volunteer For Zach A Legacy of Almost 200 Years 6 Generations of Serving Iowa - Zach's Story Zach’s mission remains rooted in a deep love for his home state - its rich traditions, strong communities, rural values, and connection to the land.

1862 Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s Call Zach’s Iowa roots trace back to 1862, when his great-great-great-grandfather, Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s call by volunteering for Iowa’s Second Cavalry — one of the storied “Hawkeyes on Horseback” during the Civil War.
1880's The Boy Who Crosses an Ocean - Alone.
Twenty years later, Friedrich Lahn, left Hamburg, Germany at age 14, traveling alone in the stowage of the S.S.
Weiland.
He arrived in New York and made his way to Belle Plaine, Iowa, where he would marry Ordinancy Schluntz.
Together, they built the Iowa homestead that remained in the Lahn family for 105 years.
1917 The War to End All Wars The Lahn's legacy of stewardship and service to Iowa continued with Zach’s great-grandfather, Alfred Lahn, who serving as an elected official in Benton County.
Alfred’s older brother, John, served overseas during World War I with Iowa’s 337th Heavy Field Artillery before returning to Belle Plaine to run the local newspaper.
1940's An Affinity for the Sky Alfred and Evelyn’s sons Victor and Roger were inspired by aviation and purchased a $700 Taylorcraft and learned to fly off a runway mowed in the family’s bean field.
That experience sparked lifelong careers in aviation, including service in the U.S.
Navy flying off aircraft carriers in the Pacific.

1990's Tradition of Serving Iowans Continues Zach’s father, Jim, carried the family traditions forward, studying agronomy and working as a conservationist while also answering the call to pastoral ministry.
Zach and his siblings were raised in rural Plymouth County, Iowa and from a young age had a deep love and respect instilled in them for the beauty of God’s creation.
2005 Closing a 105-year chapter in the Lahn family’s history.
In 2005, one year after Zach graduated from Sioux City East High School, his great-grandmother Evelyn passed away.
With her passing, the family’s 105-year farming legacy came to an end when the farm was sold.
2014 Zach Lahn the Entrepreneur, Educator, and Farmer In 2016, he launched Homeplace Ventures.
Alongside his business work, Zach launched an innovative non-profit school.
Nearly a decade after the original homestead was sold, Zach was able to buy back his family property.
2020's Rebuilding a Community - Now His State.
In his hometown, he and his family are working to restore their community — including the recent purchase of the historic King Theater and the Chicago Northwestern Train Depot.
Zach’s mission remains rooted in a deep love for his home state — its rich traditions, strong communities, rural values, and connection to the land.
Iowa Needs a Future The System is Corrupt.
Nobody else is talking about it.
As Iowans, we are facing multiple issues that will decide the fate of our State.
There has not been an election this important in decades.
Our education system is faltering, our people being poisoned for profit, and our young people are leaving whilst never coming back.
And nobody else is talking about it.
4th Highest in out migration.
Our kids are leaving and not coming back.
We are almost last in the nation for out migration of our kids.
Iowa now has to provide the same level of services to less people. –50% We are bottom half of rankings in education.
We have fallen from #1 in education to now worse than Mississippi.
A 50% drop in the rankings in just over a decade.
#1 Iowa has the fastest rate of new Cancer.
If you live in the top 10 counties in Iowa for cancer, you have about a 1 and 2 chance of getting cancer.
Nothing else matters if our people are dying.
Fight for Iowa "Our people are being pushed aside by greed, corruption, and a rigged system.

I will fight with everything I have for our future." Dear Fellow Iowan, I am asking you for your trust, and if I’m to do that you should know exactly where I stand and what I’ll fight for — without hesitation and without apology.
I am a father, a farmer, and a businessman.
I’m investing in Iowa and I’m my own biggest donor.
I don’t answer to donors or corporations — only to God, my family, and the people of this state.
I believe Iowa can be a beacon — the safest, freest, most family-centered state in America.
That future won’t come from consultants or career politicians.
It will come from courage rooted in place, history, and duty.
What drives me is simple: I want to build a future for my kids and grandkids.
One where they can stay in Iowa, build a family and thrive.
Over the next months, I will be on the road, listening in church basements, VFW halls, farms, and school gyms — where Iowa’s wisdom lives.
This is Iowa.
This is our home.
And it’s worth fighting for.
Zach's promise to Iowans As Governor, some of my top priorities: Free Iowa's Farmers.
We have the best farmland in the world, but the system is rigged so the farmer always comes in last.
It’s time for a change.
Make Iowa Healthy Again.
I believe Big Ag and Big Pharma have treated our farmers and families as numbers, not neighbors.
We will break up monopolies, defend independent farms, and demand accountability from corporations who harm our people.
Keep Iowa land in Iowa hands.
Over 25% of Iowa land is owned by out of state investors and foreign governments.
I will fight for our birthright to own the ground under our feet.
Restore our Education System I believe a classroom is not a battleground for ideology — it is a place for truth, discipline, wonder, and learning.
Anyone who uses their position to push political doctrine will not teach in this state.
Our kids deserve better.

Donate What the Campaign Is Focused On Zach Lahn is running for Governor of Iowa on an Iowa First agenda focused on families, farms, health, education, local ownership, and the future of the state.
Campaign contributions help fund the work required to run a statewide campaign, including voter outreach, advertising, events, travel, communications, printed materials, and campaign operations.
Iowa First Values We need to be able to draw the line.
Keep politics out of our schools and stop letting partisan nonsense redefine the values our communities were built on.
Make Iowa Healthy Again Too many Iowa families have a cancer story.
Zach’s published plan calls for independent safety testing of agricultural products, more Iowa-focused cancer research, and additional action on improving our water quality.
Keep Iowa Land in Iowa Hands Who owns Iowa soil twenty years from now matters.
A quarter of our land is owned by people who don’t live in Iowa – investors who treat Iowa like an annuity.

Zach will require human-level disclosure of who owns our land, tighten and enforce the laws to stop hedge funds and foreign adversaries from buying up our farms and homes, and give young Iowans a fair shot at owning a home and building a farm.
Make Education #1 Again Parents should have access to excellent schools.

Zach’s education plans include giving teachers more room to innovate, reducing reliance on standardized testing, strengthening public schools, and directing Iowa universities toward Iowa students and Iowa problems.
Keep Iowa’s Kids in Iowa Our kids should not feel like they have to leave Iowa to find opportunity.
Like many Iowa kids, Zach left, then came home.
His goal is to make sure the next generation never has to leave to find opportunity.
That means homes young families can afford, farms young Iowans can start, schools that are number one again, and an Iowa that puts Iowans first.
Count On Clean Water Clean water should be something every Iowan can count on.
Zach’s plan invests in water monitoring, targeted conservation, and proven solutions like wetlands, saturated buffers, and cover crops—while working with farmers, not against them.
Improve Affordability A great Iowa life should still be attainable.
Zach’s platform includes lowering the property tax burden on Iowans, expanding paths to homeownership, and banning hedge funds from buying single-family Iowa homes.
Expand Food Freedom Make Iowa the country’s real food capital.
Zach wants to make it easier for Iowa farmers and producers to sell directly to Iowa families and create innovation incentives for farmers who diversify into food production.

See the Food Freedom Plan Protect Iowa Culture Iowa culture should be built upon common sense principles Zach’s plan focuses on safe communities, parental rights, protecting life, supporting law enforcement, and keeping explicit material out of K–12 classrooms.

The Iowa We Leave to Our Kids.
Explore Issues • IOWA FIRST POLICIES Some Lines Are Worth Drawing.
Zach is clear about where he stands.
He will: Protect life before birth and work to improve the health of Iowa families after birth.
End state benefits for illegal immigrants.
Put Iowans first for jobs in state government and Iowa’s public universities.
Lower the tax burden on Iowa families.
Keep partisan political advocacy out of Iowa classrooms.
Iowa government should serve Iowans, first and always.
Issues Confront Iowa’s Cancer Crisis Iowa needs answers.
And we can’t wait on Washington to find them.
Zach has made confronting Iowa’s cancer rates a central priority.
His plan includes: Independent state-level safety testing of products used in Iowa.
Directing more University of Iowa and Iowa State research toward Iowa’s cancer crisis.
Investigating environmental, agricultural, and water-quality factors.
Connecting cancer research with Iowa’s water, food, and agricultural policies.
The goal is measurable: move Iowa into the bottom half of states for cancer diagnoses within four years.
Clean Water Clean water should be something every Iowan can count on.
Iowa does not have to choose between clean water and strong agriculture.
Zach’s plan is to work with farmers, not against them, and invest in proven solutions that reduce runoff while keeping family farms economically strong.
That includes: Funding Iowa I-WILL and directing funds toward the water quality crisis.
Stronger incentives for cover crops, buffer strips, and other proven conservation practices.
Focusing resources where runoff and contamination are most serious.
Supporting practices that improve both soil and water.
Putting Iowa’s universities and state resources to work solving Iowa’s water problems.
Farmers should not carry this burden alone.
Clean water is a shared responsibility.
Make Iowa More Affordable A good life in Iowa should still be attainable.
Owning a home, raising a family, and building wealth should not keep getting harder.
Zach will focus on: Lowering the tax burden on Iowa families.
Reducing property taxes, with the long-term goal of eliminating them for single-family primary homes Raising the tax burden on out-of-state institutional investors instead of Iowa families.
Banning Wall Street hedge funds from buying Iowa single-family homes.
Supporting local food and food-freedom policies that create new opportunities for Iowa farmers.
Affordability is not just about what things cost.
It is also about who owns the homes, farms, businesses, and land that make up Iowa.
Save the Family Farm Keep Iowa land in Iowa hands.
The family farm is not just part of Iowa’s past.
It has to be part of Iowa’s future.
Zach’s plan includes: Cracking down on illegal foreign ownership of Iowa farmland.
Selling illegally owned land back to young Iowa families and veterans where legally permitted.
Raising property taxes on certain institutional investors while lowering the burden on Iowa family farms.
Pursuing antitrust action against agricultural monopolies.
Stopping eminent domain from being used for private corporate gain.
Creating low-interest financing and mentorship pathways for young farmers and veterans.
Directing more Iowa research toward the problems facing Iowa agriculture.
The goal is to reverse the decline in family farms and create 10,000 new family farms in four years.
Make Iowa Education #1 Again Iowa schools should be built around learning, not bureaucracy.
Zach wants Iowa’s public schools competing with the best schools in the country.
His plan includes: Making the governor’s office the strongest advocate for public-school students.
Creating innovation zones that give superintendents, principals, and teachers more freedom to try what works.
Dramatically reducing reliance on standardized testing.
Taking disciplinary action when teachers use the classroom for partisan political advocacy instead of teaching the curriculum.
Providing non-punitive off-ramps for students needing behavioral support.
Expanding opportunities for Iowa students at the University of Iowa and Iowa State University.
The goal: put Iowa education back in the top five nationally.
Keep Iowa’s Kids in Iowa Give the next generation a reason to stay.
Young Iowans should not have to leave the state to find opportunity.
Zach wants Iowa to be a place where young people can: Buy their first home.
Come home after college or time away.
His plan includes tax rebates that can help young Iowans who stay or return with a home down payment.
But keeping young people here requires more than one program.
Fix the fundamentals: water, health, schools, farming, housing, and economic opportunity.
Let’s Not Lose the Iowa We Love.

title.after: Zach Lahn for Governor | Preserve Iowa Together

added: Skip to main content Hit enter to search or ESC to close Search Close Search Menu About Issues All Issues Cancer Clean Water Affordability Farming Education Keeping Iowa’s Youth Events Debates Merch Donate Find My Polling Location Help Zach Win The Iowa We Love Will Not Preserve Itself.

Iowa should be the state where kids grow up and want to stay, because a young couple can buy a home, a young farmer can buy ground, the water is safe to drink, the schools are the best in the country, and family is close by.
Help Zach Win Iowa for You .
Every policy decision should start with one question: What will this change do to our community?
That question has been missing from politics for too long, and it’s the foundation of Zach’s Iowa First approach: think long-term, protect what makes Iowa strong, and put our communities first.
Iowa First Values We need to be able to draw the line.
Keep politics out of our schools and stop letting partisan nonsense redefine the values our communities were built on.
Make Iowa Healthy Again Too many Iowa families have a cancer story.
Zach’s published plan calls for independent safety testing of agricultural products, more Iowa-focused cancer research, and additional action on improving our water quality.
Keep Iowa Land in Iowa Hands Who owns Iowa soil twenty years from now matters.
A quarter of our land is owned by people who don’t live in Iowa – investors who treat Iowa like an annuity.

Zach will require human-level disclosure of who owns our land, tighten and enforce the laws to stop hedge funds and foreign adversaries from buying up our farms and homes, and give young Iowans a fair shot at owning a home and building a farm.
Make Education #1 Again Parents should have access to excellent schools.

Zach’s education plans include giving teachers more room to innovate, reducing reliance on standardized testing, strengthening public schools, and directing Iowa universities toward Iowa students and Iowa problems.
Keep Iowa’s Kids in Iowa Our kids should not feel like they have to leave Iowa to find opportunity.
Like many Iowa kids, Zach left, then came home.
His goal is to make sure the next generation never has to leave to find opportunity.
That means homes young families can afford, farms young Iowans can start, schools that are number one again, and an Iowa that puts Iowans first.
Count On Clean Water Clean water should be something every Iowan can count on.
Zach’s plan invests in water monitoring, targeted conservation, and proven solutions like wetlands, saturated buffers, and cover crops—while working with farmers, not against them.
Improve Affordability A great Iowa life should still be attainable.
Zach’s platform includes lowering the property tax burden on Iowans, expanding paths to homeownership, and banning hedge funds from buying single-family Iowa homes.
Expand Food Freedom Make Iowa the country’s real food capital.
Zach wants to make it easier for Iowa farmers and producers to sell directly to Iowa families and create innovation incentives for farmers who diversify into food production.

See the Food Freedom Plan Protect Iowa Culture Iowa culture should be built upon common sense principles Zach’s plan focuses on safe communities, parental rights, protecting life, supporting law enforcement, and keeping explicit material out of K–12 classrooms.
Where Does Zach Stand on Culture?
Iowa should work for the people who call Iowa home.
Zach Lahn is a husband and father, businessman, farmer, and sixth-generation Iowan.
Learn More About Zach See His Plan for Iowa You Shouldn’t Have to Wonder If Your Family Is Next.
Cancer has touched too many Iowa families.
Iowa has the fastest-growing rate of new cancers in America.
And for too long, special interests have got our leaders to look the other way.
As governor, Zach will launch independent Iowa research into agricultural products and consumer products, with no corporate influence, and publish the results publicly.
He’ll work alongside farmers to mitigate run off and clean up our drinking water, and put prevention first.
Iowans deserve answers, and Zach is committed to getting them.
Iowa should be looking for answers.
SEE ZACH'S PLAN Iowa Values vs.
Certain people want you to forget where they stand on the controversial issues of our day.
Iowa needs a leader grounded in the values that have shaped this state for generations: Faith.
Leaving something better for the next generation.
Iowa did not become Iowa by accident.
Generations before us built a culture around Midwest values that they passed down to us.
Zach’s message is that our generation has a duty too: know what we inherited, defend our way of life, and hand Iowa to the next generation stronger than we found it.
See Where Zach Stands Build an Iowa Worth Staying For.
Every year, Iowa loses thousands, as kids graduate, pack up, and build their lives somewhere else.
That’s empty seats at Friday night football games, closed shops on Main Street, and farms with no one to take them over.
Zach is running to reverse this trend.
Still Figuring Out What You Think?
You should know more about a candidate than just the letter next to his name.
BROWSE THE ISSUES MEET ZACH A Sixth-Generation Iowan Zach’s family roots in Iowa run deep.
In 1862, his great-great-great-grandfather, Hans Schluntz, answered Governor Kirkwood’s call and rode with Iowa’s Second Cavalry in the Civil War.
Father of Seven Zach and Annie have seven kids.
He’s fighting so they, their kids, and every Iowa kid have a reason to build their life right here at home.
Farmer Zach farms the family homestead today, using regenerative practices to protect soil health and water quality.
As governor, he’ll fight to save family farms, get young Iowans back on the land, and keep Iowa land in Iowa hands.
Businessman Zach is a business owner and believes Iowa should invest in the businesses, workers, and communities that are invested here.
Investing Locally Zach and his family have worked to restore pieces of Belle Plaine’s history such as the King Theater, pictured above.
The Iowa We Love Will Not Preserve Itself.

removed: Skip to content About Merch Contact Us Donate Events Zach’s Policies Volunteer Donate Policy IOWA FIRST: CORE PHILOSOPHY Iowa First is more than a slogan—it's a commitment to prioritize Iowa families, Iowa-owned businesses, and Iowa's long-term health over corporate interests, out-of-state investors, and political expediency.
Iowans deserve things they can count on: a government that prioritizes people, low taxes, clean water, healthy kids, safe communities, and excellent schools.
Local ownership and stewardship matter—those who live here care most about our communities.
Iowa's universities should solve Iowa's problems before global ones.
Iowa economic development should focus on Iowa-based companies with deep roots in our communities.
Measurable Four-Year Goals: Reverse youth outmigration — Iowa currently ranks #4 nationally for net outmigration of 25-29 year-olds.
10,000 new family farms — Reverse the loss of 10,000 farms over the past 20 years.
Education back in top 5 nationally — It’s time to put innovation back into the classroom.
Move Iowa to bottom half of Cancer Diagnoses — Iowa currently #2 for new diagnoses, #1 for fastest rising rates.

COMMON-SENSE CONSERVATIVE POLICIES Protect Life Every life is a gift from God and it is our duty to protect life before birth, as well as after birth by addressing chronic health issues facing our kids.
No Benefits for Illegal Immigrants We will ban benefits for illegal immigrants, and stop issuing H1B visas for jobs that Iowans can do in state government and in our universities.
Focus on Affordability Lessening the tax burden on Iowans, food freedom policies and banning Wall Street hedge-funds from buying single family homes will help make life affordable for Iowa families.
CONFRONT THE CANCER CRISIS Independent Safety Testing Conduct independent state safety tests on products used in Iowa.
Hold Companies Accountable Pursue antitrust suits against monopolistic agricultural input companies to help our farmers.
University Research Redirection The University of Iowa (one of the best medical research colleges in the country) must aim its efforts at solving Iowa's cancer crisis.
Clean Water Priority Give incentives to our farmers to use proven solutions that address agricultural runoff and water contamination.
SAVE THE FAMILY FARM Foreign and Out-of-State Ownership Restrictions 1.
Lower property taxes for Iowans by raising property tax rates on Wall Street institutional investors.
Confiscate any land illegally owned by China and sell that land back to young families and veterans.
Antitrust Action Against Agricultural Monopolies File antitrust suits against the big agricultural input companies that have formed monopolies and are extorting our farmers.
No Eminent Domain for Private Gain Absolutely oppose use of eminent domain for private company profit.
Economic Development for Iowa-Owned Companies End tax credits and economic development funds for out-of-state and foreign corporations and prioritize Iowa-based companies with deep community roots.
Support Young Farmers Create pathways and incentives for young farmers to access land.
MAKE IOWA EDUCATION #1 AGAIN Revoke Teaching Licenses for Political Indoctrination If a teacher is caught pushing a political agenda in the classroom, their teaching license will be revoked, period.
The Governor Must Be the #1 Advocate for Public School Kids Focus on making public schools so good they are competing with private schools.
Innovation Zones Create innovation zones to free up superintendents, principals, and teachers to innovate.
End Teaching to the Test Eliminate or dramatically reduce standardized testing requirements and focus on mastery of skills.
University Priorities for Iowa Students Increase quota for Iowa residents at University of Iowa and Iowa State University and task them with solving Iowa's cancer and farming crisis.
KEEP IOWA'S KIDS IN IOWA Economic Incentives to Stay Create tax rebates for young Iowans who stay or return to Iowa for down payment assistance for home ownership.

Solve our other issues, and our young people will stay and come back If we solve the water, cancer, education and farming issues facing our state, Iowa will be the most attractive place in America for our young families to live. things you should just be able to count on.
Our campaign is about restoring things Iowa families should be able to count on: Clean water — you can drink it, swim in it, and your kids can play in it.
Healthy kids — not the fastest rising cancer rates in the world.
Good schools — back in the top 5 nationally where we belong.
Safe communities — built on strong families and traditions.
Family farms — not corporate consolidation and foreign ownership.
Economic opportunity — for Iowans, by Iowans, staying in Iowa.
A future in Iowa — where your kids want to stay and build their lives.
These are not too much to ask.
These are the basics.
And it's time we had a governor willing to fight for them.
“This is home.

removed: Skip to content About Merch Contact Us Donate Events Zach’s Policies Volunteer Donate Privacy Policy Who we are Suggested text: Our website address is: http://www.zachlahn.com.

Comments Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.
An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it.
The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/.
After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.
Media Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included.
Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.
Cookies Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies.
These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment.
These cookies will last for one year.
If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies.
This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.
When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices.
Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year.
If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks.
If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.
If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser.
This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited.
It expires after 1 day.
Embedded content from other websites Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.).
Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.
Who we share your data with Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.
How long we retain your data Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely.
This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.
For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile.
All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username).
Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us.
You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you.
This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.
Where your data is sent Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

added: Skip to main content Hit enter to search or ESC to close Search Close Search Menu About Issues All Issues Cancer Clean Water Affordability Farming Education Keeping Iowa’s Youth Events Debates Merch Donate Find My Polling Location Help Zach Win LAST UPDATED: SEPTEMBER 2026 Website Policies & Disclosures This page explains the terms that apply when you use zachlahn.com , how Lahn for Governor may collect and use information, and other important website, campaign, accessibility, and communication policies.
By using this website, you agree to the terms described below.

Terms of Use This website is operated by Lahn for Governor and is provided for campaign information, voter education, fundraising, volunteer coordination, events, merchandise, communications, and related purposes.

You agree to use the website only for lawful purposes and not to: Interfere with the operation or security of the website Attempt to access restricted areas without authorization Submit false, fraudulent, or misleading information Introduce malicious software or harmful code Impersonate another person or organization Use website content in violation of applicable law Privacy Policy Lahn for Governor respects your privacy and is committed to handling information responsibly.

We may collect information you voluntarily provide, including: Name Email address Phone number Mailing address ZIP code Volunteer interests Event registration information Information submitted through website forms Information related to campaign contributions Information related to merchandise purchases We may also automatically collect certain technical information, including: IP address Browser and device information Pages visited Referring websites Approximate location based on IP address Website interactions and traffic data How We Use Information Information may be used to: Send campaign news and updates Coordinate volunteers Provide event information Respond to questions and requests Provide voting and election information Process contributions Process merchandise orders Improve website performance Measure advertising and outreach Protect website security Comply with legal and campaign finance requirements Email Communications If you sign up for campaign emails, we may send you: Campaign news Event announcements Volunteer opportunities Issue updates Voting information Fundraising messages Other campaign communications You may unsubscribe at any time using the unsubscribe link included in campaign emails.

Text Message Terms If you choose to opt in to campaign text messages, you may receive recurring messages from Lahn for Governor related to campaign news, events, volunteer opportunities, fundraising, voting information, and other campaign activity.
Message and data rates may apply.
You may reply STOP to unsubscribe and HELP for help.
Consent to receive text messages is not a condition of making a contribution, purchasing merchandise, or using this website.
Wireless carriers are not responsible for delayed or undelivered messages.
Additional disclosures may appear at the point where you provide your mobile number.
Campaign Contributions Campaign contributions may be processed through third-party fundraising platforms such as WinRed.
When making a contribution, you may be required to provide information necessary to comply with applicable campaign finance laws.
Certain contributor information may be collected, retained, or publicly reported as required by law.

By making a contribution, you represent that: The information you provide is accurate You are legally permitted to make the contribution You understand and agree to any contributor certifications presented during the contribution process Third-party fundraising platforms may have additional terms and privacy policies that apply to your contribution.
Merchandise Purchases Campaign merchandise may be sold or fulfilled through third-party vendors.
Product availability, pricing, shipping, fulfillment, returns, and exchanges may be subject to the policies of those vendors.
Information necessary to complete your purchase may be shared with payment processors, fulfillment providers, shipping providers, and other vendors involved in processing the transaction.
Shipping, Returns & Exchanges Shipping times and availability may vary.
Unless otherwise stated on the merchandise store, shipping, return, exchange, and refund policies are governed by the vendor fulfilling the order.
Please refer to the applicable merchandise store or order confirmation for specific details.
Events Campaign event dates, times, locations, speakers, schedules, and availability may change.
Registration does not guarantee admission unless specifically stated.
Lahn for Governor may modify, relocate, postpone, or cancel events when necessary.
Attendance at certain events may be subject to additional rules, venue requirements, or registration terms.
Volunteer Participation Participation in campaign volunteer activities is voluntary.
Volunteers may receive additional instructions or expectations based on the type of activity.
Lahn for Governor may limit or discontinue participation in volunteer activities when appropriate.
Social Media & Shareable Campaign Content The campaign may provide supporters with graphics, videos, profile images, social media templates, signs, and other materials intended to be shared.
Campaign materials made available specifically for supporter use may be shared for their intended purpose.

Materials may not be altered or used in a way that: Falsely represents Zach Lahn or Lahn for Governor Misrepresents another candidate, person, or organization Creates the appearance of an endorsement that does not exist Violates applicable law or platform policies Intellectual Property Unless otherwise stated, website content including text, graphics, logos, photography, video, design elements, and other materials is owned by or licensed to Lahn for Governor.
Content may not be reproduced, sold, modified, distributed, or used commercially without permission, except for campaign materials specifically made available for supporter sharing.

Third-Party Websites & Services This website may contain links to or integrations with third-party services, including: Social media platforms Fundraising platforms Merchandise stores Video platforms Event registration services Email and text messaging services Analytics platforms Advertising platforms Voting information resources Lahn for Governor does not control these third-party services and is not responsible for their content, availability, security, privacy practices, or terms.
Use of third-party services is subject to the policies of those providers.

Voting Information Lahn for Governor may provide information about: Voter registration Absentee voting Election dates Polling locations Voter identification Election deadlines We make reasonable efforts to provide accurate information, but election rules, dates, locations, and procedures may change.
For official election information, voters should verify details through the Iowa Secretary of State or their county auditor or local election office .
Accessibility Lahn for Governor is committed to making zachlahn.com accessible and usable for as many people as possible.
We work to improve accessibility and aim to follow recognized accessibility standards and best practices.
Data Security We take reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational measures to protect information collected through this website.
However, no website, database, or online transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

Data Retention We may retain information for as long as reasonably necessary to: Operate the campaign Maintain campaign records Comply with legal requirements Meet campaign finance obligations Resolve disputes Protect the campaign and website Fulfill legitimate campaign purposes Certain records may be retained longer when required by law.

How We Share Information We may share information with vendors and service providers that help operate the campaign, including: Website providers Email and SMS platforms Advertising services Fundraising platforms Payment processors Merchandise vendors Event platforms Analytics providers Technology vendors We may also disclose information when required by law, regulation, court order, campaign finance requirements, or other legal obligations.
We do not sell personal information in the ordinary sense of exchanging personal information directly for money.
Children’s Privacy This website is intended for a general audience and is not directed toward children under 13.
We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 through this website.
Website Accuracy Lahn for Governor makes reasonable efforts to keep website information accurate and current.
Campaign schedules, events, policies, media appearances, endorsements, election information, and other content may change.
We do not guarantee that every page will always be complete, current, or error-free.
Disclaimer of Warranties This website and its content are provided on an “as is” and “as available” basis.
To the fullest extent permitted by law, Lahn for Governor makes no warranties regarding the availability, accuracy, reliability, or operation of the website.

Limitation of Liability To the fullest extent permitted by law, Lahn for Governor and its officers, employees, volunteers, vendors, and representatives will not be liable for indirect, incidental, consequential, special, or similar damages arising from your use of, or inability to use, this website.
Nothing in this section limits liability where doing so would be prohibited by law.

Indemnification To the extent permitted by law, you agree to indemnify and hold harmless Lahn for Governor and its officers, employees, volunteers, vendors, and representatives from claims, damages, losses, liabilities, or expenses resulting from your unlawful use of this website or violation of these terms.
Changes to These Policies We may update these Website Policies & Disclosures from time to time.
Any updates will be posted on this page with a revised “Last Updated” date.
Your continued use of the website after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.
Governing Law These policies are governed by the laws of the State of Iowa, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
Any dispute relating to these policies or use of this website is subject to applicable Iowa and federal law.

added: CHIP IN $10 TODAY TO SUPPORT ZACH NUNN >> ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER DONATE Close Trigger DONATE Nunn Calls Out Trone Garriott for Fundraising Instead of Debating Before Iowans Vote Des Moines, IA – Combat aviator and U.S.

Representative Zach Nunn (IA-03) released the following statement after voting early this morning on the first day of early voting in Iowa and accepting a KCCI debate with Sarah Trone Garriott on October 27.
“Over a month ago, I said yes to six debates on four stations, all before early voting, so I’m disappointed that Sarah Trone Garriott said no to all of them,” said Rep.
“It’s critical Iowans hear from both candidates, especially before they cast their ballots.
Early voting started today, and Trone Garriott still hasn’t said yes.
She said she’s completely booked until October 27, but she’s found time to fundraise outside Iowa.
So I’m asking one more time: let’s debate now, tomorrow, or on October 27.

The time for Iowans to hear from us is now.” Nunn accepted KCCI’s target dates of October 16 and October 20 at the beginning of September, then added October 14 and October 21 so Iowans could hear from both candidates before or in the first week of early voting.
He also accepted debates with WHO 13 and Iowa PBS for any date through October 21.

After more than a month of dodging a debate, the Trone Garriott campaign turned down every one of those dates and told KCCI and the Nunn campaign that the earliest she could debate was October 27 , two weeks after Iowans start voting.
By that point in the 2024 cycle, more than 124,000 3rd District voters had already cast their ballot.
Every other candidate for governor, U.S.
Senate and Congress in Iowa accepted a debate before early voting started.
Trone Garriott claimed her schedule was full.

Yet, as the Daily Signal reported , she has found time to fundraise in Chicago and is headlining a Dallas County fundraiser with tickets of up to $3,500 on October 21, one of the nights she said she couldn’t debate.
Nunn has now accepted October 27 under KCCI’s standard format, the same format the station has used for a decade: no notes on stage and no questions shared in advance.
The Trone Garriott campaign has yet to agree to those rules.
